`Makefile`:

```
# Savage Wind build
# macOS: Homebrew clang/SDL3/FFmpeg, Metal renderer.
# Windows: MSYS2 UCRT64 shell (see docs/BUILD-windows.md), clang + Vulkan renderer.
# Linux: clang + Vulkan renderer, x86-64 or aarch64 (see docs/linux.md).
UNAME := $(shell uname -s)
comma := ,
ifneq ($(filter MINGW% MSYS% CYGWIN% Windows_NT,$(UNAME) $(OS)),)
PLATFORM := windows
else ifeq ($(UNAME),Linux)
PLATFORM := linux
else
PLATFORM := macos
endif

# Linux: ARCH (x86_64 / aarch64, default this machine's) picks the target, separately from PLATFORM. The generated code
# differs per arch (AArch64 hosts run the guest's FP/SIMD as inline asm, others use the portable C of simd.h), so a
# cross build has its own generated-<arch>/ and build/<arch>/; SYSROOT is the target's root filesystem (headers, libs).
GEN      ?= generated
ifeq ($(PLATFORM),linux)
HOSTARCH := $(patsubst arm64,aarch64,$(shell uname -m))
ARCH     ?= $(HOSTARCH)
ifneq ($(ARCH),$(HOSTARCH))
CROSS    := --target=$(ARCH)-linux-gnu $(if $(SYSROOT),--sysroot=$(SYSROOT))
GEN      := generated-$(ARCH)
B        ?= build/$(ARCH)
endif
GENSIMD  := --simd $(if $(filter aarch64,$(ARCH)),asm,c)
endif

# B: build dir. MACOS_MIN: oldest macOS to run on (default: this one). DEPS: prefix with SDL3 / FFmpeg instead of
# Homebrew's (make deps). `make app` sets all three (build/mac15, 15.0, build/deps); plain `make` uses none.
B         ?= build
MACOS_MIN ?=
DEPS      ?=
MINFLAG  := $(if $(MACOS_MIN),-mmacosx-version-min=$(MACOS_MIN))
CC       := clang $(MINFLAG) $(CROSS)
CXX      := clang++ $(MINFLAG) $(CROSS)
IMGUI    := third_party/imgui
GENFLAGS := -O1 -fno-strict-aliasing -Wno-return-type -Wno-unused-label -fvisibility=hidden -Iruntime
# RECOMP_LOCALS=1 (the default since Alpha 5): the generator keeps each function's most used registers and its flags in
# C locals (gen.py --locals, docs/RECOMP-LOCALS.md); RECOMP_LOCALS=0 builds the plain game code. It is part of
# GAMELIB_ID, so a library built one way is never loaded for the other.
RECOMP_LOCALS ?= 1
GENLOCALS := $(if $(filter 1,$(RECOMP_LOCALS)),--locals)
# The start screen's zig cc reads -O1 as its own "fast" mode (clang -O2 with the loop and SLP vectorizers) and adds
# debug info and frame pointers: these give it what clang -O1 builds here, in a third less time (runtime/gamebuild.c)
GENFLAGS_ZIG := -Xclang $(filter -O%,$(GENFLAGS)) -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize -g0 -fomit-frame-pointer

# The game code (made by `make gen` from your own game files) is its own library next to the app (runtime/gamelib.h);
# the app itself holds none of it. $(GEN)/layout.c, then a folder per module (main, subsdk*, sdk)
GEN_SRC  := $(wildcard $(GEN)/*.c) $(wildcard $(GEN)/*/*.c)
GEN_OBJ  := $(patsubst %.c,$(B)/obj/%.o,$(patsubst $(GEN)/%,%,$(GEN_SRC))) $(B)/obj/tools/gamelib_entry.o
RT_SRC   := $(filter-out runtime/control.c runtime/control_game.c,$(wildcard runtime/*.c)) \
            runtime/control.c runtime/control_game.c $(wildcard runtime/hle/*.c) $(wildcard runtime/services/*.c) \
            $(wildcard runtime/nvn/*.c) $(wildcard runtime/nvn/maxwell/*.c) runtime/platform/$(PLATFORM).c
RT_HDRS  := $(wildcard runtime/*.h) $(wildcard runtime/platform/*.h) $(wildcard runtime/nvn/*.h) \
            $(wildcard runtime/nvn/maxwell/*.h) $(wildcard runtime/nvn/vulkan/*.h) $(wildcard runtime/ui/*.h) \
            $(wildcard runtime/services/*.h)
UI_SRC   := $(wildcard runtime/ui/*.mm)
UI_OBJ   := $(patsubst runtime/%.mm,$(B)/rt/%.o,$(UI_SRC))
IMGUI_OBJ := $(B)/imgui/imgui.o $(B)/imgui/imgui_draw.o $(B)/imgui/imgui_tables.o $(B)/imgui/imgui_widgets.o \
             $(B)/imgui/imgui_impl_sdl3.o

ifeq ($(PLATFORM),macos)
SDL      := $(or $(DEPS),/opt/homebrew/opt/sdl3)
FFMPEG   := $(or $(DEPS),/opt/homebrew/opt/ffmpeg)
EXE      := $(B)/savagewind
DEPINC   := -I$(SDL)/include -I$(FFMPEG)/include
LDFLAGS  := -L$(SDL)/lib -lSDL3 -Wl,-rpath,$(SDL)/lib -L$(FFMPEG)/lib -lavformat -lavcodec -lavutil -lswscale -Wl,-rpath,$(FFMPEG)/lib \
            -framework CoreFoundation -framework Foundation -framework Metal -framework MetalFX -framework QuartzCore -framework AppKit -framework ImageIO -framework CoreGraphics -framework UniformTypeIdentifiers
BACKEND_SRC := $(wildcard runtime/nvn/*.m)
BACKEND_OBJ := $(patsubst runtime/%.m,$(B)/rt/%.o,$(BACKEND_SRC))
IMGUI_OBJ += $(B)/imgui/imgui_impl_metal.o
UIFLAGS  := -fobjc-arc
GAMELIB  := $(B)/swgame.dylib
GAMELIB_LDFLAGS := -dynamiclib -undefined dynamic_lookup  # (the runtime functions it calls: the app's own)
GAMELIB_SHARED := -shared -Wl,-undefined,dynamic_lookup  # (the same, for the start screen's build: zig cc)
else ifeq ($(PLATFORM),linux)
EXE      := $(B)/savagewind
DEPINC   := $(if $(DEPS),-I$(DEPS)/include,$(shell pkg-config --cflags libavformat 2>/dev/null))  # (openSUSE has them in /usr/include/ffmpeg)
ifeq ($(ARCH),x86_64)
GENARCH  ?= -march=x86-64-v3  # as on Windows: AVX2 + FMA for the lifted FP/SIMD code (checked at startup)
GENARCH_COMPAT ?= -march=x86-64-v2  # CPUs without them (GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT below)
endif
GENFLAGS += $(GENARCH) -fPIC
OSFLAGS  := -Wno-format  # (%llx for uint64_t, which is unsigned long here: the same size)
# shaderc is libshaderc.so on Debian / Ubuntu and libshaderc_shared.so on Fedora, Arch and a shaderc built from source:
# tools/linux/build_deps.sh builds only the shaderc_shared target, so a DEPS prefix has no libshaderc.so at all - -lshaderc
# there would silently fall through to the system path, where Arch's shaderc package has a static libshaderc.a that is
# only the C wrapper (undefined shaderc_util symbols at the real link). A DEPS prefix therefore links -lshaderc_shared.
# Elsewhere pkg-config knows the name. Without a .pc, the probe links an executable that calls shaderc and tries
# -lshaderc_shared before -lshaderc, so an incomplete static libshaderc.a is rejected at probe time too. A shared-only
# probe cannot do that: a shared link keeps undefined symbols and only the executable link or run fails.
SHADERC_TEST := extern void *shaderc_compiler_initialize(void); int main(void){return shaderc_compiler_initialize()==0;}
SHADERC  ?= $(if $(DEPS),-lshaderc_shared,$(or $(shell pkg-config --libs shaderc 2>/dev/null),\
             $(shell echo '$(SHADERC_TEST)' | $(CC) -x c - -lshaderc_shared -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null && echo -lshaderc_shared),\
             $(shell echo '$(SHADERC_TEST)' | $(CC) -x c - -lshaderc -o /dev/null 2>/dev/null && echo -lshaderc),-lshaderc))
# -rdynamic: crash backtraces name host functions (runtime/platform/linux.c)
LDFLAGS  := -fuse-ld=lld -rdynamic $(if $(DEPS),-L$(DEPS)/lib) -lSDL3 -lavformat -lavcodec -lavutil -lswscale \
            -lvulkan $(SHADERC) -lz -lpthread -ldl -lm
BACKEND_SRC := $(wildcard runtime/nvn/vulkan/*.c) $(wildcard runtime/nvn/vulkan/*.cpp)
BACKEND_OBJ := $(patsubst runtime/%.cpp,$(B)/rt/%.o,$(patsubst runtime/%.c,$(B)/rt/%.o,$(BACKEND_SRC)))
IMGUI_OBJ += $(B)/imgui/imgui_impl_vulkan.o
UIFLAGS  := -x c++  # the .mm UI sources are plain C++ apart from __APPLE__ blocks
GAMELIB  := $(B)/swgame.so
GAMELIB_LDFLAGS := -shared -fuse-ld=lld  # (the runtime functions it calls: the app's own, -rdynamic)
GAMELIB_SHARED := -shared
else
EXE      := $(B)/savagewind.exe
DEPINC   := $(if $(DEPS),-I$(DEPS)/include)
OSFLAGS  := -D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 -D_POSIX_THREAD_SAFE_FUNCTIONS -D_CRT_RAND_S -DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN -DNOMINMAX
GENARCH  ?= -march=x86-64-v3  # AVX2 + FMA for the lifted FP/SIMD code (simd.h)
GENARCH_COMPAT ?= -march=x86-64-v2  # CPUs without them (GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT below)
GENFLAGS += -D_FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 $(GENARCH)
# --stack: every thread's default stack, reserved (committed as it grows): 256 MB, the guest threads' recursion runs on
# it (runtime/kernel.c thread_start)
LDFLAGS  := -fuse-ld=lld -Wl,--stack,268435456 $(if $(DEPS),-L$(DEPS)/lib) -lSDL3 -lavformat -lavcodec -lavutil -lswscale \
            -lvulkan-1 -lwinmm -lole32 -lshell32 -lcomdlg32 -luuid -lgdi32 -ladvapi32 -lshaderc_shared -lpdh -lws2_32 -lwinhttp -l:libz.a -lpthread \
            $(if $(RELEASE),-Wl$(comma)--subsystem$(comma)windows)  # release: no console window (log -> savagewind.log)
BACKEND_SRC := $(wildcard runtime/nvn/vulkan/*.c) $(wildcard runtime/nvn/vulkan/*.cpp)
BACKEND_OBJ := $(patsubst runtime/%.cpp,$(B)/rt/%.o,$(patsubst runtime/%.c,$(B)/rt/%.o,$(BACKEND_SRC)))
BACKEND_OBJ += $(B)/rt/platform/windows_rc.o  # the .exe's icon (Explorer, taskbar)
WINDRES  ?= windres
IMGUI_OBJ += $(B)/imgui/imgui_impl_vulkan.o
UIFLAGS  := -x c++ $(OSFLAGS)  # the .mm UI sources are plain C++ apart from __APPLE__ blocks
GAMELIB  := $(B)/swgame.dll
# the runtime functions it calls: exported by the .exe, linked through its import library
LDFLAGS  += -Wl,--export-all-symbols -Wl,--out-implib,$(B)/savagewind.dll.a
GAMELIB_LDFLAGS := -shared -fuse-ld=lld $(B)/savagewind.dll.a
GAMELIB_SHARED := -shared  # (+ the import library: runtime/gamebuild.c)
# "Savage Wind Configuration.exe" in the release: starts savagewind.exe --config (runtime/platform/windows_config.c)
CONFIG_EXE := $(B)/savagewind-config.exe
endif

# GAMELIB_ID: what the game code library is built from (the generator, the headers it is compiled against, the
# flags). A library with another id is rebuilt by the start screen, never loaded.
GAMELIB_SRCS := tools/gen.py tools/lifter.py tools/analyze.py tools/nso.py tools/passes.py tools/patches.py \
                tools/simd_c.py tools/regs.py tools/flags.py tools/gamelib_entry.c runtime/hle/hle_symbols.txt \
                runtime/cpu.h runtime/simd.h runtime/simd_fp.h runtime/simd_softfma.h runtime/gamelib.h
GAMELIB_SRCS += tools/layout.py tools/game_sites.py
GAMELIB_ID := $(shell (cat $(GAMELIB_SRCS); echo '$(strip $(GENFLAGS))'; echo '$(GENFLAGS_ZIG)'; echo 'gen $(GENLOCALS)') | (shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null || sha256sum) | cut -c1-16)
# The compatible target (#9): x86-64 CPUs without AVX2 / FMA / BMI2 get the game code built with GENARCH_COMPAT in
# place of GENARCH (no -mfma: simd.h's fma is runtime/simd_softfma.h, slower). The start screen builds the one the CPU
# runs (runtime/gamelib.h gamelib_compat); its id differs, so neither library is ever loaded in place of the other.
# `make` builds the GENARCH one.
ifneq ($(strip $(GENARCH)),)
ifneq ($(strip $(GENARCH_COMPAT)),)
GENFLAGS_COMPAT := $(subst $(strip $(GENARCH)),$(strip $(GENARCH_COMPAT)),$(GENFLAGS))
GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT := $(shell (cat $(GAMELIB_SRCS); echo '$(strip $(GENFLAGS_COMPAT))'; echo '$(GENFLAGS_ZIG)'; echo 'gen $(GENLOCALS)') | (shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null || sha256sum) | cut -c1-16)
GAMELIB_TARGETS := -DGAMELIB_ARCH='"$(strip $(GENARCH))"' -DGAMELIB_ARCH_COMPAT='"$(strip $(GENARCH_COMPAT))"' \
                   -DGAMELIB_ID_COMPAT='"$(GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT)"'
endif
endif

# TRANSLATOR_ID / SPIRV_ID: what translated shaders and their SPIR-V are made from: the Maxwell translator (its
# source and the header with the key and the output structures it fills), and the GLSL -> SPIR-V step. The shader
# caches (cache/xlate, cache/spirv, the pipeline list, the precompiled libraries) are kept while these stay the same,
# so builds and updates that do not touch those sources keep them; the device-dependent switches the translator reads
# at run time are not in here (runtime/nvn/maxwell/translate.c maxwell_translation_variant: a translation records
# them itself). Baked into the generated header $(B)/inc/shader_ids.h, rewritten only when a hash changes, which
# translate.o and spirv.o include ahead of their source (-include) and depend on.
TRANSLATOR_SRCS := runtime/nvn/maxwell/translate.c runtime/nvn/maxwell/shader.h
SPIRV_SRCS := runtime/nvn/vulkan/spirv.c
TRANSLATOR_ID := $(shell cat $(TRANSLATOR_SRCS) | (shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null || sha256sum) | cut -c1-16)
SPIRV_ID := $(shell cat $(SPIRV_SRCS) | (shasum -a 256 2>/dev/null || sha256sum) | cut -c1-16)
SHADER_IDS := $(B)/inc/shader_ids.h
# (compared with cat and test, not cmp: MSYS2 has no diffutils unless installed, and a rewrite at every make would
# recompile the translator each time)
$(shell mkdir -p $(B)/inc && printf '#define TRANSLATOR_ID "%s"\n#define SPIRV_ID "%s"\n' '$(TRANSLATOR_ID)' '$(SPIRV_ID)' > $(SHADER_IDS).new && \
        if [ "$$(cat $(SHADER_IDS) 2>/dev/null)" = "$$(cat $(SHADER_IDS).new)" ]; then rm -f $(SHADER_IDS).new; else mv -f $(SHADER_IDS).new $(SHADER_IDS); fi)

# SW_SOURCE: the source this build is made from, in the log's first line (runtime/main.c): its commit and tree, and
# "modified" when the runtime, the tools or this Makefile differ from them ("unknown" outside a git checkout). A
# commit published to test has the tree of the local commit it was made from. $(B)/source_id follows it, so main.o is
# rebuilt when it changes.
comma    := ,
SW_SOURCE := $(or $(shell git log -1 --format='commit %h, tree %t' 2>/dev/null),unknown)$(if $(shell git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no -- runtime tools Makefile 2>/dev/null),$(comma) modified)
$(shell mkdir -p $(B) && [ "$$(cat $(B)/source_id 2>/dev/null)" = '$(SW_SOURCE)' ] || echo '$(SW_SOURCE)' > $(B)/source_id)

RT_OBJ   := $(patsubst runtime/%.c,$(B)/rt/%.o,$(RT_SRC))
RTFLAGS  := -O2 -g -fno-strict-aliasing -Wall -Wno-unused-function -Iruntime -Iruntime/nvn -isystem third_party -isystem third_party/stb $(DEPINC) $(OSFLAGS)
CXXFLAGS := -O2 -g -std=c++17 -I$(IMGUI) -I$(IMGUI)/backends -Iruntime -Iruntime/nvn -isystem third_party -Ithird_party/stb $(DEPINC)

# Optional runtime-only optimization. The generated game library keeps GENFLAGS and its build ID.
# Use a separate B for each mode; the stamp also rebuilds runtime objects when flags or profiles change.
# Profile-guided build of the runtime (not the game library). tools/pgo/runtime.profdata is a ready profile, so
#   make PGO=use B=build-pgo            optimized build, no training needed
# is all most people need. To make a new profile (a profile only fits the clang that wrote it, and goes stale as
# the runtime changes; see tools/pgo/README.md), each step with its own B:
#   make PGO=gen B=build-gen            instrumented savagewind.exe
#   run it (a scripted walk ending with SAVAGEWIND_EXIT_AT=<frame>, or by hand) with LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=<dir>/rt-%p.profraw
#   llvm-profdata merge -o tools/pgo/runtime.profdata <dir>/*.profraw
PGO ?=
LTO ?=
PGO_PROFILE ?= tools/pgo/runtime.profdata
ifneq ($(filter-out gen use,$(PGO)),)
$(error PGO must be empty, gen, or use)
endif
ifneq ($(filter-out thin,$(LTO)),)
$(error LTO must be empty or thin)
endif
RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS := $(if $(LTO),-flto=thin)
RUNTIME_LINKFLAGS := $(if $(LTO),-flto=thin)
ifeq ($(PGO),gen)
RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS += -fprofile-instr-generate -fprofile-update=atomic -mllvm -enable-value-profiling=false -DSW_PGO_GENERATE=1
RUNTIME_LINKFLAGS += -fprofile-instr-generate
endif
ifeq ($(PGO),use)
ifeq ($(wildcard $(PGO_PROFILE)),)
$(error PGO=use needs PGO_PROFILE pointing to a merged runtime profile)
endif
RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS += -fprofile-instr-use=$(PGO_PROFILE)
endif
LDFLAGS += $(RUNTIME_LINKFLAGS)
RUNTIME_CONFIG := $(strip $(RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS))
$(shell mkdir -p $(B) && [ -f $(B)/runtime_config ] && [ "$$(cat $(B)/runtime_config 2>/dev/null)" = '$(RUNTIME_CONFIG)' ] || echo '$(RUNTIME_CONFIG)' > $(B)/runtime_config)
$(RT_OBJ) $(filter $(B)/rt/%,$(BACKEND_OBJ)) $(UI_OBJ): $(B)/runtime_config $(if $(filter use,$(PGO)),$(PGO_PROFILE))

.DEFAULT_GOAL := all

# AMD FidelityFX SDK 1.1.4 (third_party/FidelityFX, MIT): FSR 3 frame interpolation and optical flow
# (runtime/nvn/vulkan/framegen.cpp) and the FSR 3 upscaler (runtime/nvn/vulkan/fsr3.cpp) on its Vulkan backend. Its
# sources unchanged, with ffx_compat.h for what MSVC's headers bring; the shaders are tools/ffx_shaders.py's
# (third_party/FidelityFX/spirv).
FFX      := third_party/FidelityFX
FFX_SRC  := $(FFX)/sdk/src/components/frameinterpolation/ffx_frameinterpolation.cpp \
            $(FFX)/sdk/src/components/opticalflow/ffx_opticalflow.cpp \
            $(FFX)/sdk/src/components/fsr3upscaler/ffx_fsr3upscaler.cpp $(FFX)/sdk/src/backends/vk/ffx_vk.cpp \
            $(wildcard $(FFX)/sdk/src/shared/*.cpp)
FFX_OBJ  := $(patsubst $(FFX)/sdk/src/%.cpp,$(B)/ffx/%.o,$(FFX_SRC))
FFX_INC  := -I$(FFX)/sdk/include -I$(FFX)/sdk/src/components -I$(FFX)/sdk/src/shared -I$(FFX)/sdk/src/backends/shared
ifneq ($(PLATFORM),macos)
BACKEND_OBJ += $(FFX_OBJ)
$(B)/rt/nvn/vulkan/fsr3.o: CXXFLAGS := -DSW_FSR3=1 -include $(FFX)/ffx_compat.h $(FFX_INC) $(CXXFLAGS)
endif
$(B)/ffx/%.o: $(FFX)/sdk/src/%.cpp $(FFX)/ffx_compat.h
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) -O2 -g -std=c++17 -w -include $(FFX)/ffx_compat.h $(FFX_INC) -I$(FFX)/sdk/include/FidelityFX/gpu $(DEPINC) -c $< -o $@
# (the SDK's headers ahead of $(DEPINC)'s: another copy of them there, from a build of the SDK, has other context
# sizes, and a context smaller than the SDK's own code writes overran the next one in memory)
$(B)/rt/nvn/vulkan/framegen.o: CXXFLAGS := -include $(FFX)/ffx_compat.h $(FFX_INC) -I$(FFX)/spirv $(CXXFLAGS)
$(B)/rt/nvn/vulkan/framegen.o: $(FFX)/spirv/ffx_shaders_vk.h $(FFX)/spirv/ffx_fsr3upscaler_vk.h $(FFX)/ffx_compat.h

all: $(EXE) $(CONFIG_EXE) $(if $(strip $(GEN_SRC)),$(GAMELIB))  # (GEN_SRC is a space when there is no generated/)

$(B)/obj/%.o: $(GEN)/%.c runtime/cpu.h runtime/simd.h runtime/simd_fp.h runtime/simd_softfma.h  # (cpu.h includes them)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	@$(CC) $(GENFLAGS) -c $< -o $@
$(B)/obj/layout.o: runtime/gamelib.h

$(B)/obj/tools/gamelib_entry.o: tools/gamelib_entry.c $(GAMELIB_SRCS) Makefile  # (the id: the flags are in here too)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(GENFLAGS) -DGAMELIB_ID='"$(GAMELIB_ID)"' -c $< -o $@
$(B)/rt/nvn/maxwell/translate.o $(B)/rt/nvn/vulkan/spirv.o: $(SHADER_IDS)
$(B)/rt/nvn/maxwell/translate.o $(B)/rt/nvn/vulkan/spirv.o: RTFLAGS += -include $(SHADER_IDS)
$(B)/rt/main.o: $(B)/source_id
$(B)/rt/main.o: RTFLAGS += -DSW_SOURCE='"$(SW_SOURCE)"'
$(B)/rt/gamelib.o: $(GAMELIB_SRCS) Makefile
$(B)/rt/gamelib.o: RTFLAGS += -DGAMELIB_ID='"$(GAMELIB_ID)"' $(GAMELIB_TARGETS)
# the start screen's build of it (runtime/gamebuild.c) uses the same flags
$(B)/rt/gamebuild.o: $(GAMELIB_SRCS) Makefile
$(B)/rt/gamebuild.o: RTFLAGS += -DGAMELIB_CFLAGS='"$(strip $(filter-out -Iruntime,$(GENFLAGS)))"' \
                                $(if $(GENFLAGS_COMPAT),-DGAMELIB_CFLAGS_COMPAT='"$(strip $(filter-out -Iruntime,$(GENFLAGS_COMPAT)))"') \
                                -DGAMELIB_ZIGFLAGS='"$(GENFLAGS_ZIG)"' -DGAMELIB_SHARED='"$(GAMELIB_SHARED)"' -DGAMELIB_GENARGS='"$(GENLOCALS)"'

# The profiler's Windows sampler guards its stack walks with SEH (__try).
$(B)/rt/prof_sampler.o: RTFLAGS += -fms-extensions
# Windows guarded memory scans use SEH.
$(B)/rt/memscan_os.o: RTFLAGS += -fms-extensions

$(B)/rt/control_places.o: runtime/control_places_data.inc  # (the generated table of shrines, Koroks ...)

$(B)/rt/%.o: runtime/%.c $(RT_HDRS)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(RTFLAGS) $(RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

# SMAA (third_party/smaa, MIT): the reference shader as a C string for runtime/nvn/smaa_data.c (both backends build
# their passes from it); the non-ASCII bytes in its comments become '?', and its CRLF line ends plain LF (a CR left in
# the string literals ends them early on macOS clang)
$(B)/inc/smaa_hlsl.inc: third_party/smaa/SMAA.hlsl
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	LC_ALL=C tr -d '\r' < $< | LC_ALL=C tr '\200-\377' '?' | sed -e 's/\\/\\\\/g' -e 's/"/\\"/g' -e 's/^/"/' -e 's/$$/\\n"/' > $@
$(B)/rt/nvn/smaa_data.o: $(B)/inc/smaa_hlsl.inc
$(B)/rt/nvn/smaa_data.o: RTFLAGS += -I$(B)/inc -Ithird_party/smaa/Textures

$(B)/rt/%.o: runtime/%.cpp $(RT_HDRS)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS) $(OSFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(B)/rt/%.o: runtime/%.m $(RT_HDRS)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CC) $(RTFLAGS) $(RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS) -fobjc-arc -c $< -o $@

# linked to a temp file, then renamed over: a copy of the game still running keeps its (old) file - relinking in
# place gets running copies killed by macOS (code signature of the changed pages). The temp file keeps the real name
# (in a folder of its own): on Windows the import library records the name the game code library loads it by.
$(EXE): $(RT_OBJ) $(BACKEND_OBJ) $(UI_OBJ) $(IMGUI_OBJ)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)link
	$(CXX) -o $(dir $@)link/$(notdir $@) $^ $(LDFLAGS)
	mv -f $(dir $@)link/$(notdir $@) $@

# its id file (<library>.id) says what it was built from without loading it (runtime/gamelib.c)
$(GAMELIB): $(GEN_OBJ) | $(EXE)
	$(CC) $(GAMELIB_LDFLAGS) -o $@.tmp $^
	mv -f $@.tmp $@
	echo $(GAMELIB_ID) > $@.id

$(B)/rt/ui/i18n.o: $(wildcard runtime/ui/i18n/*.inc) runtime/ui/i18n.h
$(B)/rt/ui/%.o: runtime/ui/%.mm $(RT_HDRS)
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) $(RUNTIME_OPTFLAGS) $(UIFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(B)/imgui/%.o: $(IMGUI)/%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(B)/imgui/imgui_impl_%.o: $(IMGUI)/backends/imgui_impl_%.cpp
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(B)/imgui/imgui_impl_metal.o: $(IMGUI)/backends/imgui_impl_metal.mm
	@mkdir -p $(dir $@)
	$(CXX) $(CXXFLAGS) -fobjc-arc -c $< -o $@

# Python: tools/venv (macOS, Linux: bin/python, Windows: Scripts/python.exe)
PY := $(firstword $(wildcard tools/venv/bin/python) $(wildcard tools/venv/Scripts/python.exe))

VERSION  := $(shell sed -n 's/^\#define SAVAGEWIND_VERSION "\(.*\)"/\1/p' runtime/ui/launcher.mm)

# macOS: build/Savage Wind.app, runs on macOS $(APP_MIN)+: the game rebuilt for that in build/mac15 against build/deps
# (`make deps`: SDL3, LGPL FFmpeg, Python, from pinned sources), the generator helper when built
# (`make gen-helper` after `make deps`), packaged by tools/bundle_macos.sh. No game files or fonts.
APP_MIN  := 15.0
APP_B    := build/mac15
deps:
	MACOS_MIN=$(APP_MIN) tools/build_deps_macos.sh
app:
	@[ -f build/deps/lib/libSDL3.0.dylib ] || { echo "make deps first"; exit 1; }
	$(MAKE) B=$(APP_B) MACOS_MIN=$(APP_MIN) DEPS=$(CURDIR)/build/deps $(APP_B)/savagewind
	MACOS_MIN=$(APP_MIN) tools/bundle_macos.sh $(APP_B)/savagewind

# macOS release disk image (the .app + an Applications shortcut to drag it onto): build/dist/Savage Wind-<v>-macOS.dmg
dmg: app
	tools/make_dmg.sh

# Windows: build/dist/SavageWind-<version>-windows.zip, top folder "Savage Wind/": the exe, what the start screen
# builds the game code with on the player's machine (make gen-helper, tools/fetch_zig.sh slimmed by
# tools/zig_slim.sh: its runtime built ahead of time, gamelib-src/, the exe's import library)
# and the DLLs they load (runs without MSYS2). No game code. The exe is a release build in $(WIN_B):
# linked against the LGPL FFmpeg from `make deps-windows` (MSYS2's is a GPLv3 build) and without a console window
# (RELEASE=1: the log goes to savagewind.log next to the exe, fatal errors show a message box). Its DLLs are looked up
# with build/deps-win/bin first (the FFmpeg DLL names are the same as MSYS2's GPL ones). vulkan-1.dll is left
# out: every Vulkan driver installs the loader in System32. Saves and game files go next to the exe at run time.
# Needs: Windows 10+ x64, a Vulkan 1.3 driver, an SSE4.2 CPU (GENARCH_COMPAT x86-64-v2; checked at startup).
DIST     := build/dist/Savage Wind
WIN_B    := build/win-release
# The release runtime is profile-guided with ThinLTO (tools/pgo/runtime.profdata: +19..33% fps at 1080p/1440p TAA on a
# 5700X3D + 3080 Ti, see tools/pgo/README.md). DIST_PGO= and DIST_LTO= (empty) build it plain, e.g. with a clang other
# than the one that wrote the profile.
DIST_PGO ?= use
DIST_LTO ?= thin
deps-windows:
	tools/build_deps_windows.sh
dist:
	@[ -f build/deps-win/lib/libavcodec.dll.a ] || { echo "make deps-windows first (LGPL FFmpeg)"; exit 1; }
	@[ -d build/helper/swgen ] || { echo "make gen-helper first (the game code generator)"; exit 1; }
	@! find tools -maxdepth 1 -name '*.py' -newer build/helper/swgen/swgen.exe | grep -q . || \
	    { echo "make gen-helper first: tools/*.py changed since build/helper/swgen was frozen"; exit 1; }
	@[ -x build/zig/zig.exe ] || { echo "tools/fetch_zig.sh first (the compiler)"; exit 1; }
	$(MAKE) B=$(WIN_B) DEPS=$(CURDIR)/build/deps-win RELEASE=1 PGO=$(DIST_PGO) LTO=$(DIST_LTO) $(WIN_B)/savagewind.exe $(WIN_B)/savagewind-config.exe $(WIN_B)/sw-update.exe
	! nm $(WIN_B)/savagewind.exe | grep ' f_70' >/dev/null  # (no game code inside)
	rm -rf build/dist && mkdir -p "$(DIST)/gamelib-src"
	cp $(WIN_B)/savagewind.exe $(WIN_B)/savagewind.dll.a "$(DIST)/"
	cp $(WIN_B)/savagewind-config.exe "$(DIST)/Savage Wind Configuration.exe"
	cp $(WIN_B)/sw-update.exe "$(DIST)/SW Update.exe"
	tools/zig_slim.sh $(strip $(filter-out -Iruntime,$(GENFLAGS))) \
	    $(if $(GENFLAGS_COMPAT),-- $(strip $(filter-out -Iruntime,$(GENFLAGS_COMPAT))))  # (zig, its runtime built ahead of time)
	cp -R build/helper/swgen "$(DIST)/"
	cp -R build/zig-slim "$(DIST)/zig"
	cp runtime/cpu.h runtime/simd.h runtime/simd_fp.h runtime/simd_softfma.h runtime/gamelib.h tools/gamelib_entry.c \
	    runtime/hle/hle_symbols.txt "$(DIST)/gamelib-src/"
	cp docs/icon/icon_1024.png "$(DIST)/icon.png"
	cp runtime/nvn/vulkan/vk_pipelines.seed "$(DIST)/"  # (the pipeline seed the precompilation reads: hashes and render state, nothing of the game)
	cp third_party/fonts/FiraSans/FiraSans-SemiBold.ttf third_party/fonts/FiraSans/FiraSans-Medium.ttf "$(DIST)/"  # (menus, OFL)
	cp third_party/fonts/FiraSans/OFL.txt "$(DIST)/FiraSans-OFL.txt"
	cp third_party/fonts/NotoSansThai/NotoSansThai-Medium.ttf "$(DIST)/"  # (Thai menus, OFL)
	cp third_party/fonts/NotoSansThai/OFL.txt "$(DIST)/NotoSansThai-OFL.txt"
	cp third_party/fonts/NotoSansHebrew/NotoSansHebrew-Medium.ttf "$(DIST)/"  # (Hebrew menus, OFL)
	cp third_party/fonts/NotoSansHebrew/OFL.txt "$(DIST)/NotoSansHebrew-OFL.txt"
	cp third_party/FidelityFX/LICENSE.txt "$(DIST)/FidelityFX-LICENSE.txt"  # (AMD FidelityFX SDK, MIT: README "License")
	if [ -f build/fsr-dlls/amd_fidelityfx_loader_vk.dll ]; then cp build/fsr-dlls/amd_fidelityfx_*_vk.dll \
	    build/fsr-dlls/AMD-FidelityFX-DLL-LICENSE.txt "$(DIST)/"; fi  # (AMD FSR 4: tools/fetch_fsr_dlls.py; AMD's licence allows binary redistribution with this notice)
	mkdir "$(DIST)/colour-luts" && cp third_party/luts/*.cube third_party/luts/README.md "$(DIST)/colour-luts/"  # (CC0: Video > Colour)
	cp README.md LICENSE "$(DIST)/"  # (licenses and source links of the bundled components: README "License")
	cp recomplauncher.json "$(DIST)/"  # (RecompLauncher reads it from the release to set the game up: next to the exe)
	PATH="$(CURDIR)/build/deps-win/bin:$$PATH" ldd $(WIN_B)/savagewind.exe | awk '(/ucrt64/ || /deps-win/) && !/vulkan-1/ {print $$3}' | sort -u | \
	    xargs -I{} cp -u {} "$(DIST)/"
	! ls "$(DIST)" | grep -iE 'x264|x265|xvid|postproc'  # (no GPL codec libraries in the release)
	! ls "$(DIST)" | grep -i splash  # (no start screen picture: the player's own, never shipped)
	python3 tools/make_update_manifest.py "$(DIST)" "$(VERSION)"  # (what SW Update checks and replaces: this list, nothing else)
	cd build/dist && if command -v zip >/dev/null; then zip -qr "SavageWind-$(VERSION)-windows.zip" "Savage Wind"; \
	    else /c/Windows/System32/tar.exe -a -cf "SavageWind-$(VERSION)-windows.zip" "Savage Wind"; fi
	@echo "build/dist/SavageWind-$(VERSION)-windows.zip"

# The game code generator as a standalone helper, so players need no Python: build/helper/swgen/ (swgen[.exe] +
# _internal/), frozen by PyInstaller from tools/swgen.spec in its own venv (build/gen-venv). Shipped as swgen/ next to
# the exe (Windows, Linux) or in "Savage Wind.app"/Contents/Resources. The start screen's setup runs it on the player's own
# game files (runtime/gamebuild.c). PyInstaller only builds for the OS it runs on.
# macOS arm64: the relocatable Python 3.12 from `make deps` (macOS 11+ / 15+: the helper runs where the app does);
#   without it Homebrew's python@3.12 (then only on the macOS it was built for).
# Windows x86-64: from the MSYS2 shell with a python.org CPython 3.12 (prebuilt unicorn / capstone wheels), e.g.
#   make gen-helper GEN_PY="/c/Users/<you>/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python312/python.exe"
ifeq ($(PLATFORM),macos)
GEN_PY    ?= $(firstword $(wildcard build/deps/python/bin/python3.12) python3.12)
GEN_VPY   := build/gen-venv/bin/python
else
GEN_PY    ?= py -3.12
GEN_VPY   := build/gen-venv/Scripts/python.exe
endif

gen-helper: build/gen-venv/.ok
	$(if $(filter windows,$(PLATFORM)),USERPROFILE="$$(cygpath -w ~ 2>/dev/null || echo $$HOME)") \
	$(GEN_VPY) -m PyInstaller --noconfirm --clean --log-level WARN --distpath build/helper --workpath build/pyinstaller \
	    tools/swgen.spec
	$(if $(filter windows,$(PLATFORM)),$(GEN_VPY) tools/pe_no_cfg.py build/helper/swgen/swgen.exe)
	@du -sh build/helper/swgen

build/gen-venv/.ok:
	$(GEN_PY) -m venv build/gen-venv
	$(GEN_VPY) -m pip install -q capstone==5.0.9 unicorn==2.1.4 lz4==4.4.5 pyinstaller==6.22.3
	touch $@

# Linux: build/dist/Savage_Wind-<version>-<arch>.AppImage, built in Ubuntu 22.04 containers (podman) with SDL3, LGPL

# `make appimage` (ARCH: this machine's, or aarch64 cross-compiled), `make appimages` both. See docs/linux.md.
appimage:

appimages:

	tools/linux/appimage.sh aarch64
```

```md
<p align="center"><img src="docs/media/banner.png" alt="Savage Wind" width="640"></p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/releases/latest"><b>Download</b></a> ·
  <a href="#get-started">Get started</a> ·
  <a href="docs/STATUS.md">Status</a> ·
  <a href="docs/FAQ.md">FAQ</a> ·
  <a href="https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues">Issues</a> ·
  <a href="CHANGELOG.md">Changelog</a>
</p>

**Savage Wind Recomp** is a work-in-progress static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild*
(Nintendo Switch, version 1.9.0) into a native application for Windows and Linux, built from your own copy of the
game.

<p align="center">
  <img src="https://i.imgur.com/BaTJyr9.jpg" alt="Screenshot of Savage Wind" width="24%">
  <img src="https://i.imgur.com/USibLkg.jpg" alt="Screenshot of Savage Wind" width="24%">
  <img src="https://i.imgur.com/z6dHHLP.jpg" alt="Screenshot of Savage Wind" width="24%">
  <img src="https://i.imgur.com/p12wEHG.jpg" alt="Screenshot of Savage Wind" width="24%">
</p>
<p align="center"><sub>Screenshots taken in Savage Wind. The game is © Nintendo; you need your own copy to run it.</sub></p>

<p align="center"><img src="docs/media/progress/overall.svg" alt="Overall progress" width="420"></p>

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of the game, updated to **version 1.9.0**
> and dumped from **your own** Nintendo Switch. This project does not provide game files, keys, firmware, dumping or
> decryption tools, or instructions on how to obtain them. The game code is recompiled locally, on your machine,
> from your files.

> [!NOTE]
> **Made almost entirely with AI.** Nearly all of the code, tooling, reverse engineering and documentation is written
> by an AI (Anthropic's Claude, through Claude Code), directed, tested and reviewed by a human. It builds on
> [LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp), made the same way. If you don't trust code written by AI, you
> can simply ignore this project.

> [!WARNING]
> **This is an alpha.** The whole game can be finished from start to end, and as of Alpha 6 no known bug stops you
> from progressing, but expect bugs and crashes in some places, and some mechanics that break above 30 fps
> ([#425](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/425)). If a cutscene freezes or breaks, lower the frame
> rate to 30 fps for that scene.
>
> **Please read the [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md) before asking** about game file formats, mod support or testing. Many great
> contributors help out, but every review, approval and release test is done by one person with limited hardware.
>
> **Alpha 7 will take longer than usual:** development slows down a bit while GTA VI comes out. Game-breaking bugs
> still get quick fixes first, and bug reports and pull requests stay welcome. We're still on track for the **Beta
> within the next month**, which will focus on full mod support and more quality-of-life options.

## Features

- The whole game and both DLC, from your own copy
- Frame rates from 30 to 360 fps, or your display's own rate
- Resolutions up to 4K and beyond, and ultrawide
- Upscaling with NVIDIA DLSS, AMD FSR 3, FSR 4 and FSR 1, and FSR 3 frame generation
- Graphics presets from Potato, below console quality, to Savage, far beyond it
- Longer draw distance, sharper shadows, adjustable field of view, colour grading and HDR
- Keyboard and mouse with real mouse camera, and any controller, gyro included (Steam Input, DSU servers, handhelds)
- Button prompts that match your device
- Save profiles, backups, a custom save folder, and Wii U / Cemu save import
- Steam Deck and PC handhelds, and Add to Steam
- One-click updates from Savage Wind Configuration
- Photo mode, colour vision filters, accessibility options, cheats and a teleport
  ([Cheats and assists](docs/cheats-and-assists.md))
- Discord Rich Presence (off by default)

## Get started

**You need:** your own game files (see [Game files](docs/game-files.md)), Windows 10 or later or Linux on x86-64, a
GPU with Vulkan 1.3, 16 GB of RAM, a CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2 runs faster) and about 20 GB of free disk space.

1. Download the latest build from [Releases](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/releases/latest):
   - **Windows:** the file ending in `windows.zip`. Extract it to a folder you can write to, not Program Files.
   - **Linux and Steam Deck:** the file ending in `x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it
     ([docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md)).
   - **Linux on ARM:** the file ending in `aarch64.AppImage`. It is highly experimental.
2. Start it and choose the folder with your extracted game (`exefs/` and `romfs/`). Then choose **Set up game files**.
   It checks the version, copies the files and recompiles the game code once, about 15 minutes on a 12-thread CPU.
   Your own files aren't changed.
3. Play. Settings and languages are in the game's Options. **Savage Wind Configuration** has your game files and the
   rest of the settings.

**Updating:** from version 0.5.1 on, Savage Wind Configuration updates it in one click, on Windows and in the Linux
AppImages. Before that, extract the new zip over the old folder or use the new AppImage. Your game files, saves and
settings stay.

Something wrong? See the [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md), which also lists the known issues.

## Saves

Saves are in the `save` folder of Savage Wind's data folder: next to `savagewind.exe` on Windows, and in
`~/.local/share/savagewind/save/` on Linux and the Steam Deck. To back them up or move them, close the game and copy
the whole folder. More in [Saves](docs/saves.md), including profiles and Wii U / Cemu import.

## Cheats, assists and amiibo

Colour vision for colour-blind players, god mode, infinite stamina, damage and weapon wear settings, items, rupees,
weather, teleporting and the virtual amiibo reader: how to use them in [Cheats and assists](docs/cheats-and-assists.md).

## Controls

Any controller SDL knows works. Keyboard and mouse defaults:

| Action | Key | Action | Key |
|---|---|---|---|
| Move | W A S D | Camera | Mouse |
| Jump | Space | Sprint / back | Left Shift |
| Interact | E | Attack | Left click |
| Shield | Right click | Bow | F |
| Rune | Q | Throw | R |
| Inventory | Tab | Map | M |

Every action can be rebound in the game's Options. All the keys: [Controls](docs/controls.md).

## Found a bug?

Read the [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md) first: issues about something it already covers are closed right away. Use the latest
release and game version 1.9.0, search the [existing issues](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues?q=is%3Aissue),
and [open one](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/issues/new/choose) with your `savagewind.log`. On a crash
or a cutscene bug, attach your zipped `save` folder too. Reports without these are closed after 24 hours.

## Contributing and building

Open pull requests against the [`test`](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/tree/test) branch, which has
everything ahead of the latest release. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). To build from source:
[Windows](docs/BUILD-windows.md) and [Linux](docs/linux.md).
```

`docs/ACTIONS.md`:

```md
# Per-action bindings

Each game action owns one keyboard/mouse binding and one controller binding. Its factory defaults are copied from
its Switch button's original layout using the fixed 1.9.0 mask table below: Jump starts on Space / North, Interact
on E / East, and so on. If either device differs from its factory default, the action reads its own host bindings on
both devices, independent of raw Switch rebinds. With both devices at factory defaults, the game answers through the
Switch layer as before, preserving its Jump button change option and raw Switch injection. Multiple actions may share
an input. Reset restores each action's factory defaults. `ACT_FOLLOW` remains a reset command accepted by `act_set`;
it is no longer stored in `g_act_key` or `g_act_pad`. `ACT_NONE` unbinds an action side.

Movement and camera directions keep their keyboard-only slots and defaults (W S A D / I K J L). Walk, Tilt and all
seven gyro slots accept both devices; their new controller sides default to unbound (`-1`). Walk scales its device's
left stick to 40%. Tilt holds the mouse clutch and enables the existing sensorless controller stick tilt path. Gyro
buttons and keys combine per direction, only while `gyro_keys_live()`; simultaneous opposite directions cancel.
Walk, Tilt, gyro and game action bindings allow shared inputs on both devices. Assigning one never changes another
slot, including raw Switch menu buttons; rebinding a raw slot also leaves these shared bindings intact. Legacy
host slots still swap among themselves on the same device, including the raw Switch buttons (0 to 15).

The game's title, pause and map menus still use the raw Switch layer, including legacy raw-button rebinds. The runtime
overlay and launcher keep their fixed navigation shortcuts. The separate UI update can use `bind_input_name`,
and `bind_input_group` ("gyro" or NULL). Raw Switch inputs are named by what they do (`bind_input_name(BIND_A)` is
"Menu: confirm"), never by the button. No slots are hidden by these helpers; the page and overlay simply do not list
left stick press and D-pad Down (their functions are the actions Crouch, Call horse and Throw distance). Use `bind_pad_slot` for controller availability and `bind_is_default_slot` for defaults, including
`BIND_ACTION + id`; do not test for a stored `ACT_FOLLOW`.

## The Key bindings page

The game's own Options has a **Key bindings** page. Every row is one input: its name on the left, a keyboard/mouse
button in the middle and a controller button on the right, under a column header row (Keyboard/Mouse, Controller).
Both buttons are real native buttons of the game's Options row, not an overlay. Left/right switches the column,
up/down keeps it, and the mouse hovers and clicks each button on its own. Confirming a button waits for the next press:
a key or mouse button binds the keyboard side, a controller button the controller side (Esc cancels, as does waiting 5
seconds). The hovered button is lit; the other one sits under a darker band, so only one looks selected.

The rows are the 27 actions below, then the menu inputs (see "Menu inputs" below), then Move forward/back/left/right and Camera up/down/left/right (keyboard only: the
controller cell reads "Stick" and is greyed), Walk, Tilt and the seven gyro keys (both devices). The F1 overlay's Controls
page shows the same table from the same in-process state; the launcher is a separate process.

The two-button rows hook the game's Options code through one strict optional signature group
(`tools/game_sites.py`, tested by `tools/test_two_button_sites.py`). If any signature does not match exactly, the group is
off and the page falls back to the single-button rows. `SAVAGEWIND_TWO_BUTTON_ROWS=0` turns them off by hand. The layout
numbers live in `runtime/ui/binding_row_layout.h`; the research notes are in `docs/research/`.

## Menu inputs

No raw Switch button is listed on the page or in the overlay. The functions the Switch layer carries beyond the 41
actions are rows of their own, bound to the same raw slots with the same defaults (ini names unchanged):

| Row | Slot | Default (Switch button) | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pause menu | Plus | Plus | opens the pause menu |
| Map (Sheikah Slate) | Minus | Minus | opens the map |
| Quick menu: runes | D-pad up | D-pad up | hold for the rune quick menu |
| Quick menu: shields | D-pad left | D-pad left | shield quick menu |
| Quick menu: weapons | D-pad right | D-pad right | weapon quick menu |
| Menu: confirm | A | A | selects in the game's menus |
| Menu: back | B | B | goes back |
| Menu: Hero's Path | X | X | Hero's Path in the map |
| Menu: sort / sensor | Y | Y | sorts the inventory, Sheikah Sensor in the map |
| Menu: previous / next tab | L / R | L / R | switches the menu tab |
| Menu: previous / next tab 2 | ZL / ZR | ZL / ZR | the same, in the menus that use the triggers |
| Menu: inspect / zoom | right stick click | right stick click | inspect an item, zoom the map |

Left stick click (Crouch, a menu use) and D-pad down (Call horse, Throw distance) have no function of their own beyond
the actions, so they are not listed; they keep their slots and defaults. Two greyed rows, Esc and F2, are fixed
and cannot be rebound: Esc is Plus in play and B in menus, F2 frees the mouse cursor. F1 opens the Savage Wind overlay
(controller: Back + Start or Home / Guide), unless the game is started with `SAVAGEWIND_OVERLAY=0`; that overlay's
own page lists it greyed too.

## savagewind.ini

The schema marker is written before all action and raw-button bindings, followed by factory-default differences:

```
act_schema = 2
act_key_2 = G
act_pad_3 = south
act_pad_9 = none
```

`act_key_<id>` / `act_pad_<id>` take a key or controller button name as `bind_key_*` / `bind_pad_*` do (`none`: no
binding). `<id>` is the game's action number, 0 to 40. A missing action/device line starts from its factory default;
when loading a legacy file without `act_schema = 2`, `bind_key_<button>` and `bind_pad_<button>` lines migrate into
bindings for actions reading that button unless an explicit action line exists on that device. Explicit lines win
in either file order. Migration uses the
fixed 1.9.0 table, never the current game table. On the next save, `act_schema = 2` disables that migration for future
loads. This preserves omitted factory-default action values even when raw buttons differ. Resetting actions does not
clear the schema flag. Runtime raw-button edits do not perform migration.

Added controller keys: `bind_pad_walk`, `bind_pad_tilt`, `bind_pad_gyro_up`, `bind_pad_gyro_down`, `bind_pad_gyro_left`,
`bind_pad_gyro_right`, `bind_pad_gyro_turn_left`, `bind_pad_gyro_turn_right`, `bind_pad_gyro_center`. These and existing
raw controller bindings accept `none`. All existing keyboard, action and raw-button ini names remain unchanged.

## How it works

The game asks about an action in exactly two places: `isHold(pad, id)` (is it held) and `isTrig(pad, id)` (was it
pressed this frame). Each looks the action's pad mask up in a table of 41 and tests it against the pad object's held
or pressed word, which the game fills from the Switch-style state the runtime hands it (runtime/hle/input.c).

`tools/patches.py` `_act_query` puts a call in front of both functions (sites `act_hold`, `act_trig`; the mask table
is `act_masks`; all three are found by instruction patterns in `tools/game_sites.py`, an optional group like the
others). `rt_act_query` (runtime/hle/bindings.c) answers customized actions during gameplay. It declines for actions
at factory defaults, in menus, when the window is unfocused or the runtime overlay is open, and for invalid action ids.
An atomic custom-action mask is refreshed after edits, resets and migration; only those actions are scanned and polled.

An answered action reads host keys/mouse buttons and controller buttons directly. A device left at its factory default
uses that default host input when the other device is customized. The main thread publishes which actions each side
holds on every key or button event; the game thread freezes that once per controller poll (`act_poll`, in `fill_state`), and "pressed" is the edge between two polls. A press nobody asked about
before the next poll is kept for the next query, so a short tap is not lost.

## Known limits

- Customized actions bypass the game's own **Jump button** option; bind those actions directly. Factory-default
  actions retain the game's option.
- Raw Switch injection (`SAVAGEWIND_INPUT` or a control-endpoint button) reaches factory-default actions through the
  game, but customized actions require host key/controller injection.
- The button icons the game draws follow the Switch layer and the controller family, not the per-action bindings.
- The 13 ids the game never asks about (1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 16, 20 to 24, 29, 30) are not on the page. No id above 40 is used:
  all 175 query sites (157 calls and 18 tail branches, in 91 functions) pass a constant from 0 to 40.

## Naming the actions (logging build)

`SAVAGEWIND_ACTLOG=1` prints the queried action ids, callers and host-action answers. Use host input to exercise
these bindings (frame numbers must be after the save has loaded). For example:

```
SAVAGEWIND_ACTLOG=1 SAVAGEWIND_HOST_INPUT="3000:key:Space:60" SAVAGEWIND_EXIT_AT=5000 <the game's executable>
```

`tools/actlog_script.py` emits raw Switch injection for calibrating the game table with factory-default actions.
Use host injection for customized actions.

## Tests

`make test-two-button-rows` runs the Options row hooks, column routing, header geometry and capture engine against
synthetic rows (needs no game files).

`make test-actions` (no game files): the answers to the hold / pressed queries, menus falling back, two actions on one
key, factory-default fallthrough, customization on either device, legacy migration in either order, one-time schema
migration and reload idempotence, shared action/Walk/Tilt/gyro captures on both devices, preserved raw Switch swaps,
reset and ini round trips
(`tools/test_actions.c`), and the generated hook (`tools/test_act_site.py`).
`make test-pc-controls` also checks Walk scaling, shared key/pad Tilt, mouse routing, sensorless dual-stick eligibility,
and all gyro directions with menu/focus/context gates. `tools/test_game_sites.py` covers the site patterns.
```

`docs/BUILD-windows.md`:

```md
# Building Savage Wind on Windows (x86-64)

Status: part of main. Builds and runs the game on Vulkan (with your own game files); `make dist` packages the
release zip.

## One-time setup
Run in PowerShell from the repo root:

    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\setup_windows.ps1

This installs MSYS2 (UCRT64: clang, lld, make, SDL3, FFmpeg, Vulkan loader + headers, shaderc, Vulkan Memory
Allocator, validation layers), Python 3.12 for the tools (`tools\venv`: unicorn, capstone, lz4) and switches the
clone to LF line endings.

## Build
From an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell, or Git Bash with MSYS2 first on PATH:

    export PATH="/c/msys64/ucrt64/bin:/c/msys64/usr/bin:$PATH"
    make gen        # once: recompile the game from extracted/exefs (your own game files; see the start screen)
    make -j         # -> build/savagewind.exe and the game code library build/swgame.dll

NVIDIA DLSS needs no SDK at build time: `runtime/nvn/vulkan/dlss.c` loads the NVIDIA driver's NGX at run time, and
NGX loads `nvngx_dlss.dll` from the folder of `savagewind.exe`. It is neither in this repository nor in `make dist`: the
setup downloads NVIDIA's own copy (`runtime/dlss_fetch.c`, NVIDIA/DLSS `v310.9.16`, size and SHA-256 checked). For a
source build, run the setup once, or copy that release's `nvngx_dlss.dll` into `build/`.

Without `generated/` only the app is built: the start screen builds the game code itself when you set up the game
files (as for players), given the generator and the compiler (`make gen-helper`, `tools/fetch_zig.sh`).
`make runtime-objs` compiles the runtime only (quick check).

Run from a shell that has `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` on PATH (SDL3, FFmpeg, Vulkan, shaderc DLLs).

## Package
    make deps-windows   # once: FFmpeg built as LGPL only (build/deps-win; downloads its source, needs nasm)
    make gen-helper     # the game code generator without Python (build/helper/swgen)
    tools/fetch_zig.sh  # the compiler the start screen builds the game code with (build/zig)
    make dist           # -> build/dist/SavageWind-<version>-windows.zip (no game code inside)

`make gen-helper` freezes the generator with a python.org CPython (`py -3.12` by default; another one with
`GEN_PY="py -3.14"`, as long as unicorn and capstone have wheels for it). `make dist` also makes the slim compiler
(`tools/zig_slim.sh`: only the headers the game code includes, and zig's runtime built ahead of time), so the
start screen's build doesn't compile zig's own libraries on the player's machine. The version is
`SAVAGEWIND_VERSION` in `runtime/ui/launcher.mm`. Before a release, test the zip as a player would: extract it to a
new folder, run it with a PATH without MSYS2, set up the game files from the start screen and play.

The zip's `Savage Wind/` folder holds `savagewind.exe` (icon from `docs/icon/icon.ico`, via windres),
`Savage Wind Configuration.exe` (`build/savagewind-config.exe`, runtime/platform/windows_config.c: starts
`savagewind.exe --config`, the configuration screen; same icon), the Fira Sans font files, `swgen/`, `zig/` and the
MSYS2 DLLs. A plain start of `savagewind.exe` shows only the game files setup until they're ready, then goes
straight into the game; `--config` shows the configuration screen (Play, Settings, game files, Quit). Never in the
zip: a start screen picture (`splash.jpg` / `splash.png` is the player's own, read from the data folder; `make dist`
checks). No installer: game files, saves and settings are kept next to the exe, so
the folder must be writable (the app says so and quits if it isn't, e.g. under Program Files). A source checkout
with `extracted/` in the starting folder keeps using that folder instead.

`SW Update.exe` (`runtime/platform/windows_update.c`) installs a newer release over the folder from Savage Wind
Configuration. It replaces only the files named in the zip's `sw-manifest.txt`, which `make dist` writes, so game files,
saves, settings and anything else a player keeps there are never touched. A release is only offered if a signature is
next to its zip. After `make dist`, sign the zip and upload the `.sig` with it:

    tools/sign_update.py build/dist/SavageWind-<version>-windows.zip <private key .pem>

Sign the AppImages the same way, or Linux players won't be offered the release. The private key is never in this repository; its public half is `runtime/platform/sw_update_key.h`. `make test-update-core`
and `make test-sw-update` cover the updater: the second one goes through every failure it knows against a local server.

## Differences from macOS
- Guest window 0x70_0000_0000..0x73_2000_0000 is reserved with VirtualAlloc and committed per region
  (kernel regions, modules, HLE heap); stray first touches are committed by a vectored exception handler.
- AArch64 FP/SIMD instructions are lowered to C (`gen.py --simd=c`, the default on non-arm64 hosts) instead of
  inline-asm passthrough.
- Renderer: Vulkan (runtime/nvn/vulkan) instead of Metal; shaders are translated to GLSL and compiled with
  shaderc. macOS keeps Metal.
- "Quit to Start Screen" reboots the game in place on both (runtime/main.c); the only re-exec left is
  the startup retry when the guest window is taken, which on Windows starts a new process and exits.

## Tests
- `tools/test_translate.sh`: shader translator fuzz (every GLSL translation compiles and validates; with `REF=<commit>`,
  also the MSL output compared with that commit's translator). Exits 1 on any failure.
- `tools/test_vk_pipelines.sh`: fuzzed shaders through the backend's compile/reflection into real pipelines.
- `SAVAGEWIND_VK_VALIDATION=1` with `VK_ADD_LAYER_PATH` pointing at `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin`: Khronos validation layer.
- Run test windows directly, not under MSYS `timeout` (it stalls the window).

```

`docs/CONTROL.md`:

```md
# Control commands

One list of named commands that more than one front end can run. Today that is a local socket, for scripts, AI agents
and `tools/swctl.py`, and the in-game console. Each command is either player safe (it only reads state or copies text, it cannot break the game)
or developer only.

## Who may run what

| | player safe commands | developer commands |
|---|---|---|
| normal start | yes | no |
| `SAVAGEWIND_DEV=1` | yes | yes |
| `SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL=<port>` | yes | yes |

A normal start has no socket and no developer commands: they are not listed by `help`, not run, and answer
`Unknown command`. `SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL=<port>` also opens the socket, `SAVAGEWIND_DEV=1` only unlocks the developer
commands in the in-game console.

The socket listens on `127.0.0.1` only (not reachable from the network). A connection whose first line is an HTTP
request (a web page in a browser on the same machine can send one to `127.0.0.1`) is closed before anything runs.

```
SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL=7777 ./savagewind        (Windows: set the variable, then start savagewind.exe)
python tools/swctl.py state
```

A command is player safe when its entry in the table has the `CONTROL_PLAYER` flag (`runtime/control.h`). Leave the flag
off for anything that writes memory or files, moves things or ends the game.

## The in-game console

The same commands can be typed in the game: press F12 or the key below Esc, left of 1.
The game gets no input while the console is open. The same key, F12 or Esc closes it. Up and Down walk through what you typed,
Tab completes a command, Ctrl+V pastes from the system clipboard, `clear` empties the screen. The console is in English,
like the command names and replies it shows.

It runs the same commands as the socket, with the same rights: a normal start offers only the player safe commands
below, with no socket. Text a command asks to copy (`pos`, `report`) goes to the system clipboard. `exit` closes the
game the way the window's close button does.

## Player safe commands

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `help` | the commands you can use |
| `version` | game version, operating system and architecture |
| `report` | one block for an issue: version, graphics card, processor, memory, frame rate, position and every setting (copied to the clipboard in the console) |
| `pos` | Link's position (x, y, z) and stamina, and `place`, a line like `swr:1 x=-1234.56 y=250.00 z=789.01 yaw=90.0 pitch=-10.0 hour=18.50`, to say where a bug is. Yaw and pitch work in any AA mode, the hour when known. An error before a save is loaded |
| `camera` | where the world camera is (`x y z`) and which way it looks (`dx dy dz`, unit vector; `yaw` and `pitch` in degrees: yaw 0 looks along +z and 90 along +x, pitch positive looks up). Read only, works in any AA mode: it uses the renderer's TAA view matrix when there is one, otherwise the game's stored camera. The stored camera reports its stored eye position, which can differ from the drawn one by about two metres; the direction is the same. An error before a world is loaded |
| `get [key]` | the current settings, or one; keys are `Settings` field names, plus `window_size`, `fps` (`fps_limit`), `left_stick_deadzone` and `right_stick_deadzone`. Enum values use lowercase names; values are the configured ones (environment overrides and hardware fallbacks still apply). Read only |
| `state` | frame number, uptime, fps over the last second and the hour of the day (left out before a world exists) |
| `exit` | end the game: the console closes the window the normal way, the socket exits at once |

## Developer commands

Only with `SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL` or `SAVAGEWIND_DEV=1`. Anything that writes memory, moves things or presses buttons is here.
Most of them rely on addresses found in game version 1.9.0 and are untested on other versions.

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `ping` | Check that the game answers (data: `pong` = true) |
| `time [freeze \| unfreeze \| set <0-24> \| <0-24>]` | Show the hour of the day. `set <hour>` or just `<hour>` sets it and keeps the clock running or frozen as it was. `freeze` holds the current hour, `unfreeze` continues from it at the normal speed. It writes both `WM_Time` buffers and lifts the early game 11:00 clock cap, without touching the paraglider quest flag. `SAVAGEWIND_TEST_TIME` still holds its configured hour |
| `rupees [<0-9999> \| lock \| unlock]` | Cheat. Without an argument: whether Infinite rupees is on and the last wallet count read. `<n>` sets the wallet once; `lock` turns on Infinite rupees (the wallet kept at 9999, the same as the overlay's Cheats tab) and `unlock` turns it off. The rupee count is found in the game's memory by a background thread, so the first write takes a few seconds (`runtime/rupees.c`). Like `set`, no settings file is written |
| `weather [game \| no_rain \| no_storms \| clear \| cloudy \| rain \| heavy_rain \| snow \| heavy_snow \| thunderstorm \| thunder_rain \| sun_shower]` | Cheat. Without an argument: the weather setting and, with a world loaded, the weather now. `no_rain` turns any rain into clouds, `no_storms` turns thunderstorms into clouds or rain, a weather type holds it, and `game` gives the weather back to the game. The same as Weather in the overlay's Cheats tab: applied from the next frame, and a cutscene keeps its own weather (`runtime/weather.c`). Like `set`, no settings file is written |
| `shot <file>` | Save a screenshot as PNG, on the machine the game runs on (Vulkan only for now). The file must be a `.png` inside the game's folder: a relative path without `..` |
| `goto <x> <y> <z>` \| `goto <swr:1 line>` \| `goto <place>` | Go to a place from `pos` or `report`: move Link, set the hour of the line (the clock keeps running, or stays frozen if it was) and turn the camera to its yaw and pitch like `look`. Same limits as `teleport`. Or go to a named place: `goto shrine 5`, `goto korok H23`, `goto stable wetland`, `goto tower 7`, `goto hateno`, `goto nearest korok` (see "Named places" below). Link arrives 2 to 3 units above the ground and drops the rest |
| `tp ...` | Same as `goto`, with the same arguments |
| `places [<kind>] [words]` | List the places `goto` knows: without arguments the kinds and how many there are, with a kind (`shrine`, `tower`, `stable`, `village`, `landmark`, `korok`) their numbers and names, and words narrow the list (`places shrine akkala`). Shows 40 at most |
| `teleport <x> <y> <z>` \| `teleport status` \| `teleport forget` | Move Link. Writes the real position, reached through a pointer chain from `PlayerInfo` (found with `mem path`, checked against `pos`). If the chain does not match it falls back to a background search that never blocks a frame; poll `teleport status` (`scanning`, `probing`, `testing`, `verifying`, `settling`, `done`, `failed`). A jump of 300 units or more also holds Link at the target (`settling`) until the game has loaded the map around him: the game pauses the world while it does and loads it with the world's own update, so without the hold a far jump froze the world for good (the hold needs the `tp_gate` patch of the generated game code). Stand still when you start; do not use it while riding, in a cutscene or loading. A target below the ground makes Link fall. `forget` drops the saved address |
| `look <yaw> <pitch>` \| `look status` \| `look stop` | Turn the camera (degrees, either may be `keep`, pitch within -89..89). Writes the camera cells and checks again each frame, because the game moves the eye a little after a write. Without the cells it falls back to the right stick (needs the TAA camera read). Returns at once, poll `look status` (`running`, `done`, `timeout`, `failed`) |
| `fly [on \| off \| toggle \| mode look \| level \| speed <n>]` | Fly mode: Link floats and the controls steer him through the world. Left stick moves along the camera (`mode look`) or the ground (`mode level`), X and B go up and down, left stick press is a 6x boost, the mouse wheel changes the speed. Fall damage cells are kept at his height, so flying down costs nothing. With the endpoint on, the Controls page gets a "Fly mode (test builds)" row (default F7, ini `bind_key_fly`, gamepad `bind_pad_fly`) |
| `cell [<name> [<value>...]]` | List, read or write a named game state cell. A cell is a recipe: a root object, pointer chains found once with `mem path` and a check that tells a right chain from a stale one. Cells: `player.pos`, `player.fall_top`, `player.fall_top2`, `camera.eye`, `camera.target`, `camera.pitch`. A new cell is one entry in `runtime/control_cells.c` |
| `sites` | The known root addresses (`runtime/game_sites.h`) and the value stored at each, as the start for `mem path` |
| `set <key> <value>` | Change a setting in memory. Answers with the new value and `applied: live` or `needs_restart`. Examples: `set upscaler fsr3`, `set antialias taa`, `set vsync off`, `set fps 120`. Enums accept names or indices, booleans on/off, true/false or 1/0. Unavailable backend options are rejected. No settings file is written, but a later menu save may keep the change |
| `frames [seconds]` | Frame intervals of the last seconds (default 5, max 60): count, fps average, frame time average, p50, p95, p99 and max, and the number of frames over 33 and 50 ms. Includes pacing and hitches, not GPU time alone |
| `prof [start \| stop \| toggle \| status \| report]` | The on-demand profiler: records zones, counters, GPU time and stack samples into a capture file, reported with `tools/swprof.py` (see `docs/profiling.md`). `status` shows the state and the last file |
| `sample start <seconds> [interval_us]` \| `sample status` | Windows only: background stack capture, written to `build/samples.txt` (analyse with `tools/profile_samples.py`). Refuses overlapping captures |
| `vkprof` | Only explains how to turn the Vulkan timers on, with `SAVAGEWIND_VK_PROF` at startup, because they cannot be switched safely at runtime |
| `gpuprof` | GPU time per pass, dispatch and copy of the next frame, as `[gpuprof]` lines in the log (the capture `SAVAGEWIND_GPUPROF_AT` takes at a fixed frame). The capture waits for the GPU once, a short hitch. The `prof` command's capture has the same rows in the `gpu` thread |
| `threads` | CPU time used so far (ms) by each guest thread (`guest.<handle>_<entry>`) and by the render threads (`host.render`, the NVN queue thread; `host.recorder` when the recorder runs), with `now_ms` and `presents`. Two calls give each thread's CPU time per frame. Some threads spin while they wait, so CPU time is not work: `tools/perf_routes.py` takes the work share from `sample` |
| `mem regions` | Readable mappings inside the guest window |
| `mem read <addr> <len> [u8\|u16\|u32\|u64\|s32\|f32\|f64\|hex]` | Read 1 to 4096 bytes |
| `mem write <addr> <type> <value>` | Write one numeric value; rejects inaccessible ranges and values outside the type |
| `mem scan <type> <value> [tolerance] [region=..] [from=.. to=..] [resident=1]`, `mem scan status`, `mem rescan <changed\|unchanged\|increased\|decreased\|equal <v>\|near <v> <tol>>`, `mem list [n]`, `mem reset` | Search guest memory for a value on a background thread and narrow the candidates, like a memory scanner. One session is shared by all clients. Poll `mem scan status` |
| `mem path <root> <target> [depth=1..6] [window=16..65528]` | Find how to reach `target` from the object at `root`, as pointer offsets. Poll `mem path status`. Heap addresses move between runs but layouts do not, so a chain found once keeps working |
| `give <actor or part of a name> [count]` | Put an item in the pouch through the game's own item get, on the next frame in play. Not an exact actor: the items whose name or actor has that text in them; one is given, several are listed. What went in the pouch is in the log (`[items] <actor>: value <n>, <added> of <asked>`): weapons, bows and shields stop when the player has no free slot |
| `press <button> [frames]`, `hold <button>`, `release [<button>\|all]`, `stick <l\|r> <x> <y> [frames]`, `input` | Scripted controller input, merged with the real one. Buttons: a b x y l r zl zr plus minus up down left right lstick rstick. Sticks run from -1 to 1, positive y is up |

To use `goto` with a line from an issue, run it in developer mode: `swctl goto "swr:1 x=... y=... z=... yaw=... pitch=... hour=..."`.

### Named places

`goto` also takes a kind and a number or a name. It finds a shrine, tower, stable, village, landmark or Korok without looking up any coordinates:

```
swctl goto shrine 5            the shrine with the game's number 5 (Ne'ez Yohma)
swctl goto shrine oman au      by name; apostrophes and capital letters do not matter
swctl goto shrine pushing power   or by the title the game gives the shrine's trial
swctl goto korok H23           a Korok by the game's own id (see below)
swctl goto korok 10            the 10th of 900, in the order `places korok` shows
swctl goto stable 2            the 2nd stable in alphabetical order (East Akkala)
swctl goto tower 7             the game's tower number (7 is Great Plateau Tower)
swctl goto stable wetland      or: swctl goto wetland
swctl goto hateno              names without a kind work when only one place has that name
swctl goto nearest korok       the closest of a kind to where Link is now (works for every kind)
```

If a name matches several places, the reply names them. `places <kind>` prints the numbers and names. What the numbers mean:

- Shrines use the game's own number (`Dungeon005` is shrine 5, 0 to 135; 120 and above are the DLC shrines). That is the number in the game's data and on the ZeldaMods object map, not an order the game shows to players.
- Towers use the game's tower number (1 to 15).
- Stables, villages and landmarks are numbered alphabetically by their English name.
- Koroks have no number in the game. Each one has an id like `H23` (the id the object map uses). `korok 10` counts the 900 in map order: square `A-1`, `A-2` ... then by id. `places korok` shows the order.

The coordinates are the game's world coordinates, the same frame as `pos`. The table is `runtime/control_places_data.inc`, generated by `python3 tools/gen_places.py` (needs network access). Two sources feed it:

- 154 places (120 shrines, all 15 towers, the villages, some stables and landmarks, Hyrule Castle) use the game's own start positions: the `StartPos` entries of `Map/MainField/Static.smubin` in `Bootup.pack`, which is where the game puts Link when he warps there, so it is ground he can stand on. `tools/dump_startpos.py` reads them from your own copy of the game (`python3 tools/dump_startpos.py --pack <Bootup.pack>`) and writes `tools/places_startpos.json`, which holds only coordinates and is checked in.
- 15 more places (14 DLC shrines, the Forgotten Temple) use `tools/places_measured.json`: the height Link really stood at after a `goto` dropped him from the marker position, measured in a running game with `tools/check_places.py` (marker heights were up to 100 units too high there).
- Everything else (the 2 other DLC shrines, the remaining stables and landmarks, all Koroks) uses the data behind the [ZeldaMods object map](https://objmap.zeldamods.org) (extracted from the game files of Breath of the Wild; the map is open source at [zeldamods/objmap](https://github.com/zeldamods/objmap)): the position of the place's marker or of the Korok. Those are not standing spots.

`make test-places` tests the lookup.

`goto` adds a small lift above the table height (1 unit for the places above that stand on ground, 2 for Koroks, 3 for the rest), so Link arrives in the air and drops onto the ground. For 4 seconds after any arrival the fall damage cells follow his height, so a place that is a little too high costs no hearts.

After a far jump the screen can look wrong for a second or two (dark or stale picture, camera low in the grass or inside the terrain): the game pauses the world while it loads the map around the new spot and only then settles the camera. It corrects itself. The camera values (`camera.eye` and the rest) cannot be read yet at that point, so `goto` cannot fix it earlier.

Known crash: the game itself can crash on a loader thread while it builds a model (`access violation: write at 0x8`). It is not caused by `goto`: it also happens on a plain load of a save in the Gerudo desert, about one load in five. The model loader makes a temporary heap from the model's ResourceSizeTable entry and does not check when an allocation in it fails; a few big models (`FldObj_RuinStatueKnight_A-03`) overflow it. Giving every model's entry 64 KB more stopped it in 40 loads in a row. The fix is in PR #524 (`SAVAGEWIND_RSTB_MODEL_KB`); without it, start the game again.

Limits: places that still use marker data can put Link inside a wall, a rock or under the ground, or high above it. Use `pos` afterwards to check where he is. Move him with `teleport` if he is stuck.

`savagewind.log` gets the same line every 30 seconds while Link moves (`[place] swr:1 ...`; none while he stands still), so the log attached to an issue says where its bug happened. `SAVAGEWIND_PLACE_LOG=0` turns these lines off.

## Using swctl

`tools/swctl.py` needs only Python 3.8 or later, with no extra packages.

```
swctl help                 every command with its arguments and a one line description
swctl state                frame number, fps, hour of day, ...
swctl pos                  where Link is
swctl time set 18          set 18:00 (developer)
swctl shot out.png         save a screenshot (developer)
swctl --json state         raw reply, for scripts
swctl --port 7777 ...      other port (default: SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL, else 7777)
swctl --host 127.0.0.1 ... other host (default: 127.0.0.1)
swctl --timeout 5 ...      connect and reply timeout in seconds (default: 5)
swctl --wait 10 state      retry connecting for up to 10 seconds (default: 0)
```

Options go before the command. The default port uses `SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL` only when it is numeric, else 7777.
Ports must be from 1 to 65535. `--wait` retries only connecting, so it never sends a command twice.

Output is plain `key: value` lines, with dotted keys for nested objects and one line per object in a list.
`help` prints an aligned command table. Errors go to stderr. `--json` prints only the original reply line to
stdout, including when the game answers with an error.

Exit code 0 on success, 1 when the game answered with an error, 2 for connection failures, timeouts or invalid
replies. A reply needs its final newline, even if the game closes the connection. With no command, the client
prints usage and suggests `help`.

## Protocol

TCP, text, one request per line, one reply per line, UTF-8, `\n` line ends. Several requests may be sent over one
connection; replies come in the same order.

Request: the command and its arguments separated by spaces. Double quotes keep spaces inside one argument, and
`\"` and `\\` work inside them.

```
get fps
camera
```

Reply: one JSON object.

```
{"ok":true,"data":{"fps":60}}
{"ok":false,"error":"Unknown setting: x"}
```

A command that gives no data answers `{"ok":true,"data":{}}`. Commands run once per presented frame, on the thread
that presents, so they never run in the middle of a frame; a reply can take up to one frame. Unknown commands answer
an error that says so.

Always there: `help` (data: `commands`, a list of `{"name","args","help"}`) and `exit` (ends the game; no data).

## Adding a command

Write a handler in `runtime/control_game.c`, answer with `control_field_*()` for the data and `control_fail()` for an
error, and add it to the table at the bottom with `CONTROL_PLAYER` if it is player safe. `help` and this page pick it up
from there. `control_text()` and `control_copy()` are for front ends that print text or use a clipboard, and are
ignored by the socket.

`make test-control` covers the command layer: who may run what, the queue and the replies.

```
