`docs/research/option-row-second-button.md`:

```md
# Native Options rows with two binding buttons

Research date: 2026-11-01. Static research only; no build or game launch.

## Conclusion

**Two native controls on one row are feasible, but not through Entry fields alone.**
Every row already contains three alternative button parts. The constructor resolves
all three; initialization enables one and hides the others. Recommended prototype:
use the existing choice control and ordinary button together, remove the choice
arrows from view, position the controls in separate columns, and extend the screen's
button-to-row routing. This retains the game's layout renderer, fonts, button
animations and cursor machinery. Navigation and sound behavior still need live tests.

**The toggle is one CheckButton, not two independently selectable buttons.** Its ON
and OFF text panes can display separate bindings, but that is a custom two-half
interaction, with one shared native hit area/cursor. Also, Entry.button_off/on label
the ordinary button's two states, not the toggle's two labels.

## Evidence scope and reproduction

- Checkout inspected: `feature/action-binding` at `1c79552`.
- Read first: `runtime/ui/game_options.mm` header and Entry/Item definitions, then
  its installation, message, value, decide and refresh hooks; `tools/patches.py`.
- Binary: the extracted 1.9.0 `exefs/main`, NSO build ID
  `cd57b23fa4bbad65803d9788c01821ee` (1.9.0), SHA-256
  `f6f0b20bb1f2b67d164c24871cd473147eef1d285f12e7bd492e3126c6022e27`.
- Addresses below are **1.9.0 runtime VAs**, main base `0x7000000000`, not the
  `0x710...` labels used by the old 1.8.2 comments. No constant-delta translation.
- Used local `swr-re/tools/nso.py` for LZ4 segments, `research.py` for Capstone and
  validated unwind bounds; consulted `RESULTS.md`/`CALLSITES.md` for conventions.
- Ran `game_sites.Main.locate()` on each existing Options hook/data site: each pattern
  had exactly one match and agreed with `KNOWN['1.9.0']`, including field `0x36b0`.
- Asset parsing used this repo's `tools/botw_save_convert.py` SARC/Yaz0 readers and
  disposable Python in `/tmp`. FLYT sections were walked using their own sizes,
  including `pas1`/`pae1` hierarchy and `prt1` references. No game assets are included.
- **Verified** means decoded binary or parsed asset/source. Proposed behavior is
  marked **inferred/proposed**. No runtime object addresses or screenshots were captured.

## 1. How the game builds a row

### Screen and row functions

| VA | Verified operation |
| --- | --- |
| `0x7000e2e960` | Options screen constructor; installs vtable `0x7001cf7988` |
| `0x7000e2f0a8` | createRows, screen vtable `+0x2f0`; existing `opt_create_rows` |
| `0x7000e30b58` | 0x98-byte row constructor, counterpart of old `FUN_7100d1d828` |
| `0x7000e2f2e8` | screen row initialization/scroll setup, vtable `+0x2f8` |
| `0x7000e2f4b4` | initializes one constructed row: title, kind, flag type, value, redraw |
| `0x7000e30d30` | selects which of the three button styles is enabled/visible |
| `0x7000e2fde4` | read value, existing `opt_read` |
| `0x7000e2ee44` | store value, existing `opt_store` |
| `0x7000e2eed8` | redraw value/check state, existing `opt_row_redraw` |
| `0x7000e30700` | row decide, existing `opt_decide`; also reached by directional actions |
| `0x7000e31118` | reset, existing `opt_reset` |
| `0x7000e2f564` | screen update, existing `opt_update`, vtable `+0x300` |
| `0x7000e30ee0` | set named layout text from an OptionWindow message ID |
| `0x7000e30f70` | message lookup call intercepted by existing `opt_msg_call` |
| `0x7000e84870` | original message lookup, existing `msg_lookup` |
| `0x7000e84940` | named layout text setter from a supplied UTF-16 buffer |

createRows reads table `0x7001e2e610`: count `+0`, entries pointer `+8`, row count
`+0x10`, order pointer `+0x18`. It finds `Pa_SlideBtn_00`, clones further row layouts
as `Pa_SlideBtn_%02d`, and constructs one logical row per chosen Entry.
At `0x7000e2f258` it loads allocation size `0x98`; `0x7000e2f28c` calls the constructor.
The original template row has the equivalent allocation/call at
`0x7000e2f2a4`/`0x7000e2f2d0`. Rows are inserted into the screen array at
`screen+0x36b8`, count `screen+0x36b0`. The reverse construction/insertion order
is part of the existing implementation; do not assume array order is visual order.

`0x7000e447d8` clones a layout, attaches its pane tree and optionally builds button
and cursor registrations (`0x7000e44934`, `0x7000e44a98`). It is **not** the row
constructor. `0x7000e30ccc` resolves a previously registered button from a part
layout via `0x7000e44d0c`, then checks its runtime type. No source-level C++ class
name for the row was recovered; it is an aggregate without a vptr at `+0`.

Entry is 0x30 bytes: SafeString vptr `+0`, name pointer `+8`, kind `+0x10`, desc
`+0x14`, title `+0x18`, first/last value `+0x1c/+0x20`, button off/on IDs
`+0x24/+0x28`, pad `+0x2c`. Kinds are 0 toggle, 1 choice, 2 ordinary button.

### Runtime object map

| Row offset | Verified contents/use |
| --- | --- |
| `+0x00` | owning Options screen |
| `+0x08` | screen layout, supplied from `screen+0x30`; description targets this |
| `+0x10` | row layout |
| `+0x18` | toggle button object resolved from `Pa_Btn_00` |
| `+0x20` | choice button object resolved from `Pa_Btn_01` |
| `+0x28` | ordinary button object resolved from `Pa_Btn_02` |
| `+0x30/+0x38` | left arrow Decide/Invalid animation objects |
| `+0x40/+0x48` | right arrow Decide/Invalid animation objects |
| `+0x50` | Entry index, not Entry pointer |
| `+0x54` | bool/check value (byte) |
| `+0x58/+0x5c/+0x60` | current/max/min integer values |
| `+0x64` | ordinary button state byte |
| `+0x68` | game flag type |
| `+0x70` | embedded scroll item, initialized by `0x7000d66ec8` |
| `+0x80` | row root pane, loaded from `[row_layout+0x18]` |

A button's `+0x20` points to its layout; that layout's `+0x18` is the root pane.
`0x7000e30d30` calls button vtable `+0x60` with 1/0 for the active/inactive style,
then sets/clears **bit 0 of root pane byte `+0x58`**. Thus setting visibility alone
is insufficient: the native control also has an enable state.
`0x7000f570ec(button, bool)` stores byte `button+0x89` and drives its Check animation
at `button+0x68`; this is check/value appearance, not horizontal focus.

`runtime/pc_cursor.c` independently uses button `+0x60` as hit pane, pane `+0x50/54`
as width/height and pane matrix `+0x70..+0x8c` for transformed bounds. Its pane walk
uses name `+0xb8`, child-list head `+0x20`, child link at pane `+8`. Binary
`0x7000e44b64..0x7000e44b70` also derives a part name from root pane `+0xb8`.
No direct TextBox string-buffer offset is established: use the game's text setter.

### Exact archive and panes

Parsed files under `extracted/romfs`:

```text
Pack/Bootup.pack
  Layout/Common.sblarc                      Yaz0 -> SARC, 33,032,328 bytes
    blyt/OptionWindow_00.bflyt                5,112 bytes
    blyt/PaOptionSlideBtn_00.bflyt              948 bytes
    blyt/PaOptionBtnL_00.bflyt                6,288 bytes (toggle)
    blyt/PaOptionBtnLevel_00.bflyt            5,132 bytes (choice)
    blyt/PaOptionBtn_00.bflyt                 4,452 bytes (ordinary button)
    blyt/PaNumberArrow_00.bflyt               referenced by choice arrows
    anim/OptionWindow_00_{In,Out}.bflan
    anim/PaOptionBtn{,L,Level}_00_*.bflan
    timg/__Combined.bntx                     29,192,328 bytes
Pack/Bootup_USen.pack
  Message/Msg_USen.product.ssarc             Yaz0 -> SARC
    LayoutMsg/OptionWindow_00.msbt           3,440 bytes
```

Common.sblarc compressed size is 6,348,559; compressed SHA-256 is
`a101cc8bced46aaa823bc3e62d5f949af432166ff3b55a0c644cd5c6aef835a5`.
The supplied top-level `Layout/` contains BootUp and Horse archives, not Options.
The screen is in **Bootup.pack's Common.sblarc**, not a loose Option pack.
All 16 supplied `Bootup_<language>.pack` files contain their Message archive and
no `Layout/` member. Geometry is shared; localized messages are separate.

Screen hierarchy, omitting material/user-data sections:

```text
RootPane (1280x720)
  N_Capture_00 / P_Capture_00
  N_Option_00 (y=10)
    N_SlideArea_00 (640x360)
      Pa_SlideBtn_00 -> PaOptionSlideBtn_00
  P_CaptureMask_00
  N_Option_01
    T_OptionTitle_00 (x=-4,y=270; 320x34; Normal_00)
    T_Caption_00 (y=-280; 598.5x22; Caption_00)
    N_Align_00
      Pa_GuideY_00, Pa_GuideB_00 -> PaGuideKeyNormal_00
```

The complete pane list of the **row part** `PaOptionSlideBtn_00` is:

| Section offset in BFLYT | Type/name | Geometry / reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0xa4` | pan1 RootPane | 1280x720 |
| `0x100` | txt1 T_Option_00 | x=-14, 246x24, Caption_00 |
| `0x1d8` | prt1 Pa_Btn_00 | x=130, PaOptionBtnL_00 |
| `0x248` | prt1 Pa_Btn_01 | x=130, PaOptionBtnLevel_00 |
| `0x2e4` | prt1 Pa_Btn_02 | x=130, PaOptionBtn_00 |

There is **no description pane inside the row**. Selection writes Entry.desc to
screen `T_Caption_00` in `0x7000e30550`, call at `0x7000e305b0`.
All three button parts overlap at the same x/y; showing two without moving them
will superimpose their text and backgrounds.

Nested button pane inventory (shared names occur once per listed branch):

- All three: RootPane, N_Cursor_00, W_Base_02; N_Disable_00 containing B_Hit_00,
  W_Base_00, W_BaseLine_02, W_Decide_00, N_Loop_01/Window_00, N_Content_00;
  N_Disable_01 containing W_Base_01 and W_BaseLine_01.
- Ordinary: N_Content_00/T_Text_00; N_Disable_01/T_Text_01.
- Choice: N_Content_00/T_Text_00, Pa_ArrowR_00 and Pa_ArrowL_00 (each a
  PaNumberArrow_00 part); N_Disable_01/T_Text_01, P_Arrow_00, P_Arrow_01.
- Toggle: N_Content_00/N_Content_01/{W_CheckL_00,W_CheckR_00}, T_BtnON_00,
  T_BtnOFF_00; N_Disable_01/N_Content_02/{W_CheckL_01,W_CheckR_01},
  T_BtnON_01, T_BtnOFF_01.

These `_01` text copies are disabled-state counterparts, not spare binding controls.
`Disable.bflan` animates N_Disable_00/01; toggle `Check.bflan` targets ON/OFF text
and check-window panes. Each button layout declares **one** `UniteButton` controller
with **one** `B_Hit_00` and one `N_Cursor_00`, not a controller per label.
Button text font is `NormalS_00.bffnt`; toggle text boxes are only 120 and 80 units
wide (x=-48 and x=84); ordinary text is 240, choice text 200 units wide.
Native button hit regions are 276x40. Two full-width buttons need more horizontal
space than the current 540-unit row background; widening/repositioning is real work.

Byte checks: every parsed BFLYT begins `46 4c 59 54 ff fe 14 00 00 00 00 08`:
FLYT, little-endian BOM, 0x14 header, version word 0x08000000. Section-relative
pane name is `+0x0c`, translation `+0x2c`, size `+0x4c/+0x50`;
these are **file offsets**, not runtime pane offsets. Header `+0xc` is file size,
`+0x10` section count. A patch must also preserve parts, materials and animation groups.

## 2. Evaluate the second-button approaches

| Approach | Feasibility | Relative effort / risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a. Reveal/reposition two existing styles | Yes, structurally verified; full interaction proposed | Medium-large / medium-high: routing, geometry, focus |
| a. Use disabled text copies as buttons | No independent controls; requires custom interaction | Medium / visual-state breakage |
| b. Choice row alone | No simultaneous two bindings; only one current value | Small for a device selector, but misses requested layout |
| b. Toggle halves | Yes as two labels plus custom half selection; not two native controls | Medium / limited width, single cursor/hit box |
| c. Two Entries at same y | No stock support; possible with layout/scroll/navigation replacement | Large / high: duplicate titles, focus and scroll items |
| c. Per-row sub-layout / duplicate native part | Yes with native cloning/registration | Large / high: ownership, callbacks and resource capacity |
| d. In-memory BFLYT/archive patch | Yes; this repo already does it for HUD layouts | Medium for geometry/headers, large with new controls |

### a. Existing controls and direct pane access

Construction resolves Pa_Btn_00/01/02 at `0x7000e30bb0`, `0x7000e30bc4`,
`0x7000e30bd8`; stores objects at row `+0x18/+0x20/+0x28`. No allocation of a
new button is needed to experiment with the choice and ordinary styles together.
After row init's redraw call `0x7000e2f550`, `x19` still identifies the row;
`0x7000e2f554` is a concrete post-init hook location. Subsequent redraw entry
`0x7000e2eed8` also needs custom binding handling, otherwise it updates only one style.

Set texts with `0x7000e30ee0(layout, SafeString* pane_name, message_id)` so existing
`rt_opt_msg` supplies stable UTF-16 strings, or use `0x7000e84940` with a supplied
buffer. Target each button's own layout and T_Text_00/01 explicitly. Do not assume
changing one disabled/normal copy changes the other. SafeString needs the game's
valid vptr, as existing Entry/message hooks already use.

Enable both controls through the existing button operation and root visibility;
hide the choice arrow parts and disabled-state arrow pictures, including animation
side effects. Their row offsets `+0x30..+0x48` are animation handles, not hit panes.
**Inferred:** two registered controls can retain native cursor/Decide animations,
provided screen callbacks and geometry are fixed. Simply making them visible is not enough.

### b. What toggle/choice input actually does

Redraw's toggle branch `0x7000e2ef30..0x7000e2ef4c` calls
`0x7000f570ec(row.toggle, row.bool)`; it never reads Entry.button_off/on.
Only the ordinary-button branch fetches Entry `+0x24` or `+0x28` and writes
T_Text_00 (`0x7000e2f064` and `0x7000e2efb0`). Thus a distinct `rt_opt_msg` ID
per field still updates one ordinary button, depending on row+0x64.
Toggle relabeling must explicitly write T_BtnON_00/01 and T_BtnOFF_00/01.

Screen `+0x36c0` is an action code, **not a persistent selected column**:
0 confirm, 1 left, 2 right, 3 idle. Screen `+0x36c8` is current row. Update resets
the code to 3 at `0x7000e2f628`; confirm writes 0 at `0x7000e2f9c8`.
Left writes 1 at `0x7000e2fa50`; right writes 2 at `0x7000e2fae4`.
Input tests use screen-input bytes `+0xa/+0x12`, masks `0x44/0x88`; these cover the
shared horizontal repeat paths. Exact stick-versus-d-pad bit provenance was not
traced through the input producer; no separate persistent half-focus was found here.

Row decide `0x7000e30700` handles toggle as follows:

- Confirm: load bool at `0x7000e30768`, XOR 1 at `0x7000e30770`, update current value.
- Left/code 1: increment/clamp value at `0x7000e30a34`; right/code 2:
  decrement/clamp at `0x7000e30a14`; write bool = value != 0 at `0x7000e30a5c`.
- ON is the left label; OFF is right. This changes the option immediately; there
  is no stock “move between two bind buttons, then A activates that half” contract.

A toggle prototype could intercept this before mutation: directions select a
side without saving settings; confirm captures that side. It must preserve that
side across `rt_opt_read`, drive check appearance separately and handle mouse halves.
Current `rt_opt_decide` rejects every kind except KIND_BUTTON, and current capture
uses BIND_DEV_ANY. Both must change; left/right must never start capture.
`rt_opt_store`/`rt_opt_reset` must not call ordinary toggle get/set callbacks on a
binding pseudo-toggle. `pc_cursor.c:options_click` currently suppresses clicking the
already-checked half, so relabeling alone cannot make it a binding editor.

Choice has one value T_Text_00 between arrows; Entry.first_value + row.value selects
its message (`0x7000e2effc..0x7000e2f00c`). Arrows change that value; they are not two
text-bearing binding buttons. Reusing the whole choice control as one of two controls
is different from using its arrows as the two bindings.

### c/d. Layouts, Entries and load-time patching

Two Entries normally mean two cloned row layouts and two scroll items. Merely
assigning matching y coordinates does not merge focus, description, scrolling or
Entry identity. A new sub-layout can contain two native button parts, but a new pane
alone does not add the Options callbacks needed to route it.

The in-memory path is already implemented in `runtime/services/fs.c`:
`open_image` -> `rom_index` -> `hud_letters_patch` -> `rstb_patch`; reads pass
through `romfs_read`/`storage`, including memory-backed `Overlay.mem` ranges.
`hud_letters_patch` reads Bootup.pack, decompresses Common.sblarc, edits BFLYT files,
appends rebuilt layouts to the SARC, rewrites nodes, recompresses, shifts pack members
by 0x2000-aligned deltas and updates virtual RomFS metadata. It grows the resource
entry **`Layout/Common.blarc`**, then `rstb_patch` adjusts ResourceSizeTable sizes.
An Options patch can compose into this same pack buffer before it is published.
Do not independently replace the pack again and lose the HUD patch or user overlays.

This establishes a hookable path without shipping edited Nintendo assets. Generate
the modified data from the user's archive in memory; keep names, alignment, section
counts, file sizes, node ranges and resource allocation accounting valid. Byte-size
checks and fail-closed handling of unknown archives are needed. Existing code's
user-overlay precedence must be respected. Asset edits alone do not fix input routing.

## 3. Column headers

- T_OptionTitle_00 can carry a page title, but is a single centered 320-unit text
  box at y=270. Spaces or embedded text in it are not two independently aligned small
  column headers. No existing `Item` page-title field addresses this pane.
- T_Caption_00 is the live description; using it loses the selected action's help.
  Pa_GuideY/B are reset/back hints, not unused header panes.
- A non-selectable first row is possible with a special row-init hook: leave its
  text visible, disable all three controls, and supply two labels in separate text
  panes. No stock non-selectable Entry kind was verified. It consumes a scroll item
  and scrolls away; hiding controls must not strand initial focus on it.
- **Recommended:** add two text panes under screen N_Option_01 through the in-memory
  BFLYT transform, using its existing fonts/materials, above the scrolling region.
  Give them unique names, smaller font size, independent column positions, and no
  `cnt1` button controller. Hide outside P_BINDS. Move/shrink the list viewport if
  necessary; do not overlap title or first row. Exact final dimensions need a live
  layout check. This is proposed, not a tested resource patch.

## 4. Implementation plan and remaining limits

1. Add versioned/signature-checked sites for the new functions below to
   `tools/game_sites.py`; expose needed sites through `runtime/game_sites.h`.
   Keep additions guarded to SWR binding rows on P_BINDS. Do not enlarge the native
   0x98 row or use padding as unowned storage; keep row/column state in a sidecar.
2. At post-init `0x7000e2f554` configure row `+0x20` as keyboard/mouse control and
   `+0x28` as controller control. Keep Entry.kind=2 for ordinary read/store behavior.
   Enable both, hide choice arrows, reposition both and the action label. Verify
   runtime transform setters/dirty propagation before writing position fields;
   file offsets listed above are not runtime coordinate addresses. Alternatively
   derive geometry changes in memory at layout load while preserving native pages.
3. Intercept redraw entry `0x7000e2eed8` for these rows: write separate synthetic
   message IDs for key and pad to each T_Text_00/01 using `0x7000e30ee0` and extend
   `rt_opt_msg`. Refresh both when capture ends. Leave ordinary game rows on the
   original path. Handle keyboard-only slots with an inactive controller cell.
4. Extend native callback routing to match either control and remember the column:
   select/help `0x7000e3047c` (vtable +0x340), state callback `0x7000e305d0`
   (+0x350), decide dispatcher `0x7000e30668` (+0x360), and callback
   `0x7000e30a90` (+0x368). Each currently compares only the control selected by
   Entry.kind. Keep help through `0x7000e30550`; adapt `0x7000e302e4`'s per-kind
   state handling to both cells. Exact names of the non-decide callbacks remain inferred.
5. Fix update's active-control comparison `0x7000e2f648..0x7000e2f7d0` and its
   horizontal branches: left/right move native cursor between cells without changing
   bindings; up/down preserve the column. Initial focus `0x7000e2ffec` also chooses
   one control by kind (`0x7000e30130..0x7000e301b4`). Do not expect geometric
   placement alone to fix these hard-coded one-control assumptions.
6. Intercept `0x7000e30700` before its original body: confirm uses remembered column
   and calls `bind_capture_begin(BIND_DEV_KEY/PAD, slot)`, not BIND_DEV_ANY. Preserve
   `rt_opt_tick` refresh/capture cancellation and reset semantics. Update
   `pc_cursor.c:options_row_at/options_focus/options_click` to use both native hit
   regions; it currently selects one by kind and extends its hit area over the title.
7. Compose the header/necessary geometry transform into `hud_letters_patch`'s
   Common archive rebuild in `fs.c`, preserving RSTB accounting and overlay behavior.
   Scope visible changes to P_BINDS; shared layouts also serve original Options.
8. On a machine with dependencies, verify native cursor, hover/Decide sounds, both
   device captures, held/repeated directions, disabled cells, long/localized labels,
   scrolling, reset, cancel, reopening and both pause/title Options entry points.
   Check that inactive/disabled text copies agree and no focus reaches hidden panes.

Static feasibility is strong; the complete navigation contract, geometry setters,
text growth limits, and visual/aural acceptance are not verified. This pass cannot
supply a ready-to-apply UI patch or claim live success. No ImGui overlay, binary,
asset replacement, runtime change or build was produced.

Selected raw instruction checks (little-endian bytes):

| VA | Bytes | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0x7000e2f258` | `00 13 80 52` | mov w0, #0x98 |
| `0x7000e2f28c` | `33 06 00 94` | bl 0x7000e30b58 |
| `0x7000e30b6c` | `04 50 00 b9` | str w4, [x0,#0x50] |
| `0x7000e30c0c` / `0x7000e30c20` / `0x7000e30cc4` | `60 0e 00 f9` / `60 12 00 f9` / `60 16 00 f9` | store toggle/choice/button pointers |
| `0x7000e30d80` | `09 61 01 39` | strb w9, [x8,#0x58], root visibility |
| `0x7000e2efb0` / `0x7000e2f064` | `02 29 40 b9` / `02 25 40 b9` | load Entry on/off ID at +0x28/+0x24 |
| `0x7000e30770` | `2a 01 00 52` | eor w10, w9, #1, confirm toggles value |
| `0x7000e306fc` | `01 00 00 14` | b 0x7000e30700, native decide dispatch |

```

`docs/research/two-button-row-spike.md`:

```md
# Two native buttons in an Options row: spike

2026-11-01, BotW 1.9.0.

**Status:** the layout now applies to every binding row, with a column header row and a row band
(darkener under the non-hovered button, slightly lighter hovered button). The text below describes
the first three-row probe. Corner rounding of the row band is left for a later change.

**Result: three rows render two real native buttons side by side in the running game.**
The hidden Windows probe reached Title > Options > Key bindings without an observed crash.
Its screenshot shows Interact, Jump and Attack with separate key/pad text and the native highlight.
Native column navigation and keyboard capture also ran. Sound and physical input acceptance remain open.

## Implemented

Only the first three action rows on P_BINDS, Interact (0), Jump (2), Attack (3), use two cells.
The existing choice control is the keyboard/mouse cell; the ordinary control is the controller cell.
Both remain registered native controls. Choice arrows are hidden. Both enabled/disabled text copies
use the game's message text setter. No ImGui controls or Nintendo assets were added.

The buttons are narrowed to half width, moved apart, and their text gets inverse horizontal scaling
to retain native font proportions. The label is narrowed too. This geometry is a candidate,
not a visually approved layout. Other rows and pages retain their existing path.

Native select, state, confirm, initial-focus and update routing now recognize both cells.
Left/right changes column, up/down retains it, mouse hit testing uses two disjoint native panes,
and confirm starts BIND_DEV_KEY or BIND_DEV_PAD capture. Mouse clicks request the native
Decide animation before its confirmed callback, rather than calling capture directly. Captures redraw both cell texts.
A sidecar stores state without enlarging the game's row object.

All 13 new sites are one strict optional group. A missing, ambiguous or wrong-address match disables
the group even on a known build, preserving the existing single-button rows. Unknown row shapes
also keep their original redraw. `SAVAGEWIND_TWO_BUTTON_ROWS=0` disables the runtime experiment.

## Evidence and actual checks

- Every new signature uniquely matches the supplied 1.9.0 main NSO at its listed KNOWN address.
  Every emitted hook's replaced opcode was checked against that binary; generated hook C passed syntax checking.
- Verified pane translation `+0x30`, scale `+0x48`, size `+0x50/+0x54` and dirty bit 4 at `+0x58`.
  Native Pane calculation at `0x70000276a0` rebuilds the matrix at `+0x70` and propagates to children
  (`0x7000027744..0x7000027758`, `0x7000027ad0..0x7000027adc`, `0x7000027bb0..0x7000027bc8`).
  Cached world matrices are never edited. No BFLYT/archive patch was necessary for this candidate geometry.
- Linux and Windows: `make test-actions test-bind-capture test-pc-controls` pass.
  Windows also passes `test-input-focus`, `test-gyro`, `test-two-button-rows`, the 45 game-site checks,
  and the strict-group failure tests. The new integration test exercises the actual Options hooks and
  real capture engine with synthetic rows, including wrong-device rejection and CPU-state preservation.
- Windows release executable, configuration executable and frozen generator build pass.
  This includes the edited `.mm` file.
- `vibe-check runtime/ui/game_options.mm` reports no findings; `git diff --check` passes.

### Hidden runtime probe, completed 2026-11-01

- Private library setup completed in 602 seconds with `Game files ready. -> READY`.
  The probe loaded game version 1.9.0 and 103 sites. It used a dedicated control port. Physical input and audio were disabled.
- The existing control API navigated the actual title menu and Options to Key bindings. The page had
  62 rows. Six `[row-spike]` configuration lines show the two parts on each of the three target rows,
  with native root x positions changed from 130 to 40/190. The game continued rendering the page.
- Native cursor-node reads confirmed right selected Interact's ordinary/pad button, down selected
  Jump's pad button, up returned to Interact's pad button, and left selected its choice/key button.
  These were real runtime node/button pointers, not host-test expectations.
- Confirm on the left cell logged `capture slot 256 device key`. Its screenshot shows `Press a key...`
  only in that cell; the controller cell still shows B. The timeout produced an Interact redraw.
- Screenshots saved successfully through the control API's `shot` command:
  `two-button-row.png` (1280x720, frame 4961), `two-button-row-left.png` (frame 11652), and
  `two-button-row-key-capture.png` (frame 11769). The first and capture images were visually inspected.
- `probe-stderr.log` contains no warning/error/failure/fatal/assertion/crash matches. Stdout is empty;
  stderr is the useful game log. The last periodic entry is frame 11962, followed by control connection
  closure near the configured `SAVAGEWIND_EXIT_AT=12000` limit. Exit status was not recorded.

**Not tested live:** controller capture, assigning a physical key/pad binding, mouse hover/click,
sounds (audio was disabled), long/localized labels, scrolling, held/repeated directions, reset/reopen
and the pause-menu entry point. The frame limit ended the probe before the controller-capture step.
Device filtering and mouse routing have host tests; these do not replace physical/native acceptance.

## Recommendation

**Go with changes.** The live render and column navigation establish the core two-native-button approach.
Finish the live input/sound checks and Fabian's visual acceptance before expanding it.
Allow roughly 2 to 4 focused days for a full page:
final widths and long labels, disabled controller cells, native navigation/scroll polish and device QA.
Column headers likely need two added text panes through the existing in-memory Common archive rebuild,
scoped to P_BINDS, plus space above the list. That remains a feasibility note, outside this spike.

`docs/save-converter.md`:

```md
# Importing Wii U / Cemu saves

Savage Wind Configuration can import a *Breath of the Wild* save from the Wii U, or one played in Cemu, and turn it into
a save Savage Wind can load. You do not need Python or a terminal. It reads only your own files and ships no game data.

## Use it

1. Close the game and open **Savage Wind Configuration**. Go to **Settings > Saves**. The tab is only on the start
   screen, not in the in-game menu, because the game must not be running while its saves change.
2. Choose **Import from Wii U / Cemu...** and pick the Wii U profile folder. In Cemu it is
   `mlc01/usr/save/00050000/<title id>/user/80000001`, the folder with the numbered slots `0`, `1`, ... and
   `option.sav`. A folder above it works too: the importer looks up to ten levels down and prefers a Wii U save to
   anything else it finds. The search stops after four seconds or 100,000 folders.
3. The save is converted into a new folder next to your `save` folder. Your saves are not touched yet. When that is done,
   a question names the backup folder and shows which slots come in. Choose **Import**, or **Cancel** to leave
   everything as it is (the converted copy is removed again).
4. Your current `save` folder is moved whole to `save-backups/save-<date>-<time>`, next to `save`. The converted save
   takes its place, and whatever else the old folder held besides `save_0` (the `sdcard` folder) is copied back.
   Nothing is deleted.
5. The tab shows what was imported: the slots, how many flags were kept, set to their defaults or dropped, and how
   many Hero's Path blocks, album pictures and compendium pictures came along. The slot list below it is read again.

With [save profiles](save-profiles.md), everything on this page works on the profile in use: the import and its backup
folder are in that profile, and the other profiles are not touched. "Your `save` folder" below is the Default profile.

The import replaces the whole of `save_0` (all slots, `option.sav`, the Hero's Path, the album and the compendium
pictures), not just some files in it. Mixing slots of two games would give a Hero's Path that does not match the save.
To go back to what you had: close the game, rename `save` to something else, and rename the backup folder to `save`.

The other two buttons: **Back up saves** copies the whole `save` folder to a new dated folder in `save-backups`
and leaves the saves where they are, and **Open save folder** opens it in your file manager.

The slot list shows each slot's picture (`caption.jpg`, on the right while the row is selected), when the game wrote the
slot (the file time of its `caption.sav`) and the play time, if the save's `caption.sav` has a `PlayTime` flag. The
importer keeps the file times of the Wii U files, so an imported slot shows the date it was saved on the Wii U.

It needs your game files set up: the importer reads the flag tables from `Pack/Bootup.pack` in them (see below).

## When it does not work

Each of these ends with "Nothing was changed.", and your saves are exactly as they were:

- **No Breath of the Wild save found in that folder.** Pick the folder with the numbered slots, or one above it.
- **The search took too long. Choose a folder closer to the save.** The time or folder limit was reached.
- **That is a Switch save already.** Switch saves are used as they are: copy their files into the save folder instead.
- **A save file is damaged or incomplete.** The message names the file. A half-copied save lands here.
- **The game files weren't found / can't be read.** Set up the game files on the start screen first.
- **Savage Wind is running in a game.** Another Savage Wind has the save folder open (see below). Close the game first,
  then try again.
- **The save folder is a link.** Moving a link would move the link, not the saves, so the importer stops.
- **Files could not be read or written.** Close anything that has the save folder open (a file manager window, a
  backup program) and try again.

If the last step fails after the old folder has been moved, the move is undone. In the rare case that cannot be undone
either, the message says "The import stopped halfway" and names the backup folder: rename it to `save` to get your
saves back.

A running game holds a lock on its save folder: the empty file `save.lock` next to `save` (not inside it, so the swap
never moves it). The operating system drops the lock when the game ends, however it ends, so a crash leaves nothing to
clean up; the file itself stays. While another Savage Wind holds it, the tab refuses to import or to back up, because
the running game could save over an imported slot, or a backup could copy a file that is half written. Choosing a
folder to import from is refused straight away, before anything is converted. The game does not wait for the lock: a
second game started on the same save folder still starts, and logs that the lock is taken. The tab also holds the lock
while it swaps or copies, so two Savage Winds cannot do that at once. If the lock file cannot be made (a read-only
folder), nothing is locked and nothing is refused.

Closing the start screen or quitting waits for its save worker. A conversion can stop between files and removes its
staged copy. Once installation starts, quitting waits for the two moves and the carry-over copy to finish; it does not
cancel an installation between moves. This covers normal Quit and window close, not a crash, power failure or forced
process termination. A blocked operating-system file read or move can delay quitting until it returns.

When the tab opens, it removes abandoned dated `save-import-*` folders beside `save`, leaving a live or unconfirmed
stage alone. If `save` is missing, it keeps every import folder and shows a recovery message naming the newest import
and dated backup folders. Close Savage Wind and rename the desired folder to `save` to recover it. Imports and backups
are disabled while this recovery is needed. **Open save folder** opens the preserved import without creating an empty
`save` folder. Cleanup does not follow symbolic links or Windows junctions.

## What it does

A save is a handful of small files per slot. `game_data.sav` holds every game flag, `caption.sav` the metadata the
load screen shows, `caption.jpg` its picture; `option.sav` holds the settings, `tracker/` the Hero's Path, and `album/` and `pict_book/` the photos.

The flag files are the same on both consoles apart from three things, and the importer handles each:

- **Byte order.** The Wii U is big endian, the Switch little endian. Every 32-bit value is swapped. Text flags are
  stored as plain bytes and are not swapped.
- **Revision.** The first word of the file is the game revision (`0x471B` for the Wii U's 1.5.0, `0x4730` for
  Switch 1.9.0). Flags are matched by the CRC32 of their name, so a flag that only exists in the target revision gets
  its default value, and one that no longer exists is dropped. The report counts both.
- **Types and sizes.** Which flags exist, their types, array lengths and defaults are read from the game's own
  `GameData/savedataformat` and `gamedata` tables inside `Pack/Bootup.pack`. Nothing is hard coded, so another game
  revision works with its own `Bootup.pack`.

`option.sav` is converted the same way, but the two consoles have different options, so settings that do not exist
on both sides take the Switch default.

`tracker/` (the Hero's Path) is byte-swapped in 32-bit words, except its 8 byte header, which holds four plain bytes
and two 16-bit fields. `album/` and `pict_book/` are plain JPEG files and are copied.

Slots keep their number. The game decides which slot "Continue" loads.

The code is in `runtime/services/save_convert.c` (the importer, with no SDL in it), `runtime/services/archive.c` (the
Yaz0 and SARC readers it shares with `fs.c`) and `runtime/ui/saves_tab.mm` (the tab). The conversion runs on a worker
thread. The slot list is also read on that worker, with a loading message while it is being read, so the start
screen is not held up while it reads the game's tables and writes the files.

## The Python tool

`tools/botw_save_convert.py` does the same conversion from a terminal. It is the reference the importer follows and the
test oracle for it, and it can do two things the tab does not offer: convert a Switch save back to the Wii U layout
(`--to wiiu`) and choose slots (`--slots 0,2`) or leave the Hero's Path out (`--tracker skip`). It needs Python 3 and
nothing else.

```
python tools/botw_save_convert.py --src <Cemu profile folder> --dst save/save_0
```

`--bootup` picks another `Pack/Bootup.pack` (default `extracted/romfs/Pack/Bootup.pack`) and `--dry-run` converts in
memory and only reports. The tool never overwrites: files that already exist in the destination are skipped, and
`--overwrite` renames them to `<name>.bak-<time>` first. It does not make backups of the whole folder; the tab does.

## Tests

`python tools/test_botw_save_convert.py` runs the tests of the Python tool, which build their flag table by hand and
need no game files.

`make test-save-convert` (or `python3 tools/test_save_convert.py`) builds the importer into a test program and compares it
with the Python tool: both convert synthetic saves made against a small `Bootup.pack` built by hand, and every output
file has to match byte for byte, along with the per-file flag counts. It also covers the refusals (no save, a Switch
save, damaged saves, a missing or broken `Bootup.pack`), folders with non-ASCII names, and the safety of the backup,
the swap and its rollback. No game files are needed.

The script also runs the Saves tab itself without a window (`tools/test_saves_tab.cpp`: Dear ImGui builds the frames in
memory, the importer runs on its worker thread, and the question is answered with a click) on copies of a synthetic save
folder, and checks the files on disk afterwards: import over an existing save, a first import, Cancel, the refusals and
Back up saves, and an import and a backup refused while another process holds the save folder's lock (a second test
process stands in for the game, also killed to check that its lock goes with it). It also quits during conversion, at confirmation, and between the two installation moves, and checks
recovery after an interrupted installation. The C cases cover cancellation, stale cleanup and keeping live stages or
all imported copies when `save` is missing. That part needs a C++ compiler and SDL3's headers; set
`SDL3_INCLUDE=<folder with SDL3/SDL.h>` if they are not on the default path (without them it says SKIP), and `--no-ui` leaves it out. It draws no pixels and uses no real
window, mouse or controller, so it does not replace looking at the tab.

With your own files, the same script compares both implementations on your real save:

```
python3 tools/test_save_convert.py --src <Cemu profile folder> --bootup <Pack/Bootup.pack>
```

Nothing is written outside a temporary folder that is removed afterwards.

Against real files: converting a Switch save for Switch reproduces it byte for byte when it is already the target
revision. A published 100% save exists in both a Wii U and a Switch version. Converting the Wii U one to Switch
gives the same 349,508 of 349,538 flags (8 slots plus options) as converting the Switch one for the same game files; the other 30 are text
flags, which that Switch file stores word-swapped (a native 1.9.0 save keeps text as plain bytes, so the tool does too).
All 36 Hero's Path files, and the album and compendium pictures, come out identical to the other console's copy in both directions. A Switch save converted to the Wii U layout also loaded in Cemu without problems.

`docs/save-profiles.md`:

```md
# Save profiles

A save profile is a whole set of saves: its own slots, its own option file, its own Hero's Path, album and compendium.
You can keep several and switch between them, for example your own playthrough and a second one for testing, and they
never touch each other.

## Where they are

In **Savage Wind Configuration**, go to **Settings > Saves**. The **Profiles** section is at the top. The tab is only on
the start screen, not in the in-game menu, because the game must not be running while saves change.

**Your existing saves need nothing from you.** The `save` folder you have always used shows up as the profile called
**Default**. It is not moved, renamed or changed, and it is used until you pick another profile.

## Use it

- **Switch:** close the game, open Savage Wind Configuration, go to **Settings > Saves**, select a profile in the list
  and choose **Use this profile**. The next time you press Play the game uses that profile's saves. Switching changes
  only which profile is used. No save is copied, moved or deleted.
- **New empty profile:** type a name in **Name for a new profile**, then choose **Create empty profile**. The game
  starts a new adventure in it.
- **Copy a profile:** select the profile to copy, type the new name, choose **Copy this profile**. You get a complete
  second set of saves to experiment with. The copy is made under a temporary name and only appears in the list when it
  is whole. If the disk is too full, nothing is copied and you are told.
- **Rename** and **Delete** work on the selected profile. Delete asks first and removes that profile's saves for good,
  so check the name. The profile you are using and the Default profile can't be renamed or deleted: switch to another
  one first.
- **Open this profile's folder** shows the profile's saves in your file manager.

The other buttons on the tab (**Import from Wii U / Cemu...**, **Back up saves**, the slot list) work on the profile in
use. Importing a Wii U save replaces the saves of that profile only.

## Names

A name can have letters, digits, spaces and `- _ . ( )`, up to 32 characters. It can't start or end with a space or a
dot, can't be `Default`, and can't be a name Windows keeps for itself (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1`, ...). Upper and lower case
count as the same: `Test` and `test` can't both exist.

## Where the files are

```
save/                         the Default profile (as always)
save-profiles/<name>/save/    every other profile
save_profile.txt              the name of the profile in use
```

A profile folder has the same layout as `save`: `save_0` with the slots `0` to `5`, `tracker` and `option.sav`.
To back up one profile, close the game and copy its folder. To add a set of saves you already have, create a profile,
close Savage Wind Configuration, and copy the files into `save-profiles/<name>/save/`.

## Good to know

- A profile that a running game is using can't be switched to, copied, renamed or deleted from another Savage Wind.
  Close the game first.
- If `SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR` is set (a testing setting), it decides the save folder and profiles are switched off. The tab
  says so.
- Old profile folders and `save_profile.txt` come along when you move the data folder: copy `save-profiles/` and
  `save_profile.txt` together with `save/` (see [Moving the data folder](data-folder.md)).

# Saves

[Back to the README](../README.md)

Saves are in the `save` folder inside Savage Wind's data folder:

| Platform | Default save location |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `save\` next to `savagewind.exe` |
| Linux / Steam Deck | `~/.local/share/savagewind/save/`, or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/savagewind/save/` if `XDG_DATA_HOME` is set to an absolute path |

If you set `SAVAGEWIND_DATA_ROOT`, look for `save` inside that folder instead. Source builds started from a folder
containing `extracted/` use that starting folder as the data folder. The startup log's `[paths] data: ...` line shows
the data folder actually in use. `SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR`, when set for a test run, overrides the save folder separately.

To back up your progress or move it to another Savage Wind installation, close the game and copy the **whole
`save` folder**, including `save_0` and its contents. Keep a backup of the destination's saves before replacing them.

Want more than one set of saves, for example your own playthrough and a 100% save for testing? **Settings > Saves**
keeps several profiles and switches between them. See [Save profiles](save-profiles.md).

Played on the Wii U or in Cemu? Savage Wind Configuration can import that save: open **Settings > Saves** and choose
**Import from Wii U / Cemu...**. It backs up your current saves first and asks before it replaces them. See
[Importing Wii U / Cemu saves](save-converter.md).

# Teleport places

Every place the teleport knows, with the number and name you can give it. How to turn the teleport on and open the
console: [Cheats and assists](cheats-and-assists.md#teleport-and-console-cheats).

Type the kind, then a number or a word of the name: `tp shrine 12`, `tp shrine oman au`, `tp tower central`,

## Koroks

The game gives Koroks no numbers, so each one goes by the id the object map uses (like `H23`): `tp korok H23`.
`tp korok 10` counts all 900 in map order instead, square `A-1` first. The squares are the map's grid: letters from
west to east, numbers from north to south. `tp nearest korok` is often the easiest.

## What the Windows release bundles

The Windows release zip also bundles, unchanged unless noted, under their own licenses:

- FFmpeg 9.0.2 (libavcodec, libavformat, libavutil, libswscale), LGPL 2.1 or later: built from the official
  [source](https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz) as LGPL only, without GPL or nonfree parts, by
  [tools/build_deps_windows.sh](../tools/build_deps_windows.sh). They are separate DLLs: you can replace them with your
  own build of the same version.
- From [MSYS2](https://packages.msys2.org) (UCRT64, sources there): SDL 3.4.18 (zlib), shaderc 2026.4 (Apache 2.0),
  libiconv 1.19 (LGPL 2.1 or later), the GCC 16.2 runtime (libgcc, libstdc++: GPL 3 with the GCC Runtime Library
  Exception) and winpthreads (MIT and BSD).
- Zig 0.17.0 (MIT; its bundled LLVM, Clang and LLD: Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions; the MinGW-w64 headers and
  runtime: their own permissive licenses), trimmed to what the game code build uses.
- `swgen/`, this project's generator frozen with PyInstaller 6.22 (GPL 2.0 with the bootloader exception): Python
  3.14 (PSF License), Capstone 5.0.9 (BSD), [Unicorn 2.1.4](https://github.com/unicorn-engine/unicorn/tree/2.1.4)
  (GPL 2.0, source at that link) and python-lz4 4.4.5 (BSD).
- AMD FidelityFX SDK 1.1.4 (MIT, `FidelityFX-LICENSE.txt`), compiled into savagewind.exe: FSR 3 frame interpolation,
  optical flow and the Vulkan backend, from [its source](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK/tree/v1.1.4)
  with two alignment fixes (`third_party/FidelityFX/README.md`) and shaders compiled by `tools/ffx_shaders.py`.
- The Fira Sans font, Medium and SemiBold (SIL OFL 1.1, `FiraSans-OFL.txt`), and the Noto Sans Thai and Noto Sans
  Hebrew fonts, Medium, for the menus in Thai and Hebrew (SIL OFL 1.1, `NotoSansThai-OFL.txt`,
  `NotoSansHebrew-OFL.txt`).
- Three colour LUTs in `colour-luts/` (CC0 1.0, from FreshLUTs: see "Credits" and `colour-luts/README.md`).

`fonts/README.md`:

```md
# System fonts

The game draws its text with the Switch's built-in system font, which isn't part of the game files.
Without it, Savage Wind uses Hiragino Sans (built into macOS, the same style of Japanese gothic as the Switch's
Morisawa UD Shin Go), then Arial.

For the exact look, put a dump from your own console here (Switch system archive *FontStandard*, title
0100000000000811, and *FontNintendoExtension*, 0100000000000810):

- `nintendo_udsg-r_std_003.bfttf`: the main font (a `.ttf` with the same name, or spelled `nintendo_udsgr_std_003`, also works)
- `nintendo_ext_003.bfttf`: button glyphs (optional)

`SAVAGEWIND_FONT=<file>` overrides everything (.ttf / .otf / .ttc / .bfttf).

## Chinese and Korean text

The Standard font above is a Japanese gothic (or Arial): it has no Simplified/Traditional Chinese hanzi or Korean
hangul, so a Chinese or Korean text language shows Japanese glyphs, blank boxes or `?`. The game asks for those
through separate shared fonts (*ChineseSimple*, *ChineseSimpleExt*, *ChineseTraditional*, *Korean*), and Savage Wind
fills them from a CJK font when it finds one:

1. `SAVAGEWIND_CJK_FONT=<file>` (any of .ttf / .ttc face 0 / .bfttf), or
2. a CJK font installed on the system, in which case nothing has to be set. Chinese: Microsoft YaHei / SimSun
   (Windows), PingFang (macOS), WenQuanYi Micro Hei / Zen Hei (Linux). Korean: Malgun Gothic (Windows),
   Apple SD Gothic Neo (macOS), WenQuanYi (Linux). Microsoft YaHei has no hangul, so Korean is looked up apart from
   Chinese.

The game's own font engine only reads TrueType (`glyf`) outlines: it crashes on CFF fonts, which Noto Sans CJK
(`.otf` / most `.ttc`) are. Use a TrueType CJK font (WenQuanYi, SimSun, Microsoft YaHei, PingFang are TrueType).

The menu overlay and the start screen (Dear ImGui) use their own font path: there, `SAVAGEWIND_CJK_FONT` is also the
override, otherwise a font in the data folder's `fonts/` (e.g. `NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc`, `wqy-microhei.ttc`), otherwise
a system CJK font. ImGui reads CFF too, so Noto Sans CJK is fine there.

```

`runtime/amiibo.c`:

```c
// amiibo without figures: the figures (the player's dumps), what they hold and their game data. See amiibo.h.
//
// A dump's settings and game data are encrypted, as on the figure: with the amiibo keys (key_retail.bin in the amiibo
// folder: "unfixed infos" and "locked secret", 80 bytes each) they are read as amiitool does - the tag's pages put in
// its internal order, a key, IV and HMAC key from each master key and a seed of the tag (HMAC-SHA256 as a DRBG), the
// data deciphered with AES-128-CTR and both HMACs checked. Without the keys a figure is read without them: no owner,
// no game data.
#include "amiibo.h"

#include <dirent.h>
#include <libavutil/aes.h>
#include <libavutil/hmac.h>
#include <libavutil/mem.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#include "paths.h"
#include "platform.h"
#include "rt.h"
#include "settings.h"
#include "ui/i18n.h"

#ifdef _WIN32
#define SEP "\\"
#else
#define SEP "/"
#endif

#define MAX_FIGURES 8192

// ---- HMAC-SHA256 and AES-128 in CTR mode, from FFmpeg's libavutil (linked anyway, for the movies)
// HMAC-SHA256 of two pieces (a then b) under a 16-byte key; false if libavutil can't allocate
static bool hmac(const uint8_t key[16], const uint8_t *a, size_t an, const uint8_t *b, size_t bn, uint8_t out[32]) {
    AVHMAC *h = av_hmac_alloc(AV_HMAC_SHA256);
    if (!h) return false;
    av_hmac_init(h, key, 16);
    av_hmac_update(h, a, (unsigned)an);
    if (bn) av_hmac_update(h, b, (unsigned)bn);
    bool ok = av_hmac_final(h, out, 32) == 32;
    av_hmac_free(h);
    return ok;
}
// p (n bytes) XORed with the key stream: the IV is the whole 16-byte counter, counting up big-endian
static bool aes_ctr(const uint8_t key[16], const uint8_t iv[16], uint8_t *p, size_t n) {
    struct AVAES *aes = av_aes_alloc();
    if (!aes || av_aes_init(aes, key, 128, 0) < 0) { av_free(aes); return false; }
    uint8_t ctr[16], ks[16];
    memcpy(ctr, iv, 16);
    for (size_t o = 0; o < n; o += 16) {
        av_aes_crypt(aes, ks, ctr, 1, NULL, 0);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < 16 && o + i < n; i++) p[o + i] ^= ks[i];
        for (int i = 15; i >= 0 && !++ctr[i]; i--) {}
    }
    av_free(aes);
    return true;
}

// ---- the figures' data (amiitool's nfc3d)
typedef struct { uint8_t hmac_key[16]; char type[14]; uint8_t rfu, magic_size, magic[16], xor_pad[32]; } MasterKey;
static MasterKey g_keys[2];  // "unfixed infos" (data), "locked secret" (tag)
static bool g_have_keys;

// The tag's pages (0x208 of them) in the internal order the keys and HMACs go by
static void tag_to_internal(const uint8_t *t, uint8_t *i) {
    memcpy(i + 0x000, t + 0x008, 0x008), memcpy(i + 0x008, t + 0x080, 0x020), memcpy(i + 0x028, t + 0x010, 0x024);
    memcpy(i + 0x04c, t + 0x0a0, 0x168), memcpy(i + 0x1b4, t + 0x034, 0x020), memcpy(i + 0x1d4, t + 0x000, 0x008);
    memcpy(i + 0x1dc, t + 0x054, 0x02c);
}
// A key, IV and HMAC key (16 bytes each) from a master key and the tag's seed (false: libavutil failed)
static bool keygen(const MasterKey *m, const uint8_t *in, uint8_t out[48]) {
    uint8_t seed[64], prep[128], *p = prep, blk[32];
    memcpy(seed, in + 0x029, 2), memset(seed + 2, 0, 14), memcpy(seed + 16, in + 0x1d4, 8), memcpy(seed + 24, in + 0x1d4, 8);
    memcpy(seed + 32, in + 0x1e8, 32);
    size_t tl = strnlen(m->type, sizeof m->type);
    memcpy(p, m->type, tl), p += tl, *p++ = 0;
    int lead = 16 - (m->magic_size > 16 ? 16 : m->magic_size);
    memcpy(p, seed, (size_t)lead), p += lead;
    memcpy(p, m->magic, (size_t)(16 - lead)), p += 16 - lead;
    memcpy(p, seed + 16, 16), p += 16;
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) *p++ = seed[32 + i] ^ m->xor_pad[i];
    for (int c = 0, o = 0; o < 48; c++, o += 32) {
        uint8_t ctr[2] = {(uint8_t)(c >> 8), (uint8_t)c};
        if (!hmac(m->hmac_key, ctr, 2, prep, (size_t)(p - prep), blk)) return false;
        memcpy(out + o, blk, o + 32 <= 48 ? 32 : 48 - o);
    }
    return true;
}

static void keys_read(const char *dir) {
    char p[1200];
    snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s" SEP "key_retail.bin", dir);
    FILE *f = fopen(p, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    g_have_keys = fread(g_keys, 1, sizeof g_keys, f) == sizeof g_keys && g_keys[0].magic_size <= 16 && g_keys[1].magic_size <= 16;
    fclose(f);
    LOG("[amiibo] amiibo keys: %s\n", g_have_keys ? "read" : "not valid");
}

bool amiibo_read_data(const Amiibo *a, AmiiboData *d) {
    memset(d, 0, sizeof *d);
    if (!g_have_keys || !a->path) return false;
    uint8_t tag[0x21c] = {0}, in[0x208], plain[0x208], dk[48], tk[48], h[32];
    FILE *f = fopen(a->path, "rb");
    if (!f) return false;
    size_t n = fread(tag, 1, sizeof tag, f);
    fclose(f);
    if (n < 0x208) return false;
    tag_to_internal(tag, in);
    memcpy(plain, in, sizeof plain);
    if (!keygen(&g_keys[0], in, dk) || !keygen(&g_keys[1], in, tk) || !aes_ctr(dk, dk + 16, plain + 0x02c, 0x188) ||
        !hmac(tk + 32, plain + 0x1d4, 0x34, NULL, 0, h)) {
        LOG("[amiibo] %s: libavutil failed\n", a->name);
        return false;
    }
    bool ok = !memcmp(h, in + 0x1b4, 32);
    memcpy(plain + 0x1b4, h, 32);
    ok = ok && hmac(dk + 32, plain + 0x029, 0x1df, NULL, 0, h) && !memcmp(h, in + 0x008, 32);
    if (!ok) { LOG("[amiibo] %s: the keys don't fit its data\n", a->name); return false; }
    d->flags = plain[0x2c];
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) d->nickname[i] = (uint16_t)(plain[0x38 + 2 * i] << 8 | plain[0x39 + 2 * i]);
    d->app_id = (uint32_t)plain[0xb6] << 24 | plain[0xb7] << 16 | plain[0xb8] << 8 | plain[0xb9];
    memcpy(d->area, plain + 0xdc, sizeof d->area);
    return true;
}

static Amiibo *g_figs;
static int g_nfigs;
static pthread_once_t g_once = PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT;

static char *copy(const char *s) {
    size_t n = strlen(s) + 1;
    char *c = malloc(n);
    if (c) memcpy(c, s, n);
    return c;
}

// One dump: an NTAG215 image (540 bytes; 532 and 572 too), its serial number in pages 0-1 and the amiibo ID, not
// encrypted, at 0x54
static void read_dump(const char *path, const char *name, const char *series) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    uint8_t d[0x5c];
    size_t n = fread(d, 1, sizeof d, f);
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long size = ftell(f);
    fclose(f);
    if (n < sizeof d || (size != 532 && size != 540 && size != 572) || d[0] != 0x04 || d[0x5b] != 0x02) return;
    uint8_t uid[7] = {d[0], d[1], d[2], d[4], d[5], d[6], d[7]};
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nfigs; i++)
        if (!memcmp(g_figs[i].id, d + 0x54, 8) && !memcmp(g_figs[i].uid, uid, 7)) return;  // (the same tag twice)
    if (g_nfigs >= MAX_FIGURES) return;
    Amiibo *a = &g_figs[g_nfigs++];
    char nm[256];
    snprintf(nm, sizeof nm, "%s", name);
    char *dot = strrchr(nm, '.');
    if (dot) *dot = 0;
    a->name = copy(nm), a->series = copy(series), a->path = copy(path);
    memcpy(a->id, d + 0x54, 8), memcpy(a->uid, uid, 7);
}

// The dumps in dir and its folders (series: the folder under the amiibo folder, "" for its own files)
static void scan(const char *dir, const char *series, int depth) {
    DIR *d = opendir(dir);
    if (!d) return;
    struct dirent *e;
    while ((e = readdir(d))) {
        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;
        char p[1200];
        snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s" SEP "%s", dir, e->d_name);
        struct stat st;
        if (stat(p, &st) != 0) continue;
        if (S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) {
            if (depth < 4) scan(p, depth ? series : e->d_name, depth + 1);
            continue;
        }
        size_t n = strlen(e->d_name);
        if (n > 4 && !strcasecmp(e->d_name + n - 4, ".bin")) read_dump(p, e->d_name, series);
    }
    closedir(d);
}


static int by_series_name(const void *x, const void *y) {
    const Amiibo *a = x, *b = y;
    int s = strcmp(a->series, b->series);
    return s ? s : strcmp(a->name, b->name);
}

static void list_read(void) {
    g_figs = calloc(MAX_FIGURES, sizeof *g_figs);
    if (!g_figs) return;
    const char *dir = amiibo_folder();
    mkdir(dir, 0755);  // (made for the player to drop dumps into)
    keys_read(dir);
    scan(dir, "", 0);
    qsort(g_figs, (size_t)g_nfigs, sizeof *g_figs, by_series_name);
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nfigs; i++) {
        ui_register_glyphs(g_figs[i].name);
        ui_register_glyphs(g_figs[i].series);
    }
    LOG("[amiibo] %d figures in %s\n", g_nfigs, dir);
}

int amiibo_count(void) { pthread_once(&g_once, list_read); return g_nfigs; }
const Amiibo *amiibo_at(int i) { return i >= 0 && i < amiibo_count() ? &g_figs[i] : NULL; }

const char *amiibo_folder(void) {
    static char dir[1100];
    if (!dir[0]) snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, "%s" SEP "amiibo", rt_data_root());
    return dir;
}

bool amiibo_has_keys(void) { pthread_once(&g_once, list_read); return g_have_keys; }

bool amiibo_key(int i, char *out, size_t n) {
    const Amiibo *a = amiibo_at(i);
    if (!a) return false;
    snprintf(out, n, "%s%s%s", a->series[0] ? a->series : "", a->series[0] ? "/" : "", a->name);
    return true;
}

int amiibo_on_reader(void) {
    if (!g_settings.amiibo_reader[0]) return -1;
    char k[256];
    for (int i = 0, n = amiibo_count(); i < n; i++)
        if (amiibo_key(i, k, sizeof k) && !strcmp(k, g_settings.amiibo_reader)) return i;
    return -1;
}

// ---- game data: <data>/amiibo_data/<amiibo ID>-<serial>.bin, the access ID (4 bytes, little-endian) then the data
static void area_path(const Amiibo *a, char *p, size_t n) {
    char dir[1100];
    snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, "%s" SEP "amiibo_data", rt_data_root());
    mkdir(dir, 0755);
    int k = snprintf(p, n, "%s" SEP, dir);
    for (int i = 0; i < 8 && k < (int)n; i++) k += snprintf(p + k, n - k, "%02x", a->id[i]);
    k += snprintf(p + k, n - k, "-");
    for (int i = 0; i < 7 && k < (int)n; i++) k += snprintf(p + k, n - k, "%02x", a->uid[i]);
    snprintf(p + k, n - k, ".bin");
}

int amiibo_area_load(const Amiibo *a, uint32_t *access_id, uint8_t *buf, int cap) {
    char p[1300];
    area_path(a, p, sizeof p);
    FILE *f = fopen(p, "rb");
    if (!f) {  // (none written here yet: the figure's own, from its dump)
        AmiiboData d;
        if (!amiibo_read_data(a, &d) || !(d.flags & AMIIBO_HAS_AREA)) return -1;
        int k = cap < (int)sizeof d.area ? cap : (int)sizeof d.area;
        memcpy(buf, d.area, (size_t)k);
        *access_id = d.app_id;
        return k;
    }
    uint8_t h[4];
    int n = fread(h, 1, 4, f) == 4 ? (int)fread(buf, 1, (size_t)cap, f) : -1;
    fclose(f);
    if (n >= 0) *access_id = h[0] | h[1] << 8 | h[2] << 16 | (uint32_t)h[3] << 24;
    return n;
}

bool amiibo_area_save(const Amiibo *a, uint32_t access_id, const uint8_t *buf, int size) {
    char p[1300];
    area_path(a, p, sizeof p);
    FILE *f = fopen(p, "wb");
    if (!f) return false;
    uint8_t h[4] = {(uint8_t)access_id, (uint8_t)(access_id >> 8), (uint8_t)(access_id >> 16), (uint8_t)(access_id >> 24)};
    bool ok = fwrite(h, 1, 4, f) == 4 && fwrite(buf, 1, (size_t)size, f) == (size_t)size;
    ok = fclose(f) == 0 && ok;
    LOG("[amiibo] %s's game data saved (%d bytes)%s\n", a->name, size, ok ? "" : ": failed");
    return ok;
}

`runtime/amiibo.h`:

```h
// amiibo without figures (runtime/amiibo.c; the reader: runtime/services/nfp.c). The game's NFC reader (nfp:user)
// reads the player's own figure dumps (.bin, NTAG215) from <data>/amiibo (made on first use; its folders are the
// series). The figure chosen in Savage Wind's options (the amiibo tab, settings amiibo_reader) is on the reader when
// the game looks for a figure (the amiibo rune): the game's own scan, animation and drops, no window over the game.
// With the player's amiibo keys there too (key_retail.bin) it also reads what a figure holds: whether it was set up,
// its nickname and its game data (Wolf Link's hearts). Nothing of a figure, nor any key, is shipped.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef struct {
    const char *name;    // the dump's file name, without .bin
    const char *series;  // its folder in the amiibo folder ("" for the folder's own files)
    uint8_t id[8];       // amiibo ID: character (2), variant, type, model number (2, big-endian), series, 2
    uint8_t uid[7];      // the tag's serial number
    const char *path;    // the dump
} Amiibo;

// What a figure holds, from its dump with the amiibo keys
enum { AMIIBO_SET_UP = 0x10, AMIIBO_HAS_AREA = 0x20 };
typedef struct {
    uint8_t flags;          // AMIIBO_*
    uint16_t nickname[10];  // UTF-16, as set up
    uint32_t app_id;        // the game its game data is for (Twilight Princess HD: 0x1019c800)
    uint8_t area[0xd8];     // the game data
} AmiiboData;
// false: no keys, or they don't fit the dump (d zeroed)
bool amiibo_read_data(const Amiibo *a, AmiiboData *d);

// The figures, sorted by series and name (read on first use)
int amiibo_count(void);
const Amiibo *amiibo_at(int i);

// The figure the player chose for the reader: its index (amiibo_at), -1 for none or one that's gone
int amiibo_on_reader(void);
// Figure i's key for the settings: "<series>/<name>", or its name alone for a file in the amiibo folder
bool amiibo_key(int i, char *out, size_t n);
// The folder the dumps are read from (<data>/amiibo; made on first use)
const char *amiibo_folder(void);
// Whether the amiibo keys (key_retail.bin in that folder) are there: without them a figure gives no game data
bool amiibo_has_keys(void);

// A figure's game data (its application area: Wolf Link's hearts, for one), a file per figure in <data>/amiibo_data
// once the game has written it, before that the figure's own (amiibo_read_data): its size, -1 if it has none
int amiibo_area_load(const Amiibo *a, uint32_t *access_id, uint8_t *buf, int cap);
bool amiibo_area_save(const Amiibo *a, uint32_t access_id, const uint8_t *buf, int size);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

`runtime/assists.c`:

```c
// Options > Accessibility (settings.h): the assists, each off by default. Their patches in the game code
// (tools/patches.py) ask here while it runs; a game version whose code has no place for one (tools/game_sites.py
// OPTIONAL_GROUPS) goes without it.
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "settings.h"

// The damage multipliers: d percent of a loss, rounded, and at least 1 while there is a loss
static int32_t scaled(int32_t d, int pct) {
    if (d <= 0 || pct == 100) return d;
    int32_t s = (int32_t)(((int64_t)d * pct + 50) / 100);
    return s < 1 ? 1 : s;
}

// The cost a hit takes off a life (tools/patches.py _no_wear_hit: every life goes through that function), by whose life
// it is: a weapon's, bow's or shield's durability (LIFE_WEAPON: Unbreakable weapons, from #296, else Weapon wear's share
// of the game's cost, rounded down: a light hit at a low setting can cost nothing), Link's hearts
// (LIFE_LINK: left to rt_link_life, which sees every loss of his), or anything else's (One-hit kill, the damage dealt).
enum { LIFE_OTHER, LIFE_WEAPON, LIFE_LINK };
uint32_t rt_life_cost(uint32_t cost, int32_t life, int whose) {
    if (whose == LIFE_WEAPON) {
        if (g_settings.no_weapon_wear || g_settings.weapon_wear <= 0) return 0;
        int pct = g_settings.weapon_wear;
        return pct == 100 || (int32_t)cost <= 0 ? cost : (uint32_t)((uint64_t)cost * (uint32_t)pct / 100);
    }
    if (whose == LIFE_LINK || (int32_t)cost <= 0) return cost;
    if (g_settings.one_hit_kill) return life > (int32_t)cost ? (uint32_t)life : cost;
    return (uint32_t)scaled((int32_t)cost, g_settings.damage_dealt);
}

// Unbreakable weapons (from #296), the pouch's copy: its setter for an equipped item's value doesn't store a lower one
// (tools/patches.py _no_wear). Arrows (type 2) are counts, not wear, and are left alone.
int rt_keep_wear(uint32_t type, int32_t newv, int32_t oldv) {
    return (g_settings.no_weapon_wear || g_settings.weapon_wear <= 0) && type != 2 && newv < oldv;
}

// God mode, the damage taken: Link's damage handling stores his new life, in quarter hearts, through here (tools/patches.py
// _link_life): God mode keeps the old one, the multiplier scales the loss.
int32_t rt_link_life(int32_t oldv, int32_t newv) {
    if (newv >= oldv) return newv;
    if (g_settings.god_mode) return oldv;
    int32_t v = oldv - scaled(oldv - newv, g_settings.damage_taken);
    return v < 0 ? 0 : v;
}

// Infinite stamina: the stamina setter keeps the old value instead of storing a lower one (tools/patches.py _stamina)
uint32_t rt_stamina(uint32_t oldv, uint32_t newv) {
    float o, n;
    memcpy(&o, &oldv, 4), memcpy(&n, &newv, 4);
    return g_settings.infinite_stamina && n < o ? oldv : newv;
}

// Infinite arrows: the bow's shot takes its arrows off the pouch through one function, which returns before taking
// any (tools/patches.py _remove_arrows). One arrow is still needed to shoot.
int rt_infinite_arrows(void) { return g_settings.infinite_arrows; }

```

`runtime/audio_mix.h`:

```h
// Multichannel 5.1 surround pass-through, stereo downmix, and 3D binaural headphone spatializer.
// Channel order (Nintendo Switch DeviceSink / audout and SDL3 5.1): 0=FL, 1=FR, 2=FC, 3=LFE, 4=BL, 5=BR.
#pragma once
#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "settings.h"

#define AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN 64u  // power-of-two per-channel delay line (~1.33 ms at 48 kHz)

typedef struct {
    float fl_d[AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN], fr_d[AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN];
    float bl_d[AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN], br_d[AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN];
    float fc_d[4];
    uint32_t pos;
    float fl_x_lp, fr_x_lp;  // contralateral head-shadow low-pass (~2.2 kHz) for front +/-30 deg
    float bl_i_lp, br_i_lp;  // ipsilateral pinna high-shelf (~6.5 kHz) for rear +/-110 deg
    float bl_x_lp, br_x_lp;  // contralateral head-shadow low-pass (~1.3 kHz) for rear +/-110 deg
    float lfe_lp;            // subwoofer low-pass (~120 Hz)
} Audio3DState;

static inline void audio_3d_reset(Audio3DState *st) {
    if (st) memset(st, 0, sizeof *st);
}

// Active channel count reported to the game through IAudioDevice::GetActiveChannelCount(Auto).
// Both Surround 5.1 and 3D Headphones ask the game for its full 6-channel (FL, FR, FC, LFE, BL, BR) mix.
static inline uint32_t audio_device_channels(int mode) {
    return (mode == AUDIO_OUT_SURROUND_51 || mode == AUDIO_OUT_HEADPHONES_3D) ? 6u : 2u;
}

// Host SDL_AudioStream channel count: 6 discrete channels for 5.1 speaker output, 2 for Stereo and 3D Headphones.
static inline uint32_t audio_output_channels(int mode) {
    return mode == AUDIO_OUT_SURROUND_51 ? 6u : 2u;
}

static inline float audio_clampf(float x, float lo, float hi) {
    return x < lo ? lo : x > hi ? hi : x;
}

// Smooth C1-continuous soft-knee limiter above 0.85 for binaural summing headroom.
static inline float audio_soft_clip(float x) {
    if (!(x >= -16.0f && x <= 16.0f)) return 0.0f;
    float a = fabsf(x);
    if (a <= 0.85f) return x;
    float d = a - 0.85f;
    float s = 0.85f + 0.15f * (d / (0.15f + d));
    return x < 0.0f ? -s : s;
}

// Mixes one frame of up to 6 normalized input channels (in[0..5] in [-1, 1]: FL, FR, FC, LFE, BL, BR) into
// out[0..audio_output_channels(mode)-1].
static inline void audio_mix_sample(Audio3DState *st, const float in[6], uint32_t inputs, int mode, float *out) {
    if (mode == AUDIO_OUT_SURROUND_51) {
        float fl = inputs >= 1 ? in[0] : 0.0f;
        float fr = inputs == 1 ? in[0] : (inputs >= 2 ? in[1] : 0.0f);
        out[0] = audio_clampf(fl, -1.0f, 1.0f);
        out[1] = audio_clampf(fr, -1.0f, 1.0f);
        for (uint32_t k = 2; k < 6; k++)
            out[k] = inputs > k ? audio_clampf(in[k], -1.0f, 1.0f) : 0.0f;
        return;
    }
    if (mode == AUDIO_OUT_HEADPHONES_3D && st) {
        uint32_t p = st->pos & (AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN - 1);
        float fl = inputs >= 1 ? in[0] : 0.0f;
        float fr = inputs == 1 ? in[0] : (inputs >= 2 ? in[1] : 0.0f);
        float fc = inputs >= 6 ? in[2] : 0.0f;
        float lfe = inputs >= 6 ? in[3] : 0.0f;
        float bl = inputs >= 6 ? in[4] : 0.0f;
        float br = inputs >= 6 ? in[5] : 0.0f;

        st->fl_d[p] = fl;
        st->fr_d[p] = fr;
        st->bl_d[p] = bl;
        st->br_d[p] = br;
        st->fc_d[p & 3] = fc;

        // Front speakers (+/-30 deg): 0-sample near ear, 12-sample (~0.25 ms @ 48 kHz) ITD + 2.2 kHz head-shadow LP to far ear
        float fl_far = st->fl_d[(p - 12) & (AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN - 1)];
        float fr_far = st->fr_d[(p - 12) & (AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN - 1)];
        st->fl_x_lp += 0.25f * (fl_far - st->fl_x_lp);
        st->fr_x_lp += 0.25f * (fr_far - st->fr_x_lp);

        // Rear surround speakers (+/-110 deg): 8-sample depth offset + pinna high-shelf to near ear;
        // 34-sample (~0.71 ms @ 48 kHz) ITD + 1.3 kHz head-shadow LP to far ear
        float bl_near = st->bl_d[(p - 8) & (AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN - 1)];
        float br_near = st->br_d[(p - 8) & (AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN - 1)];
        st->bl_i_lp += 0.58f * (bl_near - st->bl_i_lp);
        st->br_i_lp += 0.58f * (br_near - st->br_i_lp);
        float bl_ipsi = 0.70f * st->bl_i_lp + 0.30f * bl_near;
        float br_ipsi = 0.70f * st->br_i_lp + 0.30f * br_near;

        float bl_far = st->bl_d[(p - 34) & (AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN - 1)];
        float br_far = st->br_d[(p - 34) & (AUDIO_MIX_DELAY_LEN - 1)];
        st->bl_x_lp += 0.16f * (bl_far - st->bl_x_lp);
        st->br_x_lp += 0.16f * (br_far - st->br_x_lp);

        // Front Center (0 deg): anchored in front with a 2-sample micro-early reflection
        float fc_early = st->fc_d[(p - 2) & 3];
        float center = 0.68f * fc + 0.06f * fc_early;

        // LFE subwoofer: ~120 Hz low-pass + low-mid punch
        st->lfe_lp += 0.016f * (lfe - st->lfe_lp);
        float sub = 0.32f * st->lfe_lp + 0.08f * lfe;

        st->pos = p + 1;

        float L = 0.88f * fl + 0.22f * st->fr_x_lp + center + sub + 0.76f * bl_ipsi + 0.28f * st->br_x_lp;
        float R = 0.88f * fr + 0.22f * st->fl_x_lp + center + sub + 0.76f * br_ipsi + 0.28f * st->bl_x_lp;
        out[0] = audio_soft_clip(L);
        out[1] = audio_soft_clip(R);
        return;
    }
    float L = inputs >= 1 ? in[0] : 0.0f;
    float R = inputs == 1 ? in[0] : (inputs >= 2 ? in[1] : 0.0f);
    if (inputs >= 6) {
        L += 0.707f * in[2] + 0.251f * in[3] + 0.707f * in[4];
        R += 0.707f * in[2] + 0.251f * in[3] + 0.707f * in[5];
    }
    out[0] = audio_clampf(L, -1.0f, 1.0f);
    out[1] = audio_clampf(R, -1.0f, 1.0f);
}
