```c
#include "color_grade.h"

#include <ctype.h>
#include <dirent.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#include "imageload.h"
#include "paths.h"
#include "platform.h"
#include "rt.h"
#include "settings.h"

#ifdef _WIN32
#define SEP "\\"
#else
#define SEP "/"
#endif

// ---- presets: set by eye on BOTW's own picture (Great Plateau, day and evening), from the sliders alone
const ColorPreset g_color_presets[] = {
    {"Natural", 0, 0, 0, 0, 0},
    {"Warm", 0, 5, 5, 35, 5},
    {"Cool", 0, 5, -5, -35, 0},
    {"Vivid", 0, 15, 30, 0, 0},
    {"Cinematic", -2, 25, -15, 15, -5},
    {"Muted", 1, -10, -40, 5, 0},
};
const int g_color_preset_count = (int)(sizeof g_color_presets / sizeof g_color_presets[0]);

int color_preset_current(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g_color_preset_count; i++) {
        const ColorPreset *p = &g_color_presets[i];
        if (p->exposure == g_settings.color_exposure && p->contrast == g_settings.color_contrast &&
            p->saturation == g_settings.color_saturation && p->temperature == g_settings.color_temperature &&
            p->tint == g_settings.color_tint)
            return i;
    }
    return -1;
}

void color_preset_apply(int i) {
    if (i < 0 || i >= g_color_preset_count) return;
    const ColorPreset *p = &g_color_presets[i];
    g_settings.color_exposure = p->exposure, g_settings.color_contrast = p->contrast;
    g_settings.color_saturation = p->saturation, g_settings.color_temperature = p->temperature;
    g_settings.color_tint = p->tint;
}

bool color_grade_get(ColorGrade *g) {
    const Settings *s = &g_settings;
    Settings filtered;
    {   // the free camera's photo filter (hle/photo.c), over these settings: they stay as they are
        extern bool photo_filter_get(int *saturation, int *contrast, int *temperature, int *exposure);
        int sat, con, tem, ev;
        if (photo_filter_get(&sat, &con, &tem, &ev)) {
            filtered = g_settings;
            filtered.color_saturation = sat, filtered.color_contrast = con, filtered.color_temperature = tem;
            filtered.color_exposure = ev, filtered.color_tint = 0, filtered.color_lut[0] = 0;
            s = &filtered;
        }
    }
    // white balance: temperature moves red against blue, tint green against both (+: magenta), at the same brightness
    float t = s->color_temperature / 100.0f, m = s->color_tint / 100.0f;
    float wb[3] = {1 + 0.3f * t, 1 - 0.2f * m, 1 - 0.3f * t};
    float y = 0.2126f * wb[0] + 0.7152f * wb[1] + 0.0722f * wb[2];
    float ev = exp2f(s->color_exposure / 10.0f);
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) g->gain[i] = ev * wb[i] / y;
    g->contrast = 1 + s->color_contrast / 100.0f;
    g->saturation = 1 + s->color_saturation / 100.0f;
    g->lut_strength = s->color_lut[0] ? s->color_lut_strength / 100.0f : 0;
    return s->color_exposure || s->color_contrast || s->color_saturation || s->color_temperature || s->color_tint ||
           g->lut_strength > 0;
}

// ---- the LUT folders
typedef struct { char name[96], id[128]; } LutEntry;
static LutEntry g_luts[COLOR_LUT_MAX];
static int g_nluts;
static char g_user_dir[1024];

const char *color_lut_folder(void) {
    if (!g_user_dir[0]) snprintf(g_user_dir, sizeof g_user_dir, "%s" SEP "luts", rt_data_root());
    return g_user_dir;
}

static bool lut_file(const char *f) {
    const char *x = strrchr(f, '.');
    if (!x || f[0] == '.') return false;
    char e[8] = "";
    for (int i = 0; x[i] && i < 7; i++) e[i] = (char)tolower((unsigned char)x[i]);
    return !strcmp(e, ".cube") || !strcmp(e, ".png");
}

static int by_name(const void *a, const void *b) { return strcmp(((const LutEntry *)a)->name, ((const LutEntry *)b)->name); }

// dir's LUT files into g_luts, sorted by name (prefix: the id's, "" for the player's)
static void scan(const char *dir, const char *prefix) {
    DIR *d = opendir(dir);
    if (!d) return;
    int first = g_nluts;
    struct dirent *e;
    while ((e = readdir(d)) && g_nluts < COLOR_LUT_MAX) {
        if (!lut_file(e->d_name)) continue;
        LutEntry *l = &g_luts[g_nluts++];
        snprintf(l->id, sizeof l->id, "%s%s", prefix, e->d_name);
        snprintf(l->name, sizeof l->name, "%s", e->d_name);
        char *x = strrchr(l->name, '.');
        if (x) *x = 0;
        for (char *c = l->name; *c; c++) if (*c == '_') *c = ' ';
    }
    closedir(d);
    qsort(g_luts + first, (size_t)(g_nluts - first), sizeof g_luts[0], by_name);
}

int color_lut_list(void) {
    g_nluts = 1;
    snprintf(g_luts[0].name, sizeof g_luts[0].name, "None");
    g_luts[0].id[0] = 0;
    char dir[1100];
    if (rt_resource("colour-luts", "third_party/luts", dir, sizeof dir)) scan(dir, "sw:");
    for (int i = 2; i < g_nluts; i++)  // (the recommended one first)
        if (!strcmp(g_luts[i].id, COLOR_LUT_RECOMMENDED)) {
            LutEntry t = g_luts[i];
            memmove(&g_luts[2], &g_luts[1], sizeof g_luts[0] * (size_t)(i - 1));
            g_luts[1] = t;
        }
    const char *user = color_lut_folder();
    mkdir(user, 0755);  // (made for the player to drop files into)
    scan(user, "");
    return g_nluts;
}

const char *color_lut_name(int i) { return i >= 0 && i < g_nluts ? g_luts[i].name : ""; }
const char *color_lut_id(int i) { return i >= 0 && i < g_nluts ? g_luts[i].id : ""; }

int color_lut_index(const char *id) {
    if (!g_nluts) color_lut_list();
    for (int i = 1; id && *id && i < g_nluts; i++)
        if (!strcmp(g_luts[i].id, id)) return i;
    return 0;
}

// ---- reading LUTs
static ColorLut *lut_new(int n) {
    ColorLut *l = calloc(1, sizeof *l);
    l->n = n;
    l->dmax[0] = l->dmax[1] = l->dmax[2] = 1;
    l->rgb = malloc(sizeof(float) * 3 * (size_t)n * n * n);
    return l;
}

void color_lut_free(ColorLut *l) {
    if (!l) return;
    free(l->rgb);
    free(l);
}

// Adobe's .cube: keywords (TITLE, LUT_3D_SIZE, DOMAIN_MIN / MAX), # comments, then n^3 lines of three numbers
#define BAD(why) do { LOG("[colour] %s: " why "\n", path); goto fail; } while (0)
static ColorLut *read_cube(const char *path) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    ColorLut *l = NULL;
    float dmin[3] = {0, 0, 0}, dmax[3] = {1, 1, 1};
    size_t got = 0, want = 0;
    char line[512];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof line, f)) {
        char *s = line;
        while (*s == ' ' || *s == '\t' || *s == '\xef' || *s == '\xbb' || *s == '\xbf') s++;  // (a UTF-8 BOM)
        if (!*s || *s == '#' || *s == '\r' || *s == '\n') continue;
        float a, b, c;
        if (!strncmp(s, "LUT_3D_SIZE", 11)) {
            int n = atoi(s + 11);
            if (l || n < 2 || n > 64) BAD("LUT_3D_SIZE not 2..64");
            l = lut_new(n), want = (size_t)n * n * n;
        } else if (!strncmp(s, "LUT_1D_SIZE", 11)) {
            BAD("a 1D LUT (only 3D LUTs are read)");
        } else if (!strncmp(s, "DOMAIN_MIN", 10)) {
            if (sscanf(s + 10, "%f %f %f", &dmin[0], &dmin[1], &dmin[2]) != 3) BAD("bad DOMAIN_MIN");
        } else if (!strncmp(s, "DOMAIN_MAX", 10)) {
            if (sscanf(s + 10, "%f %f %f", &dmax[0], &dmax[1], &dmax[2]) != 3) BAD("bad DOMAIN_MAX");
        } else if (isalpha((unsigned char)*s)) {
            continue;  // (TITLE and other keywords)
        } else if (sscanf(s, "%f %f %f", &a, &b, &c) == 3) {
            if (!l) BAD("data before LUT_3D_SIZE");
            if (got == want) BAD("more data than LUT_3D_SIZE");
            l->rgb[got * 3] = a, l->rgb[got * 3 + 1] = b, l->rgb[got * 3 + 2] = c, got++;
        } else {
            BAD("a line that isn't a keyword or three numbers");
        }
    }
    if (!l) BAD("no LUT_3D_SIZE");
    if (got != want) BAD("less data than LUT_3D_SIZE");
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
        if (!(dmax[i] > dmin[i])) BAD("DOMAIN_MAX not above DOMAIN_MIN");
    fclose(f);
    memcpy(l->dmin, dmin, sizeof dmin), memcpy(l->dmax, dmax, sizeof dmax);
    return l;
fail:
    fclose(f);
    color_lut_free(l);
    return NULL;
}
#undef BAD

// ReShade's strip: n slices side by side (n*n x n pixels), slice = blue, x in a slice = red, y = green
static ColorLut *read_strip(const char *path) {
    int w, h;
    unsigned char *px = rt_image_rgba(path, &w, &h);
    if (!px) {
        LOG("[colour] %s: %s\n", path, rt_image_error());
        return NULL;
    }
    int n = h;
    if (n < 2 || n > 64 || w != n * n) {
        LOG("[colour] %s: %d x %d is not a LUT strip (N*N x N, e.g. 1024 x 32 or 4096 x 64)\n", path, w, h);
        rt_image_free(px);
        return NULL;
    }
    ColorLut *l = lut_new(n);
    for (int b = 0; b < n; b++)
        for (int g = 0; g < n; g++)
            for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) {
                const unsigned char *p = px + ((size_t)g * w + (size_t)b * n + r) * 4;
                float *o = l->rgb + (((size_t)b * n + g) * n + r) * 3;
                o[0] = p[0] / 255.0f, o[1] = p[1] / 255.0f, o[2] = p[2] / 255.0f;
            }
    rt_image_free(px);
    return l;
}

// (the path from the id alone: the render thread loads it while the menus may be listing the folders again)
ColorLut *color_lut_load(const char *id) {
    char p[1300], dir[1100];
    if (!id || !*id || strchr(id, '/') || strchr(id, '\\')) return NULL;
    if (!strncmp(id, "sw:", 3)) {
        if (!rt_resource("colour-luts", "third_party/luts", dir, sizeof dir)) return NULL;
        snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s" SEP "%s", dir, id + 3);
    } else {
        snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s" SEP "%s", color_lut_folder(), id);
    }
    const char *x = strrchr(p, '.');
    ColorLut *l = x && (x[1] == 'p' || x[1] == 'P') ? read_strip(p) : read_cube(p);
    if (l) LOG("[colour] LUT %s: %d^3\n", p, l->n);
    return l;
}
```

`runtime/color_grade.h`:

```h
// Colour grading of the 3D image (Video > Colour; runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c scene_post): exposure, contrast,
// saturation, white balance (temperature, tint) and a look-up table (LUT), applied to the 3D scene before the game
// draws its HUD over it, so the HUD keeps its colours. With every setting neutral nothing runs.
//
// LUTs: .cube files (LUT_3D_SIZE 2..64, DOMAIN_MIN / DOMAIN_MAX) and ReShade-style PNG strips (N*N x N: 1024 x 32,
// 4096 x 64), from two folders: the ones that ship with the app (colour-luts/ next to the executable, CC0: README
// "Credits") and the player's own (<data root>/luts/, made at the first listing).
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

// Ready-made looks (Video > Colour preset): slider values only, set by eye on BOTW's own picture. 0 = Natural (all
// neutral: grading off).
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    int exposure, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint;  // (as in Settings: tenths of an EV, percent)
} ColorPreset;
extern const ColorPreset g_color_presets[];
extern const int g_color_preset_count;
int color_preset_current(void);  // the preset the sliders match, or -1 (custom)
void color_preset_apply(int i);  // its slider values into g_settings (the LUT stays)

// The grading the settings ask for: false when it changes nothing (the pass doesn't run).
// gain: linear RGB multipliers (exposure x white balance), contrast: the S curve's slope at mid-grey (1 = none),
// saturation: 1 = as is, 0 = grey; lut_strength 0..1 (0: no LUT).
typedef struct { float gain[3], contrast, saturation, lut_strength; } ColorGrade;
bool color_grade_get(ColorGrade *g);

// The LUTs offered: the shipped ones first (their own names), then the player's (file name without extension),
// rescanned on each call. Index 0 is "None". The setting stores color_lut_id().
enum { COLOR_LUT_MAX = 200 };
#define COLOR_LUT_RECOMMENDED "sw:Savage_Wind.cube"  // Savage Wind's own look (third_party/luts), offered at the setup
#define COLOR_LUT_RECOMMENDED_STRENGTH 50  // (percent) its LUT intensity in the recommended setup
int color_lut_list(void);            // how many (with None)
const char *color_lut_name(int i);   // as shown
const char *color_lut_id(int i);     // as stored in the ini ("" for None; shipped: "sw:<file>", the player's: "<file>")
int color_lut_index(const char *id); // 0 (None) when not listed
const char *color_lut_folder(void);  // the player's folder (absolute)

// A LUT read from its file: n^3 RGB triples, red fastest, then green, then blue (as in .cube files); inputs map from
// dmin..dmax. NULL with a log line when the file can't be read. Free with color_lut_free.
typedef struct { int n; float dmin[3], dmax[3]; float *rgb; } ColorLut;
ColorLut *color_lut_load(const char *id);
void color_lut_free(ColorLut *l);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

`runtime/colour_vision.c`:

```c
#include "colour_vision.h"

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "settings.h"

// Machado et al. 2009, severity 1.0 (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia), linear RGB, row-major
static const float k_sim[3][9] = {
    {0.152286f, 1.052583f, -0.204868f, 0.114503f, 0.786281f, 0.099216f, -0.003882f, -0.048116f, 1.051998f},
    {0.367322f, 0.860646f, -0.227968f, 0.280085f, 0.672501f, 0.047413f, -0.011820f, 0.042940f, 0.968881f},
    {1.255528f, -0.076749f, -0.178779f, -0.078411f, 0.930809f, 0.147602f, 0.004733f, 0.691367f, 0.303900f},
};
// Where the lost difference goes: red-green into green and blue; blue-yellow into red and green
static const float k_shift[3][9] = {
    {0, 0, 0, 0.7f, 1, 0, 0.7f, 0, 1},
    {0, 0, 0, 0.7f, 1, 0, 0.7f, 0, 1},
    {1, 0, 0.7f, 0, 1, 0.7f, 0, 0, 0},
};

static void identity(float m[9]) {
    memset(m, 0, 9 * sizeof m[0]);
    m[0] = m[4] = m[8] = 1;
}

static void mul(const float a[9], const float b[9], float out[9]) {
    float r[9];
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
        for (int j = 0; j < 3; j++) r[i * 3 + j] = a[i * 3] * b[j] + a[i * 3 + 1] * b[3 + j] + a[i * 3 + 2] * b[6 + j];
    memcpy(out, r, sizeof r);
}

void colour_vision_correction(int type, float strength, float m[9]) {
    identity(m);
    if (type < 1 || type > 3 || strength <= 0) return;
    float d[9];  // I - S
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) d[i] = (i % 4 == 0 ? 1.0f : 0.0f) - k_sim[type - 1][i];
    float e[9];
    mul(k_shift[type - 1], d, e);
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) m[i] += strength * e[i];
}

void colour_vision_simulation(int type, float severity, float m[9]) {
    identity(m);
    if (type < 1 || type > 3 || severity <= 0) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) m[i] += severity * (k_sim[type - 1][i] - m[i]);
}

bool colour_vision_matrix(float m[9]) {
    static int sim_type = -1;
    static float sim_severity = 1;
    if (sim_type < 0) {
        sim_type = 0;
        const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_CVD_SIMULATE");
        if (e && *e) {
            sim_type = !strncmp(e, "protan", 6) ? 1 : !strncmp(e, "deutan", 6) ? 2 : !strncmp(e, "tritan", 6) ? 3 : 0;
            const char *c = strchr(e, ':');
            if (c) sim_severity = (float)atoi(c + 1) / 100.0f;
        }
    }
    int type = g_settings.colour_vision;
    bool corr = type >= 1 && type <= 3;
    if (!corr && !sim_type) return false;
    colour_vision_correction(corr ? type : 0, g_settings.colour_vision_strength / 100.0f, m);
    if (sim_type) {
        float s[9];
        colour_vision_simulation(sim_type, sim_severity, s);
        mul(s, m, m);
    }
    return true;
}
```

`runtime/colour_vision.h`:

```h
// Options > Accessibility > Colour vision: a correction of the whole presented picture (the 3D world, the game's HUD
// and menus) for players with a colour vision deficiency, so colours they confuse (red and green; blue and yellow)
// come apart. Applied at the present (runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c vk_present_draw for SDR, device.c's HDR10 present),
// after the game has drawn its HUD; the Savage Wind menu and Album photos keep their colours. Off: nothing runs.
//
// The model: Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009), "A Physiologically-based Model for Simulation of Color Vision
// Deficiency", severity 1.0 matrices S in linear RGB (a dichromat's view). The correction ("daltonize") moves the
// difference the player cannot see, c - S c, into channels they can: c' = c + k E (c - S c), with E sending the lost
// red-green difference to green and blue (protan, deutan) or the lost blue-yellow one to red and green (tritan), and k
// the setting's strength. That is one 3x3 matrix, M = I + k E (I - S); white and greys stay as they are.
//
// (testing) SAVAGEWIND_CVD_SIMULATE=protan|deutan|tritan[:<percent>]: the picture as a dichromat sees it (S, mixed
// with the identity at that percent), after the correction if one is on (S M: "corrected, as they see it").
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

// The matrix for the current settings, row-major (m[0..2]: output red from input r, g, b): applied to linear RGB.
// false when it is the identity (option off, no simulation): the present draws the picture unchanged.
bool colour_vision_matrix(float m[9]);

// The matrix for one type (1 protanopia, 2 deuteranopia, 3 tritanopia) at a strength (0..1), and the simulation of
// that type at a severity (0..1, mixed with the identity), row-major. (tests, colour_vision_matrix)
void colour_vision_correction(int type, float strength, float m[9]);
void colour_vision_simulation(int type, float severity, float m[9]);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

`runtime/console_core.c`:

```c
// The in-game console without the drawing: lines, history, completion (runtime/console_core.h).
#include "console_core.h"

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct { ConKind kind; char *text; } Line;
static Line lines[CON_LINES];
static int first, count;  // a ring: lines[(first + i) % CON_LINES]
static unsigned revision;

static void add_line(ConKind kind, const char *text, size_t len) {
    int slot = (first + count) % CON_LINES;
    if (count == CON_LINES) { free(lines[first].text); first = (first + 1) % CON_LINES; }
    else count++;
    char *copy = malloc(len + 1);
    if (copy) { memcpy(copy, text, len); copy[len] = 0; }
    lines[slot].kind = kind;
    lines[slot].text = copy;
    revision++;
}
void console_print(ConKind kind, const char *text) {
    if (!text) return;
    for (;;) {
        const char *eol = strchr(text, '\n');
        size_t len = eol ? (size_t)(eol - text) : strlen(text);
        if (len && text[len - 1] == '\r') len--;
        add_line(kind, text, len);
        if (!eol) break;
        text = eol + 1;
    }
}
void console_clear(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) free(lines[(first + i) % CON_LINES].text);
    first = count = 0;
    revision++;
}
int console_line_count(void) { return count; }
const char *console_line(int index, ConKind *kind) {
    if (index < 0 || index >= count) return NULL;
    Line *l = &lines[(first + index) % CON_LINES];
    if (kind) *kind = l->kind;
    return l->text ? l->text : "";
}
unsigned console_revision(void) { return revision; }

// ---- history
static char *history[CON_HISTORY];
static int history_count;
static int walk = -1;      // -1: not walking; else the index shown
static char *walk_typed;   // what was in the field when the walk began

void console_history_rewind(void) { walk = -1; free(walk_typed); walk_typed = NULL; }
void console_history_add(const char *line) {
    console_history_rewind();
    if (!line || !*line) return;
    if (history_count && !strcmp(history[history_count - 1], line)) return;
    if (history_count == CON_HISTORY) { free(history[0]); memmove(history, history + 1, (CON_HISTORY - 1) * sizeof *history); history_count--; }
    history[history_count] = strdup(line);
    if (history[history_count]) history_count++;
}
const char *console_history_step(int dir, const char *typed) {
    if (!history_count) return NULL;
    if (walk < 0) {
        if (dir > 0) return NULL;  // already on the new line
        free(walk_typed);
        walk_typed = strdup(typed ? typed : "");
        walk = history_count - 1;
        return history[walk];
    }
    if (dir < 0) {
        if (walk > 0) walk--;
        return history[walk];
    }
    if (walk < history_count - 1) { walk++; return history[walk]; }
    walk = -1;  // past the newest: the line that was being typed
    return walk_typed ? walk_typed : "";
}

// ---- completion
int console_complete(const char *typed, const char *const *names, int count_in, char *out, size_t cap) {
    if (cap) { strncpy(out, typed, cap - 1); out[cap - 1] = 0; }
    if (strchr(typed, ' ')) return 0;
    size_t len = strlen(typed);
    int matches = 0;
    const char *first_match = NULL;
    size_t common = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < count_in; i++) {
        if (strncmp(names[i], typed, len)) continue;
        if (!matches) { first_match = names[i]; common = strlen(names[i]); }
        else { size_t k = 0; while (k < common && names[i][k] == first_match[k]) k++; common = k; }
        matches++;
    }
    if (!matches || !cap) return matches;
    if (matches == 1) snprintf(out, cap, "%s ", first_match);
    else if (common > len) { size_t k = common < cap - 1 ? common : cap - 1; memcpy(out, first_match, k); out[k] = 0; }
    return matches;
}
```

```h
// The in-game console without the drawing (runtime/ui/console.mm draws it): the lines on screen, the history of what
// was typed, and tab completion. Plain C so tools/test_console_core.c can test it. UI thread only.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>

typedef enum { CON_INPUT, CON_TEXT, CON_ERROR, CON_NOTE } ConKind;  // what was typed, a reply, a failed reply, a remark

// ---- the lines on screen (the newest CON_LINES stay)
#define CON_LINES 400
void console_clear(void);
void console_print(ConKind kind, const char *text);  // text may hold \n: one line each; empty lines are kept
int console_line_count(void);
const char *console_line(int index, ConKind *kind);  // 0 is the oldest; NULL out of range
unsigned console_revision(void);                     // changes whenever a line was added (to stick to the bottom)

// ---- history of typed lines (newest last, no repeats of the last one, at most CON_HISTORY)
#define CON_HISTORY 64
void console_history_add(const char *line);
// Up (dir -1) or down (dir +1) through the history, starting from `typed` (what is in the field now, kept so down
// brings it back). Returns the text to show, or NULL when there is no further entry in that direction.
const char *console_history_step(int dir, const char *typed);
void console_history_rewind(void);                   // typing or sending ends a walk through the history

// ---- completion of the first word. `names` are the candidate commands (sorted), `count` how many.
// Returns how many match what is typed; `out` gets the text the field should show: the one match and a space, or
// the longest common start of the matches; unchanged when nothing matches. Only a first word (no space yet) is completed.
int console_complete(const char *typed, const char *const *names, int count, char *out, size_t cap);
```

`runtime/control.c`:

```c
// Control commands: the registry, the local socket and the queue other front ends use (runtime/control.h). Only the socket thread touches sockets; handlers run at the frame boundary.
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <winsock2.h>
#include <ws2tcpip.h>
#else
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/select.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#endif
#include <errno.h>
#include <inttypes.h>
#include <locale.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "rt.h"
#include "control.h"

enum { MAX_COMMANDS = 128, MAX_CLIENTS = 4, MAX_LINE = 4096, MAX_PENDING = 64, MAX_JSON = 1024 * 1024 };
#ifdef _WIN32
typedef SOCKET ControlSocket;
#define BAD_SOCKET INVALID_SOCKET
#define close_socket closesocket
static bool socket_again(void) { int e = WSAGetLastError(); return e == WSAEWOULDBLOCK || e == WSAEINTR; }
static bool nonblocking(ControlSocket s) { u_long on = 1; return ioctlsocket(s, FIONBIO, &on) == 0; }
#else
typedef int ControlSocket;
#define BAD_SOCKET (-1)
#define close_socket close
static bool socket_again(void) { return errno == EAGAIN || errno == EWOULDBLOCK || errno == EINTR; }
static bool nonblocking(ControlSocket s) {
    int flags = fcntl(s, F_GETFL, 0);
    return s < FD_SETSIZE && flags >= 0 && fcntl(s, F_SETFL, flags | O_NONBLOCK) == 0;
}
#endif

typedef struct { char *s; size_t len, cap; bool bad; } Json;
struct ControlReply { Json data; Json lines; char *copy; char *error; bool failed, exit_after; };
typedef struct Request {
    struct Request *next;
    int client, argc;
    uint64_t generation;
    char *line, **argv, *reply;
    const char *error;
    size_t len, sent;
    bool exit_after;
} Request;
typedef struct {
    ControlSocket socket;
    uint64_t generation;
    char line[MAX_LINE + 1], input[MAX_LINE];
    size_t used, pos, end, bytes;
    int pending;
    bool dropping, eof;
    bool checked;  // the first line was looked at (not a web page's request: http_request)
    Request *head, *tail;
} Connection;

static ControlCmd commands[MAX_COMMANDS];
static int command_count;
static pthread_mutex_t registry_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_mutex_t queue_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static Request *requests, *requests_tail, *finished, *finished_tail;
static _Atomic bool enabled, queued;  // enabled: developer mode (see control_enabled); the socket is up when listener is set
static bool dev_mode, initialized;
static bool running_for_console;  // (a handler is running for the console: help lists only what it may run)
static ControlSocket listener = BAD_SOCKET;
static Connection clients[MAX_CLIENTS];  // owned by the socket thread
static int inflight;

static void append(Json *j, const char *s, size_t n) {
    if (j->bad) return;
    if (n > MAX_JSON - j->len) { j->bad = true; return; }
    size_t need = j->len + n + 1;
    if (need > j->cap) {
        size_t cap = need * 2;
        if (cap > MAX_JSON + 1) cap = MAX_JSON + 1;
        char *p = realloc(j->s, cap);
        if (!p) { j->bad = true; return; }
        j->s = p;
        j->cap = cap;
    }
    memcpy(j->s + j->len, s, n);
    j->len += n;
    j->s[j->len] = 0;
}
static void text(Json *j, const char *s) { append(j, s, strlen(s)); }
static void string(Json *j, const char *s) {
    text(j, "\"");
    const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)(s ? s : ""), *start = p;
    for (; *p && !j->bad; p++) {
        if (*p >= 0x20 && *p != '"' && *p != '\\') continue;
        append(j, (const char *)start, (size_t)(p - start));
        if (*p == '"' || *p == '\\') { char esc[] = {'\\', (char)*p}; append(j, esc, 2); }
        else { char esc[7]; snprintf(esc, sizeof esc, "\\u%04x", *p); text(j, esc); }
        start = p + 1;
    }
    append(j, (const char *)start, (size_t)(p - start));
    text(j, "\"");
}
static void field(ControlReply *r, const char *key) {
    if (r->data.len) text(&r->data, ",");
    string(&r->data, key);
    text(&r->data, ":");
}
void control_field_str(ControlReply *r, const char *key, const char *value) {
    field(r, key); string(&r->data, value);
}
void control_field_int(ControlReply *r, const char *key, int64_t value) {
    char s[32]; snprintf(s, sizeof s, "%" PRId64, value);
    field(r, key); text(&r->data, s);
}
void control_field_num(ControlReply *r, const char *key, double value) {
    char s[128];
    if (!isfinite(value)) strcpy(s, "null");
    else {
        snprintf(s, sizeof s, "%.17g", value);
        // The runtime can use the system locale, but JSON always has a decimal point.
        const char *point = localeconv()->decimal_point;
        char *p = *point ? strstr(s, point) : NULL;
        if (p && strcmp(point, ".")) { memmove(p + 1, p + strlen(point), strlen(p + strlen(point)) + 1); *p = '.'; }
    }
    field(r, key); text(&r->data, s);
}
void control_field_bool(ControlReply *r, const char *key, bool value) {
    field(r, key); text(&r->data, value ? "true" : "false");
}
void control_fail(ControlReply *r, const char *fmt, ...) {
    if (r->failed) return;
    r->failed = true;
    va_list ap, copy;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    va_copy(copy, ap);
    int n = vsnprintf(NULL, 0, fmt, copy);
    va_end(copy);
    if (n >= 0 && n < MAX_JSON / 2) {
        r->error = malloc((size_t)n + 1);
        if (r->error) vsnprintf(r->error, (size_t)n + 1, fmt, ap);
    }
    va_end(ap);
}

void control_text(ControlReply *r, const char *fmt, ...) {
    char line[1024];
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    vsnprintf(line, sizeof line, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
    if (r->lines.len) text(&r->lines, "\n");
    text(&r->lines, line);
}
void control_copy(ControlReply *r, const char *copy) {
    free(r->copy);
    r->copy = copy ? strdup(copy) : NULL;
}

bool control_reply_failed(const ControlReply *r) { return r->failed; }

void control_register(const ControlCmd *cmds, int count) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&registry_lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        const ControlCmd *c = &cmds[i];
        if (!c->name || !*c->name || !c->fn) { LOG("[control] invalid command registration\n"); continue; }
        bool duplicate = false;
        for (int k = 0; k < command_count; k++) if (!strcmp(commands[k].name, c->name)) duplicate = true;
        if (duplicate) { LOG("[control] duplicate command: %s\n", c->name); continue; }
        if (command_count == MAX_COMMANDS) { LOG("[control] command table full: %s\n", c->name); continue; }
        commands[command_count++] = *c;
    }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&registry_lock);
}
// What the caller may run: the socket and developer mode run everything; a player's console only the player safe commands.
static bool allowed(const ControlCmd *c, bool console) { return !console || dev_mode || (c->flags & CONTROL_PLAYER); }
static int by_name(const void *a, const void *b) { return strcmp((*(const ControlCmd *const *)a)->name, (*(const ControlCmd *const *)b)->name); }
static void help(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    ControlCmd snapshot[MAX_COMMANDS];
    pthread_mutex_lock(&registry_lock);
    int count = command_count;
    memcpy(snapshot, commands, (size_t)count * sizeof *snapshot);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&registry_lock);
    field(r, "commands");
    text(&r->data, "[");
    int shown = 0;
    size_t wide = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (!allowed(&snapshot[i], running_for_console)) continue;
        if (shown++) text(&r->data, ",");
        text(&r->data, "{\"name\":"); string(&r->data, snapshot[i].name);
        text(&r->data, ",\"args\":"); string(&r->data, snapshot[i].args);
        text(&r->data, ",\"help\":"); string(&r->data, snapshot[i].help);
        text(&r->data, "}");
        size_t w = strlen(snapshot[i].name) + (*snapshot[i].args ? 1 + strlen(snapshot[i].args) : 0);
        if (w > wide) wide = w;
    }
    text(&r->data, "]");
    // the console's table: sorted, the usage and the one line description lined up
    const ControlCmd *sorted[MAX_COMMANDS];
    int n = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) if (allowed(&snapshot[i], running_for_console)) sorted[n++] = &snapshot[i];
    qsort(sorted, (size_t)n, sizeof *sorted, by_name);
    if (wide > 40) wide = 40;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        char usage[160];
        snprintf(usage, sizeof usage, "%s%s%s", sorted[i]->name, *sorted[i]->args ? " " : "", sorted[i]->args);
        control_text(r, "%-*s  %s", (int)wide, usage, sorted[i]->help);
    }
}
static void ping(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    control_field_bool(r, "pong", true);
}
static void quit(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    LOG("[control] exit command: the game ends once its reply is sent\n");  // (stop() leaves no other trace)
    r->exit_after = true;
}

static void push(Request **head, Request **tail, Request *q) {
    q->next = NULL;
    if (*tail) (*tail)->next = q;
    else *head = q;
    *tail = q;
}
static void free_request(Request *q) {
    free(q->argv); free(q->line); free(q->reply); free(q);
    inflight--;
}
static bool space(char c) { return c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\r'; }
// Split a NUL terminated line into words in place: double quotes keep spaces in one word, \" and \\ work inside them.
// argv needs room for strlen(line) / 2 + 1 words. Returns NULL, or what is wrong with the line.
static const char *tokenize(char *line, char **argv, int *argc) {
    char *src = line, *dst = line;
    const char *error = NULL;
    *argc = 0;
    while (*src && !error) {
        while (space(*src)) src++;
        if (!*src) break;
        argv[(*argc)++] = dst;
        bool quoted = false;
        while (*src && (quoted || !space(*src))) {
            if (*src == '"') { quoted = !quoted; src++; }
            else if (quoted && *src == '\\' && (src[1] == '"' || src[1] == '\\')) { src++; *dst++ = *src++; }
            else *dst++ = *src++;
        }
        if (quoted) error = "unterminated double quote";
        while (space(*src)) src++;
        *dst++ = 0;
    }
    return error;
}
static bool enqueue(int slot, const char *error) {
    Connection *c = &clients[slot];
    Request *q = calloc(1, sizeof *q);
    if (!q) return false;
    q->client = slot;
    q->generation = c->generation;
    q->error = error;
    if (!error) {
        q->line = malloc(c->used + 1);
        q->argv = malloc((c->used + 1) * sizeof *q->argv);
        if (!q->line || !q->argv) { free(q->line); free(q->argv); free(q); return false; }
        memcpy(q->line, c->line, c->used);
        q->line[c->used] = 0;
        if (memchr(q->line, 0, c->used)) q->error = "request contains NUL";
        else q->error = tokenize(q->line, q->argv, &q->argc);
        if (!q->argc && !q->error) { free(q->line); free(q->argv); free(q); return true; }
    }
    inflight++;
    c->pending++;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&queue_lock);
    push(&requests, &requests_tail, q);
    queued = true;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue_lock);
    return true;
}

bool control_enabled(void) { return dev_mode; }
bool control_endpoint_on(void) { return enabled; }

// Run one command (on the frame hook). console: the caller is the in-game console, not the socket.
static void execute(int argc, char **argv, bool console, ControlReply *r) {
    ControlFn fn = NULL;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&registry_lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < command_count; i++)
        if (!strcmp(commands[i].name, argv[0]) && allowed(&commands[i], console)) { fn = commands[i].fn; break; }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&registry_lock);
    if (!fn) { control_fail(r, "Unknown command: %s", argv[0]); return; }
    running_for_console = console;
    fn(argc, argv, r);
    running_for_console = false;
}
static void reply_free(ControlReply *r) { free(r->data.s); free(r->lines.s); free(r->copy); free(r->error); }

// ---- the reply as one JSON line
static char *reply_json(ControlReply *r, size_t *len) {
    Json out = {0};
    if (r->failed || r->data.bad) {
        text(&out, "{\"ok\":false,\"error\":");
        string(&out, r->data.bad ? "reply too large or out of memory" : r->error ? r->error : "command failed");
        text(&out, "}\n");
    } else {
        text(&out, "{\"ok\":true,\"data\":{");
        if (r->data.len) append(&out, r->data.s, r->data.len);
        text(&out, "}}\n");
    }
    if (out.bad) {
        free(out.s);
        out.s = strdup("{\"ok\":false,\"error\":\"reply too large or out of memory\"}\n");
        out.len = out.s ? strlen(out.s) : 0;
    }
    *len = out.len;
    return out.s;
}

// ---- the reply as lines for the console: `key: value`, nested keys dotted, a list of objects one line each
// (the JSON is our own, so it is well formed; this reads just enough of it)
typedef struct { const char *p; Json *out; char prefix[160]; } Flat;
static void flat_ws(Flat *f) { while (*f->p == ' ' || *f->p == ',' || *f->p == '\n') f->p++; }
static void flat_string(Flat *f, Json *dst) {  // at the opening quote; appends the unescaped text
    f->p++;
    while (*f->p && *f->p != '"') {
        if (*f->p == '\\' && f->p[1]) {
            f->p++;
            char c = *f->p++;
            if (c == 'u') {
                unsigned v = 0;
                for (int i = 0; i < 4 && f->p[i]; i++) v = v * 16 + (unsigned)(f->p[i] <= '9' ? f->p[i] - '0' : (f->p[i] | 32) - 'a' + 10);
                f->p += 4;
                char ch = v < 0x80 ? (char)v : '?';
                append(dst, &ch, 1);
            } else { char ch = c == 'n' ? '\n' : c == 't' ? '\t' : c; append(dst, &ch, 1); }
        } else append(dst, f->p++, 1);
    }
    if (*f->p == '"') f->p++;
}
static void flat_scalar(Flat *f, Json *dst) {  // a string, number, true, false or null
    if (*f->p == '"') { flat_string(f, dst); return; }
    const char *start = f->p;
    while (*f->p && *f->p != ',' && *f->p != '}' && *f->p != ']') f->p++;
    size_t n = (size_t)(f->p - start);
    char tok[64];
    char *end;
    bool plain = n > 0 && n < sizeof tok;
    if (plain) { memcpy(tok, start, n); tok[n] = 0; }
    // 17 digit doubles print as 0.10000000000000001: show 7 significant digits instead (whole numbers stay as they are)
    if (plain && memchr(tok, '.', n)) {
        double v = strtod(tok, &end);
        if (end == tok + n) {
            char pretty[40];
            snprintf(pretty, sizeof pretty, "%.7g", v);
            const char *point = localeconv()->decimal_point;
            char *q = strstr(pretty, point);
            if (q && strcmp(point, ".")) { memmove(q + 1, q + strlen(point), strlen(q + strlen(point)) + 1); *q = '.'; }
            text(dst, pretty);
            return;
        }
    }
    append(dst, start, n);
}
static void flat_value(Flat *f, const char *key);
static void flat_object(Flat *f, const char *prefix) {  // at '{'
    f->p++;
    for (;;) {
        flat_ws(f);
        if (*f->p != '"') break;
        Json k = {0};
        flat_string(f, &k);
        while (*f->p == ' ' || *f->p == ':') f->p++;
        char full[160];
        snprintf(full, sizeof full, "%s%s%s", prefix, *prefix ? "." : "", k.s ? k.s : "");
        free(k.s);
        flat_value(f, full);
    }
    if (*f->p == '}') f->p++;
}
static void flat_line(Flat *f, const char *key, const char *value) {
    if (f->out->len) text(f->out, "\n");
    text(f->out, key);
    text(f->out, ": ");
    text(f->out, value);
}
static void flat_value(Flat *f, const char *key) {
    if (*f->p == '{') { flat_object(f, key); return; }
    if (*f->p == '[') {
        f->p++;
        int index = 0;
        for (;;) {
            flat_ws(f);
            if (*f->p == ']' || !*f->p) break;
            char full[200];
            snprintf(full, sizeof full, "%s.%d", key, index++);
            if (*f->p == '{') {  // an object in a list: its members on one line
                Json one = {0};
                Json *keep = f->out;
                f->out = &one;
                flat_object(f, "");
                f->out = keep;
                for (char *c = one.s; c && *c; c++) if (*c == '\n') *c = ' ';
                flat_line(f, full, one.s ? one.s : "");
                free(one.s);
            } else {
                Json v = {0};
                flat_scalar(f, &v);
                flat_line(f, full, v.s ? v.s : "");
                free(v.s);
            }
        }
        if (*f->p == ']') f->p++;
        return;
    }
    Json v = {0};
    flat_scalar(f, &v);
    flat_line(f, key, v.s ? v.s : "");
    free(v.s);
}
static char *reply_lines(ControlReply *r) {
    if (r->failed) return strdup(r->error ? r->error : "command failed");
    if (r->data.bad) return strdup("reply too large or out of memory");
    if (r->lines.len) return strdup(r->lines.s);
    if (!r->data.len) return strdup("ok");
    Json wrapped = {0}, out = {0};
    text(&wrapped, "{");
    append(&wrapped, r->data.s, r->data.len);
    text(&wrapped, "}");
    Flat f = {wrapped.s, &out, {0}};
    if (!wrapped.bad && wrapped.s) flat_object(&f, "");
    free(wrapped.s);
    if (out.bad || !out.s) { free(out.s); return strdup("reply too large or out of memory"); }
    return out.s;
}

// ---- the console's queue: lines in from the UI thread, results out; commands run in control_frame()
typedef struct Line { struct Line *next; char *text; ControlConsoleResult result; } Line;
static pthread_mutex_t console_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static Line *console_in, *console_in_tail, *console_out, *console_out_tail;
static int console_pending;
enum { CONSOLE_MAX_PENDING = 16, CONSOLE_MAX_LINE = 1024 };

void control_exec_line(const char *line, bool console, ControlConsoleResult *out) {
    memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);
    size_t n = strlen(line);
    char *copy = malloc(n + 1);
    char **argv = malloc((n / 2 + 2) * sizeof *argv);
    ControlReply r = {0};
    int argc = 0;
    if (!copy || !argv) control_fail(&r, "Out of memory");
    else {
        memcpy(copy, line, n + 1);
        const char *error = tokenize(copy, argv, &argc);
        if (error) control_fail(&r, "%s", error);
        else if (!argc) control_fail(&r, "Empty command");
        else execute(argc, argv, console, &r);
    }
    out->failed = r.failed || r.data.bad;
    out->exit_after = r.exit_after && !r.failed;
    out->text = reply_lines(&r);
    out->copy = r.copy; r.copy = NULL;
    reply_free(&r);
    free(argv); free(copy);
}
bool control_console_submit(const char *line) {
    while (*line == ' ' || *line == '\t') line++;
    if (!*line || strlen(line) >= CONSOLE_MAX_LINE) return false;
    Line *q = calloc(1, sizeof *q);
    if (!q) return false;
    q->text = strdup(line);
    if (!q->text) { free(q); return false; }
    pthread_mutex_lock(&console_lock);
    bool room = console_pending < CONSOLE_MAX_PENDING;
    if (room) {
        console_pending++;
        if (console_in_tail) console_in_tail->next = q; else console_in = q;
        console_in_tail = q;
    }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&console_lock);
    if (!room) { free(q->text); free(q); }
    return room;
}
static void console_pump(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&console_lock);
    Line *batch = console_in;
    console_in = console_in_tail = NULL;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&console_lock);
    while (batch) {
        Line *q = batch;
        batch = q->next;
        q->next = NULL;
        control_exec_line(q->text, true, &q->result);
        free(q->text); q->text = NULL;
        if (q->result.exit_after) { LOG("console: exit\n"); fflush(stderr); exit(0); }  // (like the window's close button, so the game's normal exit runs)
        pthread_mutex_lock(&console_lock);
        if (console_out_tail) console_out_tail->next = q; else console_out = q;
        console_out_tail = q;
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&console_lock);
    }
}
bool control_console_poll(ControlConsoleResult *out) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&console_lock);
    Line *q = console_out;
    if (q) {
        console_out = q->next;
        if (!console_out) console_out_tail = NULL;
        console_pending--;
    }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&console_lock);
    if (!q) return false;
    *out = q->result;
    free(q);
    return true;
}
void control_console_free(ControlConsoleResult *r) { free(r->text); free(r->copy); memset(r, 0, sizeof *r); }
int control_console_names(const char *prefix, const char **out, int max) {
    const ControlCmd *hit[MAX_COMMANDS];
    int n = 0;
    size_t len = strlen(prefix);
    pthread_mutex_lock(&registry_lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < command_count; i++)
        if (allowed(&commands[i], true) && !strncmp(commands[i].name, prefix, len)) hit[n++] = &commands[i];
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&registry_lock);  // (the table only grows, and names are string literals: the pointers stay valid)
    qsort(hit, (size_t)n, sizeof *hit, by_name);
    for (int i = 0; i < n && i < max; i++) out[i] = hit[i]->name;
    return n;
}

void control_frame(uint64_t frame) {
    if (!initialized) return;
    control_place_frame();
    if (dev_mode) control_game_frame(frame);
    console_pump();
    if (!queued) return;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&queue_lock);
    Request *batch = requests;
    requests = requests_tail = NULL;
    queued = false;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue_lock);
    while (batch) {
        Request *q = batch;
        batch = q->next;
        ControlReply r = {0};
        if (q->error) control_fail(&r, "%s", q->error);
        else execute(q->argc, q->argv, false, &r);
        q->reply = reply_json(&r, &q->len);
        q->exit_after = r.exit_after;
        reply_free(&r);
        pthread_mutex_lock(&queue_lock);
        push(&finished, &finished_tail, q);
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue_lock);
    }
}

static void disconnect(int slot) {
    Connection *c = &clients[slot];
    close_socket(c->socket);
    while (c->head) { Request *q = c->head; c->head = q->next; free_request(q); }
    uint64_t generation = c->generation + 1;
    memset(c, 0, sizeof *c);
    c->socket = BAD_SOCKET;
    c->generation = generation;
}
static void stop(void) { fflush(stderr); _exit(0); }
// A web page in the player's browser can send to 127.0.0.1 too: an HTTP request whose body is lines of commands
// (fetch with no-cors, a form, a WebSocket handshake). Such a connection starts with an HTTP request line; it is
// closed before any of its lines run. (The protocol's own first line is a command, never "WORD /path" or "HTTP/".)
static bool http_request(const char *line, size_t n) {
    static const char *const methods[] = {"GET ", "POST ", "PUT ", "HEAD ", "OPTIONS ", "DELETE ", "PATCH ",
                                          "CONNECT ", "TRACE "};
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof methods / sizeof *methods; i++) {
        size_t m = strlen(methods[i]);
        if (n >= m && !memcmp(line, methods[i], m)) return true;
    }
    for (size_t i = 0; i + 5 <= n; i++)
        if (!memcmp(line + i, "HTTP/", 5)) return true;
    return false;
}
static bool buffered(int slot) {
    Connection *c = &clients[slot];
    while (c->pos < c->end && c->pending < MAX_PENDING && inflight < MAX_CLIENTS * MAX_PENDING) {
        char ch = c->input[c->pos++];
        if (!c->checked && (ch == '\n' || c->used == MAX_LINE)) {
            c->checked = true;
            if (http_request(c->line, c->used)) {
                LOG("[control] closed a connection that sent an HTTP request (a web page?)\n");
                return false;
            }
        }
        if (ch == '\n') {
            if (!c->dropping && !enqueue(slot, NULL)) return false;
            c->used = 0; c->dropping = false;
        } else if (!c->dropping) {
            if (c->used == MAX_LINE) {
                if (!enqueue(slot, "line exceeds 4096 bytes")) return false;
                c->used = 0; c->dropping = true;
            } else c->line[c->used++] = ch;
        }
    }
    return true;
}
static void *serve(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    uint64_t exit_deadline = 0;
    for (;;) {
        pthread_mutex_lock(&queue_lock);
        Request *batch = finished;
        finished = finished_tail = NULL;
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&queue_lock);
        while (batch) {
            Request *q = batch;
            batch = q->next;
            Connection *c = &clients[q->client];
            if (q->exit_after && !exit_deadline) exit_deadline = plat_now_ns() + 1000000000;
            if (c->socket == BAD_SOCKET || c->generation != q->generation) { free_request(q); continue; }
            if (!q->reply || q->len > MAX_JSON - c->bytes) { int slot = q->client; free_request(q); disconnect(slot); continue; }
            c->bytes += q->len;
            push(&c->head, &c->tail, q);
        }
        // Give exit's reply a bounded chance to drain, even if its client stopped reading.
        if (exit_deadline && plat_now_ns() >= exit_deadline) stop();
        fd_set reads, writes;
        FD_ZERO(&reads); FD_ZERO(&writes);
        FD_SET(listener, &reads);
        ControlSocket high = listener;
        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
            Connection *c = &clients[i];
            if (c->socket == BAD_SOCKET) continue;
            if (!buffered(i) || (c->eof && !c->pending)) { disconnect(i); continue; }
            if (!c->eof && c->pos == c->end && c->pending < MAX_PENDING && inflight < MAX_CLIENTS * MAX_PENDING)
                FD_SET(c->socket, &reads);
            if (c->head) FD_SET(c->socket, &writes);
            if (c->socket > high) high = c->socket;
        }
        struct timeval timeout = {0, 10000};
        if (select((int)(high + 1), &reads, &writes, NULL, &timeout) < 0) continue;
        if (FD_ISSET(listener, &reads)) {
            ControlSocket s = accept(listener, NULL, NULL);
            if (s != BAD_SOCKET) {
                int slot = 0;
                while (slot < MAX_CLIENTS && clients[slot].socket != BAD_SOCKET) slot++;
                if (slot == MAX_CLIENTS || !nonblocking(s)) close_socket(s);
                else {
#ifdef SO_NOSIGPIPE
                    int on = 1;
                    if (setsockopt(s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_NOSIGPIPE, &on, sizeof on)) { close_socket(s); continue; }
#endif
                    clients[slot].socket = s;
                    // This socket was not in this select call's sets (a descriptor may have been reused).
                    FD_CLR(s, &reads); FD_CLR(s, &writes);
                }
            }
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) {
            Connection *c = &clients[i];
            if (c->socket == BAD_SOCKET) continue;
            if (FD_ISSET(c->socket, &writes)) {
                Request *q = c->head;
                int flags = 0;
#ifdef MSG_NOSIGNAL
                flags = MSG_NOSIGNAL;
#endif
                int n = (int)send(c->socket, q->reply + q->sent, (int)(q->len - q->sent), flags);
                if (n < 0 && socket_again()) continue;
                if (n <= 0) { disconnect(i); continue; }
                q->sent += (size_t)n; c->bytes -= (size_t)n;
                if (q->sent == q->len) {
                    bool exit_after = q->exit_after;
                    c->head = q->next;
                    if (!c->head) c->tail = NULL;
                    c->pending--; free_request(q);
                    if (exit_after) stop();
                }
            }
            if (FD_ISSET(c->socket, &reads)) {
                int n = (int)recv(c->socket, c->input, sizeof c->input, 0);
                if (n < 0 && socket_again()) continue;
                if (n < 0) { disconnect(i); continue; }
                if (!n) { c->eof = true; continue; }  // allow a write-half-closed client to read its replies
                c->pos = 0; c->end = (size_t)n;
                if (!buffered(i)) disconnect(i);
            }
        }
    }
    return NULL;
}

// Developer mode: the socket (SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL=<port>) or the console's developer commands alone (SAVAGEWIND_DEV=1).
static bool env_on(const char *name) { const char *v = getenv(name); return v && *v && *v != '0'; }

static bool listen_on(unsigned value) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    WSADATA wsa;
    if (WSAStartup(MAKEWORD(2, 2), &wsa)) { LOG("[control] Winsock initialization failed\n"); return false; }
#endif
    listener = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    struct sockaddr_in address = {0};
    address.sin_family = AF_INET;
    address.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK);
    address.sin_port = htons((uint16_t)value);
    bool ready = listener != BAD_SOCKET && nonblocking(listener);
    int on = 1;
#ifdef _WIN32
    // (no other program may bind the same port and take the connections meant for the game)
    if (ready) ready = setsockopt(listener, SOL_SOCKET, SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE, (const char *)&on, sizeof on) == 0;
#else
    if (ready) ready = setsockopt(listener, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &on, sizeof on) == 0;
#endif
    if (!ready || bind(listener, (struct sockaddr *)&address, sizeof address) || listen(listener, MAX_CLIENTS)) {
        LOG("[control] cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:%u\n", value);
        if (listener != BAD_SOCKET) close_socket(listener);
        listener = BAD_SOCKET;
#ifdef _WIN32
        WSACleanup();
#endif
        return false;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < MAX_CLIENTS; i++) clients[i].socket = BAD_SOCKET;
    pthread_t thread;
    if (pthread_create(&thread, NULL, serve, NULL)) {
        LOG("[control] cannot start socket thread\n");
        close_socket(listener); listener = BAD_SOCKET;
#ifdef _WIN32
        WSACleanup();
#endif
        return false;
    }
    pthread_detach(thread);
    return true;
}

void control_init(void) {
    const char *port = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL");
    unsigned value = 0;
    bool serve_socket = false;
    if (port) {
        const char *p = port;
        while (*p >= '0' && *p <= '9' && value <= 65535) value = value * 10 + (unsigned)(*p++ - '0');
        if (!*port || *p || !value || value > 65535) LOG("[control] invalid port: %s\n", port);
        else serve_socket = true;
    }
    if (serve_socket && listen_on(value)) enabled = true;
    dev_mode = enabled || env_on("SAVAGEWIND_DEV");
    static const ControlCmd builtins[] = {
        {"help", "", "List the commands", help, CONTROL_PLAYER},
        {"ping", "", "Check that the game answers", ping, 0},
        {"exit", "", "Close the game", quit, CONTROL_PLAYER},
    };
    control_register(builtins, sizeof builtins / sizeof *builtins);
    control_game_init();  // (the player safe commands always; the developer ones only in developer mode)
    initialized = true;
    if (enabled) LOG("[control] listening on 127.0.0.1:%u\n", value);
    else if (dev_mode) LOG("[control] developer commands on in the console (SAVAGEWIND_DEV)\n");
}
```

`runtime/control.h`:

```h
// Control commands: one registry of named commands that more than one front end can run. The local socket (tools/swctl.py,
// scripts, AI agents; off unless SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL=<port> is set) runs all of them; the player safe ones (CONTROL_PLAYER)
// are also what a normal start offers a player. Protocol and command list: docs/CONTROL.md.
//
// Threads: the server thread only reads lines and queues them. Every command runs in control_frame(), once per
// presented frame on the thread that presents, so a command never runs in the middle of a frame.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

typedef struct ControlReply ControlReply;  // what a command answers with (opaque; use the functions below)

// A command handler. argv[0] is the command name, argv[1..argc-1] the arguments (quotes already resolved).
// Answer with control_ok() / control_fail() (at most one; nothing counts as control_ok with no data).
typedef void (*ControlFn)(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r);

#define CONTROL_PLAYER 1u  // ControlCmd.flags: reads state or copies text, cannot break anything: any player may run it

typedef struct {
    const char *name;  // "time", "shot", ...; subcommands are plain arguments: "set hour 12" is name "set"
    const char *args;  // usage of the arguments for `help`, e.g. "<hour 0-24 | free>" ("" if none)
    const char *help;  // one line: what it does
    ControlFn fn;
    unsigned flags;    // CONTROL_PLAYER, or 0: developer mode only (writes memory or files, moves things, ends the game)
} ControlCmd;

// Register a table of commands (once, e.g. from control_game_init); the names must be unique.
void control_register(const ControlCmd *cmds, int count);

// Answers. A reply is a JSON object: control_field_*() add members to "data" (strings are escaped for you).
void control_field_str(ControlReply *r, const char *key, const char *value);
void control_field_int(ControlReply *r, const char *key, int64_t value);
void control_field_num(ControlReply *r, const char *key, double value);
void control_field_bool(ControlReply *r, const char *key, bool value);
// Front end extras, ignored by the socket (scripts read the fields): control_text() adds a line the console prints
// instead of listing the fields (when a command adds none, the console prints the fields as `key: value`);
// control_copy() is text the console puts on the clipboard (the last call wins).
void control_text(ControlReply *r, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
void control_copy(ControlReply *r, const char *text);
bool control_reply_failed(const ControlReply *r);  // has control_fail been called (a command that runs another one)
void control_fail(ControlReply *r, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));  // {"ok":false,"error":...}

// Start the server if SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL is set (does nothing otherwise). Called once at startup.
void control_init(void);
// Once per presented frame: run the queued commands. Cheap when nothing is queued.
void control_frame(uint64_t frame);

// The game's commands (state, pos, camera, time, shot, ...), registered by control_init() through this.
void control_game_init(void);
// Called by control_frame() at the start of every frame, also when no command is queued, but only when the
// endpoint is on (the game side keeps its fps average with it).
void control_game_frame(uint64_t frame);
// Called by control_frame() every frame: Link's place into savagewind.log every 30 s while he moves ("[place] swr:1 ...").
void control_place_frame(void);

// Live input hook: frame publication on the presenter; apply may run on guest threads.
// A NULL lx requests buttons only. Otherwise all four axis pointers must be valid.
void control_input_frame(uint64_t frame);
bool control_enabled(void);      // developer mode (SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL=<port> or SAVAGEWIND_DEV=1): the commands that are not player safe
bool control_endpoint_on(void);  // is the socket server listening (SAVAGEWIND_CONTROL)?
void control_fly_wheel(float notches);  // mouse wheel while flying: faster / slower
bool control_fly_toggle(void);   // fly mode on/off (the hotkey, bound as bind_key_fly); false when it could not turn on
void control_input_apply(uint64_t *buttons, int32_t *lx, int32_t *ly, int32_t *rx, int32_t *ry);

// ---- a front end that is not the socket (the in-game console): lines go in from its thread, run in control_frame()
typedef struct {
    char *text;     // what to print: lines separated by \n, no trailing newline (malloc; free with control_console_free)
    char *copy;     // for the clipboard, or NULL (malloc)
    bool failed;
    bool exit_after;  // the command was `exit`: the console front end ends the game
} ControlConsoleResult;

bool control_console_submit(const char *line);          // queue a line (any thread); false: queue full or empty
bool control_console_poll(ControlConsoleResult *out);   // next finished result, in order (any thread); false: none
void control_console_free(ControlConsoleResult *r);
// Names of the commands the console may run that start with `prefix`, sorted; returns the count and copies up to
// `max` pointers (valid for the life of the process).
int control_console_names(const char *prefix, const char **out, int max);
// For tests and `report`: run a line now on the calling thread, with the console's rights. Not for other threads.
void control_exec_line(const char *line, bool console, ControlConsoleResult *out);
```

`runtime/control_cells.c`:

```c
// Named game state cells (control_cells.h) and the `cell` command (developer only).
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "control.h"
#include "control_cells.h"
#include "control_mem.h"
#include "game_sites.h"

static uint64_t root_object(const ControlCell *c) {
    uint64_t site = *(const uint64_t *)((const char *)&g_site + c->root);
    uint64_t obj = 0;
    return site && control_mem_peek(site, &obj, sizeof obj) ? obj : 0;
}
static size_t elem_size(CellType t) { (void)t; return 4; }  // (all three types are 32 bits)

uint64_t control_cell_addr(const ControlCell *c) {
    uint64_t root = root_object(c);
    if (!root) return 0;
    size_t sz = elem_size(c->type) * (size_t)c->count;
    for (int k = 0; k < c->nchains; k++) {
        const CellChain *ch = &c->chains[k];
        uint64_t p = root;
        int i = 0;
        for (; i + 1 < ch->len; i++)
            if (!control_mem_peek(p + ch->off[i], &p, sizeof p) || p < 0x10000) break;
        if (i + 1 < ch->len) continue;
        p += ch->off[ch->len - 1];
        uint8_t v[16];
        if (!control_mem_peek(p, v, sz)) continue;
        if (!c->check || c->check(v)) return p;
    }
    return 0;
}

bool control_cell_get(const ControlCell *c, double *out) {
    uint64_t a = control_cell_addr(c);
    uint8_t v[16];
    if (!a || !control_mem_peek(a, v, elem_size(c->type) * (size_t)c->count)) return false;
    for (int i = 0; i < c->count; i++) {
        switch (c->type) {
        case CELL_F32: { float f; memcpy(&f, v + 4 * i, 4); out[i] = f; break; }
        case CELL_U32: { uint32_t u; memcpy(&u, v + 4 * i, 4); out[i] = u; break; }
        case CELL_S32: { int32_t s; memcpy(&s, v + 4 * i, 4); out[i] = s; break; }
        }
    }
    return true;
}

bool control_cell_camera_angles(double e[3], double t[3], double *yaw, double *pitch) {
    double p[1];
    if (!control_cell_get(&control_cell_camera_eye, e) || !control_cell_get(&control_cell_camera_target, t) ||
        !control_cell_get(&control_cell_camera_pitch, p)) return false;
    double dx = t[0] - e[0], dy = t[1] - e[1], dz = t[2] - e[2];
    if (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz < 1e-12) return false;
    *yaw = atan2(dx, dz) * 57.29577951308232;
    *pitch = -p[0];
    return true;
}

bool control_cell_set(const ControlCell *c, const double *in) {
    uint64_t a = control_cell_addr(c);
    uint8_t v[16];
    if (!a) return false;
    for (int i = 0; i < c->count; i++) {
        switch (c->type) {
        case CELL_F32: { float f = (float)in[i]; memcpy(v + 4 * i, &f, 4); break; }
        case CELL_U32: { uint32_t u = (uint32_t)in[i]; memcpy(v + 4 * i, &u, 4); break; }
        case CELL_S32: { int32_t s = (int32_t)in[i]; memcpy(v + 4 * i, &s, 4); break; }
        }
    }
    return control_mem_poke(a, v, elem_size(c->type) * (size_t)c->count);
}

// ---- the cells

// Link's position: the copy at PlayerInfo +0x88 is what the game rewrites each frame, so a chain is accepted only if it
// ends on a vec3 within a metre (x and z) of that copy. Primary chain first; the other two reach the same object through
// an array whose slot moved by 8 between boots (found with mem path, 1.9.0).
static bool pos_check(const void *value) {
    uint64_t pinfo = g_site.player_info ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)g_site.player_info : 0;
    if (!pinfo) return false;
    const float *pp = (const float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x88), *v = value;
    return fabsf(v[0] - pp[0]) <= 1.0f && fabsf(v[2] - pp[2]) <= 1.0f;
}
static const CellChain pos_chains[] = {
    {5, {0x60, 0x578, 0x80, 0x410, 0x1c0}},
    {5, {0x10, 0xe8, 0x750, 0x78, 0x1c0}},
    {5, {0x10, 0xe8, 0x758, 0x78, 0x1c0}},
};
const ControlCell control_cell_player_pos = {
    "player.pos", "Link's real position x y z (what `teleport` writes)", offsetof(GameSites, player_info), CELL_F32, 3,
    pos_chains, (int)(sizeof pos_chains / sizeof *pos_chains), pos_check,
};

// Fall damage: the game keeps the highest point Link reached since he left the ground and, on landing, takes the drop from
// there. It lives in two copies on the player object (found by flying up, then down, and reading which slots follow the
// peak and not the current height, 1.9.0). A reading is accepted when it is not below Link's own height (the copy at
// PlayerInfo +0x8c) and not absurdly above it.
static bool fall_check(const void *value) {
    uint64_t pinfo = g_site.player_info ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)g_site.player_info : 0;
    if (!pinfo) return false;
    float py = *(const float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x8c), v = *(const float *)value;
    return isfinite(v) && v >= py - 2.0f && v <= py + 20000.0f;
}
static const CellChain fall_top_chains[] = {{2, {0x60, 0x860}}};
static const CellChain fall_top2_chains[] = {{2, {0x60, 0x20d0}}};
const ControlCell control_cell_player_fall_top = {
    "player.fall_top", "highest y since Link left the ground (fall damage is the drop from it)", offsetof(GameSites, player_info), CELL_F32, 1,
    fall_top_chains, 1, fall_check,
};
const ControlCell control_cell_player_fall_top2 = {
    "player.fall_top2", "second copy of player.fall_top (the game keeps both)", offsetof(GameSites, player_info), CELL_F32, 1,
    fall_top2_chains, 1, fall_check,
};

// The orbit camera behind Link (found by rotating candidate eye positions around him and watching the camera, 1.9.0).
// One object holds eye (x y z), target (x y z, a little above Link), up, fov, near and far; the game keeps the eye as
// state, not as a copy: moving it around the target turns the camera, and it stays there. The pitch is a separate float
// (minus the pitch in degrees, positive = looking down) a few objects further on. Yaw has no cell of its own: it is the
// direction of eye -> target. Both chains start at the same two objects (PlayerInfo +0x60 -> +0x2b8, or the twin through
// +0x328) and were found with mem path. A reading is accepted when it is near Link's own position copy.
static bool near_link(const float *v, float within) {
    uint64_t pinfo = g_site.player_info ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)g_site.player_info : 0;
    if (!pinfo) return false;
    const float *pp = (const float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x88);
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) if (!isfinite(v[i])) return false;
    float dx = v[0] - pp[0], dy = v[1] - pp[1], dz = v[2] - pp[2];
    return dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz <= within * within;
}
static bool eye_check(const void *value) { return near_link(value, 300.0f); }
static bool target_check(const void *value) { return near_link(value, 20.0f); }
static bool pitch_check(const void *value) { float v = *(const float *)value; return isfinite(v) && fabsf(v) <= 90.01f; }
static const CellChain eye_chains[] = {{3, {0x60, 0x2b8, 0x5b0}}, {3, {0x60, 0x328, 0x540}}};
static const CellChain target_chains[] = {{3, {0x60, 0x2b8, 0x5bc}}, {3, {0x60, 0x328, 0x54c}}};
static const CellChain pitch_chains[] = {{4, {0x60, 0x2b8, 0x2a8, 0xd14}}, {4, {0x60, 0x328, 0x238, 0xd14}}};
const ControlCell control_cell_camera_eye = {
    "camera.eye", "the camera's position x y z (move it around camera.target to turn the camera)", offsetof(GameSites, player_info), CELL_F32, 3,
    eye_chains, 2, eye_check,
};
const ControlCell control_cell_camera_target = {
    "camera.target", "the point the camera looks at x y z (a little above Link)", offsetof(GameSites, player_info), CELL_F32, 3,
    target_chains, 2, target_check,
};
const ControlCell control_cell_camera_pitch = {
    "camera.pitch", "minus the camera pitch in degrees (positive looks down; the game clamps it to +-89)", offsetof(GameSites, player_info), CELL_F32, 1,
    pitch_chains, 2, pitch_check,
};

static const ControlCell *const all_cells[] = {&control_cell_player_pos, &control_cell_player_fall_top, &control_cell_player_fall_top2,
                                               &control_cell_camera_eye, &control_cell_camera_target, &control_cell_camera_pitch};

const ControlCell *control_cell_find(const char *name) {
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof all_cells / sizeof *all_cells; i++)
        if (!strcmp(all_cells[i]->name, name)) return all_cells[i];
    return NULL;
}

// cell | cell <name> | cell <name> <v> [<v>...]
static void cmd_cell(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    if (argc == 1) {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof all_cells / sizeof *all_cells; i++) {
            const ControlCell *c = all_cells[i];
            control_field_str(r, c->name, c->what);
        }
        return;
    }
    const ControlCell *c = control_cell_find(argv[1]);
    if (!c) { control_fail(r, "Unknown cell: %s", argv[1]); return; }
    if (argc > 2) {
        if (argc - 2 != c->count) { control_fail(r, "%s needs %d value(s)", c->name, c->count); return; }
        double v[4];
        for (int i = 0; i < c->count; i++) {
            char *end;
            v[i] = strtod(argv[2 + i], &end);
            if (end == argv[2 + i] || *end || !isfinite(v[i])) { control_fail(r, "Not a number: \"%s\"", argv[2 + i]); return; }
        }
        if (!control_cell_set(c, v)) { control_fail(r, "Cannot write %s", c->name); return; }
    }
    double v[4];
    if (!control_cell_get(c, v)) { control_fail(r, "%s not found", c->name); return; }
    char a[32];
    snprintf(a, sizeof a, "0x%llx", (unsigned long long)control_cell_addr(c));
    control_field_str(r, "address", a);
    for (int i = 0; i < c->count; i++) {
        char k[16];
        snprintf(k, sizeof k, "v%d", i);
        control_field_num(r, k, v[i]);
    }
}

// sites: the game's known root addresses (game_sites.h) and the pointer stored at each, the starting points for mem path
static void cmd_sites(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argv;
    if (argc != 1) { control_fail(r, "Usage: sites"); return; }
#define SITE(n)                                                                                                      \
    do {                                                                                                             \
        char a[32], k[48];                                                                                           \
        uint64_t v = 0;                                                                                              \
        snprintf(k, sizeof k, "%s", #n);                                                                             \
        snprintf(a, sizeof a, "0x%llx", (unsigned long long)g_site.n);                                               \
        control_field_str(r, k, a);                                                                                  \
        if (g_site.n && control_mem_peek(g_site.n, &v, sizeof v)) {                                                  \
            snprintf(k, sizeof k, "%s.value", #n);                                                                   \
            snprintf(a, sizeof a, "0x%llx", (unsigned long long)v);                                                  \
            control_field_str(r, k, a);                                                                              \
        }                                                                                                            \
    } while (0);
    GAME_SITES(SITE)
#undef SITE
}

void control_cells_init(void) {
    static const ControlCmd cmds[] = {
        {"cell", "[<name> [<value>...]]", "List, read or write a named game state cell", cmd_cell},
        {"sites", "", "Known root addresses and their values", cmd_sites},
    };
    control_register(cmds, (int)(sizeof cmds / sizeof *cmds));
}
```
