`runtime/control_cells.h`:

```h
// Named game state cells for the control endpoint: values the game keeps in memory (Link's
// position, later the weather, the time, ...) that a command reads or writes. Heap addresses move between runs, object
// layouts do not, so a cell is not an address but a recipe: a root object, one or more pointer chains found once with
// `mem path` (docs/CONTROL.md), and a check that tells a chain that lands on the right value from one that lands on a
// stale slot. Add a cell: write its entry in control_cells.c, nothing else.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

typedef enum { CELL_F32, CELL_U32, CELL_S32 } CellType;
#define CELL_DEPTH 8

typedef struct {
    int len;                   // how many offsets
    uint32_t off[CELL_DEPTH];  // read the pointer at root+off[0], then at that+off[1], ...; the last offset is added, not read
} CellChain;

typedef struct {
    const char *name;          // "player.pos"
    const char *what;          // one line for `cell list`
    size_t root;               // offsetof(GameSites, ...): the game site that holds a pointer to the root object
    CellType type;
    int count;                 // elements of that type in a row (3: a vec3), at most 4
    const CellChain *chains;   // tried in order; the first one whose value passes `check` wins
    int nchains;
    bool (*check)(const void *value);  // does this value look right (compared to a reading we trust)? NULL: any pointer chain that ends in mapped memory
} ControlCell;

// Where the cell is right now: its address, or 0 when no chain resolves (the object does not exist yet, or another game version)
uint64_t control_cell_addr(const ControlCell *c);
// Read / write the cell (count elements as doubles); false when it does not resolve or the memory is not accessible
bool control_cell_get(const ControlCell *c, double *v);
bool control_cell_set(const ControlCell *c, const double *v);
const ControlCell *control_cell_find(const char *name);

// The cells themselves
extern const ControlCell control_cell_player_pos;  // Link's real position (x y z); `pos` reads a copy the game rewrites every frame
extern const ControlCell control_cell_camera_eye, control_cell_camera_target, control_cell_camera_pitch;  // the orbit camera; yaw is the direction eye -> target
extern const ControlCell control_cell_player_fall_top, control_cell_player_fall_top2;  // highest y since he left the ground (two copies); fall damage is the drop from it

// Read the stored orbit camera, in any AA mode. Yaw 0 looks along +z, 90 along +x; pitch positive looks up.
bool control_cell_camera_angles(double eye[3], double target[3], double *yaw, double *pitch);

```

`runtime/control_fly.c`:

```c
// (test and development only) Fly mode for the control endpoint (docs/CONTROL.md): Link floats and goes where the
// controls point, through anything, so a spot anywhere on the map can be reached and looked at without walking.
//
// How: while it is on, the left stick, the up / down buttons (X and B: Space and Left Shift by default) and the boost
// (left stick press, Left Ctrl) are taken out of the game's input (control_fly_input, called where the game combines
// keyboard, gamepad and scripted input, so all three work) and, once per presented frame, turned into a step that is
// written to Link's real position (the player.pos cell, control_cells.c). The step follows the camera, read from the
// renderer's view matrix, or the stored orbit camera when unavailable, like `camera`: forward / back along where it looks (mode look) or along the
// ground (mode level), left / right along the ground, up / down straight along y.
//
// The position written is our own running value, not re-read from the game, so gravity or a push the game applies
// between two frames never builds up. If the game moves Link a long way on its own (a load, a teleport, a death) the
// running value is dropped and taken from the game again. Flying counts as falling to the game, whose fall damage is the
// drop from the highest point since Link left the ground, so that highest point (player.fall_top) is kept at his height.
#include <math.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "control.h"
#include "control_cells.h"
#include "rt.h"

bool control_camera_view(float view[12]);  // runtime/nvn/*

static _Atomic bool on;
static _Atomic int32_t in_x, in_y;       // left stick as the game would have seen it (-32767..32767)
static _Atomic bool in_up, in_down, in_boost;
static bool level;                       // mode: false look, true level
#define SPRINT_SPEED 8.0                 // Link's sprint, units per second: an assumption from memory, NOT measured
#define DEFAULT_SPEED (1.75 * SPRINT_SPEED)  // every entry starts here (units are about metres, at full stick); the mouse wheel changes it while flying
#define MIN_SPEED 1.0
#define MAX_SPEED 2000.0
#define WHEEL_STEP 1.2                   // one wheel notch multiplies the speed by this
static _Atomic double speed = DEFAULT_SPEED;
#define BOOST 6.0
#define RESYNC_DIST 25.0                 // the game moved Link this far on its own: take its value again
static double fp[3];
static uint64_t last_ns;

// Button bits as numbered in control_input.c (names[]).
#define BIT_B 1
#define BIT_X 2
#define BIT_LSTICK 4

// Called where the game's input is assembled (control_input_apply). lx, ly are NULL when only buttons are asked for.
void control_fly_input(uint64_t *b, int32_t *lx, int32_t *ly) {
    if (!atomic_load_explicit(&on, memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    atomic_store(&in_up, (*b >> BIT_X) & 1);
    atomic_store(&in_down, (*b >> BIT_B) & 1);
    atomic_store(&in_boost, (*b >> BIT_LSTICK) & 1);
    *b &= ~((1ull << BIT_X) | (1ull << BIT_B) | (1ull << BIT_LSTICK));
    if (lx) {
        atomic_store(&in_x, *lx); atomic_store(&in_y, *ly);
        *lx = 0; *ly = 0;
    }
}

static void norm(double v[3]) {
    double l = sqrt(v[0] * v[0] + v[1] * v[1] + v[2] * v[2]);
    if (l > 1e-6) { v[0] /= l; v[1] /= l; v[2] /= l; }
}

void control_fly_frame(uint64_t frame) {
    (void)frame;
    if (!atomic_load_explicit(&on, memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    uint64_t now = plat_now_ns();
    double dt = last_ns ? (double)(now - last_ns) / 1e9 : 0;
    last_ns = now;
    if (dt > 0.1) dt = 0.1;  // (a stall must not become a jump)
    double cur[3];
    if (!control_cell_get(&control_cell_player_pos, cur)) return;  // (Link is loading: wait)
    if (!(fabs(cur[0] - fp[0]) + fabs(cur[2] - fp[2]) < RESYNC_DIST) || fabs(cur[1] - fp[1]) > 200) memcpy(fp, cur, sizeof fp);
    float v[12];
    double fwd[3], right[3];
    if (control_camera_view(v)) {
        // camera basis in world space: the rows of the view matrix are right, up and backwards
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) fwd[i] = -v[8 + i];
        right[0] = v[0]; right[1] = 0; right[2] = v[2];
        if (level) {
            fwd[1] = 0;
            if (fwd[0] * fwd[0] + fwd[2] * fwd[2] < 1e-6) { fwd[0] = v[4]; fwd[2] = v[6]; }  // looking straight up or down: the camera's up points ahead
        }
    } else {
        double eye[3], target[3], yaw, pitch;
        if (!control_cell_camera_angles(eye, target, &yaw, &pitch)) return;
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) fwd[i] = target[i] - eye[i];
        double rad = yaw / 57.29577951308232;
        right[0] = -cos(rad); right[1] = 0; right[2] = sin(rad);
        if (level) fwd[1] = 0;
    }
    norm(fwd); norm(right);
    double sx = atomic_load(&in_x) / 32767.0, sy = atomic_load(&in_y) / 32767.0;
    double m = hypot(sx, sy);
    if (m > 1) { sx /= m; sy /= m; }
    double vy = (atomic_load(&in_up) ? 1.0 : 0.0) - (atomic_load(&in_down) ? 1.0 : 0.0);
    double k = atomic_load(&speed) * (atomic_load(&in_boost) ? BOOST : 1.0) * dt;
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) fp[i] += k * (sy * fwd[i] + sx * right[i]);
    fp[1] += k * vy;
    control_cell_set(&control_cell_player_pos, fp);
    // Fall damage is the drop from the highest point since Link left the ground; flying counts as falling, so land from a
    // long flight and the game sees a 100 m fall. Keep that highest point at his height: landing while flying costs nothing.
    control_cell_set(&control_cell_player_fall_top, &fp[1]);
    control_cell_set(&control_cell_player_fall_top2, &fp[1]);
}

// The hotkey and the `fly` command both come here. Returns the new state; false (and on stays off) when Link is not there.
bool control_fly_set(bool want) {
    if (want == atomic_load(&on)) return want;
    if (want) {
        if (!control_cell_get(&control_cell_player_pos, fp)) {
            LOG("[control] fly mode: not started, Link has no position yet (title screen or loading)\n");
            return false;
        }
        last_ns = 0;
        atomic_store(&speed, DEFAULT_SPEED);  // (every entry starts at the normal speed)
        atomic_store(&in_x, 0); atomic_store(&in_y, 0);
        atomic_store(&in_up, false); atomic_store(&in_down, false); atomic_store(&in_boost, false);
        LOG("[control] fly mode: on at %.1f %.1f %.1f, speed %g, mode %s\n", fp[0], fp[1], fp[2], DEFAULT_SPEED, level ? "level" : "look");
    } else {
        LOG("[control] fly mode: off (speed was %g)\n", atomic_load(&speed));
    }
    atomic_store(&on, want);
    return want;
}
// The mouse wheel (runtime/hle/input.c): up is faster, down slower, each notch a fixed ratio, so it works the same from 1 to 2000.
void control_fly_wheel(float notches) {
    if (!atomic_load(&on)) return;
    double s = atomic_load(&speed) * pow(WHEEL_STEP, notches);
    atomic_store(&speed, s < MIN_SPEED ? MIN_SPEED : s > MAX_SPEED ? MAX_SPEED : s);
}
bool control_fly_toggle(void) { return control_fly_set(!atomic_load(&on)); }

static void fields(ControlReply *r) {
    control_field_bool(r, "fly", atomic_load(&on));
    control_field_str(r, "mode", level ? "level" : "look");
    control_field_num(r, "speed", atomic_load(&speed));
}

// fly | fly on | fly off | fly toggle | fly mode look|level | fly speed <units per second>
static void cmd_fly(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    if (argc == 1) { fields(r); return; }
    if (argc == 2 && (!strcmp(argv[1], "on") || !strcmp(argv[1], "off") || !strcmp(argv[1], "toggle"))) {
        bool want = !strcmp(argv[1], "toggle") ? !atomic_load(&on) : !strcmp(argv[1], "on");
        if (control_fly_set(want) != want) { control_fail(r, "No world loaded"); return; }
        fields(r); return;
    }
    if (argc == 3 && !strcmp(argv[1], "mode") && (!strcmp(argv[2], "look") || !strcmp(argv[2], "level"))) {
        level = !strcmp(argv[2], "level"); fields(r); return;
    }
    if (argc == 3 && !strcmp(argv[1], "speed")) {
        char *end; double s = strtod(argv[2], &end);
        if (end == argv[2] || *end || !isfinite(s) || s <= 0 || s > MAX_SPEED) { control_fail(r, "Speed must be above 0 and at most 2000"); return; }
        atomic_store(&speed, s < MIN_SPEED ? MIN_SPEED : s); fields(r); return;
    }
    control_fail(r, "Usage: fly [on | off | toggle | mode look|level | speed <n>]");
}

void control_fly_init(void) {
    static const ControlCmd cmds[] = {
        {"fly", "[on|off|toggle | mode look|level | speed <n>]",
         "Free flight: left stick moves along the camera, X and B move up and down, left stick press boosts", cmd_fly},
    };
    control_register(cmds, (int)(sizeof cmds / sizeof *cmds));
}

```

`runtime/control_game.c`:

```c
// The game's commands of the control endpoint (runtime/control.h, docs/CONTROL.md): the player safe ones (state, pos,
// camera, version, report) and the developer ones (time, shot, goto). Add a command here by writing a handler and putting it in the table at the bottom.
#include <errno.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#include "control.h"
#include "control_cells.h"
#include "control_places.h"
#include "discord_rpc.h"
#include "game_place.h"
#include "language.h"
#include "perfmon.h"
#include "rt.h"
#include "game_sites.h"

uint64_t renderer_present_count(void);  // presented frames (the backend)
bool control_camera_view(float view[12]);  // the world camera's view matrix (the backend; false: none)
bool control_shot_now(const char *path);  // the image of the frame being presented -> PNG (the backend; false: can't)
void test_warp_set_hour(float hour);  // runtime/services/test_warp.c
void test_warp_hold_hour(float hour);
float test_warp_hour(bool *held);

// ---- fps over the last second, kept every frame
#define FPS_WINDOW_NS 1000000000ull
static uint64_t win_start_ns, win_start_frame;
static double fps_now = -1;
static uint64_t boot_ns;

void control_prof_frame(uint64_t frame);  // runtime/control_prof.c
void control_tp_frame(uint64_t frame);    // runtime/control_tp.c

void control_game_frame(uint64_t frame) {
    if (control_enabled()) {  // (the profiler and teleport are developer mode only)
        control_prof_frame(frame);
        control_tp_frame(frame);
    }
    uint64_t now = plat_now_ns();
    if (!boot_ns) boot_ns = now;
    if (!win_start_ns) { win_start_ns = now; win_start_frame = frame; return; }
    if (now - win_start_ns >= FPS_WINDOW_NS) {
        fps_now = (double)(frame - win_start_frame) * 1e9 / (double)(now - win_start_ns);
        win_start_ns = now;
        win_start_frame = frame;
    }
}

// ---- state: frame number, uptime, fps over the last second, hour of day
static void cmd_state(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argc; (void)argv;
    control_field_int(r, "frame", (int64_t)renderer_present_count());
    control_field_num(r, "uptime_s", boot_ns ? (double)(plat_now_ns() - boot_ns) / 1e9 : 0);
    if (fps_now >= 0) control_field_num(r, "fps", fps_now);
    bool held = false;
    float hour = test_warp_hour(&held);
    if (hour >= 0) control_field_num(r, "hour", hour);  // (left out before the world exists)
    control_field_bool(r, "hour_held", held);
}

// ---- time [freeze | unfreeze | set <0-24> | <0-24>]: with no argument just the hour; a bare number is the same as set
static void cmd_time(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    static const char *usage = "Usage: time [freeze | unfreeze | set <0-24> | <0-24>]";
    bool set = argc == 3 && !strcmp(argv[1], "set");
    if (argc > 3 || (argc == 3 && !set)) { control_fail(r, "%s", usage); return; }
    if (argc == 2 && (!strcmp(argv[1], "unfreeze") || !strcmp(argv[1], "free"))) {
        test_warp_hold_hour(-1);
    } else if (argc == 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "freeze")) {
        float hour = test_warp_hour(NULL);
        if (hour < 0) { control_fail(r, "No world loaded"); return; }
        test_warp_hold_hour(hour);
    } else if (argc >= 2) {
        const char *arg = argv[argc - 1];  // time <hour> or time set <hour>
        char *end;
        errno = 0;
        double h = strtod(arg, &end);
        if (set && !*arg) { control_fail(r, "%s", usage); return; }
        if (end == arg || *end || errno || !(h >= 0 && h <= 24)) {  // (also rejects nan)
            control_fail(r, "%s", usage);
            return;
        }
        test_warp_set_hour((float)h);
    }
    bool held = false;
    float hour = test_warp_hour(&held);
    if (hour >= 0) control_field_num(r, "hour", hour);
    control_field_bool(r, "hour_held", held);
}

// ---- pos: Link's position (x y z) and stamina (uking::act::PlayerInfo +0x88 / +0xa4, as the clock probe in framepace.c reads them)
static uint64_t player_info(void) { return g_site.player_info ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)g_site.player_info : 0; }

bool control_camera_angles(double *yaw, double *pitch);

// The line `pos` puts on the clipboard and `goto` reads back, so a place travels through an issue:
//   swr:1 x=-1234.56 y=250.00 z=789.01 yaw=90.0 pitch=-10.0 hour=18.50
// (yaw and pitch work in any AA mode; the hour needs the world). x y z are Link's position.
static void place_string(char *buf, size_t n, const float p[3]) {
    int len = snprintf(buf, n, "swr:1 x=%.2f y=%.2f z=%.2f", p[0], p[1], p[2]);
    double yaw, pitch;
    if (len > 0 && (size_t)len < n && control_camera_angles(&yaw, &pitch)) len += snprintf(buf + len, n - (size_t)len, " yaw=%.1f pitch=%.1f", yaw, pitch);
    float hour = test_warp_hour(NULL);
    if (len > 0 && (size_t)len < n && hour >= 0) snprintf(buf + len, n - (size_t)len, " hour=%.2f", hour);
}

// Link's position, false before there is a Link in the world: no object yet, or one that still reads 0 0 0 (the title
// screen has the object but not a place; nobody stands at exactly 0 0 0).
static bool link_position(float p[3]) {
    uint64_t pinfo = player_info();
    if (!pinfo) return false;
    p[0] = *(float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x88); p[1] = *(float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x8c); p[2] = *(float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x90);
    return p[0] != 0 || p[1] != 0 || p[2] != 0;
}

// The place in savagewind.log: the `pos` line every PLACE_LOG_NS while Link moves (no line while he stands still: the
// last one still says where), so a report's log says where its bug happened and `goto` takes the line back.
// SAVAGEWIND_PLACE_LOG=0: no lines.
#define PLACE_LOG_NS 30000000000ull
#define PRESENCE_NS 5000000000ull
// The text's language: SAVAGEWIND_DISCORD_LANG (en, es, or a game language's folder), or the game's. Discord doesn't tell
// its own to a local program.
static const char *presence_language(void) {
    const char *lang = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_DISCORD_LANG"), *code = language_text_code();
    if (lang && *lang) return lang;
    for (int i = 1; i < g_ntext_languages; i++)
        if (!strcmp(code, g_text_languages[i].code)) return g_text_languages[i].folder;
    return "USen";
}

static void presence_frame(void) {
    static uint64_t last_ns;
    uint64_t now = plat_now_ns();
    if (last_ns && now - last_ns < PRESENCE_NS) return;
    last_ns = now;
    game_place_set_language(presence_language());  // (each time: the options can change the game's language while it runs)
    float p[3] = {0};
    bool has_link = link_position(p);
    char details[128], state[128];
    if (game_place_text(p[0], p[2], has_link, details, sizeof details, state, sizeof state)) discord_rpc_set(details, state);
}

void control_place_frame(void) {
    presence_frame();
    static int on = -1;
    static uint64_t last_ns;
    static float last[3];
    if (on < 0) on = !getenv("SAVAGEWIND_PLACE_LOG") || atoi(getenv("SAVAGEWIND_PLACE_LOG")) != 0;
    if (!on) return;
    uint64_t now = plat_now_ns();
    if (last_ns && now - last_ns < PLACE_LOG_NS) return;
    float p[3];
    if (!link_position(p)) return;
    last_ns = now;
    float dx = p[0] - last[0], dy = p[1] - last[1], dz = p[2] - last[2];
    if (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz < 1.0f) return;
    memcpy(last, p, sizeof last);
    char place[160];
    place_string(place, sizeof place, p);
    LOG("[place] %s\n", place);
}

static void cmd_pos(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argv;
    if (argc != 1) { control_fail(r, "Usage: pos"); return; }
    uint64_t pinfo = player_info();
    float p[3];
    if (!link_position(p)) { control_fail(r, "No world loaded"); return; }
    control_field_num(r, "x", p[0]);
    control_field_num(r, "y", p[1]);
    control_field_num(r, "z", p[2]);
    control_field_num(r, "stamina", *(float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0xa4));
    char a[32]; snprintf(a, sizeof a, "0x%llx", (unsigned long long)pinfo);
    control_field_str(r, "player_info", a);  // (the object, for finding pointer paths with mem read)
    char place[160];
    place_string(place, sizeof place, p);
    control_field_str(r, "place", place);
    control_text(r, "%s", place);
    control_copy(r, place);
}

// ---- camera: prefer the last finished frame's view matrix, then the game's stored orbit camera in any AA mode.
// view = [R | t]: a world point p is R*p + t in camera space; the rows of R are right, up and backwards in world space.
static bool camera_read(double eye[3], double fwd[3], double *yaw, double *pitch) {
    float v[12];
    if (!control_camera_view(v)) {
        double target[3];
        if (!control_cell_camera_angles(eye, target, yaw, pitch)) return false;
        double len = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { fwd[i] = target[i] - eye[i]; len += fwd[i] * fwd[i]; }
        len = sqrt(len);
        for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) fwd[i] /= len;
        return true;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) fwd[i] = -v[8 + i];
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) eye[i] = -(v[0 + i] * v[3] + v[4 + i] * v[7] + v[8 + i] * v[11]);
    const double deg = 57.29577951308232;
    *yaw = atan2(fwd[0], fwd[2]) * deg;
    *pitch = asin(fwd[1] < -1 ? -1 : fwd[1] > 1 ? 1 : fwd[1]) * deg;
    return true;
}

static void cmd_camera(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argv;
    if (argc != 1) { control_fail(r, "Usage: camera"); return; }
    double eye[3], fwd[3], yaw, pitch;
    if (!camera_read(eye, fwd, &yaw, &pitch)) { control_fail(r, "No world loaded"); return; }
    control_field_num(r, "x", eye[0]); control_field_num(r, "y", eye[1]); control_field_num(r, "z", eye[2]);
    control_field_num(r, "dx", fwd[0]); control_field_num(r, "dy", fwd[1]); control_field_num(r, "dz", fwd[2]);
    control_field_num(r, "yaw", yaw);
    control_field_num(r, "pitch", pitch);
}

// yaw and pitch in degrees (yaw 0 looks along +z and 90 along +x, pitch positive looks up); false when neither source exists.
bool control_camera_angles(double *yaw, double *pitch) {
    double eye[3], fwd[3];
    return camera_read(eye, fwd, yaw, pitch);
}

// ---- shot <file>: a PNG of the frame being presented (written before the reply)
// Only a .png inside the game's folder: a relative path without "..", so a command can neither write nor delete a
// file anywhere else.
static bool shot_path_ok(const char *p) {
    size_t n = strlen(p);
    if (n < 5 || n > 260 || strcmp(p + n - 4, ".png") || p[0] == '/' || p[0] == '\\' || strchr(p, ':')) return false;
    for (const char *q = p; *q; q++) {
        if ((unsigned char)*q < 0x20) return false;
        bool start = q == p || q[-1] == '/' || q[-1] == '\\';
        if (start && q[0] == '.' && q[1] == '.' && (!q[2] || q[2] == '/' || q[2] == '\\')) return false;
    }
    return true;
}
static void cmd_shot(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    if (argc != 2) { control_fail(r, "Usage: shot <file>"); return; }
    if (!shot_path_ok(argv[1])) {
        control_fail(r, "The file must be a .png in the game's folder (a relative path without \"..\")");
        return;
    }
    remove(argv[1]);  // (so a failed save can't pass for a new file)
    if (!control_shot_now(argv[1])) { control_fail(r, "No image available"); return; }
    struct stat st;
    if (stat(argv[1], &st) || st.st_size <= 0) { control_fail(r, "Cannot write \"%s\"", argv[1]); return; }
    control_field_str(r, "path", argv[1]);
    control_field_int(r, "bytes", (int64_t)st.st_size);
    control_field_int(r, "frame", (int64_t)renderer_present_count());
}

// ---- version / report: what to paste into an issue
static const char *os_name(void) {
#if defined(_WIN32)
    return "Windows";
#elif defined(__APPLE__)
    return "macOS";
#else
    return "Linux";
#endif
}
static const char *arch_name(void) {
#if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(_M_X64)
    return "x86-64";
#elif defined(__aarch64__) || defined(_M_ARM64)
    return "arm64";
#else
    return "unknown";
#endif
}
const char *rt_version(void);  // runtime/ui/launcher.mm

static void cmd_version(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argv;
    if (argc != 1) { control_fail(r, "Usage: version"); return; }
    control_field_str(r, "version", rt_version());
    control_field_str(r, "os", os_name());
    control_field_str(r, "arch", arch_name());
    control_text(r, "Savage Wind %s (%s %s)", rt_version(), os_name(), arch_name());
}

// report: one block for an issue (also copied): version, machine, the place, how it runs, every setting.
static void cmd_report(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argv;
    if (argc != 1) { control_fail(r, "Usage: report"); return; }
    char block[4096];
    size_t n = 0;
#define ADD(...) do { if (n < sizeof block) { int w = snprintf(block + n, sizeof block - n, __VA_ARGS__); if (w > 0) n += (size_t)w < sizeof block - n ? (size_t)w : sizeof block - n - 1; } } while (0)
    ADD("Savage Wind %s (%s %s)\n", rt_version(), os_name(), arch_name());
    PerfStats ps;
    perfmon_snapshot(&ps);
    if (ps.gpu_name[0] || ps.cpu_name[0]) ADD("GPU: %s | CPU: %s\n", ps.gpu_name[0] ? ps.gpu_name : "unknown", ps.cpu_name[0] ? ps.cpu_name : "unknown");
    if (ps.ram_total_mb > 0) ADD("RAM: %.0f of %.0f MB used", ps.ram_used_mb, ps.ram_total_mb);
    if (ps.vram_total_mb > 0) ADD(" | VRAM: %.0f of %.0f MB used", ps.vram_used_mb, ps.vram_total_mb);
    if (ps.ram_total_mb > 0 || ps.vram_total_mb > 0) ADD("\n");
    if (ps.fps > 0) ADD("Frame rate: %.1f fps (average %.1f ms, worst %.1f ms)\n", ps.fps, ps.frame_ms_avg, ps.frame_ms_max);
    float p[3];
    if (link_position(p)) {
        char place[160];
        place_string(place, sizeof place, p);
        ADD("Place: %s\n", place);
        control_field_str(r, "place", place);
    } else ADD("Place: not in the world yet\n");
    ControlConsoleResult g;
    control_exec_line("get", false, &g);
    if (!g.failed && g.text) {
        ADD("Settings:");
        for (const char *c = g.text; *c;) {
            const char *eol = strchr(c, '\n');
            size_t len = eol ? (size_t)(eol - c) : strlen(c);
            char item[128];
            if (len >= sizeof item) len = sizeof item - 1;
            memcpy(item, c, len); item[len] = 0;
            char *sep = strstr(item, ": ");
            if (sep) { sep[0] = '='; memmove(sep + 1, sep + 2, strlen(sep + 2) + 1); }
            ADD(" %s", item);
            c += len + (eol ? 1 : 0);
            if (!eol) break;
        }
        ADD("\n");
    }
    control_console_free(&g);
#undef ADD
    while (n && block[n - 1] == '\n') block[--n] = 0;
    control_field_str(r, "report", block);
    control_text(r, "%s", block);
    control_copy(r, block);
}

// ---- goto <x> <y> <z> | goto <swr:1 line> | goto <named place>: back to a place `pos` or `report` gave, or to a shrine, Korok,
// tower, stable, village ... by number or name (developer mode)
void control_tp_run(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r);  // runtime/control_tp.c: the teleport command
static bool parse_number(const char *s, double *out) {
    char *end;
    errno = 0;
    double v = strtod(s, &end);
    if (end == s || *end || errno || !isfinite(v)) return false;
    *out = v;
    return true;
}
bool control_look_start(bool use_yaw, double yaw, bool use_pitch, double pitch, int settle);  // runtime/control_input.c
void control_tp_then_look(bool use_yaw, double yaw, bool use_pitch, double pitch);           // runtime/control_tp.c
// Split the arguments at spaces (a quoted line arrives as one argument). Returns how many words (at most max).
static int split_words(int argc, char **argv, char (*store)[64], char **words, int max) {
    int n = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
        char copy[256];
        if (snprintf(copy, sizeof copy, "%s", argv[i]) >= (int)sizeof copy) return -1;
        for (char *a = strtok(copy, " \t"); a; a = strtok(NULL, " \t")) {
            if (n >= max || snprintf(store[n], 64, "%s", a) >= 64) return -1;
            words[n] = store[n];
            n++;
        }
    }
    return n;
}
// The first word says what the rest is: a number, a name=value pair or the swr:1 tag mean coordinates, a word means a place.
static bool goto_is_place(int nwords, char **words) {
    double d;
    return nwords > 0 && strcmp(words[0], "swr:1") && !strchr(words[0], '=') && !parse_number(words[0], &d);
}
// How far above a place's position Link arrives (he drops the last bit, it is not enough to hurt). A start position of the game
// is ground, so a small lift is enough (a stable floor can be 0.5 above it); marker positions are not, they get a larger one.
static double place_lift(const Place *p) { return p->ground ? 1.0 : p->kind == PLACE_KOROK ? 2.0 : 3.0; }
static void cmd_goto(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    double v[3];
    const Place *place = NULL;
    {
        char store[24][64], *words[24];
        int nwords = split_words(argc, argv, store, words, 24);
        if (nwords < 0) { control_fail(r, "goto: too many words"); return; }
        if (goto_is_place(nwords, words)) {
            float here[3];
            char why[400];
            place = place_find(nwords, words, link_position(here) ? here : NULL, why, sizeof why);
            if (!place) { control_fail(r, "%s", why); return; }
            v[0] = place->x; v[1] = place->y + place_lift(place); v[2] = place->z;
        }
    }
    double hour = -1, yaw = 0, pitch = 0;
    bool have_look[2] = {false, false};
    bool have[3] = {false, false, false};
    char usage[300];  // (named after the command used, goto or tp)
    snprintf(usage, sizeof usage, "%s: use %s <x> <y> <z>, a line from pos or report (swr:1 x=.. y=.. z=.. [hour=..]), "
             "or a place (shrine 5, korok H23, stable wetland, tower 2, hateno)", argv[0], argv[0]);
    int numbers = 0;
    if (place) have[0] = have[1] = have[2] = true;
    for (int i = 1; i < argc && !place; i++) {
        // A quoted line (swctl goto "swr:1 x=.. y=.. z=..") arrives as one argument, so split every argument at spaces.
        char word[256];
        if (snprintf(word, sizeof word, "%s", argv[i]) >= (int)sizeof word) { control_fail(r, "%s", usage); return; }
        for (char *a = strtok(word, " \t"); a; a = strtok(NULL, " \t")) {
            if (!strcmp(a, "swr:1")) continue;
            const char *eq = strchr(a, '=');
            if (eq) {
                double x;
                if (!parse_number(eq + 1, &x)) { control_fail(r, "Not a number: \"%s\"", a); return; }
                size_t k = (size_t)(eq - a);
                if (k == 1 && a[0] >= 'x' && a[0] <= 'z') { v[a[0] - 'x'] = x; have[a[0] - 'x'] = true; }
                else if (k == 4 && !strncmp(a, "hour", 4)) hour = x;
                else if (k == 3 && !strncmp(a, "yaw", 3)) { yaw = x; have_look[0] = true; }
                else if (k == 5 && !strncmp(a, "pitch", 5)) { pitch = x; have_look[1] = true; }
                // (anything else is ignored)
            } else if (numbers < 3 && parse_number(a, &v[numbers])) have[numbers++] = true;
            else { control_fail(r, "Cannot read \"%s\"", a); return; }
        }
    }
    if (!have[0] || !have[1] || !have[2]) { control_fail(r, "%s", usage); return; }
    if (hour > 24) { control_fail(r, "Hour must be from 0 to 24"); return; }
    uint64_t pinfo = player_info();
    if (!pinfo) { control_fail(r, "No world loaded"); return; }
    float cur[3] = {*(float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x88), *(float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x8c), *(float *)(uintptr_t)(pinfo + 0x90)};
    bool already = fabs(v[0] - cur[0]) < 0.05 && fabs(v[2] - cur[2]) < 0.05;  // (teleport refuses a move this small)
    if (!already) {
        char xs[40], ys[40], zs[40];
        snprintf(xs, sizeof xs, "%.4f", v[0]); snprintf(ys, sizeof ys, "%.4f", v[1]); snprintf(zs, sizeof zs, "%.4f", v[2]);
        char *tp[] = {(char *)"teleport", xs, ys, zs};
        control_tp_run(4, tp, r);  // (answers with the teleport's own fields: state, x, y, z, ...)
        if (control_reply_failed(r)) return;
    } else control_field_str(r, "state", "already_there");
    if (hour >= 0) test_warp_set_hour((float)hour);
    if (place) {
        control_field_str(r, "place", place->name);
        control_field_str(r, "kind", place_kind_name(place->kind));
        control_field_int(r, "number", place->number);
    }
    if (place) control_text(r, already ? "Already at %s" : "Going to %s", place->name);
    else control_text(r, already ? "Already there" : "Teleporting to %.2f %.2f %.2f", v[0], v[1], v[2]);
    if (hour >= 0) control_text(r, "Time set to %.2f", hour);
    if (have_look[0] || have_look[1]) {   // the camera turns once Link is there (look status shows when it holds)
        if (already ? control_look_start(have_look[0], yaw, have_look[1], pitch, 30) : (control_tp_then_look(have_look[0], yaw, have_look[1], pitch), true))
            control_text(r, "Camera yaw %.1f pitch %.1f", yaw, pitch);
        else
            control_text(r, "Camera not found");
    }
}

// ---- places [kind] [words]: what `goto` knows
#define PLACES_SHOWN 40
static void cmd_places(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    char store[24][64], *words[24];
    int nwords = split_words(argc, argv, store, words, 24);
    if (nwords < 0) { control_fail(r, "places: too many words"); return; }
    if (nwords == 0) {
        for (int k = 0; k < PLACE_KINDS; k++) control_text(r, "%-9s %4d", place_kind_name((PlaceKind)k), place_kind_count((PlaceKind)k));
        control_text(r, "places <kind> [words] lists them, goto <kind> <number or name> goes there");
        return;
    }
    int kind = place_kind_from_word(words[0]);
    const Place *shown[PLACES_SHOWN];
    int total = place_list(kind, nwords - (kind >= 0), words + (kind >= 0), shown, PLACES_SHOWN);
    control_field_int(r, "count", total);
    for (int i = 0; i < total && i < PLACES_SHOWN; i++) {
        const Place *p = shown[i];
        if (kind >= 0) control_text(r, "%4d  %s%s%s%s", p->number, p->name, *p->sub ? " (" : "", p->sub, *p->sub ? ")" : "");
        else control_text(r, "%-8s %4d  %s", place_kind_name(p->kind), p->number, p->name);
    }
    if (total > PLACES_SHOWN) control_text(r, "... %d more, add words to narrow it down", total - PLACES_SHOWN);
    if (!total) control_text(r, "Nothing found");
}

void control_game_init(void) {
    static const ControlCmd player[] = {
        {"state", "", "Frame number, uptime, fps and hour", cmd_state, CONTROL_PLAYER},
        {"pos", "", "Show the position and copy it as a line for goto or an issue", cmd_pos, CONTROL_PLAYER},
        {"camera", "", "Show the camera position and direction", cmd_camera, CONTROL_PLAYER},
        {"version", "", "Show the game version and system", cmd_version, CONTROL_PLAYER},
        {"report", "", "Build an issue report and copy it", cmd_report, CONTROL_PLAYER},
    };
    control_register(player, (int)(sizeof player / sizeof *player));
    control_settings_init();  // (get for everyone, set only in developer mode)
    if (!control_enabled()) return;
    static const ControlCmd dev[] = {
        {"time", "[freeze | unfreeze | set <0-24> | <0-24>]", "Show or change the hour of the day", cmd_time, 0},
        {"shot", "<file>", "Save a screenshot as PNG", cmd_shot, 0},
        {"goto", "<x> <y> <z> | <swr:1 line> | <place>", "Go to coordinates, a place from pos or report, or a shrine, Korok, tower, stable, village by number or name", cmd_goto, 0},
        {"places", "[<kind>] [words]", "List the places goto knows (shrine, tower, stable, village, landmark, korok)", cmd_places, 0},
        {"tp", "<x> <y> <z> | <swr:1 line> | <place>", "Same as goto", cmd_goto, 0},
    };
    control_register(dev, (int)(sizeof dev / sizeof *dev));
    control_prof_init();
    control_input_init();
    control_mem_init();
    control_cells_init();
    control_fly_init();
    control_items_init();
    control_tp_init();
    rupees_control_init();
    weather_control_init();
}
```

`runtime/control_input.c`:

```c
// Live test input. Commands and frame publication have one writer (the presenter).
#include "control.h"
#include "control_cells.h"
#include <errno.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#ifndef M_PI
#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846
#endif

uint64_t renderer_present_count(void);
static const char *const names[] = {
    "a", "b", "x", "y", "lstick", "rstick", "l", "r", "zl", "zr",
    "plus", "minus", "left", "up", "right", "down"
};
static uint64_t until[16];
static bool held[16];
static struct { int32_t x, y; uint64_t until; bool held; } sticks[2];
static _Atomic bool enabled;
static _Atomic uint64_t buttons, axes[2];
static uint64_t published_frame;
enum { LOOK_IDLE, LOOK_RUN, LOOK_DONE, LOOK_TIMEOUT, LOOK_FAILED };
static const char *const look_names[] = {"idle", "running", "done", "timeout", "failed"};
static struct { int state; bool use[2]; double target[2], last[2]; bool have_last, snap; uint64_t start, ok, settle; } look;

static bool duration(const char *s, uint64_t *n, ControlReply *r) {
    char *end;
    errno = 0;
    unsigned long v = strtoul(s, &end, 10);
    if (*s < '0' || *s > '9' || *end || errno || !v || v > 1000000) {
        control_fail(r, "Frames must be an integer from 1 to 1000000"); return false;
    }
    *n = v; return true;
}
static int button(const char *s, ControlReply *r) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) if (!strcmp(s, names[i])) return i;
    control_fail(r, "Invalid button; valid: a b x y l r zl zr plus minus up down left right lstick rstick");
    return -1;
}
static void queued(ControlReply *r, const char *what) {
    control_field_str(r, "queued", what);
    control_field_int(r, "frame", (int64_t)renderer_present_count());
    control_field_int(r, "apply_frame", (int64_t)(renderer_present_count() + 1));
}
static void cmd_button(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    bool hold = !strcmp(argv[0], "hold");
    if (argc < 2 || argc > (hold ? 2 : 3)) {
        control_fail(r, "Usage: %s", hold ? "hold <button>" : "press <button> [frames]"); return;
    }
    int i = button(argv[1], r);
    uint64_t n = 3;
    if (i < 0 || (argc == 3 && !duration(argv[2], &n, r))) return;
    held[i] = hold;
    until[i] = hold ? 0 : renderer_present_count() + 1 + n;
    queued(r, argv[0]);
    control_field_str(r, "button", names[i]);
    if (!hold) control_field_int(r, "frames", (int64_t)n);
}
static void cmd_release(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    if (argc > 2) { control_fail(r, "Usage: release [<button> | all]"); return; }
    if (argc == 1 || !strcmp(argv[1], "all")) {
        memset(held, 0, sizeof held); memset(until, 0, sizeof until);
        memset(sticks, 0, sizeof sticks);
        if (look.state == LOOK_RUN) look.state = LOOK_IDLE;
    } else {
        int i = button(argv[1], r);
        if (i < 0) return;
        held[i] = false; until[i] = 0;
    }
    queued(r, "release");
    control_field_str(r, "button", argc == 1 ? "all" : argv[1]);
}
static void cmd_stick(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    if ((argc != 4 && argc != 5) || (strcmp(argv[1], "l") && strcmp(argv[1], "r"))) {
        control_fail(r, "Usage: stick <l|r> <x> <y> [frames]"); return;
    }
    double v[2];
    for (int j = 0; j < 2; j++) {
        char *end; errno = 0; v[j] = strtod(argv[j + 2], &end);
        if (end == argv[j + 2] || *end || errno || !(v[j] >= -1 && v[j] <= 1)) {
            control_fail(r, "Axes must be from -1 to 1"); return;
        }
    }
    uint64_t n = 0;
    if (argc == 5 && !duration(argv[4], &n, r)) return;
    int i = !strcmp(argv[1], "r");
    if (i && look.state == LOOK_RUN) look.state = LOOK_IDLE;
    sticks[i].x = (int32_t)(v[0] * 32767); sticks[i].y = (int32_t)(v[1] * 32767);
    sticks[i].held = argc == 4 && (v[0] != 0 || v[1] != 0);
    sticks[i].until = n ? renderer_present_count() + 1 + n : 0;
    queued(r, "stick"); control_field_str(r, "stick", argv[1]);
    control_field_num(r, "x", v[0]); control_field_num(r, "y", v[1]);
    control_field_int(r, "frames", (int64_t)n);
}


// ---- look <yaw> <pitch>: turn the camera to these angles. The orbit camera keeps its eye position and its pitch as real
// state (camera.eye, camera.target, camera.pitch cells, control_cells.c): yaw is the direction eye -> target, so a write
// that moves the eye around the target turns the camera and it stays there. look reads the angles from those cells, writes
// the eye / pitch and checks again each frame, since the game moves the eye a few degrees after a write (wall
// collision, a follow correction); it settles in a few frames. When the cells do not resolve (another game version, no
// camera object yet) it falls back to moving the right stick until the camera (the `camera` command's matrix, needs
// Anti-aliasing TAA) points there: stick right lowers yaw, stick up raises pitch, proportional on the error, damped by how
// fast the camera is already turning (the game answers a frame or two late), with a floor so the stick leaves its dead zone.
bool control_camera_angles(double *yaw, double *pitch);  // runtime/control_game.c
void control_fly_input(uint64_t *b, int32_t *lx, int32_t *ly);  // runtime/control_fly.c
void control_fly_frame(uint64_t frame);
#define LOOK_TOL 0.6          // degrees
#define LOOK_FRAMES 900       // give up after this many presented frames
#define LOOK_SETTLE 6         // frames within tolerance in a row before "done"
static double wrap180(double a) { while (a > 180) a -= 360; while (a <= -180) a += 360; return a; }
#define LOOK_TOL_SNAP 0.15    // degrees, when the cells are used
#define LOOK_SETTLE_SNAP 3
static bool look_angles(double *yaw, double *pitch) {
    double e[3], t[3];
    return control_cell_camera_angles(e, t, yaw, pitch) || control_camera_angles(yaw, pitch);
}
static void look_end(int state) {
    look.state = state;
    sticks[1].x = sticks[1].y = 0; sticks[1].held = false; sticks[1].until = 0;
}
static void look_snap_step(uint64_t frame) {
    double e[3], t[3], cur[2];
    if (!control_cell_camera_angles(e, t, &cur[0], &cur[1])) { look_end(LOOK_FAILED); return; }
    if (frame - look.start > LOOK_FRAMES) { look_end(LOOK_TIMEOUT); return; }
    double err0 = look.use[0] ? wrap180(look.target[0] - cur[0]) : 0, err1 = look.use[1] ? look.target[1] - cur[1] : 0;
    if (fabs(err0) <= LOOK_TOL_SNAP && fabs(err1) <= LOOK_TOL_SNAP) {
        if (++look.ok >= (look.settle ? look.settle : LOOK_SETTLE_SNAP)) look_end(LOOK_DONE);
        return;
    }
    look.ok = 0;
    if (fabs(err0) > LOOK_TOL_SNAP) {   // put the eye on the circle around the target, aimed at the yaw we want
        double r = hypot(t[0] - e[0], t[2] - e[2]);
        if (r < 0.01) { look_end(LOOK_FAILED); return; }
        double y = (cur[0] + err0) * (M_PI / 180.0), ne[3] = {t[0] - sin(y) * r, e[1], t[2] - cos(y) * r};
        if (!control_cell_set(&control_cell_camera_eye, ne)) { look_end(LOOK_FAILED); return; }
    }
    if (fabs(err1) > LOOK_TOL_SNAP) {
        double np = -look.target[1];
        if (!control_cell_set(&control_cell_camera_pitch, &np)) { look_end(LOOK_FAILED); return; }
    }
}
static void look_step(uint64_t frame) {
    if (look.snap) { look_snap_step(frame); return; }
    double cur[2];
    if (!control_camera_angles(&cur[0], &cur[1])) { look_end(LOOK_FAILED); return; }
    if (frame - look.start > LOOK_FRAMES) { look_end(LOOK_TIMEOUT); return; }
    double err[2], vel[2] = {0, 0}, u[2];
    bool inside = true;
    for (int a = 0; a < 2; a++) {
        err[a] = look.use[a] ? (a == 0 ? wrap180(look.target[a] - cur[a]) : look.target[a] - cur[a]) : 0;
        if (look.have_last) vel[a] = a == 0 ? wrap180(cur[a] - look.last[a]) : cur[a] - look.last[a];
        look.last[a] = cur[a];
        if (fabs(err[a]) > LOOK_TOL) inside = false;
        static const double kp[2] = {0.05, 0.15}, floor_[2] = {0.2, 0.3};  // (pitch answers more slowly than yaw)
        double o = kp[a] * err[a] - 0.5 * vel[a];
        if (fabs(err[a]) > LOOK_TOL && fabs(o) < floor_[a]) o = err[a] < 0 ? -floor_[a] : floor_[a];
        if (fabs(err[a]) <= LOOK_TOL) o = 0;
        u[a] = o > 1 ? 1 : o < -1 ? -1 : o;
    }
    look.have_last = true;
    look.ok = inside ? look.ok + 1 : 0;
    if (look.ok >= LOOK_SETTLE) { look_end(LOOK_DONE); return; }
    sticks[1].x = (int32_t)(-u[0] * 32767);   // right lowers yaw
    sticks[1].y = (int32_t)(u[1] * 32767);    // up raises pitch
    sticks[1].held = true; sticks[1].until = 0;
}
static bool angle_arg(const char *s, int a, ControlReply *r) {
    if (!strcmp(s, "keep")) { look.use[a] = false; return true; }
    char *end; double v = strtod(s, &end);
    if (end == s || *end || !isfinite(v) || fabs(v) > 1000) { control_fail(r, "Angles must be degrees or keep"); return false; }
    look.use[a] = true; look.target[a] = v;
    return true;
}
static void look_fields(ControlReply *r) {
    control_field_str(r, "state", look_names[look.state]);
    control_field_str(r, "mode", look.snap ? "cells" : "stick");
    double y, p;
    if (look_angles(&y, &p)) {
        control_field_num(r, "yaw", y); control_field_num(r, "pitch", p);
        if (look.use[0]) control_field_num(r, "yaw_error", wrap180(look.target[0] - y));
        if (look.use[1]) control_field_num(r, "pitch_error", look.target[1] - p);
    }
}
static void cmd_look(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    if (argc == 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "status")) { look_fields(r); return; }
    if (argc == 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "stop")) { if (look.state == LOOK_RUN) look_end(LOOK_IDLE); look_fields(r); return; }
    if (argc != 3) { control_fail(r, "Usage: look <yaw> <pitch> | status | stop"); return; }
    double y, p, e[3], t[3];
    bool snap = control_cell_camera_angles(e, t, &y, &p);   // the camera cells; else the stick loop, which reads the TAA matrix
    if (!snap && !control_camera_angles(&y, &p)) { control_fail(r, "No camera"); return; }
    if (!angle_arg(argv[1], 0, r) || !angle_arg(argv[2], 1, r)) return;
    if (look.use[1] && (look.target[1] > 89 || look.target[1] < -89)) { control_fail(r, "Pitch must be from -89 to 89"); return; }
    look.snap = snap; look.settle = 0;
    look.state = LOOK_RUN; look.have_last = false; look.ok = 0; look.start = renderer_present_count();
    queued(r, "look");
    look_fields(r);
}

// Start a look from inside the runtime (goto, after its teleport): the same snap as the command, cells only (the stick loop
// is too slow and fragile to run unattended), and `settle` frames in tolerance in a row before it counts as done: the game
// may still turn the camera for a moment after a teleport, and the loop keeps correcting it until it holds.
bool control_look_start(bool use_yaw, double yaw, bool use_pitch, double pitch, int settle) {
    double y, p, e[3], t[3];
    if (!control_cell_camera_angles(e, t, &y, &p) || !isfinite(yaw) || !isfinite(pitch)) return false;
    if (pitch > 89) pitch = 89;
    if (pitch < -89) pitch = -89;
    look.use[0] = use_yaw; look.target[0] = yaw;
    look.use[1] = use_pitch; look.target[1] = pitch;
    look.snap = true; look.settle = (uint64_t)settle;
    look.state = LOOK_RUN; look.have_last = false; look.ok = 0; look.start = renderer_present_count();
    return true;
}

// Called even when no script exists. Expiry uses presented frames, never script time or poll count.
void control_input_frame(uint64_t frame) {
    if (!atomic_load_explicit(&enabled, memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    if (look.state == LOOK_RUN) look_step(frame);
    control_fly_frame(frame);
    uint64_t b = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) if (held[i] || frame < until[i]) b |= 1ull << i;
    atomic_store(&buttons, b);
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        bool active = sticks[i].held || frame < sticks[i].until;
        uint64_t a = active ? (uint16_t)sticks[i].x | ((uint64_t)(uint16_t)sticks[i].y << 16) |
                     ((uint64_t)sticks[i].held << 32) : 0;
        atomic_store(&axes[i], a);
    }
    published_frame = frame;
}
static int32_t clamp(int32_t v) { return v > 32767 ? 32767 : v < -32767 ? -32767 : v; }
void control_input_apply(uint64_t *b, int32_t *lx, int32_t *ly, int32_t *rx, int32_t *ry) {
    if (!atomic_load_explicit(&enabled, memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    *b |= atomic_load(&buttons);
    if (!lx) { control_fly_input(b, NULL, NULL); return; }
    int32_t *x[] = {lx, rx}, *y[] = {ly, ry};
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        uint64_t a = atomic_load(&axes[i]);
        int32_t ax = (int16_t)a, ay = (int16_t)(a >> 16);
        *x[i] = clamp((a >> 32 ? 0 : *x[i]) + ax);
        *y[i] = clamp((a >> 32 ? 0 : *y[i]) + ay);
    }
    control_fly_input(b, lx, ly);
}
static void cmd_input(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    (void)argv;
    if (argc != 1) { control_fail(r, "Usage: input"); return; }
    control_field_int(r, "frame", (int64_t)published_frame);
    uint64_t b = atomic_load(&buttons);
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++) control_field_bool(r, names[i], (b >> i) & 1);
    const char *keys[][3] = {{"l.x", "l.y", "l.held"}, {"r.x", "r.y", "r.held"}};
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        uint64_t a = atomic_load(&axes[i]);
        control_field_num(r, keys[i][0], (int16_t)a / 32767.0);
        control_field_num(r, keys[i][1], (int16_t)(a >> 16) / 32767.0);
        control_field_bool(r, keys[i][2], a >> 32);
    }
}
void control_input_init(void) {
    static const ControlCmd cmds[] = {
        {"press", "<button> [frames]", "Press a button (3 frames by default)", cmd_button},
        {"hold", "<button>", "Hold a button until released", cmd_button},
        {"release", "[<button>|all]", "Release a button, or all input", cmd_release},
        {"stick", "<l|r> <x> <y> [frames]", "Move a stick (axes -1 to 1)", cmd_stick},
        {"look", "<yaw> <pitch> | status | stop", "Turn the camera to a yaw and pitch in degrees (either may be keep)", cmd_look},
        {"input", "", "Show the input currently applied", cmd_input},
    };
    control_register(cmds, sizeof cmds / sizeof *cmds);
    atomic_store(&enabled, true);
}
```
