`runtime/gamebuild.c`:

```c
// Builds the game code library on the player's machine (runtime/gamebuild.h).
#include "gamebuild.h"

#include <dirent.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#include "gamelib.h"
#include "paths.h"
#include "platform.h"
#include "rt.h"

// From the Makefile: the flags the game code is compiled and linked with (as `make` builds it in a source checkout)
#ifndef GAMELIB_CFLAGS
#define GAMELIB_CFLAGS "-O1 -fno-strict-aliasing -fvisibility=hidden"
#endif
// GAMELIB_CFLAGS_COMPAT: the same for the compatible target (gamelib.h gamelib_compat), where there is one
#ifndef GAMELIB_ZIGFLAGS  // (zig cc only: what makes it build what clang does with GAMELIB_CFLAGS)
#define GAMELIB_ZIGFLAGS "-Xclang -O1 -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize -g0 -fomit-frame-pointer"
#endif
#ifndef GAMELIB_SHARED
#define GAMELIB_SHARED "-shared"
#endif
#ifndef GAMELIB_GENARGS  // the generator's options that change the game code (RECOMP_LOCALS=1: --locals)
#define GAMELIB_GENARGS ""
#endif

#ifdef _WIN32
#define SEP "\\"
#else
#define SEP "/"
#endif

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ child processes
// Every one running, so that quitting mid-build ends them too (atexit) instead of leaving compilers behind.
#define MAX_PROCS 80
static pthread_mutex_t g_plock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static PlatProc g_procs[MAX_PROCS];
static int g_nprocs;
static bool g_quitting;

static void end_all(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    g_quitting = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nprocs; i++) plat_proc_kill(g_procs[i]);
    g_nprocs = 0;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
}

static PlatProc spawn(char **argv, const char *log) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    PlatProc p = g_quitting ? 0 : plat_spawn((const char *const *)argv, log, false);
    if (p && g_nprocs < MAX_PROCS) g_procs[g_nprocs++] = p;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
    return p;
}

// plat_proc_wait without blocking, then forgotten once it has ended
static int finished(PlatProc p) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    int r = plat_proc_wait(p, false);
    if (r >= 0)
        for (int i = 0; i < g_nprocs; i++)
            if (g_procs[i] == p) { g_procs[i] = g_procs[--g_nprocs]; break; }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
    return r;
}

static void stop(PlatProc p) {  // ends one that is still running, then forgotten
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    bool ours = false;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nprocs; i++)
        if (g_procs[i] == p) { g_procs[i] = g_procs[--g_nprocs]; ours = true; break; }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
    if (ours) plat_proc_kill(p);
}

static void sleep_ms(int ms) { plat_sleep_until_ns(plat_now_ns() + (uint64_t)ms * 1000000ull); }

static int wait_for(PlatProc p) {
    int r;
    while ((r = finished(p)) < 0) sleep_ms(20);
    return r;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ argument lists
typedef struct { char **v; int n, cap; } Args;
static void add(Args *a, const char *s) {
    if (a->n + 2 > a->cap) {
        a->cap = a->cap ? a->cap * 2 : 32;
        a->v = (char **)realloc(a->v, sizeof *a->v * a->cap);
    }
    a->v[a->n++] = strdup(s);
    a->v[a->n] = NULL;
}
static void add_split(Args *a, const char *flags) {  // (space-separated, no quoting)
    char buf[1024];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", flags);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, " "); t; t = strtok(NULL, " ")) add(a, t);
}
static void args_free(Args *a) {
    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) free(a->v[i]);
    free(a->v);
    memset(a, 0, sizeof *a);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the tools
typedef struct {
    char gen[1100], gen_script[1100];  // generator: swgen, or (source checkout) the venv's python + tools/gen.py
    char cc[1100];                     // compiler: zig (as `zig cc`), or SAVAGEWIND_CC / clang
    bool zig;
    char inc[1100], entry[1100], hle[1100];  // headers the game code includes, tools/gamelib_entry.c, HLE names
#ifdef _WIN32
    char implib[1100];  // the .exe's import library (the runtime functions the game code calls)
    char zig_rt[1100];  // the release's zig: its runtime built ahead of time (zig/rt, tools/zig_slim.sh), "" = none
#endif
} Tools;

static bool file_exists(const char *p) {
    struct stat st;
    return stat(p, &st) == 0;
}

static bool find_tools(Tools *t) {
    memset(t, 0, sizeof *t);
    const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_GEN");
    if (e && *e) snprintf(t->gen, sizeof t->gen, "%s", e);
    else if (!rt_resource("swgen" SEP "swgen" PLAT_EXE_SUFFIX, NULL, t->gen, sizeof t->gen) &&
             !(rt_resource(NULL, "tools/" PLAT_VENV_PYTHON, t->gen, sizeof t->gen) &&
               rt_resource(NULL, "tools/gen.py", t->gen_script, sizeof t->gen_script)))
        return false;
    e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_CC");
    if (e && *e) snprintf(t->cc, sizeof t->cc, "%s", e);
    else if (rt_resource("zig" SEP "zig" PLAT_EXE_SUFFIX, NULL, t->cc, sizeof t->cc)) t->zig = true;
#ifndef _WIN32
    else if (rt_dev_mode() && file_exists("/usr/bin/clang")) snprintf(t->cc, sizeof t->cc, "/usr/bin/clang");
#endif
    else return false;
    if (!rt_resource("gamelib-src" SEP "cpu.h", "runtime/cpu.h", t->inc, sizeof t->inc) ||
        !rt_resource("gamelib-src" SEP "gamelib_entry.c", "tools/gamelib_entry.c", t->entry, sizeof t->entry) ||
        !rt_resource("gamelib-src" SEP "hle_symbols.txt", "runtime/hle/hle_symbols.txt", t->hle, sizeof t->hle))
        return false;
    char *s = strrchr(t->inc, '/'), *b = strrchr(t->inc, '\\');
    if (b > s) s = b;
    if (s) *s = 0;
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!rt_resource("savagewind.dll.a", "build/savagewind.dll.a", t->implib, sizeof t->implib)) return false;
    t->zig_rt[0] = 0;
    if (t->zig && rt_resource("zig" SEP "rt" SEP "link.rsp", NULL, t->zig_rt, sizeof t->zig_rt)) {
        char *s = strrchr(t->zig_rt, '/'), *b = strrchr(t->zig_rt, '\\');
        if (b > s) s = b;
        if (s) *s = 0;
        else t->zig_rt[0] = 0;
    }
#endif
    return true;
}

bool gamebuild_available(void) {
    Tools t;
    return find_tools(&t);
}

static void compiler(Args *a, const Tools *t) {
    add(a, t->cc);
    if (t->zig) add(a, "cc");
#ifdef __linux__
    // zig's own glibc headers and stubs (lib/libc, tools/fetch_zig.sh keeps them), as old as the oldest glibc the
    // release runs on (docs/linux.md). Without a target it builds for the native libc and wants the system's headers,
    // which SteamOS and other read-only systems don't have: "failed to find libc installation:
    // LibCStdLibHeaderNotFound" (#191). The game code only takes memcpy / math / fenv from it.
#if defined(__aarch64__)
    if (t->zig) { add(a, "-target"); add(a, "aarch64-linux-gnu.2.35"); }
#else
    if (t->zig) { add(a, "-target"); add(a, "x86_64-linux-gnu.2.35"); }
#endif
#endif
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ generator progress (its log)
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    char log[1100], out[1100];
    PlatProc p;
    int exit;                // -1 while running
    int files;               // chunk files written so far (complete)
    unsigned long long ci, n;  // functions written / all
} Gen;

static void read_gen_log(Gen *g) {
    FILE *f = fopen(g->log, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    static char buf[1 << 16];
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long size = ftell(f);
    long from = size > (long)sizeof buf - 1 ? size - (long)sizeof buf + 1 : 0;
    fseek(f, from, SEEK_SET);
    size_t n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf - 1, f);
    fclose(f);
    buf[n] = 0;
    const char *last = NULL;
    for (const char *p = strstr(buf, ": progress "); p; p = strstr(p + 1, ": progress ")) last = p;
    unsigned long long ci, all;
    int files;
    if (last && sscanf(last, ": progress %llu/%llu files %d", &ci, &all, &files) == 3) {
        g->ci = ci, g->n = all;
        if (files > g->files) g->files = files;
    }
}

// The modules of <work>/layout.txt (`gen layout`, tools/layout.py), in load order; their image sizes in size[].
static int read_layout(const char *path, Gen *gens, double *size) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return 0;
    static char names[MAX_MODULES][16];
    char line[256];
    int n = 0;
    while (n < MAX_MODULES && fgets(line, sizeof line, f)) {
        unsigned long long base, sz;
        if (line[0] == '#' || sscanf(line, "%15s %llx %llx", names[n], &base, &sz) != 3) continue;
        memset(&gens[n], 0, sizeof gens[n]);
        gens[n].name = names[n];
        size[n++] = (double)sz;
    }
    fclose(f);
    return n;
}

static void log_tail(const char *path, char *out, size_t n) {  // the last line of a log (an error message)
    out[0] = 0;
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    char buf[4096];
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long size = ftell(f);
    fseek(f, size > (long)sizeof buf - 1 ? size - (long)sizeof buf + 1 : 0, SEEK_SET);
    size_t k = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf - 1, f);
    fclose(f);
    buf[k] = 0;
    while (k && (buf[k - 1] == '\n' || buf[k - 1] == '\r')) buf[--k] = 0;
    char *nl = strrchr(buf, '\n');
    snprintf(out, n, "%s", nl ? nl + 1 : buf);
}

// The end of a failed generator's or compile's log, into this log: the work folder (and their own logs with it) is
// deleted after the build, a crash leaves a stack (faulthandler, tools/gen.py) of many lines, and a compile's last
// line is only "1 error generated", after the error itself.
static void log_gen_tail(const char *path, int exit_code) {
    if (exit_code > 128 && exit_code < 255)  // (Linux, macOS: ended by a signal; 9, killed: often out of memory)
        LOG("[gamebuild]   ended by signal %d\n", exit_code - 128);
    else  // (255 on Windows: also a crash, e.g. an access violation)
        LOG("[gamebuild]   exit status %d\n", exit_code);
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    static char buf[16384];
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long size = ftell(f);
    fseek(f, size > (long)sizeof buf - 1 ? size - (long)sizeof buf + 1 : 0, SEEK_SET);
    size_t k = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf - 1, f);
    fclose(f);
    buf[k] = 0;
    const char *line[40];
    int n = 0;
    for (char *s = buf, *e; *s; s = e) {
        e = s + strcspn(s, "\n");
        if (*e) *e++ = 0;
        size_t l = strlen(s);
        if (l && s[l - 1] == '\r') s[l - 1] = 0;
        if (!*s || strstr(s, ": progress ")) continue;  // (the progress bar's lines)
        if (n == 40) memmove(line, line + 1, sizeof line[0] * --n);
        line[n++] = s;
    }
    if (!n) LOG("[gamebuild]   (no message in its log)\n");
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) LOG("[gamebuild]   | %s\n", line[i]);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ compiling
typedef struct {
    char src[1100], obj[1100], log[1100];
    unsigned long long bytes;
} Unit;

typedef struct {
    Unit *u;
    int n, cap;
} Units;

static void add_unit(Units *us, const char *src, const char *work, const char *stem) {
    if (us->n == us->cap) {
        us->cap = us->cap ? us->cap * 2 : 64;
        us->u = (Unit *)realloc(us->u, sizeof *us->u * us->cap);
    }
    Unit *u = &us->u[us->n++];
    snprintf(u->src, sizeof u->src, "%s", src);
    snprintf(u->obj, sizeof u->obj, "%s" SEP "%s.o", work, stem);
    snprintf(u->log, sizeof u->log, "%s" SEP "%s.log", work, stem);
    struct stat st;
    u->bytes = stat(src, &st) == 0 ? (unsigned long long)st.st_size : 0;
}

// The flags the game code is built with: this CPU's target's (gamelib.h; part of its id). zig cc reads -march=<cpu>
// with its own CPU names (x86_64_v3) and takes "-<feature>" off the end, so x86-64-v3 would be CPU "x86": the same CPU
// as -mcpu there.
static const char *target_cflags(void) {
#ifdef GAMELIB_CFLAGS_COMPAT
    if (gamelib_compat()) return GAMELIB_CFLAGS_COMPAT;
#endif
    return GAMELIB_CFLAGS;
}

static void add_cflags(Args *a, const Tools *t) {
    char buf[1024];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", target_cflags());
    for (char *f = strtok(buf, " "); f; f = strtok(NULL, " ")) {
        if (t->zig && !strncmp(f, "-march=", 7)) {
            char cpu[128];
            snprintf(cpu, sizeof cpu, "-mcpu=%s", f + 7);
            for (char *c = cpu + 6; *c; c++) if (*c == '-') *c = '_';
            add(a, cpu);
        } else {
            add(a, f);
        }
    }
    if (t->zig) add_split(a, GAMELIB_ZIGFLAGS);  // (after them: the last -O that reaches clang wins)
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ pieces kept between builds
// Every compiled piece of game code is kept in <data root>/cache/gamecode/, named by a hash of its C, the compiler
// (zig's executable), the flags and the headers it includes. The game code is rebuilt after every Savage Wind update,
// but most of the generated C comes out the same, so a rebuild compiles only the pieces that changed. After a good
// build only the pieces it used stay, so the folder holds about one build. SAVAGEWIND_NO_GAMECODE_CACHE=1: not used.
// Unit 0, the shipped entry file, is always compiled: it carries this build's GAMELIB_ID.
static char gc_dir[1100];
static uint64_t gc_seed;  // the hash everything but the C itself adds up to; 0: off
static uint64_t *gc_used;
static int gc_nused, gc_cap, gc_reused;

static uint64_t gc_hash_bytes(uint64_t h, const void *p_, size_t n) {  // (FNV-1a)
    const uint8_t *p = (const uint8_t *)p_;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) h = (h ^ p[i]) * 1099511628211ull;
    return h;
}

static uint64_t gc_hash_file(uint64_t h, const char *path) {  // 0: unreadable
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return 0;
    static char buf[1 << 16];  // (the build's own thread only)
    size_t n;
    while ((n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, f)) > 0) h = gc_hash_bytes(h, buf, n);
    fclose(f);
    return h ? h : 1;
}

static void gc_begin(const Tools *t) {
    gc_nused = gc_reused = 0;
    gc_seed = 0;
    const char *off = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_NO_GAMECODE_CACHE");
    if (off && *off && strcmp(off, "0")) return;
    uint64_t h = gc_hash_file(1469598103934665603ull, t->cc);
    if (!h) return;
    Args a = {0};  // the compile line but the file names: the flags, the target, the id define left out (unit 0 only)
    add_cflags(&a, t);
    for (int i = 0; i < a.n; i++) h = gc_hash_bytes(h, a.v[i], strlen(a.v[i]) + 1);
    args_free(&a);
    DIR *d = opendir(t->inc);  // the headers: names and contents, summed so the order readdir gives doesn't matter
    if (!d) return;
    uint64_t sum = 0;
    for (struct dirent *e; (e = readdir(d));) {
        if (e->d_name[0] == '.') continue;
        char p[1400];
        snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s" SEP "%s", t->inc, e->d_name);
        sum += gc_hash_file(gc_hash_bytes(h, e->d_name, strlen(e->d_name)), p);
    }
    closedir(d);
    h = gc_hash_bytes(h, &sum, sizeof sum);
    snprintf(gc_dir, sizeof gc_dir, "%s" SEP "cache", rt_data_root());
    mkdir(gc_dir, 0755);
    snprintf(gc_dir, sizeof gc_dir, "%s" SEP "cache" SEP "gamecode", rt_data_root());
    mkdir(gc_dir, 0755);
    gc_seed = h ? h : 1;
}

static bool gc_copy(const char *from, const char *to) {
    FILE *a = fopen(from, "rb"), *b = a ? fopen(to, "wb") : NULL;
    static char buf[1 << 16];
    bool ok = a && b;
    size_t n;
    while (ok && (n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, a)) > 0) ok = fwrite(buf, 1, n, b) == n;
    if (a) fclose(a);
    if (b && fclose(b)) ok = false;
    if (!ok && b) remove(to);
    return ok;
}

static void gc_path(uint64_t key, char *p, size_t n) {
    snprintf(p, n, "%s" SEP "%016llx.o", gc_dir, (unsigned long long)key);
}

static void gc_note(uint64_t key) {
    if (gc_nused == gc_cap) gc_used = (uint64_t *)realloc(gc_used, sizeof *gc_used * (gc_cap = gc_cap ? gc_cap * 2 : 1024));
    gc_used[gc_nused++] = key;
}

// A piece compiled before: its object put in place, true
static bool gc_take(const Unit *u) {
    uint64_t key = gc_seed ? gc_hash_file(gc_seed, u->src) : 0;
    char p[1200];
    gc_path(key, p, sizeof p);
    if (!key || !gc_copy(p, u->obj)) return false;
    gc_note(key);
    gc_reused++;
    return true;
}

static void gc_store(const Unit *u) {
    uint64_t key = gc_seed ? gc_hash_file(gc_seed, u->src) : 0;
    char p[1200], tmp[1300];
    gc_path(key, p, sizeof p);
    snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s.tmp", p);  // (then renamed: a build stopped midway leaves no half piece behind)
    if (!key || !gc_copy(u->obj, tmp)) return;
    remove(p);
    if (rename(tmp, p) == 0) gc_note(key);
    else remove(tmp);
}

static int gc_cmp(const void *a, const void *b) {
    uint64_t x = *(const uint64_t *)a, y = *(const uint64_t *)b;
    return x < y ? -1 : x > y;
}

// After the build: only the pieces it used stay. After a failed one that took pieces, none: the next build compiles
// everything, in case a kept piece was the problem.
static void gc_finish(bool ok, int units) {
    if (!gc_seed || (!ok && !gc_reused)) return;  // (failed with nothing taken: what it compiled is good to keep)
    if (!ok) gc_nused = 0;
    qsort(gc_used, gc_nused, sizeof *gc_used, gc_cmp);
    int removed = 0;
    DIR *d = opendir(gc_dir);
    for (struct dirent *e; d && (e = readdir(d));) {
        unsigned long long k;
        char end;
        size_t n = strlen(e->d_name);
        if ((n != 18 && n != 22) || sscanf(e->d_name, "%16llx.%c", &k, &end) != 2 || end != 'o') continue;  // (.o, .o.tmp)
        uint64_t key = k;
        if (n == 18 && gc_nused && bsearch(&key, gc_used, gc_nused, sizeof *gc_used, gc_cmp)) continue;
        char p[1200];
        snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s" SEP "%s", gc_dir, e->d_name);
        if (remove(p) == 0) removed++;
    }
    if (d) closedir(d);
    LOG("[gamebuild] %d of %d pieces reused from cache/gamecode (%d old ones removed)\n", gc_reused, units - 1, removed);
}

static PlatProc start_compile(const Tools *t, const Unit *u) {
    Args a = {0};
    compiler(&a, t);
    add_cflags(&a, t);
    char inc[1200];
    snprintf(inc, sizeof inc, "-I%s", t->inc);
    add(&a, inc);
    char id[128];
    snprintf(id, sizeof id, "-DGAMELIB_ID=\"%s\"", gamelib_id());
    add(&a, id);
    add(&a, "-c");
    add(&a, u->src);
    add(&a, "-o");
    add(&a, u->obj);
    PlatProc p = spawn(a.v, u->log);
    args_free(&a);
    return p;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the build
bool gamebuild_run(const char *game_dir, const GameBuildOpts *o, char *why, size_t why_size) {
    uint64_t t0 = plat_now_ns();
    static bool registered;
    if (!registered) registered = true, atexit(end_all);
    Tools t;
    if (!find_tools(&t)) {
        snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code builder is missing from this copy of Savage Wind");
        return false;
    }
    char work[1100], lib[1100], tmp[1100];
    snprintf(work, sizeof work, "%s" SEP ".gamebuild", game_dir);
    snprintf(lib, sizeof lib, "%s" SEP "%s", game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME);
    snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s" SEP "%s.tmp", work, GAMELIB_NAME);
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, ".gamebuild");
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME);
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME ".id");
    mkdir(work, 0755);
    if (t.zig) {  // its caches in the work folder too (deleted below), not ~/.cache: hundreds of MB, used once
        char zc[1200];
        snprintf(zc, sizeof zc, "%s" SEP "zig-cache", work);
#ifdef _WIN32
        _putenv_s("ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR", zc);
        _putenv_s("ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR", zc);
#else
        setenv("ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR", zc, 1);
        setenv("ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR", zc, 1);
#endif
    }
    LOG("[gamebuild] generator %s%s%s, compiler %s%s, %d jobs\n", t.gen, t.gen_script[0] ? " " : "", t.gen_script,
        t.cc, t.zig ? " cc" : "", o->jobs);
    LOG("[gamebuild] target%s: %s\n", gamelib_compat() ? " (compatible: no FMA instructions, slower)" : "",
        target_cflags());

    // 1. the modules' layout (tools/layout.py): which modules, at which addresses
    Gen gens[MAX_MODULES];
    double weight[MAX_MODULES], total = 0;  // (each module's share of the generator's progress: its size)
    int ngen = 0;
    char exefs[1100], layout[1100], layout_c[1100];
    snprintf(exefs, sizeof exefs, "%s" SEP "exefs", game_dir);
    snprintf(layout, sizeof layout, "%s" SEP "layout.txt", work);
    snprintf(layout_c, sizeof layout_c, "%s" SEP "layout.c", work);
    bool ok = true;
    {
        char log[1100];
        snprintf(log, sizeof log, "%s" SEP "gen_layout.log", work);
        Args a = {0};
        add(&a, t.gen);
        if (t.gen_script[0]) add(&a, t.gen_script);
        add(&a, "layout");
        add(&a, exefs);
        add(&a, work);
        PlatProc p = spawn(a.v, log);
        args_free(&a);
        int r = p ? wait_for(p) : 255;
        if (r == 0) ngen = read_layout(layout, gens, weight);
        if (!ngen) {
            char last[300];
            log_tail(log, last, sizeof last);
            LOG("[gamebuild] module layout failed: %s\n", last);
            snprintf(why, why_size, "%s: %s",
                     p ? "the game files' code modules can't be loaded" : "the game code builder didn't start", last);
            ok = false;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < ngen; i++) total += weight[i];
        for (int i = 0; i < ngen; i++) weight[i] /= total;
    }

    // 2. the generator, every module at once; their finished files are compiled while it goes on
    for (int i = 0; i < ngen && ok; i++) {
        Gen *g = &gens[i];
        g->exit = -1;
        snprintf(g->log, sizeof g->log, "%s" SEP "gen_%s.log", work, g->name);
        snprintf(g->out, sizeof g->out, "%s" SEP "%s", work, g->name);
        char nso[1100];
        snprintf(nso, sizeof nso, "%s" SEP "%s", exefs, g->name);
        Args a = {0};
        add(&a, t.gen);
        if (t.gen_script[0]) add(&a, t.gen_script);
        add(&a, g->name);
        add(&a, nso);
        add(&a, layout);
        add(&a, g->out);
        if (strcmp(g->name, "main")) { add(&a, "--hle"); add(&a, t.hle); }
        add_split(&a, GAMELIB_GENARGS);
        g->p = spawn(a.v, g->log);
        args_free(&a);
        if (!g->p) { snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code builder didn't start"); ok = false; }
    }

    gc_begin(&t);
    Units units = {0};
    int queued[MAX_MODULES] = {0};  // chunk files of each module put in units so far
    bool tables[MAX_MODULES] = {false};
    int next = 0, jobs = o->jobs < 1 ? 1 : o->jobs > 64 ? 64 : o->jobs;
    struct { PlatProc p; int unit; } run[64];
    int nrun = 0;
    unsigned long long done_bytes = 0;
    double shown = 0;
    {
        add_unit(&units, t.entry, work, "gamelib_entry");
        add_unit(&units, layout_c, work, "layout");
    }
    while (ok) {
        // generator progress, newly finished files
        bool gens_done = true;
        double gen_frac = 0;
        unsigned long long written = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < ngen; i++) {
            Gen *g = &gens[i];
            if (g->exit < 0) {
                read_gen_log(g);
                int r = finished(g->p);
                if (r >= 0) {
                    g->exit = r;
                    read_gen_log(g);
                    if (r != 0) {
                        char last[300];
                        log_tail(g->log, last, sizeof last);
                        LOG("[gamebuild] generator (%s) failed: %s\n", g->name, last);
                        log_gen_tail(g->log, r);
                        snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code couldn't be prepared: %s", last);
                        ok = false;
                    }
                }
            }
            if (g->exit != 0) gens_done = false;
            for (; queued[i] < g->files; queued[i]++) {
                char src[1100], stem[64];
                snprintf(stem, sizeof stem, "%s_%03d", g->name, queued[i]);
                snprintf(src, sizeof src, "%s" SEP "%s.c", g->out, stem);
                add_unit(&units, src, work, stem);
            }
            if (g->exit == 0 && !tables[i]) {
                char src[1100], stem[64];
                snprintf(stem, sizeof stem, "%s_table", g->name);
                snprintf(src, sizeof src, "%s" SEP "%s.c", g->out, stem);
                add_unit(&units, src, work, stem);
                tables[i] = true;
            }
            gen_frac += g->exit == 0 ? weight[i] : g->n ? weight[i] * (double)g->ci / (double)g->n : 0;
        }
        if (!ok) break;
        for (int k = 0; k < units.n; k++) written += units.u[k].bytes;

        // compiles
        while (nrun < jobs && next < units.n) {
            if (next > 0 && gc_take(&units.u[next])) {  // (compiled by an earlier build: no compile)
                done_bytes += units.u[next].bytes;
                remove(units.u[next].src);
                next++;
                continue;
            }
            PlatProc p = start_compile(&t, &units.u[next]);
            if (!p) { snprintf(why, why_size, "the compiler didn't start"); ok = false; break; }
            run[nrun].p = p, run[nrun].unit = next++;
            nrun++;
        }
        for (int k = 0; k < nrun; k++) {
            int r = finished(run[k].p);
            if (r < 0) continue;
            Unit *u = &units.u[run[k].unit];
            if (r != 0) {
                char last[300];
                log_tail(u->log, last, sizeof last);
                LOG("[gamebuild] compiling %s failed: %s\n", u->src, last);
                log_gen_tail(u->log, r);  // (the compiler's errors: its last line is only "1 error generated", #123)
                snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code didn't compile: %s", last);
                ok = false;
            }
            if (r == 0 && run[k].unit > 0 && gc_seed) gc_store(u);
            done_bytes += u->bytes;
            if (run[k].unit > 0) remove(u->src);  // (generated C, done with: not kept. Unit 0 is the shipped entry file)
            run[k--] = run[--nrun];
        }
        if (!ok) break;
        if (gens_done && next == units.n && nrun == 0) break;

        // progress: the generator's share (its functions written), the compiler's (bytes of C compiled, of an
        // estimate of all of it while the generator still writes)
        double est_total = gens_done ? (double)written : gen_frac > 0.02 ? (double)written / gen_frac : 0;
        double comp_frac = est_total > 0 ? (double)done_bytes / est_total : 0;
        if (comp_frac > 1) comp_frac = 1;
        double f = 0.2 * gen_frac + 0.75 * comp_frac;
        double secs = (double)(plat_now_ns() - t0) / 1e9;
        if (gen_frac == 0) f = 0.05 * (secs / (secs + 20));  // (the generator's first pass: no count yet)
        if (f > shown) shown = f;
        if (o->progress) o->progress(shown, gen_frac < 1 && !gens_done ? "Reading the game code..." : "Recompiling...");
        sleep_ms(50);
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < nrun; k++) stop(run[k].p);  // (a failure: the rest is of no use - the failure shows at once)
    for (int i = 0; i < ngen; i++)
        if (gens[i].p && gens[i].exit < 0) stop(gens[i].p);

    // 3. link
    if (ok) {
        if (o->progress) o->progress(shown > 0.95 ? shown : 0.95, "Finishing...");
        char rsp[1100], log[1100];
        snprintf(rsp, sizeof rsp, "%s" SEP "link.rsp", work);
        snprintf(log, sizeof log, "%s" SEP "link.log", work);
        FILE *f = fopen(rsp, "wb");
        if (f) {
            for (int k = 0; k < units.n; k++) {  // (forward slashes: the response file's backslashes are escapes)
                fputc('"', f);
                for (const char *c = units.u[k].obj; *c; c++) fputc(*c == '\\' ? '/' : *c, f);
                fputs("\"\n", f);
            }
            fclose(f);
        }
        Args a = {0};
        char at[1200];
        snprintf(at, sizeof at, "@%s", rsp);
#ifdef _WIN32
        if (t.zig_rt[0]) {  // the linker itself, with the runtime built ahead of time (its flags and libraries: link.rsp)
            char opt[1200];
            add(&a, t.cc);
            add(&a, "lld-link");
            snprintf(opt, sizeof opt, "@%s" SEP "link.rsp", t.zig_rt);
            add(&a, opt);
            snprintf(opt, sizeof opt, "-LIBPATH:%s", t.zig_rt);
            add(&a, opt);
            snprintf(opt, sizeof opt, "-OUT:%s", tmp);
            add(&a, opt);
            add(&a, at);
            add(&a, t.implib);
        } else
#endif
        {
            compiler(&a, &t);
            add_split(&a, GAMELIB_SHARED);
            add(&a, "-o");
            add(&a, tmp);
            add(&a, at);
#ifdef _WIN32
            add(&a, t.implib);
#endif
        }
        PlatProc p = f ? spawn(a.v, log) : 0;
        args_free(&a);
        int r = p ? wait_for(p) : 255;
        if (r != 0) {
            char last[300];
            log_tail(log, last, sizeof last);
            LOG("[gamebuild] linking failed: %s\n", last);
            snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code didn't link: %s", last);
            ok = false;
        }
    }
    if (ok) {
        remove(lib);
        char idp[1100];
        snprintf(idp, sizeof idp, "%s.id", lib);
        FILE *f = NULL;
        if (rename(tmp, lib) != 0 || !(f = fopen(idp, "wb")) || fprintf(f, "%s\n", gamelib_id()) < 0) {
            snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code couldn't be saved");
            ok = false;
        }
        if (f) fclose(f);
    }
    gc_finish(ok, units.n);
    free(units.u);
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, ".gamebuild");  // the C, the objects, the logs
    LOG("[gamebuild] %s in %.0fs\n", ok ? "done" : "failed", (double)(plat_now_ns() - t0) / 1e9);
    if (ok && o->progress) o->progress(1, "Finishing...");
    return ok;
}

```

`runtime/gamebuild.h`:

```h
// Builds the game code library (runtime/gamelib.h) on the player's machine, from their own game files: the generator
// (tools/gen.py; shipped frozen as swgen/) turns exefs/main and exefs/sdk into C, the bundled compiler (zig/) builds
// that into <game_dir>/swgame.*. The C and the objects are deleted afterwards.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef struct {
    // now and then, from the calling thread: how far the whole build is (0..1) and what it's doing
    void (*progress)(double fraction, const char *step);
    int jobs;  // compiler processes at once (>= 1)
} GameBuildOpts;

// Builds it (a few minutes). false: why says what went wrong (details in the log).
bool gamebuild_run(const char *game_dir, const GameBuildOpts *opts, char *why, size_t why_size);
// The generator and the compiler are there (shipped builds; a source checkout with tools/venv and clang).
bool gamebuild_available(void);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

`runtime/gamelib.c`:

```c
// Loads the recompiled game code library (runtime/gamelib.h).
#include "gamelib.h"

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <dlfcn.h>
#endif

#include "game_sites.h"
#include "paths.h"
#include "rt.h"
#include "settings.h"

static const GameLibTables *g_tables;
static char g_error[256];

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the target (gamelib.h)
// GAMELIB_ARCH / GAMELIB_ARCH_COMPAT: the -march of each (Makefile GENARCH, GENARCH_COMPAT); GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT only
// where there is a compatible target.
#ifndef GAMELIB_ARCH
#define GAMELIB_ARCH ""
#endif

// Whether this CPU runs code built for arch: the x86-64 levels the Makefile uses. Another -march (a build's own
// GENARCH) isn't checked.
static bool cpu_runs(const char *arch) {
#if defined(__x86_64__)
    __builtin_cpu_init();
    if (strstr(arch, "x86-64-v3"))
        return __builtin_cpu_supports("avx2") && __builtin_cpu_supports("fma") && __builtin_cpu_supports("bmi2");
    if (strstr(arch, "x86-64-v2")) return __builtin_cpu_supports("sse4.2") && __builtin_cpu_supports("popcnt");
#endif
    (void)arch;
    return true;
}

bool gamelib_compat(void) {
#ifdef GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT
    static int compat = -1;
    if (compat < 0) {
        const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_COMPAT_CPU");
        compat = (e && *e && strcmp(e, "0")) || !cpu_runs(GAMELIB_ARCH);
    }
    return compat;
#else
    return false;
#endif
}

const char *gamelib_id(void) {
#ifdef GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT
    if (gamelib_compat()) return GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT;
#endif
    return GAMELIB_ID;
}

const char *gamelib_cpu_problem(void) {
#ifdef GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT
    if (!cpu_runs(GAMELIB_ARCH_COMPAT))
        return "a CPU with SSE4.2 (Intel Nehalem / 2008 or newer, AMD Bulldozer / 2011 or newer)";
    return NULL;
#else
    return cpu_runs(GAMELIB_ARCH) ? NULL
                                  : "a CPU with AVX2 (Intel Haswell / 2013 or newer, AMD Excavator / Zen or newer)";
#endif
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ loading

GameSites g_site;
const char *g_game_version = "";

// Required sites must be present. Optional feature groups can be absent on an
// older game build; clear their helpers instead of preventing the game loading.
static bool take_sites(const GameLibTables *t) {
    static const struct {
        const char *name;
        size_t off;
        bool optional;
    } want[] = {
#define GAME_SITE_ENTRY(n) {#n, offsetof(GameSites, n), false},
        GAME_SITES(GAME_SITE_ENTRY)
#undef GAME_SITE_ENTRY
#define GAME_SITE_ENTRY(n) {#n, offsetof(GameSites, n), true},
        GAME_SITES_OPTIONAL(GAME_SITE_ENTRY)
#undef GAME_SITE_ENTRY
    };
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof want / sizeof want[0]; i++) {
        uint32_t k = 0;
        while (k < *t->nsites && strcmp(t->sites[k].name, want[i].name)) k++;
        if (k == *t->nsites) {
            if (want[i].optional) {
                *(uint64_t *)((char *)&g_site + want[i].off) = 0;
                continue;
            }
            snprintf(g_error, sizeof g_error, "the game code has no address for %s", want[i].name);
            return false;
        }
        *(uint64_t *)((char *)&g_site + want[i].off) = t->sites[k].addr;
    }
    g_game_version = t->version;
    return true;
}

// The library's id file (<library>.id, written next to it by the build): its GAMELIB_ID, read without loading it.
static bool read_id(const char *lib, char id[128]) {
    char path[1100];
    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s.id", lib);
    memset(id, 0, 128);
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return false;
    size_t n = fread(id, 1, 127, f);
    fclose(f);
    while (n && (id[n - 1] == '\n' || id[n - 1] == '\r')) id[--n] = 0;
    return true;
}

static bool id_matches(const char *lib) {
    char id[128];
    return read_id(lib, id) && !strcmp(id, gamelib_id());
}

bool gamelib_other_cpu(const char *game_dir) {
#ifdef GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT
    char lib[1100], id[128];
    snprintf(lib, sizeof lib, "%s/%s", game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME);
    return read_id(lib, id) && !strcmp(id, gamelib_compat() ? GAMELIB_ID : GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT);
#else
    (void)game_dir;
    return false;
#endif
}

static bool exists(const char *p) {
    FILE *f = fopen(p, "rb");
    if (f) fclose(f);
    return f != NULL;
}

// The places to look, in order (gamelib.h). Returns how many were filled.
static int candidates(const char *game_dir, char out[3][1100]) {
    int n = 0;
    const char *env = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_GAME_LIB");
    if (env && *env) snprintf(out[n++], 1100, "%s", env);
    char exe_side[1024];
    if (rt_resource(GAMELIB_NAME, NULL, exe_side, sizeof exe_side) && exists(exe_side))
        snprintf(out[n++], 1100, "%s", exe_side);
    if (game_dir) snprintf(out[n++], 1100, "%s/%s", game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME);
    return n;
}

bool gamelib_present(const char *game_dir) {
    if (g_tables) return true;
    char c[3][1100];
    int n = candidates(game_dir, c);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        if (exists(c[i]) && id_matches(c[i])) return true;
    return false;
}

static const GameLibTables *open_lib(const char *path) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    HMODULE h = LoadLibraryA(path);
    if (!h) { snprintf(g_error, sizeof g_error, "can't load %s (error %lu)", path, GetLastError()); return NULL; }
    GameLibEntry entry = (GameLibEntry)(void *)GetProcAddress(h, GAMELIB_ENTRY);
#else
    void *h = dlopen(path, RTLD_NOW | RTLD_LOCAL);
    if (!h) { snprintf(g_error, sizeof g_error, "%s", dlerror()); return NULL; }
    GameLibEntry entry = (GameLibEntry)dlsym(h, GAMELIB_ENTRY);
#endif
    if (!entry) { snprintf(g_error, sizeof g_error, "%s: not game code", path); return NULL; }
    const GameLibTables *t = entry();
    if (!t || t->abi != GAMELIB_ABI || !t->id || strcmp(t->id, gamelib_id())) {
        snprintf(g_error, sizeof g_error, "%s was built for another version", path);
        return NULL;  // (left loaded: nothing of it runs)
    }
    return t;
}

bool gamelib_load(const char *game_dir, char *why, size_t why_size) {
    static bool tried;
    if (!tried) {
        tried = true;
        snprintf(g_error, sizeof g_error, "the game code hasn't been built: set up the game files on the start screen");
        char c[3][1100];
        int n = candidates(game_dir, c);
        const char *env = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_GAME_LIB");
        for (int i = 0; i < n && !g_tables; i++) {
            if (!exists(c[i])) continue;
            bool given = i == 0 && env && *env;  // SAVAGEWIND_GAME_LIB: loaded as given, the library's own id decides
            if (!given && !id_matches(c[i])) {
                snprintf(g_error, sizeof g_error, "%s was built for another version", c[i]);
                continue;
            }
            g_tables = open_lib(c[i]);
            if (g_tables && !take_sites(g_tables)) g_tables = NULL;
            if (g_tables) {
                LOG("[gamelib] %s (game version %s, %u sites)\n", c[i], g_game_version, *g_tables->nsites);
#ifdef GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT
                LOG("[gamelib] target: %s\n", gamelib_compat() ? "compatible (" GAMELIB_ARCH_COMPAT
                                                                  ", no FMA instructions: slower)"
                                                                : GAMELIB_ARCH);
#endif
                for (uint32_t k = 0; k < *g_tables->nmodules; k++) {
                    const GameLibModule *m = &g_tables->modules[k];
                    LOG("[gamelib]   %-8s %llx-%llx %llu functions\n", m->name, (unsigned long long)m->base,
                        (unsigned long long)(m->base + m->size), (unsigned long long)*m->count);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if (!g_tables && why) snprintf(why, why_size, "%s", g_error);
    return g_tables != NULL;
}

const GameLibTables *gamelib_tables(void) { return g_tables; }

#ifndef _WIN32
__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))
#endif
int simd_fma_unfused;  // (the runtime's own copy, for its code built without FMA instructions)

void gamelib_sync(void) {
    static int env = -2, cur = -1;
    if (env == -2) {  // SAVAGEWIND_FAST_FMA=0/1: in place of the setting
        const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_FAST_FMA");
        env = e && *e ? strcmp(e, "0") != 0 : -1;
    }
    int want = gamelib_compat() && (env >= 0 ? env : g_settings.fast_fma);
    if (!g_tables || want == cur) return;
    cur = want;
    if (g_tables->fma_unfused) *g_tables->fma_unfused = want;
    simd_fma_unfused = want;
    if (gamelib_compat()) LOG("[gamelib] fma: %s\n", want ? "fast (two roundings)" : "exact (as the console)");
}
```

`runtime/gamelib.h`:

```h
// The recompiled game code: a library built from the player's own game files (`make gen` + `make` in a source
// checkout, the start screen's setup otherwise; runtime/gamebuild.c) and loaded at startup (runtime/gamelib.c).
// Nothing from the game ships with the app.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "cpu.h"

#if defined(_WIN32)
#define GAMELIB_NAME "swgame.dll"
#define GAMELIB_EXPORT __declspec(dllexport)
#elif defined(__APPLE__)
#define GAMELIB_NAME "swgame.dylib"
#define GAMELIB_EXPORT __attribute__((visibility("default")))
#else
#define GAMELIB_NAME "swgame.so"
#define GAMELIB_EXPORT __attribute__((visibility("default")))
#endif

// GAMELIB_ID (-D, from the Makefile): a hash of the generator and the headers the game code is compiled against. A
// library built with another one is rebuilt, not loaded.
#ifndef GAMELIB_ID
#define GAMELIB_ID "dev"
#endif
#define GAMELIB_ABI 4

// One exefs module as the game code was generated for it: where it goes (tools/layout.py, the generated layout.c)
// and its functions. runtime/loader.c loads the module there.
typedef struct {
    const char *name;        // its exefs file: main, subsdk0..9, sdk
    uint64_t base, size;     // guest address, image size (page-rounded)
    const char *build_id;    // NSO build id (64 hex digits) of the file the code was generated from
    const uint64_t *addrs;   // sorted guest addresses
    const GuestFn *fns;      // the functions at them
    const uint64_t *count;
} GameLibModule;

// An address in the main module the runtime uses, by name (tools/game_sites.py finds them for the game version the
// code was generated from; runtime/game_sites.h).
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    uint64_t addr;
} GameLibSite;

typedef struct {
    uint32_t abi;    // GAMELIB_ABI
    const char *id;  // GAMELIB_ID
    const GameLibModule *modules;  // in load order, main first
    const uint32_t *nmodules;
    const char *version;  // the game version ("1.8.2")
    const GameLibSite *sites;
    const uint32_t *nsites;
    int *fma_unfused;  // the library's simd_fma_unfused (simd.h; only read by the compatible target's code)
} GameLibTables;

// The library's one exported function (tools/gamelib_entry.c).
typedef const GameLibTables *(*GameLibEntry)(void);
#define GAMELIB_ENTRY "swgame_tables"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

// Loads the game code for the game files in game_dir (once; later calls return the first result). Looks at
// SAVAGEWIND_GAME_LIB, next to the executable (a source checkout's build/), then game_dir. false: why says what's wrong.
bool gamelib_load(const char *game_dir, char *why, size_t why_size);
// The tables of the loaded library (NULL before gamelib_load succeeds).
const GameLibTables *gamelib_tables(void);
// Once a game frame: passes settings.h fast_fma on to the compatible target's game code (logs each change)
void gamelib_sync(void);
// True when a library usable with this build is in one of those places (without loading it).
bool gamelib_present(const char *game_dir);

// The game code's target on this CPU (#9). x86-64 builds the game code for x86-64-v3 (AVX2, FMA, BMI2: the Makefile's
// GENARCH) where the CPU has those, else for the compatible target (GENARCH_COMPAT: x86-64-v2, no FMA instructions -
// runtime/simd_softfma.h instead, slower). Each has its own id, so a library is never loaded on a CPU that can't run
// it, and a game folder moved to a PC of the other kind gets its game code built again. SAVAGEWIND_COMPAT_CPU=1 picks
// the compatible target on any CPU (to compare the two). Other hosts have one target.
bool gamelib_compat(void);
const char *gamelib_id(void);  // the id a library for this CPU has (GAMELIB_ID or GAMELIB_ID_COMPAT)
// NULL when the CPU runs the game code's target, else what it lacks ("a CPU with ...") - checked at startup
const char *gamelib_cpu_problem(void);
// True when game_dir holds a library built for the other target (a game folder moved from a PC of the other kind)
bool gamelib_other_cpu(const char *game_dir);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

`runtime/gpu_select.h`:

```h
// Vulkan adapter indices follow the startup log's zero-based enumeration.
#pragma once
#include <errno.h>
#include <limits.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

// -1 is automatic; reject malformed values rather than accidentally selecting GPU 0.
static inline int gpu_index_parse(const char *value) {
    if (!value || !*value || !strcmp(value, "auto")) return -1;
    for (const char *p = value; *p; p++) if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') return -1;
    char *end;
    errno = 0;
    long index = strtol(value, &end, 10);
    return errno || *end || index > INT_MAX ? -1 : (int)index;
}
```

`runtime/handheld.h`:

```h
// PC handhelds (included by runtime/settings.c only; settings.h has what the rest uses): this machine by its firmware's
// maker and model, and the size of its screen. A handheld not in the table but of a maker that only makes them takes
// the desktop's size (w 0). SAVAGEWIND_HANDHELD=0, 1, deck or WxH decides it (tests).
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#ifdef _WIN32
#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#include <windows.h>
#endif

typedef struct { const char *vendor, *product; short w, h; bool deck; } HandheldModel;
static const HandheldModel k_handhelds[] = {
    {"Valve", "Jupiter", 1280, 800, true},    // Steam Deck LCD
    {"Valve", "Galileo", 1280, 800, true},    // Steam Deck OLED
    {"ASUS", "RC71L", 1920, 1080, false},     // ROG Ally
    {"ASUS", "RC72L", 1920, 1080, false},     // ROG Ally X
    {"ASUS", "RC73", 1920, 1080, false},      // ROG Xbox Ally, Ally X
    {"LENOVO", "83E1", 2560, 1600, false},    // Legion Go
    {"LENOVO", "83L3", 1920, 1200, false},    // Legion Go S
    {"LENOVO", "83N6", 1920, 1200, false},
    {"LENOVO", "83Q2", 1920, 1200, false},
    {"LENOVO", "83Q3", 1920, 1200, false},
    {"LENOVO", "83N0", 1920, 1200, false},    // Legion Go 2
    {"LENOVO", "83N1", 1920, 1200, false},
    {"Micro-Star", "Claw A1M", 1920, 1080, false},
    {"Micro-Star", "Claw 8", 1920, 1200, false},
    {"Micro-Star", "Claw 7", 1920, 1200, false},
    {"Micro-Star", "Claw", 0, 0, false},
    {"ZOTAC", "ZONE", 1920, 1080, false},
    {"GPD", "G1617", 1920, 1080, false},      // Win Mini
    {"GPD", "G1618", 1920, 1080, false},      // Win 4
    {"AYANEO", "", 0, 0, false},
    {"AYADEVICE", "", 0, 0, false},
    {"ONE-NETBOOK", "", 0, 0, false},
};

static void handheld_firmware(char *vendor, char *product, size_t n) {
    vendor[0] = product[0] = 0;
#ifdef _WIN32
    static const char key[] = "HARDWARE\\DESCRIPTION\\System\\BIOS";
    DWORD s = (DWORD)n;
    if (RegGetValueA(HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, key, "SystemManufacturer", RRF_RT_REG_SZ, NULL, vendor, &s)) vendor[0] = 0;
    s = (DWORD)n;
    if (RegGetValueA(HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, key, "SystemProductName", RRF_RT_REG_SZ, NULL, product, &s)) product[0] = 0;
#elif defined(__linux__)
    FILE *f = fopen("/sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/sys_vendor", "r");
    if (f) { if (!fgets(vendor, (int)n, f)) vendor[0] = 0; fclose(f); }
    f = fopen("/sys/devices/virtual/dmi/id/product_name", "r");
    if (f) { if (!fgets(product, (int)n, f)) product[0] = 0; fclose(f); }
    vendor[strcspn(vendor, "\r\n")] = 0, product[strcspn(product, "\r\n")] = 0;
#else
    (void)n;
#endif
}

typedef struct { bool on, deck; int w, h; } Handheld;

static Handheld handheld_detect(void) {
    Handheld h = {0};
    const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_HANDHELD");
    if (e && *e) {
        int w, ht;
        if (!strcmp(e, "deck")) h = (Handheld){true, true, 1280, 800};
        else if (sscanf(e, "%dx%d", &w, &ht) == 2) h = (Handheld){true, false, w, ht};
        else h.on = atoi(e) != 0;
        return h;
    }
    char vendor[128], product[128];
    handheld_firmware(vendor, product, sizeof vendor);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof k_handhelds / sizeof k_handhelds[0]; i++) {
        const HandheldModel *m = &k_handhelds[i];
        if (strstr(vendor, m->vendor) && strstr(product, m->product)) return (Handheld){true, m->deck, m->w, m->h};
    }
    e = getenv("SteamDeck");  // (Steam's own, in Gaming Mode)
    if (e && atoi(e) != 0) h = (Handheld){true, true, 1280, 800};
    return h;
}
```

`runtime/hle.h`:

```h
// Registration of host implementations for guest symbols.
#pragma once
#include <stdlib.h>
// Environment lookups that run every frame / per call: looked up once per call site (the variables don't change
// while the game runs). ENV("SAVAGEWIND_X") -> const char * or NULL.
#define ENV(name) ({ static const char *env_v_; static int env_i_; if (!env_i_) { env_v_ = getenv(name); env_i_ = 1; } env_v_; })

#include "rt.h"

typedef struct { const char *name; HostFn fn; } HleImplEntry;

// HLE_FUNC("mangled_symbol", c_function) binds a guest import to a host function.
#define HLE_CAT2(a, b) a##b
#define HLE_CAT(a, b) HLE_CAT2(a, b)
#ifdef __APPLE__
#define HLE_SECTION "__DATA,__hle_impls"
#elif defined(__linux__)
#define HLE_SECTION "hle_impls"  // ELF: the linker defines __start_ / __stop_ for C-identifier section names
#else
#define HLE_SECTION ".hle$m"  // between the .hle$a / .hle$z markers in runtime/dispatch.c
#endif
#define HLE_FUNC(sym, fn)                                                                   \
    static void fn(Cpu *c);                                                                 \
    __attribute__((used, section(HLE_SECTION))) static const HleImplEntry                   \
        HLE_CAT(hle_entry_, __LINE__) = {sym, fn};                                          \
    static void fn(Cpu *c)

// Per-boot host state. RT_ON_RESET(fn) { ... } runs when the game is torn down for an in-place reboot (back to the
// start screen: runtime/main.c), after every guest thread has stopped and before
// guest memory is wiped: drop guest pointers, kernel handles and lazily-initialised state, so the next
// boot starts as from a fresh process. (Settings, the window, the GPU device and ENV() lookups stay.)
typedef void (*ResetFn)(void);
#ifdef __APPLE__
#define RESET_SECTION "__DATA,__rt_reset"
#elif defined(__linux__)
#define RESET_SECTION "resets"
#else
#define RESET_SECTION ".rst$m"  // between the .rst$a / .rst$z markers in runtime/main.c
#endif
#define RT_ON_RESET(fn)                                                                     \
    static void fn(void);                                                                   \
    __attribute__((used, section(RESET_SECTION))) static const ResetFn                      \
        HLE_CAT(reset_entry_, __LINE__) = fn;                                               \
    static void fn(void)

#define RES_OK 0u
#define MAKE_RESULT(module, desc) ((uint32_t)(module) | ((uint32_t)(desc) << 9))
```

```c
static const char *const k_mouse[5] = {"Mouse Left", "Mouse Middle", "Mouse Right", "Mouse Back", "Mouse Forward"};

const char *bind_key_label(int sc) {
    if (sc > BIND_MOUSE && sc <= BIND_MOUSE_LAST) return k_mouse[sc - BIND_MOUSE - 1];
    if (sc <= 0 || sc >= SDL_SCANCODE_COUNT) return "(none)";
    const char *n = SDL_GetScancodeName((SDL_Scancode)sc);
    return n && *n ? n : "(unnamed key)";
}

// Steam Input (a Deck's Gaming Mode) shows every controller as a virtual one of Valve's, an "Xbox 360" pad; SDL gives
// the controller behind it (type, name) when Steam says, often it doesn't (an 8BitDo: "Steam Virtual Gamepad"). So:
// PlayStation by its type; Nintendo's by theirs; a controller not Valve's by its type (Xbox, or none of these); a Valve pad is the Deck's own controls when it says so (the Deck's product, its
// name) or, saying nothing, when it is the first one opened (Steam Input's for the Deck's controls, there from boot) in
// Steam Deck mode; Steam Input's for another controller, an Xbox one. (A Valve vendor alone made each the Deck's.)
int bind_pad_family(int type, int vendor, int product, const char *name, bool first) {
    if (type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_PS3 || type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_PS4 || type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_PS5) return 2;
    if (type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_NINTENDO_SWITCH_PRO || type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_NINTENDO_SWITCH_JOYCON_LEFT ||
        type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_NINTENDO_SWITCH_JOYCON_RIGHT || type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_NINTENDO_SWITCH_JOYCON_PAIR)
        return 0;
    if (vendor != BIND_VALVE_VENDOR) return type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_XBOX360 || type == SDL_GAMEPAD_TYPE_XBOXONE ? 1 : 0;
    if (product == BIND_DECK_PRODUCT || (name && strstr(name, "Steam Deck"))) return 3;
    bool unnamed = !name || !*name || strstr(name, "Steam Virtual") || strstr(name, "Steam Controller");
    return unnamed && first && settings_steam_deck() ? 3 : 1;
}

int bind_label_family(void) {
    extern int input_pad_family(void);  // runtime/hle/input.c (the game's open pad, or SAVAGEWIND_PAD_TYPE)
    int f = input_pad_family();
    if (f) return f;
    int n = 0;  // start screen: input.c hasn't opened a pad yet
    SDL_JoystickID *ids = SDL_GetGamepads(&n);
    if (ids && n > 0)
        f = bind_pad_family(SDL_GetGamepadTypeForID(ids[0]), SDL_GetGamepadVendorForID(ids[0]),
                            SDL_GetGamepadProductForID(ids[0]), SDL_GetGamepadNameForID(ids[0]), true);
    SDL_free(ids);
    return f;
}

static void result(int kind, int dev, int slot, int other);
static int act_default(int dev, int id);
static void act_refresh(void);

void bind_reset(int dev) {
    if (dev == BIND_DEV_PAD) memcpy(g_bind_pad, k_def_pad, sizeof g_bind_pad);
    else memcpy(g_bind_key, k_def_key, sizeof g_bind_key);
    for (int id = 0; id < ACT_COUNT; id++) act_set(dev, id, ACT_FOLLOW);
    LOG("[input] %s bindings reset to the defaults\n", dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? "controller" : "keyboard");
    result(5, dev, -1, -1);
}

void bind_reset_slot(int slot) {
    if (bind_slot_is_action(slot)) {
        act_set(BIND_DEV_PAD, slot - BIND_ACTION, ACT_FOLLOW);
        act_set(BIND_DEV_KEY, slot - BIND_ACTION, ACT_FOLLOW);
        return;
    }
    if (slot < 0 || slot >= BIND_KEY_COUNT) return;
    g_bind_key[slot] = k_def_key[slot];
    if (bind_pad_slot(slot)) g_bind_pad[slot] = k_def_pad[slot];
    act_refresh();
}

// The controller's confirm and back buttons swapped: the Switch's A and B, and every action on either of the two host
// buttons they are on, take each other's (Nintendo's A on the right becomes the bottom one, the Xbox convention).
// Nothing else changes, and swapping again undoes it.
void bind_swap_ab(void) {
    int a = g_bind_pad[BIND_A], b = g_bind_pad[BIND_B];
    if (a < 0 || b < 0 || a == b) return;
    g_bind_pad[BIND_A] = (int16_t)b, g_bind_pad[BIND_B] = (int16_t)a;
    for (int id = 0; id < ACT_COUNT; id++) {
        if (g_act_pad[id] == a) act_set(BIND_DEV_PAD, id, b);
        else if (g_act_pad[id] == b) act_set(BIND_DEV_PAD, id, a);
    }
    LOG("[input] controller: confirm and back swapped (A on %s, B on %s)\n", k_pad_ini[b], k_pad_ini[a]);
    result(6, BIND_DEV_PAD, -1, -1);
}

bool bind_is_default(int dev) {
    for (int id = 0; id < ACT_COUNT; id++)
        if (!bind_is_default_slot(dev, BIND_ACTION + id)) return false;
    return dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? !memcmp(g_bind_pad, k_def_pad, sizeof g_bind_pad) : !memcmp(g_bind_key, k_def_key, sizeof g_bind_key);
}

bool bind_is_default_slot(int dev, int slot) {
    if (bind_slot_is_action(slot)) return act_default(dev, slot - BIND_ACTION) ==
        (dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? g_act_pad[slot - BIND_ACTION] : g_act_key[slot - BIND_ACTION]);
    if (slot < 0 || slot >= BIND_KEY_COUNT) return true;
    return dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? g_bind_pad[slot] == k_def_pad[slot] : g_bind_key[slot] == k_def_key[slot];
}


// ------------------------------------------------------------------ capture
static _Atomic int cap_dev = -1, cap_slot = -1;
static _Atomic uint64_t cap_deadline;
static _Atomic int res_kind, res_dev, res_slot, res_other, res_serial;

static void result(int kind, int dev, int slot, int other) {
    res_kind = kind, res_dev = dev, res_slot = slot, res_other = other;
    res_serial++;
}

void bind_capture_begin(int dev, int slot) {
    if (!bind_slot_is_action(slot) &&
        (slot < 0 || slot >= BIND_KEY_COUNT || (dev == BIND_DEV_PAD && !bind_pad_slot(slot)))) return;
    if (dev == BIND_DEV_ANY && !bind_slot_is_action(slot) && slot >= BIND_KEY_COUNT) return;
    cap_deadline = SDL_GetTicks() + BIND_CAPTURE_MS;
    cap_slot = slot;
    cap_dev = dev;
}

void bind_capture_cancel(void) {
    if (cap_dev < 0) return;
    result(3, cap_dev, cap_slot, -1);
    cap_dev = -1;
}

bool bind_capture_active(int *dev, int *slot, int *ms_left) {
    int d = cap_dev;
    if (d >= 0 && SDL_GetTicks() >= cap_deadline) { result(4, d, cap_slot, -1); cap_dev = d = -1; }
    if (dev) *dev = d;
    if (slot) *slot = d >= 0 ? cap_slot : -1;
    if (ms_left) *ms_left = d >= 0 ? (int)(cap_deadline - SDL_GetTicks()) : 0;
    return d >= 0;
}

int bind_last_result(int *dev, int *slot, int *other, int *serial) {
    if (dev) *dev = res_dev;
    if (slot) *slot = res_slot;
    if (other) *other = res_other;
    if (serial) *serial = res_serial;
    return res_kind;
}

// Bind `host` to `slot`; only legacy host slots swap. Actions, Walk, Tilt and gyro allow shared inputs.
static void assign(int dev, int slot, int host) {
    if (bind_slot_is_action(slot)) {  // an action may share its key with any other: nothing swaps
        act_set(dev, slot - BIND_ACTION, host);
        LOG("[input] %s action %d -> %s\n", dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? "controller" : "keyboard", slot - BIND_ACTION,
            dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? k_pad_ini[host] : bind_key_label(host));
        result(1, dev, slot, -1);
        return;
    }
    int16_t *t = dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? g_bind_pad : g_bind_key;
    int other = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < BIND_KEY_COUNT; i++)
        if (i != slot && (dev == BIND_DEV_KEY ? bind_key_same_context(i, slot) : (bind_pad_slot(i) && bind_key_same_context(i, slot))) && t[i] == host) {
            other = i;
            t[i] = t[slot];
        }
    t[slot] = (int16_t)host;
    LOG("[input] %s %s -> %s%s%s%s\n", dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? "controller" : "keyboard", k_names[slot],
        dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? k_pad_ini[host] : bind_key_label(host), other >= 0 ? " (swapped with " : "",
        other >= 0 ? k_names[other] : "", other >= 0 ? ")" : "");
    if (other >= 0) LOG("[input]   %s -> %s\n", k_names[other], dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? bind_pad_label(t[other], 0) : bind_key_label(t[other]));
    result(other >= 0 ? 2 : 1, dev, slot, other);
    act_refresh();
}

bool bind_capture_event(const SDL_Event *e) {
    int dev = cap_dev;
    if (dev < 0) return false;
    // which sides this capture takes (BIND_DEV_ANY: both, the controller only where the input has a controller side)
    const bool kd = dev != BIND_DEV_PAD;
    const bool pd = dev == BIND_DEV_PAD || (dev == BIND_DEV_ANY && (bind_slot_is_action(cap_slot) || bind_pad_slot(cap_slot)));
    switch (e->type) {
    case SDL_EVENT_KEY_DOWN:
        if (e->key.repeat) return true;
        if (e->key.scancode == SDL_SCANCODE_ESCAPE) { bind_capture_cancel(); return true; }
        // F1 (menu), F9 (frame dump), F11 (fullscreen), F12 and the key left of 1 (the console), and PrintScreen
        // (screenshot) stay the overlay's; a controller capture ignores keys
        if (!kd || e->key.scancode == SDL_SCANCODE_F1 || e->key.scancode == SDL_SCANCODE_F9 ||
            e->key.scancode == SDL_SCANCODE_F11 || e->key.scancode == SDL_SCANCODE_F12 ||
            e->key.scancode == SDL_SCANCODE_PRINTSCREEN ||
            e->key.scancode == SDL_SCANCODE_GRAVE || e->key.scancode >= SDL_SCANCODE_COUNT) return true;
        cap_dev = -1;
        assign(BIND_DEV_KEY, cap_slot, e->key.scancode);
        return true;
    // Keep host held-state current even while capturing. Swallowing the release of the confirm key / button left
    // it down in input.c, so ending a capture pressed confirm again and reopened the binding row (#175).
    case SDL_EVENT_KEY_UP:
        return false;
    case SDL_EVENT_TEXT_INPUT:
        return true;
    case SDL_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON_DOWN:  // a keyboard binding can be a mouse button (a controller capture ignores it)
        if (!kd || e->button.button < SDL_BUTTON_LEFT || e->button.button > SDL_BUTTON_X2) return true;
        cap_dev = -1;
        assign(BIND_DEV_KEY, cap_slot, BIND_MOUSE + e->button.button);
        return true;
    case SDL_EVENT_MOUSE_BUTTON_UP:
        return false;
    case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_DOWN:
        // Home / Guide opens the menu; a keyboard capture ignores the controller (it times out, or Esc)
        if (!pd || e->gbutton.button == SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_GUIDE || e->gbutton.button >= SDL_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_COUNT) return true;
        cap_dev = -1;
        assign(BIND_DEV_PAD, cap_slot, e->gbutton.button);
        return true;
    case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_BUTTON_UP:
        return false;
    case SDL_EVENT_GAMEPAD_AXIS_MOTION:
        if ((e->gaxis.axis == SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_LEFT_TRIGGER || e->gaxis.axis == SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_RIGHT_TRIGGER) &&
            e->gaxis.value <= 16000) return false;  // a trigger may also have been bound to confirm
        if (pd && e->gaxis.value > 16000 &&
            (e->gaxis.axis == SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_LEFT_TRIGGER || e->gaxis.axis == SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_RIGHT_TRIGGER)) {
            cap_dev = -1;
            assign(BIND_DEV_PAD, cap_slot, e->gaxis.axis == SDL_GAMEPAD_AXIS_LEFT_TRIGGER ? PADB_LTRIGGER : PADB_RTRIGGER);
        }
        return true;  // (sticks: no menu movement while waiting)
    default:
        return false;
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ savagewind.ini
static bool act_settings_load(const char *key, const char *val);
static void act_migrate(int dev, int slot);
bool bind_settings_load(const char *key, const char *val) {
    if (!strncmp(key, "act_", 4)) return act_settings_load(key, val);
    bool pad = !strncmp(key, "bind_pad_", 9), kb = !strncmp(key, "bind_key_", 9);
    if (!pad && !kb) return false;
    for (int i = 0; i < BIND_KEY_COUNT; i++) {
        if (strcmp(key + 9, k_ini[i]) || (pad && !bind_pad_slot(i))) continue;
        if (pad) {
            int h = !strcmp(val, "none") ? -1 : bind_pad_from_name(val);
            if (h < 0 && strcmp(val, "none")) continue;
            g_bind_pad[i] = (int16_t)h;
        } else {
            int sc = strcmp(val, "none") ? (int)SDL_GetScancodeFromName(val) : SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN;
            for (int m = 0; m < 5; m++)
                if (!strcmp(val, k_mouse[m])) sc = BIND_MOUSE + 1 + m;
            if (sc == SDL_SCANCODE_UNKNOWN && strcmp(val, "none")) continue;
            g_bind_key[i] = (int16_t)sc;
        }
        if (i < BIND_PAD_COUNT) act_migrate(pad ? BIND_DEV_PAD : BIND_DEV_KEY, i);
    }
    act_refresh();
    return true;
}

static void act_settings_save(FILE *f);
void bind_settings_save(FILE *f) {
    act_settings_save(f);
    for (int i = 0; i < BIND_KEY_COUNT; i++)
        if (bind_pad_slot(i) && g_bind_pad[i] != k_def_pad[i] && g_bind_pad[i] >= -1 && g_bind_pad[i] < PADB_HOST_COUNT)
            fprintf(f, "bind_pad_%s = %s\n", k_ini[i], g_bind_pad[i] < 0 ? "none" : k_pad_ini[g_bind_pad[i]]);
    for (int i = 0; i < BIND_KEY_COUNT; i++)
        if (g_bind_key[i] != k_def_key[i])
            fprintf(f, "bind_key_%s = %s\n", k_ini[i], g_bind_key[i] ? bind_key_label(g_bind_key[i]) : "none");
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ per-action bindings
// Each action owns its host defaults, copied from the factory Switch layout. ACT_FOLLOW remains an API reset
// command for the existing UI, never a stored binding. Only actions differing from their defaults use host answers.
int16_t g_act_key[ACT_COUNT], g_act_pad[ACT_COUNT];
static bool a_schema;  // schema 2 or newer: legacy raw-button migration has already happened
static _Atomic uint64_t a_custom;  // at least one device differs from its factory action default (or live mask swapped)
static _Atomic uint64_t a_mask_diff;  // k_masks[id] != k_masks_190[id] at the last act_refresh()
static uint64_t a_explicit_key, a_explicit_pad;  // ini/action edits take precedence over legacy raw-button lines

static const uint32_t *k_masks;  // the game's table: one pad mask (sead::Controller bit) per action
static _Atomic uint64_t a_keys, a_pads;  // held now, by the keyboard side / the controller side (main thread)
static _Atomic uint64_t a_hold, a_trig;  // frozen at the last poll: what the game's queries see
static _Atomic bool a_live;

// What the game calls them. NULL until a run with the logging build (SAVAGEWIND_ACTLOG) has seen what an action does;
// only the ones whose use is certain are named.
static const char *const k_act_names[ACT_COUNT] = {
    [0] = "Interact", [2] = "Jump", [3] = "Attack", [5] = "Shield bash", [9] = "Lower shield", [10] = "Crouch step", [11] = "Dodge",
    [12] = "Sprint", [13] = "Guard / lock on", [14] = "Cancel", [15] = "Scope", [17] = "Crouch", [18] = "Bow",
    [19] = "Paraglider", [25] = "Dismount", [26] = "Speed up horse", [27] = "Pet horse", [28] = "Throw weapon", [31] = "Take photo",
    [33] = "Aim rune", [34] = "Activate rune", [35] = "Call horse", [36] = "Water spin attack", [37] = "Throw distance", [38] = "Cycle accelerate", [39] = "Cycle brake", [40] = "Cycle jump",
};
// No code in the game reaches these by a number (they may still be asked by a computed one): kept off the page.
// 32 is asked while wall climbing but nothing happens with the answer, so a row for it would only mislead.
#define ACT_HIDDEN_MASK ((1ull << 1) | (1ull << 4) | (1ull << 6) | (1ull << 7) | (1ull << 8) | (1ull << 16) | \
                         (1ull << 20) | (1ull << 21) | (1ull << 22) | (1ull << 23) | (1ull << 24) | (1ull << 29) | \
                         (1ull << 30) | (1ull << 32))

const char *act_name(int id) { return id >= 0 && id < ACT_COUNT ? k_act_names[id] : NULL; }
bool act_hidden(int id) { return id >= 0 && id < ACT_COUNT && (ACT_HIDDEN_MASK >> id & 1); }

// The game's mask bits are sead's pad indices (open-ead: PadIdx), not the Switch's nn::hid bits.
static int mask_button(uint32_t m) {
    switch (m) {
    case 0x1: return BIND_A;
    case 0x2: return BIND_B;
    case 0x4: return BIND_ZL;
    case 0x8: return BIND_X;
    case 0x10: return BIND_Y;
    case 0x20: return BIND_ZR;
    case 0x40: return BIND_RSTICK;
    case 0x80: return BIND_LSTICK;
    case 0x2000: return BIND_L;
    case 0x4000: return BIND_R;
    case 0x10000: return BIND_UP;
    case 0x20000: return BIND_DOWN;
    default: return -1;
    }
}

// The game's table for 1.9.0 (all 41 masks): factory defaults and legacy migration always use this fixed table.
// act_switch_button also uses it before the game has supplied its live table.
static const uint32_t k_masks_190[ACT_COUNT] = {
    0x1, 0x2, 0x8, 0x10, 0x8, 0x1, 0x8, 0x2, 0x8, 0x2, 0x8, 0x8, 0x2, 0x4, 0x2, 0x40, 0x1, 0x80, 0x20, 0x8, 0x2,
    0x10000, 0x20000, 0x10000, 0x20000, 0x2, 0x1, 0x2000, 0x4000, 0x4, 0x2, 0x4000, 0x4000, 0x2000, 0x1, 0x20000,
    0x10, 0x20000, 0x1, 0x2, 0x2000};

int act_switch_button(int id) {
    if (id < 0 || id >= ACT_COUNT) return -1;
    return mask_button((k_masks ? k_masks : k_masks_190)[id]);
}

static int act_default(int dev, int id) {
    int b = mask_button(k_masks_190[id]);
    if (b < 0) return ACT_NONE;
    return dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? k_def_pad[b] : k_def_key[b];
}

bool act_is_default(int id) {
    return id < 0 || id >= ACT_COUNT ||
        (g_act_key[id] == act_default(BIND_DEV_KEY, id) && g_act_pad[id] == act_default(BIND_DEV_PAD, id));
}

static void act_refresh(void) {
    uint64_t custom = 0, diff = 0;
    for (int id = 0; id < ACT_COUNT; id++) {
        bool swapped = k_masks && k_masks[id] != k_masks_190[id];
        if (swapped) diff |= 1ull << id;
        if (!act_is_default(id) || swapped) custom |= 1ull << id;
    }
    a_mask_diff = diff;
    a_custom = custom;
}

void act_set(int dev, int id, int host) {
    if (id < 0 || id >= ACT_COUNT) return;
    if (host < 0 && host != ACT_NONE) host = act_default(dev, id);
    if (dev == BIND_DEV_PAD) {
        g_act_pad[id] = (int16_t)host;
        a_explicit_pad |= 1ull << id;
    } else {
        g_act_key[id] = (int16_t)host;
        a_explicit_key |= 1ull << id;
    }
    act_refresh();
}

void act_reset(void) {
    for (int i = 0; i < ACT_COUNT; i++) {
        g_act_key[i] = (int16_t)act_default(BIND_DEV_KEY, i);
        g_act_pad[i] = (int16_t)act_default(BIND_DEV_PAD, i);
    }
    a_explicit_key = a_explicit_pad = 0;
    act_refresh();
}

// Initialized before settings or either Controls page can read the public arrays (also in standalone tests).
__attribute__((constructor)) static void act_init(void) { act_reset(); }

void act_masks(const uint32_t *table) {
    k_masks = table;
    act_refresh();
}

// Applied while reading legacy ini lines, independent of line order and independently for each device.
static void act_migrate(int dev, int slot) {
    if (a_schema) return;
    uint64_t explicit = dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? a_explicit_pad : a_explicit_key;
    int16_t *actions = dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? g_act_pad : g_act_key;
    int host = dev == BIND_DEV_PAD ? g_bind_pad[slot] : g_bind_key[slot];
    for (int id = 0; id < ACT_COUNT; id++)
        if (!(explicit >> id & 1) && mask_button(k_masks_190[id]) == slot)
            actions[id] = host < 0 || (dev == BIND_DEV_KEY && !host) ? ACT_NONE : (int16_t)host;
    act_refresh();
}

uint64_t act_scan_keys(uint64_t key_buttons, int (*held)(int scancode)) {
    (void)key_buttons;  // kept for callers; actions read host inputs, never the live Switch layout
    uint64_t out = 0, custom = a_custom;
    for (int id = 0; id < ACT_COUNT; id++) {
        if (!(custom >> id & 1)) continue;
        int k = g_act_key[id];
        out |= (uint64_t)(k > 0 && held(k)) << id;
    }
    return out;
}

uint64_t act_scan_pad(uint64_t pad_buttons, uint32_t host_buttons) {
    (void)pad_buttons;
    uint64_t out = 0, custom = a_custom;
    for (int id = 0; id < ACT_COUNT; id++) {
        if (!(custom >> id & 1)) continue;
        int k = g_act_pad[id];
        if (k_masks && k_masks[id] != k_masks_190[id] && k == act_default(BIND_DEV_PAD, id)) {
            int b = mask_button(k_masks[id]);
            if (b >= 0) k = k_def_pad[b];
        }
        out |= (uint64_t)(k >= 0 && k < PADB_HOST_COUNT && (host_buttons >> k & 1)) << id;
    }
    return out;
}

static bool act_held_host(int id, int (*held)(int scancode), uint32_t host) {
    if (id < 0 || id >= ACT_COUNT) return false;
    int k = g_act_key[id], p = g_act_pad[id];
    return (k > 0 && held && held(k)) || (p >= 0 && p < PADB_HOST_COUNT && (host >> p & 1));
}

// During gameplay, decouple in-game action buttons (Y/X/A/B) from raw menu rebinds
// so that rebinding a menu slot (e.g. "Menu: sort / sensor") never hijacks actions in play.
// Only the raw keyboard/pad mask is rewritten; script/console/cursor/auto-continue bits stay untouched.
uint64_t act_gameplay_buttons(uint64_t raw, int (*held)(int scancode), uint32_t host) {
    raw &= ~((1ull << BIND_Y) | (1ull << BIND_X) | (1ull << BIND_A) | (1ull << BIND_B));
    if (act_held_host(3, held, host) || act_held_host(36, held, host)) raw |= 1ull << BIND_Y;
    if (act_held_host(2, held, host)) raw |= 1ull << BIND_X;
    if (act_held_host(0, held, host)) raw |= 1ull << BIND_A;
    if (act_held_host(12, held, host) || act_held_host(14, held, host)) raw |= 1ull << BIND_B;
    return raw;
}

// Each side publishes its own half (the keyboard and the controller change at different times)
void act_publish(uint64_t keys, uint64_t pads) {
    if (keys != ~0ull) a_keys = keys;
    if (pads != ~0ull) a_pads = pads;
}

// ---- logging build: SAVAGEWIND_ACTLOG=1 prints which actions the game asks about, from where, and which of them its
// own pad object answers yes to (the unswapped mask test), once per change, so a scripted run that presses one Switch
// button at a time shows what each action is.
static int act_log_on(void) {
    static int on = -1;
    if (on < 0) on = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_ACTLOG") != NULL;
    return on;
}
static _Atomic uint64_t l_seen[2], l_true[2], l_last[2];
static _Atomic uint64_t l_pads[4];
static _Atomic unsigned l_polls, l_queries[2];
// for the on-screen list (written on the game thread, read by the menu layer)
static _Atomic unsigned l_cnt[2][ACT_COUNT];
static _Atomic uint32_t l_last_ms[ACT_COUNT];
static _Atomic uint64_t l_holding;

bool act_log_enabled(void) { return act_log_on(); }

int act_log_rows(ActLogRow *out, int max) {
    ActLogRow all[ACT_COUNT];
    int n = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < ACT_COUNT; i++) {
        unsigned p = l_cnt[1][i], h = l_cnt[0][i];
        if (!p && !h) continue;
        ActLogRow r = {i, p, h, l_last_ms[i], (l_holding >> i & 1) != 0};
        int j = n++;
        while (j > 0 && all[j - 1].last_ms < r.last_ms) { all[j] = all[j - 1]; j--; }  // (newest first)
        all[j] = r;
    }
    if (n > max) n = max;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) out[i] = all[i];
    return n;
}

static void act_log_ids(char *out, size_t n, uint64_t set) {
    size_t o = 0;
    out[0] = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < ACT_COUNT && o + 6 < n; i++)
        if (set >> i & 1) o += (size_t)snprintf(out + o, n - o, "%s%d", o ? "," : "", i);
    if (!o) snprintf(out, n, "-");
}

static void act_log_query(int kind, uint64_t pad, unsigned id, uint64_t lr, bool custom) {
    l_queries[kind]++;
    if (id >= ACT_COUNT || !pad) return;
    if (!(l_seen[kind] >> id & 1)) {
        l_seen[kind] |= 1ull << id;
        LOG("[act] %s of action %u: first asked from %llx on pad object %llx (mask %#x)\n", kind ? "pressed" : "held", id,
            (unsigned long long)lr, (unsigned long long)pad, k_masks ? k_masks[id] : 0);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {  // distinct pad objects
        uint64_t p = l_pads[i];
        if (p == pad) break;
        if (!p) { l_pads[i] = pad; LOG("[act] pad object %llx asked\n", (unsigned long long)pad); break; }
    }
    if (custom) return;  // an action with a binding of its own is logged by what the game is told (rt_act_query)
    uint32_t word = *(const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(pad + (kind ? 0x10 : 0x11c));
    if (k_masks && (word & k_masks[id])) l_true[kind] |= 1ull << id;
}

static void act_log_poll(void) {
    unsigned n = ++l_polls;
    for (int kind = 0; kind < 2; kind++) {
        uint64_t t = l_true[kind];
        l_true[kind] = 0;
        if (t == l_last[kind]) continue;
        uint64_t fresh = t & ~l_last[kind];
        l_last[kind] = t;
        if (!kind) l_holding = t;
        uint32_t ms = SDL_GetTicks();
        for (int i = 0; i < ACT_COUNT; i++)
            if (fresh >> i & 1) { l_cnt[kind][i]++; l_last_ms[i] = ms; }
        char ids[200];
        act_log_ids(ids, sizeof ids, t);
        LOG("[act] poll %u: game says %s: %s (t=%.1f s)\n", n, kind ? "pressed" : "held", ids, ms / 1000.0);
    }
    if (n % 600 == 0) {
        LOG("[act] %u polls: %u held queries, %u pressed queries\n", n, (unsigned)l_queries[0], (unsigned)l_queries[1]);
        l_queries[0] = l_queries[1] = 0;
    }
}

// ---- the HUD's A prompt (Talk, Pick up, Open, Climb down...) comes first
// An action moved onto the same button as Interact (Jump on A, say) would also fire whenever that button answers the
// prompt: picking something up while swimming dashed, talking jumped. While the prompt is on screen, those actions are
// "not pressed": the button does what the prompt says, as on the Switch where they are different buttons. The actions
// the game itself puts on Switch A (Interact, Activate rune, ...) keep answering. The prompt: DoCommand_00's N_A_00,
// shown while the A prompt is up (its N_InOut_00 fades the whole HUD group out).
static uint64_t pane_child(uint64_t pane, const char *name, unsigned depth, unsigned *budget) {
    if (pane < GUEST_LO || pane >= GUEST_HI - 0x100 || depth > 16 || !*budget) return 0;
    --*budget;
    if (!strncmp((const char *)(uintptr_t)(pane + 0xb8), name, 24)) return pane;
    uint64_t head = pane + 0x20, link = LD64(head + 8);  // (children: links 8 bytes into the child)
    for (int k = 0; link >= GUEST_LO && link < GUEST_HI && link != head && k < 64 && *budget; k++, link = LD64(link + 8)) {
        uint64_t found = pane_child(link - 8, name, depth + 1, budget);
        if (found) return found;
    }
    return 0;
}
static bool named(uint64_t obj, unsigned off, const char *name) {
    uint64_t p = obj >= GUEST_LO && obj < GUEST_HI - 0x100 ? LD64(obj + off) : 0;
    return p >= GUEST_LO && p < GUEST_HI - 64 && !strcmp((const char *)(uintptr_t)p, name);
}
static bool interact_prompt_up(void) {
    static uint64_t screen, group, hud;  // DoCommand_00, its N_A_00 and N_InOut_00 (found again when the HUD is rebuilt)
    if (!g_site.screen_mgr) return false;
    if (!named(screen, 0xd0, "DoCommand_00") || !group || !hud ||
        strncmp((const char *)(uintptr_t)(group + 0xb8), "N_A_00", 8) ||
        strncmp((const char *)(uintptr_t)(hud + 0xb8), "N_InOut_00", 12)) {
        screen = group = hud = 0;
        uint64_t mgr = LD64(g_site.screen_mgr), arr = mgr ? LD64(mgr + 0x30) : 0;
        unsigned count = mgr ? LD32(mgr + 0x28) : 0;
        for (unsigned i = 0; arr && i < count && i < 256 && !screen; i++)
            if (named(LD64(arr + 8 * i), 0xd0, "DoCommand_00")) screen = LD64(arr + 8 * i);
        uint64_t layout = screen ? LD64(screen + 0x30) : 0, root = layout >= GUEST_LO ? LD64(layout + 0x18) : 0;
        unsigned budget = 64;
        hud = pane_child(root, "N_InOut_00", 0, &budget);
        budget = 64;
        group = pane_child(hud, "N_A_00", 0, &budget);
        if (!group) { screen = group = hud = 0; return false; }
    }
    return (LD8(group + 0x58) & 1) && (LD8(hud + 0x58) & 1) && LD8(hud + 0x5a) >= 0x80;  // (visible; global alpha)
}

// When the prompt was last seen (each controller poll): answering it takes it away within the same frame, before the
// game asks about Jump, so the press that picked something up still counts as the prompt's for a moment
#define PROMPT_GRACE_MS 250
static _Atomic uint64_t a_prompt_ms;

// id would answer through Interact's button although the game puts it on another Switch button
static bool shares_interact(int id) {
    if (id <= 0 || id >= ACT_COUNT || mask_button(k_masks_190[id]) == mask_button(k_masks_190[0])) return false;
    int p = g_act_pad[id], k = g_act_key[id];
    return (p >= 0 && p == g_act_pad[0]) || (k > 0 && k == g_act_key[0]);
}
static bool any_shares_interact(void) {
    for (int id = 1; id < ACT_COUNT; id++)
        if (a_custom >> id & 1 && shares_interact(id)) return true;
    return false;
}

// ---- the controller poll and the game's queries
#define EDGE_KEEP_MS 100  // (several of the game's updates at any frame rate it runs at)
static _Atomic uint64_t a_prev;
static _Atomic bool a_served;  // a pressed query was answered since the last poll

void act_poll(bool live) {
    static bool was_live;
    uint64_t custom = a_custom;
    uint64_t cur = live ? (a_keys | a_pads) & custom : 0, prev = a_prev;
    if (live && !was_live) prev = cur;  // held through a menu closing: not a new press
    uint64_t edge = cur & ~prev;
    // A poll nobody read (no pressed query since the last one) keeps its edge for the next, so a press is never lost
    // however often the game polls compared with how often it updates its pad - but only for EDGE_KEEP_MS: while a
    // message is up ("You got ..." after a new item) the game asks about no player action, and the press that closed
    // it, kept until the player was asked again, jumped as soon as the message was gone
    static uint64_t edge_ms;
    uint64_t now = SDL_GetTicks(), kept = a_served ? 0 : a_trig;
    if (kept && now - edge_ms > EDGE_KEEP_MS) kept = 0;
    if (edge) edge_ms = now;
    a_trig = (kept | edge) & custom;
    a_served = false;
    a_hold = cur;
    a_prev = cur;
    a_live = live;
    was_live = live;
    if (live && any_shares_interact() && interact_prompt_up()) a_prompt_ms = now;
    if (act_log_on()) act_log_poll();
}

// The last time the game asked the Master Cycle Zero's accelerate action (38): it does every frame while Link rides it
static _Atomic uint64_t cycle_asked_ns;
bool act_cycle_live(void) {
    uint64_t t = cycle_asked_ns;
    return t && SDL_GetTicksNS() - t < 250000000ull;
}

int rt_act_query(int kind, uint64_t pad, uint64_t id, uint64_t lr, uint64_t masks) {
    if (id == 38) cycle_asked_ns = SDL_GetTicksNS();
```
