`runtime/hle/pl.c`:

```c
// nn::pl shared system fonts. The Switch's system fonts are not part of the game; in order of preference:
//  1. SAVAGEWIND_FONT=<file> (.ttf / .otf / .ttc face 0 / .bfttf) for the Standard type, and SAVAGEWIND_CJK_FONT=<file>
//     for the Chinese and Korean types (they need hanzi/hangul the Standard font does not have)
//  2. a dump from the user's own console in fonts/: nintendo_udsg-r_std_003.bfttf (Standard, Morisawa UD Shin Go)
//     and nintendo_ext_003.bfttf (NintendoExt button glyphs); plain .ttf versions of those names also work
//  3. a Japanese gothic like UD Shin Go (much closer to the game's look than Arial): Hiragino Sans W4 on macOS,
//     Yu Gothic Regular / Medium on Windows
//  4. Arial
// .bfttf is the console's obfuscated TTF: 8-byte header (magic, size) then every u32 XORed with a fixed key.
// .ttc collections get face 0 copied out as a standalone font (the game's font engine wants one sfnt).
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <strings.h>

#include "../hle.h"

typedef struct { uint64_t addr, size; } Font;
// [0] Standard (Latin, kana, cyrillic and the rest), [1] NintendoExt when a dump provides it, [2] Chinese (hanzi),
// [3] Korean (hangul) - each when a font with them was found. The game asks for its text in one of the
// SharedFontTypes below and does not fall back itself: a Chinese or Korean type given the Standard (Japanese) font
// shows Japanese or blank glyphs, and a Chinese font has no hangul (Windows' Microsoft YaHei is one).
static Font fonts[4];

static uint32_t be32(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint32_t)p[0] << 24 | p[1] << 16 | p[2] << 8 | p[3]; }
static void put32(uint8_t *p, uint32_t v) { p[0] = v >> 24; p[1] = v >> 16; p[2] = v >> 8; p[3] = v; }

static uint8_t *read_file(const char *path, size_t *len) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    *len = (size_t)ftell(f);
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
    uint8_t *p = malloc(*len + 4);
    if (fread(p, 1, *len, f) != *len) { free(p); p = NULL; }
    fclose(f);
    return p;
}

// .bfttf -> TTF in place (returns the new length, 0 if it isn't one)
static size_t bfttf_decode(uint8_t *d, size_t len) {
    static const uint32_t KEY = 0x49621806;
    if (len < 12) return 0;
    for (int swap = 0; swap < 2; swap++) {  // the key's byte order differs between descriptions; accept both
        uint32_t k = swap ? __builtin_bswap32(KEY) : KEY;
        uint32_t w0, w1, w2;
        memcpy(&w0, d, 4); memcpy(&w1, d + 4, 4); memcpy(&w2, d + 8, 4);
        uint32_t size = w1 ^ k, ver = w2 ^ k;
        if (size == 0 || size > len - 8 || (ver != 0x00000100u && ver != 0x4F54544Fu)) continue;  // sfnt 1.0 / OTTO
        (void)w0;
        for (size_t i = 0; i + 4 <= size; i += 4) {
            uint32_t w;
            memcpy(&w, d + 8 + i, 4);
            w ^= k;
            memcpy(d + i, &w, 4);
        }
        return size;
    }
    return 0;
}

// .ttc -> face 0 as its own sfnt (table data copied, offsets rewritten)
static uint8_t *ttc_face0(const uint8_t *f, size_t len, size_t *out_len) {
    if (len < 16 || memcmp(f, "ttcf", 4)) return NULL;
    uint32_t o = be32(f + 12);
    if (o + 12 > len) return NULL;
    uint32_t nt = (uint32_t)f[o + 4] << 8 | f[o + 5];
    size_t total = 12 + 16 * nt;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nt; i++) total += (be32(f + o + 12 + 16 * i + 12) + 3) & ~3u;
    uint8_t *out = calloc(1, total);
    memcpy(out, f + o, 12);
    size_t pos = 12 + 16 * nt;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nt; i++) {
        const uint8_t *e = f + o + 12 + 16 * i;
        uint32_t off = be32(e + 8), n = be32(e + 12);
        if ((size_t)off + n > len) { free(out); return NULL; }
        memcpy(out + 12 + 16 * i, e, 8);  // tag, checksum
        put32(out + 12 + 16 * i + 8, (uint32_t)pos);
        put32(out + 12 + 16 * i + 12, n);
        memcpy(out + pos, f + off, n);
        pos += (n + 3) & ~3u;
    }
    *out_len = total;
    return out;
}

static int load_one(const char *path, Font *ft) {
    size_t len;
    uint8_t *d = read_file(path, &len);
    if (!d) return 0;
    size_t n = strlen(path);
    if (n > 6 && !strcasecmp(path + n - 6, ".bfttf")) {
        len = bfttf_decode(d, len);
        if (!len) { LOG("[pl] %s: not a valid .bfttf\n", path); free(d); return 0; }
    } else if (len >= 4 && !memcmp(d, "ttcf", 4)) {
        size_t l2;
        uint8_t *f0 = ttc_face0(d, len, &l2);
        free(d);
        if (!f0) { LOG("[pl] %s: bad font collection\n", path); return 0; }
        d = f0;
        len = l2;
    }
    void *p = hle_alloc(len + 16);
    memcpy(p, d, len);
    free(d);
    ft->addr = (uint64_t)p;
    ft->size = len;
    LOG("[pl] system font %s (%zu bytes)\n", path, len);
    return 1;
}

static int g_fonts_loaded;
RT_ON_RESET(pl_reset) { g_fonts_loaded = 0; memset(fonts, 0, sizeof fonts); }  // (they were in the HLE heap)

static void load_fonts(void) {
    if (g_fonts_loaded) return;
    g_fonts_loaded = 1;
    const char *env = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_FONT");
    const char *cjk_env = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_CJK_FONT");
    const char *std[] = {env, "fonts/nintendo_udsg-r_std_003.bfttf", "fonts/nintendo_udsg-r_std_003.ttf",
                         "fonts/nintendo_udsgr_std_003.ttf", "fonts/nintendo_udsgr_std_003.bfttf",
                         "/System/Library/Fonts/ヒラギノ角ゴシック W4.ttc", "C:/Windows/Fonts/YuGothR.ttc",
                         "C:/Windows/Fonts/YuGothM.ttc", "/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial.ttf",
                         "C:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf",
                         // Linux: DejaVu Sans (Debian / Ubuntu, Arch, Fedora). Not Noto Sans CJK: CFF outlines,
                         // which the game's font engine crashes on (it wants TrueType)
                         "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf", "/usr/share/fonts/TTF/DejaVuSans.ttf",
                         "/usr/share/fonts/dejavu-sans-fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf"};
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof std / sizeof *std && !fonts[0].addr; i++)
        if (std[i]) load_one(std[i], &fonts[0]);
    if (!fonts[0].addr) FATAL("no usable system font substitute\n");
    if (!load_one("fonts/nintendo_ext_003.bfttf", &fonts[1])) load_one("fonts/nintendo_ext_003.ttf", &fonts[1]);

    // Chinese (ChineseSimple/Ext, ChineseTraditional) and Korean: the Standard font above is a Japanese gothic or
    // Arial and has no hanzi or hangul. Only TrueType outlines (glyf): the game's font engine crashes on CFF, and
    // Noto Sans CJK (.otf / most .ttc) is CFF, so it is not listed here. SAVAGEWIND_CJK_FONT first (one font for
    // both, as WenQuanYi has hanzi and hangul), then a TrueType font a system already has. Not found: those types
    // keep the Standard font, as before.
    const char *cjk_zh[] = {cjk_env,
                            "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/wqy/wqy-microhei.ttc",  // hanzi + hangul
                            "/usr/share/fonts/wqy-microhei/wqy-microhei.ttc",
                            "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/wqy/wqy-zenhei.ttc",
                            "/usr/share/fonts/wqy-zenhei/wqy-zenhei.ttc",
                            "C:/Windows/Fonts/msyh.ttc", "C:/Windows/Fonts/simsun.ttc",  // (TrueType, unlike Noto CJK)
                            "/System/Library/Fonts/PingFang.ttc"};
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof cjk_zh / sizeof *cjk_zh && !fonts[2].addr; i++)
        if (cjk_zh[i]) load_one(cjk_zh[i], &fonts[2]);

    // Korean needs hangul, which Microsoft YaHei has not: a font of its own, after the env override and a CJK font
    // that has both (WenQuanYi). Malgun Gothic is the Korean font of every Windows since Vista.
    const char *cjk_ko[] = {cjk_env,
                            "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/wqy/wqy-microhei.ttc",
                            "/usr/share/fonts/wqy-microhei/wqy-microhei.ttc",
                            "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/wqy/wqy-zenhei.ttc",
                            "/usr/share/fonts/wqy-zenhei/wqy-zenhei.ttc",
                            "C:/Windows/Fonts/malgun.ttf",
                            "/System/Library/Fonts/AppleSDGothicNeo.ttc"};
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof cjk_ko / sizeof *cjk_ko && !fonts[3].addr; i++)
        if (cjk_ko[i]) load_one(cjk_ko[i], &fonts[3]);
}

// SharedFontType: 0 Standard, 1 ChineseSimple, 2 ChineseSimpleExt, 3 ChineseTraditional, 4 Korean, 5 NintendoExt
static const Font *font_for(uint64_t type) {
    load_fonts();
    if (type == 5) return fonts[1].addr ? &fonts[1] : &fonts[0];
    if (type >= 1 && type <= 3 && fonts[2].addr) return &fonts[2];  // Chinese: hanzi
    if (type == 4) {
        if (fonts[3].addr) return &fonts[3];  // Korean: hangul
        if (fonts[2].addr) return &fonts[2];  // (a CJK font with hangul in it, e.g. WenQuanYi)
    }
    return &fonts[0];
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2pl22GetSharedFontLoadStateENS0_14SharedFontTypeE", pl_get_load_state) { c->x[0] = 1; }
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2pl20GetSharedFontAddressENS0_14SharedFontTypeE", pl_get_address) { c->x[0] = font_for(c->x[0])->addr; }
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2pl17GetSharedFontSizeENS0_14SharedFontTypeE", pl_get_size) { c->x[0] = font_for(c->x[0])->size; }
```

`runtime/hle/setjmp.c`:

```c
// Guest setjmp / longjmp (musl's, in sdk). libjpeg and libpng in nn::image leave their errors with longjmp: the
// JPEG encoder of the autosave's screenshot, for one. The guest longjmp returns into the middle of the function
// that called setjmp, and recompiled code can't resume there (dispatch only knows function entries). So the
// generator (tools/gen.py setjmp_call) wraps every call to the guest setjmp in a host setjmp, in the C function of
// the caller: rt_setjmp_slot gives it a host jmp_buf for the guest one (per thread, by guest address). The guest
// setjmp still runs and fills the guest jmp_buf. The guest longjmp is HLE (runtime/hle/hle_symbols.txt): it
// restores the registers musl saved there and jumps to the host jmp_buf, back into that C function with x0 set.
//   musl aarch64 jmp_buf: x19-x28 at 0x00, x29 0x50, x30 0x58, sp 0x68, d8-d15 0x70
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../hle.h"

#define SLOTS 32
typedef struct {
    uint64_t gbuf;  // guest jmp_buf (0: free)
    uint64_t gsp;   // guest sp at the setjmp: the sp musl saves in it
    jmp_buf hb;
} JmpSlot;
static __thread JmpSlot slots[SLOTS];
static __thread unsigned slot_next;

jmp_buf *rt_setjmp_slot(Cpu *c, uint64_t gbuf) {
    JmpSlot *s = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < SLOTS && !s; i++)
        if (slots[i].gbuf == gbuf) s = &slots[i];
    // a new buffer: a free slot, else one set up by a deeper frame (its sp below ours: that function has returned)
    for (int i = 0; i < SLOTS && !s; i++)
        if (!slots[i].gbuf || slots[i].gsp < c->sp) s = &slots[i];
    if (!s) s = &slots[slot_next++ % SLOTS];
    s->gbuf = gbuf;
    s->gsp = c->sp;
    return &s->hb;
}

static uint64_t g_longjmps;  // (stats)

void hle_longjmp(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t gbuf = c->x[0];
    uint32_t val = (uint32_t)c->x[1];
    JmpSlot *s = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < SLOTS && !s; i++)
        if (slots[i].gbuf == gbuf) s = &slots[i];
    if (!s) FATAL("[setjmp] longjmp to %llx: no setjmp of it on this thread (lr=%llx)\n", gbuf, c->x[30]);
    if (LD64(gbuf + 0x68) != s->gsp)
        FATAL("[setjmp] longjmp to %llx: its sp %llx isn't the setjmp's %llx\n", gbuf, LD64(gbuf + 0x68), s->gsp);
    if (g_longjmps++ < 8 || ENV("SAVAGEWIND_LOG_LONGJMP"))
        LOG("[setjmp] longjmp to %llx val %u (lr=%llx, back to %llx)\n", gbuf, val, c->x[30], LD64(gbuf + 0x58));
    for (int r = 19; r <= 30; r++) c->x[r] = LD64(gbuf + 8 * (r - 19));
    c->sp = s->gsp;
    for (int r = 8; r <= 15; r++) c->v[r] = LD64(gbuf + 0x70 + 8 * (r - 8));  // (ldp d: upper half zeroed)
    c->x[0] = val ? val : 1;
    longjmp(s->hb, 1);
}

// SAVAGEWIND_LOG_JPEG=1: log each nn::image::JpegEncoder::Encode (its image, quality, output room and result: the
// autosave's caption.jpg goes through it); SAVAGEWIND_LOG_JPEG=dump also saves the first image's pixels to
// build/jpeg_in.raw. JpegEncoder: pixels at +0x18, pixel format +0x20, width/height +0x24, quality +0x30.
static GuestFn jpeg_encode;
static void jpeg_encode_logged(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t self = c->x[0], out_size = c->x[1], room = c->x[3];
    uint32_t w = LD32(self + 0x24), h = LD32(self + 0x28);
    static int dumped;
    if (!dumped && !strcmp(ENV("SAVAGEWIND_LOG_JPEG"), "dump")) {
        FILE *f = fopen("build/jpeg_in.raw", "wb");
        if (f) { fwrite((void *)(uintptr_t)LD64(self + 0x18), 4, (size_t)w * h, f); fclose(f); }
        dumped = 1;
    }
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], px = LD64(self + 0x18);
    static int described;
    if (!described++) {
        extern void nvn_debug_textures_at(uint64_t a), backend_debug_copies_at(uint64_t a);
        LOG("[jpeg] pixels at %llx, line alignment %u\n", px, LD32(self + 0x2c));
        nvn_debug_textures_at(px);
        backend_debug_copies_at(px);
    }
    jpeg_encode(c);
    LOG("[jpeg] Encode %ux%u format %u quality %u room %llu -> %d, %llu bytes (lr=%llx)\n", w, h, LD32(self + 0x20),
        LD32(self + 0x30), room, (int)c->x[0], out_size ? LD64(out_size) : 0, lr);
}

void jpeg_debug_init(void) {
    if (!ENV("SAVAGEWIND_LOG_JPEG") || jpeg_encode) return;
    uint64_t a = guest_sym("_ZN2nn5image11JpegEncoder6EncodeEPmPvmPNS0_11ExifBuilderE");
    if (!(jpeg_encode = dispatch_lookup(a))) return;
    hle_override(a, jpeg_encode_logged, "JpegEncoder::Encode");
}
```

`runtime/hle/swkbd.c`:

```c
// Software keyboard (naming Link on a new file, ...). On the Switch nn::swkbd::ShowKeyboard launches the keyboard
// library applet; our am service has no applets, so the game crashed. ShowKeyboard is replaced here: the overlay
// (runtime/ui/menu.mm menu_keyboard_run) asks for the text - typed directly with a keyboard, an on-screen keyboard
// with a controller - while this (game) thread keeps re-presenting the last frame.
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../hle.h"

int menu_keyboard_run(const char *initial, int max_len, char *out, int cap);  // runtime/ui/menu.mm

static uint32_t next_char(const unsigned char **text) {
    const unsigned char *p = *text;
    unsigned n = *p < 0x80 ? 1 : *p >= 0xc2 && *p <= 0xdf ? 2 :
                 *p >= 0xe0 && *p <= 0xef ? 3 : *p >= 0xf0 && *p <= 0xf4 ? 4 : 0;
    uint32_t ch = n == 1 ? *p : *p & (0x7f >> n);
    if (!n) goto invalid;
    for (unsigned i = 1; i < n; i++) {
        if ((p[i] & 0xc0) != 0x80) goto invalid;
        ch = (ch << 6) | (p[i] & 0x3f);
    }
    if ((n == 2 && ch < 0x80) || (n == 3 && ch < 0x800) || (n == 4 && ch < 0x10000) ||
        (ch >= 0xd800 && ch <= 0xdfff) || ch > 0x10ffff) goto invalid;
    *text = p + n;
    return ch;
invalid:
    *text = p + 1;
    return 0xfffd;
}

static void write_text(unsigned char *out, size_t cap, const char *text, bool utf8) {
    size_t used = 0, terminator = utf8 ? 1 : 2;
    if (cap < terminator) return;
    const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)text;
    while (*p) {
        uint32_t ch = next_char(&p);
        unsigned char bytes[4];
        size_t n;
        if (utf8) {
            if (ch < 0x80) {
                bytes[0] = (unsigned char)ch;
                n = 1;
            } else if (ch < 0x800) {
                bytes[0] = 0xc0 | (ch >> 6);
                bytes[1] = 0x80 | (ch & 0x3f);
                n = 2;
            } else if (ch < 0x10000) {
                bytes[0] = 0xe0 | (ch >> 12);
                bytes[1] = 0x80 | ((ch >> 6) & 0x3f);
                bytes[2] = 0x80 | (ch & 0x3f);
                n = 3;
            } else {
                bytes[0] = 0xf0 | (ch >> 18);
                bytes[1] = 0x80 | ((ch >> 12) & 0x3f);
                bytes[2] = 0x80 | ((ch >> 6) & 0x3f);
                bytes[3] = 0x80 | (ch & 0x3f);
                n = 4;
            }
        } else {
            uint16_t first = (uint16_t)ch, second = 0;
            n = 2;
            if (ch >= 0x10000) {
                ch -= 0x10000;
                first = (uint16_t)(0xd800 + (ch >> 10));
                second = (uint16_t)(0xdc00 + (ch & 0x3ff));
                n = 4;
            }
            bytes[0] = first & 0xff;
            bytes[1] = first >> 8;
            bytes[2] = second & 0xff;
            bytes[3] = second >> 8;
        }
        // Keep a whole character and its terminator, even when the byte capacity is odd.
        if (n > cap - terminator - used) break;
        memcpy(out + used, bytes, n);
        used += n;
    }
    memset(out + used, 0, terminator);
}

// nn::swkbd::ShowKeyboard(nn::swkbd::String *out, const nn::swkbd::ShowKeyboardArg &arg) -> nn::Result
// String = {void *ptr; size_t bufSize}, capacity in bytes.
// ShowKeyboardArg (probed 2026-10-08, naming Link): +0x3ac text max length, +0x3b0 min length, +0x3c0 / +0x3c4
// initial text offset / length (UTF-16) in the work buffer at +0x4d0. +0x3bd selects UTF-8 output; otherwise UTF-16LE.
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn5swkbd12ShowKeyboardEPNS0_6StringERKNS0_15ShowKeyboardArgE", swkbd_show) {
    uint64_t out = c->x[0], arg = c->x[1];
    uint64_t ptr = LD64(out), size = LD64(out + 8);
    int max_len = (int)*(const int32_t *)(uintptr_t)(arg + 0x3ac);
    uint32_t off = *(const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(arg + 0x3c0), n = *(const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(arg + 0x3c4);
    uint64_t wb = LD64(arg + 0x4d0);
    char initial[96] = "";
    for (uint32_t i = 0; wb && i < n && i < sizeof initial - 1; i++) {
        uint16_t ch = *(const uint16_t *)(uintptr_t)(wb + off + 2 * i);
        initial[i] = ch < 0x80 ? (char)ch : '?';
    }
    char text[96];
    int ok = menu_keyboard_run(initial, max_len, text, sizeof text);
    if (!ok) snprintf(text, sizeof text, "%s", initial);  // cancelled: keep what was there
    LOG("[swkbd] name entry (max %d, initial \"%s\"): %s \"%s\"\n", max_len, initial, ok ? "entered" : "cancelled", text);
    if (ptr && size) {
        memset((void *)(uintptr_t)ptr, 0, size);
        // Horse naming leaves IsUseUtf8 clear and copies the result as 16-bit units (#271).
        write_text((unsigned char *)(uintptr_t)ptr, size, text, LD8(arg + 0x3bd) != 0);
    }
    c->x[0] = 0;
}
```

`runtime/hle/vi.c`:

```c
// nn::vi (display/layer) and nv:: (graphics driver init), implemented on the host.
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "../hle.h"
#include "../kernel.h"
#include "../prof.h"

static uint32_t vsync_r, vsync_w;
static KEvent *vsync_event;
uint32_t vi_vsync_handle(void) { return vsync_r; }
uint64_t g_native_window;

static void *vsync_thread(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    prof_thread_name("vsync");
    const uint64_t period = 16666667;
    plat_thread_realtime(period);
    uint64_t next = plat_now_ns();
    for (;;) {
        next += period;
        plat_sleep_until_ns(next);
        uint64_t now = plat_now_ns();
        if (now > next + period * 3) {
            static int warned;
            if (warned++ < 20) LOG("[vi] vsync timer late by %llums (host throttling?)\n", (unsigned long long)((now - next) / 1000000));
            next = now;  // don't burst-signal to catch up
        }
        klock();
        kernel_signal(vsync_event);
        kunlock();
    }
    return NULL;
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi10InitializeEv", vi_initialize) { (void)c; }
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi8FinalizeEv", vi_finalize) { (void)c; }

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi18OpenDefaultDisplayEPPNS0_7DisplayE", vi_open_default_display) {
    *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[0] = (uint64_t)hle_alloc(0x100);
    c->x[0] = 0;
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi12CloseDisplayEPNS0_7DisplayE", vi_close_display) { (void)c; }

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi11CreateLayerEPPNS0_5LayerEPNS0_7DisplayE", vi_create_layer) {
    *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[0] = (uint64_t)hle_alloc(0x100);
    c->x[0] = 0;
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi12DestroyLayerEPNS0_5LayerE", vi_destroy_layer) { (void)c; }
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi12SetLayerCropEPNS0_5LayerEiiii", vi_set_layer_crop) { c->x[0] = 0; }

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi15GetNativeWindowEPPvPNS0_5LayerE", vi_get_native_window) {
    if (!g_native_window) g_native_window = (uint64_t)hle_alloc(0x100);
    *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[0] = g_native_window;
    c->x[0] = 0;
}

// Reboot: the vsync timer and its event live on (the kernel's handle table doesn't): new handles at the next boot.
RT_ON_RESET(vi_reset) {
    vsync_r = vsync_w = 0;
    g_native_window = 0;  // (HLE heap)
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn2vi20GetDisplayVsyncEventEPNS_2os15SystemEventTypeEPNS0_7DisplayE", vi_get_vsync_event) {
    if (!vsync_event) {
        vsync_event = kernel_create_event_pair(&vsync_w, &vsync_r);
        pthread_t t;
        pthread_create(&t, NULL, vsync_thread, NULL);
    } else if (!vsync_r) {
        vsync_w = kernel_new_handle(vsync_event);
        vsync_r = kernel_new_handle(vsync_event);
    }
    // nn::os::AttachReadableHandleToSystemEvent(event, handle, managed=false, clear_mode=AutoClear)
    c->x[1] = vsync_r;
    c->x[2] = 0;
    c->x[3] = 1;
    guest_call(c, guest_sym("_ZN2nn2os33AttachReadableHandleToSystemEventEPNS0_15SystemEventTypeEjbNS0_14EventClearModeE"));
    c->x[0] = 0;
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nv18InitializeGraphicsEPvm", nv_initialize_graphics) { (void)c; }
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nv16FinalizeGraphicsEv", nv_finalize_graphics) { (void)c; }
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nv20SetGraphicsAllocatorEPFPvmmS0_EPFvS0_S0_EPFS0_S0_mS0_ES0_", nv_set_allocator) { (void)c; }
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nv28SetGraphicsDevtoolsAllocatorEPFPvmmS0_EPFvS0_S0_EPFS0_S0_mS0_ES0_", nv_set_dt_allocator) { (void)c; }
```

`runtime/hle/vibration.c`:

```c
// The SDK mixes its vibration nodes itself, then sends HID commands 201 / 206. SDL's two motors cannot reproduce
// HD rumble frequencies: use the strongest low / high band across the two device values instead.
#include <SDL3/SDL.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../hle.h"
#include "../vibration.h"
#include "../settings.h"

static pthread_mutex_t lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static VibrationValue values[2] = {{0, 160, 0, 320}, {0, 160, 0, 320}};
static bool permitted = true;

// These are the handles returned by hid_vibration_handles (input.c), for our one player or handheld mode.
static int device(uint32_t handle) {
    uint32_t id = (handle >> 8) & 0xff;
    return (handle & 0xfffe00ffu) == 3 && (id == 0 || id == 0x20) ? (int)((handle >> 16) & 1) : -1;
}

static float amplitude(float a) { return !isfinite(a) || a < 0 ? 0 : a > 1 ? 1 : a; }

void vibration_send(uint32_t handle, const VibrationValue *value) {
    int i = device(handle);
    if (i < 0) return;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
    if (permitted && g_settings.rumble) {
        VibrationValue previous = values[i];
        values[i] = *value;
        values[i].low_amplitude = amplitude(value->low_amplitude);
        values[i].high_amplitude = amplitude(value->high_amplitude);
        if ((previous.low_amplitude != values[i].low_amplitude || previous.high_amplitude != values[i].high_amplitude) &&
            getenv("SAVAGEWIND_VIBRATION"))
            LOG("[vibration] handle %#x low %.3f high %.3f\n", handle, values[i].low_amplitude, values[i].high_amplitude);
    }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

VibrationValue vibration_get(uint32_t handle) {
    VibrationValue v = {0, 160, 0, 320};
    int i = device(handle);
    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
    if (i >= 0 && permitted && g_settings.rumble) v = values[i];
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    return v;
}

void vibration_clear(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) values[i] = (VibrationValue){0, 160, 0, 320};
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

void vibration_permit(bool allow) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
    permitted = allow;
    if (!allow) memset(values, 0, sizeof values);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
}

bool vibration_permitted(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
    bool allow = permitted;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    return allow;
}

RT_ON_RESET(vibration_reset) {
    vibration_clear();
    vibration_permit(true);
}

static pthread_mutex_t rumble_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_cond_t rumble_cond = PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER;
static pthread_cond_t rumble_done_cond = PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER;
static SDL_Gamepad *req_pad, *inflight_pad, *failed_pad;
static uint16_t req_low, req_high;
static uint64_t req_seq, done_seq;
static bool worker_started;

static void *rumble_worker(void *arg) {
    (void)arg;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&rumble_lock);
    for (;;) {
        while (done_seq == req_seq || !req_pad) {
            if (!req_pad && done_seq < req_seq) {
                done_seq = req_seq;
                pthread_cond_broadcast(&rumble_done_cond);
            }
            pthread_cond_wait(&rumble_cond, &rumble_lock);
        }
        SDL_Gamepad *p = req_pad;
        uint16_t lo = req_low, hi = req_high;
        uint64_t seq = req_seq;
        inflight_pad = p;
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&rumble_lock);

        if (!SDL_RumbleGamepad(p, lo, hi, 100)) {
            pthread_mutex_lock(&rumble_lock);
            if (failed_pad != p) {
                failed_pad = p;
                LOG("[input] controller rumble unavailable: %s\n", SDL_GetError());
            }
            pthread_mutex_unlock(&rumble_lock);
        }

        pthread_mutex_lock(&rumble_lock);
        inflight_pad = NULL;
        if (seq > done_seq) done_seq = seq;
        pthread_cond_broadcast(&rumble_done_cond);
    }
    return NULL;
}

void vibration_pad_closed(SDL_Gamepad *gone) {
    if (!gone) return;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&rumble_lock);
    if (req_pad == gone) {
        req_pad = NULL;
        done_seq = req_seq;
    }
    if (failed_pad == gone) failed_pad = NULL;
    while (inflight_pad == gone) pthread_cond_wait(&rumble_done_cond, &rumble_lock);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&rumble_lock);
}

void vibration_flush(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&rumble_lock);
    while (done_seq < req_seq) pthread_cond_wait(&rumble_done_cond, &rumble_lock);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&rumble_lock);
}

void vibration_update(SDL_Gamepad *pad, bool focused) {
    static SDL_Gamepad *last_pad;
    static uint16_t last_low, last_high;
    static uint64_t last_ms;
    if (!pad || !focused || !g_settings.rumble) vibration_clear();
    bool changed = pad != last_pad;
    if (changed) {
        last_pad = pad;
        last_low = last_high = 0;
        last_ms = 0;
    }
    if (!pad) return;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
    float scale = (float)g_settings.rumble_strength / 100.0f;
    uint16_t low = focused && permitted && g_settings.rumble ? (uint16_t)lroundf(fmaxf(values[0].low_amplitude, values[1].low_amplitude) * scale * 65535) : 0;
    uint16_t high = focused && permitted && g_settings.rumble ? (uint16_t)lroundf(fmaxf(values[0].high_amplitude, values[1].high_amplitude) * scale * 65535) : 0;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
    uint64_t now = SDL_GetTicks();
    // A short lease stops the motors if the event loop stalls; refresh unchanged effects while it is alive.
    if (!changed && low == last_low && high == last_high && (!(low || high) || now - last_ms < 50)) return;
    static int nlog;  // (SAVAGEWIND_MOTION_LOG: rumble going on and off, next to the sensor stream's health - a
                      // controller might change its sensor reports once it rumbles, #220)
    if (!(low || high) != !(last_low || last_high) && ENV("SAVAGEWIND_MOTION_LOG") && nlog < 200) {
        nlog++;
        LOG("[motion] rumble %s\n", low || high ? "on" : "off");
    }
    last_low = low;
    last_high = high;
    last_ms = now;
    // SDL_RumbleGamepad can block on Bluetooth HID writes (e.g. DualSense on Windows); run it off the event thread
    // and coalesce in-flight updates to the latest request.
    pthread_mutex_lock(&rumble_lock);
    if (!worker_started) {
        pthread_t t;
        if (pthread_create(&t, NULL, rumble_worker, NULL) == 0) {
            pthread_detach(t);
            worker_started = true;
        }
    }
    if (worker_started) {
        req_pad = pad;
        req_low = low;
        req_high = high;
        req_seq++;
        pthread_cond_signal(&rumble_cond);
    }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&rumble_lock);
}

```

`runtime/hle/yaz0.c`:

```c
// BOTW's streaming Yaz0 decoder (1.9.0 0x700131d674, tools/patches.py yaz0_stream) in native code. The game streams most
// of its resources Yaz0-compressed, a chunk at a time, from a loading thread its main thread waits for. Generated, every
// byte went through a volatile guest load and store and a flag computation: at Hyrule Castle most frames over 8 ms while
// running were the main thread waiting for this loop. Same steps, same state, same results as the game's code.
//
// The state (x0): +0 output pointer, +8 bytes still to write (s32), +0xc nonzero: a copy past the end is cut (else
// an error), +0x10 the current group's next flag bit, +0x11 the group's flag byte, +0x12 a copy's first byte,
// +0x14 what the next input byte is (0 a flag byte / literal / a copy's first byte, 1 a copy's second byte, 2 a copy's
// length byte), +0x18 the copy's distance, +0x1a the 16-byte header still to read. x1, w2: the input chunk. Returns the
// bytes still to write, -1 (done with input left over and no cutting), -2 (a copy past the end).
//
// SAVAGEWIND_YAZ0=0: the game's code. =2: both, compared: the native result is worked out on a copy, the game's code
// runs, and its exit (yaz0_stream_ret) checks the state, the result and every byte written ("[yaz0] check").
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../cpu.h"
#include "../rt.h"

static int yaz0_mode(void) {
    static int m = -1;
    if (m < 0) m = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_YAZ0") ? atoi(getenv("SAVAGEWIND_YAZ0")) : 1;
    return m;
}

// The decoder on host pointers: s the 0x1c-byte state, dst its output pointer (s's own +0, or a copy's), src/len the
// chunk. Returns the result; *stored: whether the state was written back (not on the -2 path, as in the game's code).
static uint32_t yaz0_run(uint8_t *s, uint8_t *dst, const uint8_t *src, uint32_t len, bool *stored) {
    uint32_t x0, x13, x10, x9, x12, x14 = 0, x20 = len;
    uint64_t x11;
    uint8_t *x8 = dst;
    memcpy(&x0, s + 8, 4); memcpy(&x13, s + 0x14, 4);
    uint16_t d16; memcpy(&d16, s + 0x18, 2); x11 = d16;
    x10 = s[0x10], x9 = s[0x11], x12 = s[0x12];
    uint32_t cut; memcpy(&cut, s + 0xc, 4);
    *stored = false;
    if ((int32_t)x0 < 1) goto store;
    for (;;) {
        // A whole group at once (flag byte and its 8 literals or copies) while neither the input nor the room left can
        // run out inside it: a group takes at most 1 + 8 * 3 bytes and writes at most 8 * 0x111. It ends in the state
        // the step-by-step loop below would be in: the flag bit used up (0), no copy half read (0), the group's flag
        // byte, the last copy's first byte and distance.
        while (x13 == 0 && x10 == 0 && x20 > 25 && (int32_t)x0 > 8 * 0x111) {
            uint32_t hdr = *src++;
            x20 -= 1;
            if (hdr == 0xff) {  // 8 literals (most of a texture)
                memcpy(x8, src, 8);
                x8 += 8, src += 8, x20 -= 8, x0 -= 8;
                x9 = hdr;
                continue;
            }
            for (uint32_t bit = 0x80; bit; bit >>= 1) {
                if (hdr & bit) {
                    *x8++ = *src++;
                    x20 -= 1, x0 -= 1;
                    continue;
                }
                uint32_t b1 = src[0], n;
                x11 = ((uint64_t)(b1 & 0xf) << 8 | src[1]) + 1;
                if (b1 >> 4) n = (b1 >> 4) + 2, src += 2, x20 -= 2;
                else n = (uint32_t)src[2] + 0x12, src += 3, x20 -= 3;
                x12 = b1;
                const uint8_t *from = x8 - x11;
                // (a short copy as one 16-byte move: the bytes past n are inside the room left and written again later)
                if (x11 >= 16 && n <= 16) memcpy(x8, from, 16), x8 += n;
                else if (x11 >= n) memcpy(x8, from, n), x8 += n;
                else if (x11 == 1) memset(x8, *from, n), x8 += n;
                else { uint32_t k = n; do { *x8++ = *from++; } while (--k); }
                x0 -= n;
            }
            x9 = hdr;
        }
        if (x13 == 1) {  // a copy's second byte: the distance's low 8 bits
            uint32_t first = x12 & 0xff;
            x11 = ((uint64_t)(x12 & 0xf) << 8 | src[0]) + 1;
            if (first < 0x10) { x13 = 2; goto next; }  // (its length in a third byte)
            x14 = (first >> 4) + 2;
        } else if (x13 == 2) {  // a copy's length byte
            x14 = (uint32_t)src[0] + 0x12;
        } else {  // a literal or a copy's first byte, after the group's flag byte when it is used up
            if (x10 == 0) {
                x9 = *src++;
                if (--x20 == 0) { x10 = 0x80; goto store; }
                x10 = 0x80;
            }
            uint32_t b = src[0];
            if (x9 & x10) { *x8++ = (uint8_t)b; x0 -= 1; x14 = x12; }
            else { x13 = 1; x14 = b; }
            x10 >>= 1;
            x12 = x14;
            goto next;
        }
        if (x14 > x0) {  // past the end: cut, or an error (state not written back)
            if (!cut) return 0xfffffffeu;
            x14 = x0 & 0xffff;
        }
        {   // byte by byte where it overlaps what it writes (the same bytes as memcpy where it doesn't, memset at 1)
            uint32_t n = x14;
            const uint8_t *from = x8 - x11;
            if (x11 >= n) memcpy(x8, from, n), x8 += n;
            else if (x11 == 1) memset(x8, *from, n), x8 += n;
            else do { *x8++ = *from++; } while (--n);
        }
        x13 = 0;
        x0 -= x14;
    next:
        if (--x20 == 0) goto store;
        src++;
        if ((int32_t)x0 > 0) continue;
        goto store;
    }
store:
    *stored = true;
    memcpy(s + 8, &x0, 4); memcpy(s + 0x14, &x13, 4);
    uint64_t p = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)x8; memcpy(s, &p, 8);
    d16 = (uint16_t)x11; memcpy(s + 0x18, &d16, 2);
    s[0x10] = (uint8_t)x10, s[0x11] = (uint8_t)x9, s[0x12] = (uint8_t)x12;
    if (x0 != 0) return x0;
    if (x20 < 0x21 || cut) return 0;
    return 0xffffffffu;
}

// (SAVAGEWIND_YAZ0=2) the native result of the call in progress on this thread, checked at the game code's return
static __thread struct {
    bool on, stored;
    uint8_t *s, *dst;
    uint8_t state[0x1c], before[0x1c];
    uint32_t result;
    uint8_t *out;  // the bytes the native code wrote, from dst
    uint64_t n;
} chk;
static uint64_t chk_calls, chk_bad;

// The decoder's entry: 1 when done here (x0 set; the game's code is skipped), 0 for the game's code (the header still to
// read, an empty chunk, SAVAGEWIND_YAZ0=0, or the check mode).
int rt_yaz0(Cpu *c) {
    int mode = yaz0_mode();
    uint8_t *s = (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[0];
    const uint8_t *src = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[1];
    uint32_t len = (uint32_t)c->x[2];
    if (!mode || s[0x1a] || !len) return 0;
    uint64_t d; memcpy(&d, s, 8);
    if (mode != 2) {
        bool stored;
        c->x[0] = yaz0_run(s, (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)d, src, len, &stored);
        return 1;
    }
    // check mode: on a copy of the state and of the output (and the 4 KB before it, which copies read)
    int32_t rem; memcpy(&rem, s + 8, 4);
    uint64_t room = rem > 0 ? (uint64_t)rem : 0;
    if (room > (64u << 20) || d < GUEST_LO + 0x1000 || d + room > GUEST_HI) return 0;
    uint8_t *buf = malloc(0x1000 + room + 16);
    if (!buf) return 0;
    memcpy(buf, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(d - 0x1000), 0x1000);
    memcpy(chk.before, s, 0x1c);
    memcpy(chk.state, s, 0x1c);
    uint8_t *ndst = buf + 0x1000;
    chk.result = yaz0_run(chk.state, ndst, src, len, &chk.stored);
    uint64_t end; memcpy(&end, chk.state, 8);
    chk.n = chk.stored ? end - (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)ndst : 0;
    if (chk.stored) { uint64_t real = d + chk.n; memcpy(chk.state, &real, 8); }  // (the pointer as the game's code leaves it)
    free(chk.out);
    chk.out = malloc(chk.n + 1);
    if (chk.out) memcpy(chk.out, ndst, chk.n);
    free(buf);
    chk.on = chk.out != NULL, chk.s = s, chk.dst = (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)d;
    return 0;
}

// The decoder's return (game code): the check mode's comparison
void rt_yaz0_done(Cpu *c) {
    if (!chk.on) return;
    chk.on = false;
    bool ok = (uint32_t)c->x[0] == chk.result;
    if (chk.stored) ok = ok && !memcmp(chk.s, chk.state, 0x1c) && !memcmp(chk.dst, chk.out, chk.n);
    else ok = ok && !memcmp(chk.s, chk.before, 0x1c);
    uint64_t n = __atomic_add_fetch(&chk_calls, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    if (!ok) {
        __atomic_add_fetch(&chk_bad, 1, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
        LOG("[yaz0] check MISMATCH: game result %x native %x, %llu bytes\n", (unsigned)c->x[0], chk.result,
            (unsigned long long)chk.n);
    }
    if (!(n & 1023) || !ok) LOG("[yaz0] check: %llu calls, %llu mismatches\n", (unsigned long long)n,
                                (unsigned long long)chk_bad);
}
```

`runtime/imageload.c`:

```c
// The runtime's own image decoding and PNG writing (runtime/imageload.h). One C implementation for both users: the
// start screen's picture (runtime/ui/splash.mm) and the window icon (runtime/paths.c), plus the screenshots and
// texture dumps of the Vulkan backend (runtime/nvn/vulkan/device.c, exec.c). JPEG and PNG only, no HDR/linear
// conversions - the same stb_image options the start screen compiled in itself before.
#define STBI_ONLY_JPEG
#define STBI_ONLY_PNG
#define STBI_NO_HDR
#define STBI_NO_LINEAR
#define STB_IMAGE_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "stb_image.h"
#define STB_IMAGE_WRITE_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "stb_image_write.h"

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "imageload.h"

bool rt_image_info(const char *path, int *w, int *h) {
    int n;
    return stbi_info(path, w, h, &n) != 0;
}

unsigned char *rt_image_rgba(const char *path, int *w, int *h) { return stbi_load(path, w, h, NULL, 4); }

const char *rt_image_error(void) { return stbi_failure_reason(); }

void rt_image_free(void *px) { stbi_image_free(px); }

bool rt_save_png(const char *path, const unsigned char *rgba, int w, int h) {
    if (w <= 0 || h <= 0) return false;
    size_t n = (size_t)w * (size_t)h * 4;
    unsigned char *px = malloc(n);
    if (!px) return false;
    memcpy(px, rgba, n);
    for (size_t i = 3; i < n; i += 4) px[i] = 255;
    bool ok = stbi_write_png(path, w, h, 4, px, w * 4) != 0;
    free(px);
    return ok;
}
```

```h
// The runtime overlay and launcher keep fixed navigation shortcuts. The game's menus read the raw Switch layer.

enum {
    BIND_A, BIND_B, BIND_X, BIND_Y, BIND_LSTICK, BIND_RSTICK, BIND_L, BIND_R, BIND_ZL, BIND_ZR, BIND_PLUS, BIND_MINUS,

// ---- Per-action bindings
// The game asks "is action N held / pressed" through two functions (tools/patches.py _act_query); each action reads one
// Switch button (a table in the game: several actions share a button). Every action owns an explicit host key and

void act_set(int dev, int id, int host);      // ACT_FOLLOW = restore factory default (not stored); ACT_NONE = nothing

void act_publish(uint64_t keys, uint64_t pads);                             // (bit per action)

// live = false in the game's menus, with the window unfocused or the overlay up: the Switch layer answers then.

// answers (factory defaults, a menu or an id out of range). `masks` is the game's mask table.

// layer (ui/menu.mm act_overlay_draw) next to the "[act] poll N" lines in the log.
```

`runtime/ipc.c`:

```c
// IPC message parsing/serialization and session management.
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "hle.h"
#include "ipc.h"

#ifdef __APPLE__
extern const ServiceDef __start_services[] __asm__("section$start$__DATA$__services");
extern const ServiceDef __stop_services[] __asm__("section$end$__DATA$__services");
#elif defined(__linux__)
extern const ServiceDef __start_services[], __stop_services[];  // (ELF: defined by the linker)
#else
// PE/COFF: .svc$a < .svc$m (entries, ipc.h) < .svc$z (the linker sorts by the text after '$')
__attribute__((section(".svc$a"), used)) static const ServiceDef __start_services[1];
__attribute__((section(".svc$z"), used)) static const ServiceDef __stop_services[1];
#endif

static void stub_handler(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp) {
    LOG("[ipc] STUB %s cmd %u (in %u bytes, x%d a%d b%d c%d) -> ok\n", s->name, req->cmd, req->data_size, req->nx,
        req->na, req->nb, req->nc);
    resp->result = 0;
    resp_size(resp, 0x40);  // zeroed outputs
}

Service *service_new(const char *name, ServiceHandler h, void *state) {
    Service *s = calloc(1, sizeof *s);
    s->name = strdup(name);
    s->handler = h;
    s->state = state;
    return s;
}

Service *service_lookup(const char *name) {
    const ServiceDef *start = __start_services, *stop = __stop_services;
    __asm__("" : "+r"(start), "+r"(stop));  // separate objects: keep the compiler from reasoning about them
    for (const ServiceDef *d = start; d < stop; d++)
        if (d->name && !strcmp(d->name, name)) return service_new(name, d->handler, NULL);
    LOG("[ipc] no HLE implementation for service '%s', using logging stub\n", name);
    return service_new(name, stub_handler, NULL);
}

void ipc_return_object(IpcResp *resp, Service *s) { resp->objects[resp->nobjects++] = s; }

// Guest threads send requests at the same time, with no kernel lock held (SendSyncRequest), and the clones of a domain
// session share its object table: the table's slots and the services' reference counts change under this lock. Two
// objects made at once could take the same free slot, and closing one then left the other "missing" (Steam Deck,
// Continue: the game's resource loading stopped on the failed request). Handlers run without it.
static pthread_mutex_t g_domain_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

static uint32_t session_new(Service *s) {
    KSession *k = calloc(1, sizeof *k);
    k->obj.type = KOBJ_SESSION;
    k->svc = s;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_domain_lock);
    s->refs++;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_domain_lock);
    return kernel_new_handle(&k->obj);
}

// (caller holds g_domain_lock) -> the service to close once the lock is released (its last holder went), or NULL
static Service *service_release(Service *s) {
    return s && --s->refs == 0 && s->on_close ? s : NULL;
}

uint32_t ipc_connect_named_port(const char *name) {
    if (!strcmp(name, "sm:")) return session_new(service_lookup("sm:"));
    LOG("[ipc] ConnectToNamedPort('%s') unsupported\n", name);
    return 0;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ sm:
SERVICE("sm:", sm_handler) {
    (void)s;
    switch (req->cmd) {
    case 0:  // RegisterClient
        break;
    case 1: {  // GetServiceHandle(name)
        char name[9] = {0};
        memcpy(name, req->data, 8);
        LOG("[sm] GetService %s\n", name);
        ipc_return_object(resp, service_lookup(name));
        break;
    }
    default:
        LOG("[sm] unknown cmd %u\n", req->cmd);
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ message codec
static uint64_t buf_addr(const uint32_t *w) {
    return w[1] | ((uint64_t)(w[2] >> 28) << 32) | ((uint64_t)((w[2] >> 2) & 7) << 36);
}

// TIPC (sm: and a few other system services since 12.0.0) replies with the same HIPC header type as
// the request, the handles in the special header, and raw words holding the result followed by the
// outputs: no SFCO header, no 16-byte alignment and no domains.
static int tipc_write_response(uint32_t *msg, uint32_t type, IpcResp *resp) {
    for (int i = 0; i < resp->nobjects; i++) resp->move_handles[resp->nmove++] = session_new(resp->objects[i]);
    memset(msg, 0, 0x100);
    int has_handles = resp->ncopy || resp->nmove;
    uint32_t words = 1 + (resp->data_size + 3) / 4;
    msg[0] = type;
    msg[1] = words | (has_handles ? 0x80000000u : 0);
    uint32_t *q = msg + 2;
    if (has_handles) {
        *q++ = (resp->ncopy << 1) | (resp->nmove << 5);
        for (int i = 0; i < resp->ncopy; i++) *q++ = resp->copy_handles[i];
        for (int i = 0; i < resp->nmove; i++) *q++ = resp->move_handles[i];
    }
    *q++ = resp->result;
    memcpy(q, resp->data, resp->data_size);
    return 0;
}

int ipc_handle_request(Cpu *c, uint32_t handle) {
    KObject *o = handle_get(handle);
    if (!o || o->type != KOBJ_SESSION) {
        LOG("[ipc] SendSyncRequest on bad handle %x\n", handle);
        return 0xE401;
    }
    KSession *sess = (KSession *)o;
    uint32_t *msg = (uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)c->tpidrro;
    IpcReq req = {0};
    IpcResp resp = {0};
    req.type = msg[0] & 0xFFFF;
    int nx = (msg[0] >> 16) & 0xF, na = (msg[0] >> 20) & 0xF, nb = (msg[0] >> 24) & 0xF;
    uint32_t raw_words = msg[1] & 0x3FF;
    uint32_t cflags = (msg[1] >> 10) & 0xF;
    uint32_t *p = msg + 2;
    if (msg[1] & 0x80000000u) {
        uint32_t hd = *p++;
        if (hd & 1) { req.pid = p[0] | ((uint64_t)p[1] << 32); p += 2; }
        req.ncopy = (hd >> 1) & 0xF;
        req.nmove = (hd >> 5) & 0xF;
        for (int i = 0; i < req.ncopy; i++) req.copy_handles[i] = *p++;
        for (int i = 0; i < req.nmove; i++) req.move_handles[i] = *p++;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < nx; i++, p += 2) {
        req.x[i].addr = p[1] | ((uint64_t)((p[0] >> 12) & 0xF) << 32) | ((uint64_t)((p[0] >> 6) & 0x7) << 36);
        req.x[i].size = p[0] >> 16;
    }
    req.nx = nx;
    for (int i = 0; i < na; i++, p += 3) {
        req.a[i].size = p[0] | ((uint64_t)((p[2] >> 24) & 0xF) << 32);
        req.a[i].addr = buf_addr(p);
    }
    req.na = na;
    for (int i = 0; i < nb; i++, p += 3) {
        req.b[i].size = p[0] | ((uint64_t)((p[2] >> 24) & 0xF) << 32);
        req.b[i].addr = buf_addr(p);
    }
    req.nb = nb;
    uint32_t *raw = p;
    // raw data is aligned to 16 bytes relative to the message start
    uint32_t *aligned = (uint32_t *)(((uintptr_t)raw + 15) & ~(uintptr_t)15);
    if (cflags >= 2) {
        uint32_t *cdesc = raw + raw_words;
        int ncd = cflags == 2 ? 1 : (int)cflags - 2;
        for (int i = 0; i < ncd; i++) {
            req.c[i].addr = cdesc[2 * i] | ((uint64_t)(cdesc[2 * i + 1] & 0xFFFF) << 32);
            req.c[i].size = cdesc[2 * i + 1] >> 16;
        }
        req.nc = ncd;
    }

    if (req.type == 2 || req.type == 15) {  // close (CMIF / TIPC)
        LOG("[ipc] close session %s (handle %x)\n", sess->svc->name, handle);
        if (!sess->domain) {  // (a domain's objects stay: closed one by one)
            pthread_mutex_lock(&g_domain_lock);
            Service *last = service_release(sess->svc);
            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_domain_lock);
            if (last) last->on_close(last);
        }
        return 0;
    }
    if (req.type >= 16) {  // TIPC: the command is in the type, the raw words are the arguments
        req.cmd = req.type - 16;
        req.data = (const uint8_t *)raw;
        req.data_size = raw_words * 4;
        sess->svc->handler(sess->svc, &req, &resp);
        return tipc_write_response(msg, req.type, &resp);
    }
    uint8_t *payload = (uint8_t *)aligned;
    bool dom = false;  // response is domain-wrapped
    if (req.type == 4 || req.type == 6) {
        if (sess->domain) {
            dom = true;
            uint8_t dcmd = payload[0];
            uint8_t nin = payload[1];
            uint16_t dsize = *(uint16_t *)(payload + 2);
            req.domain_obj = *(uint32_t *)(payload + 4);
            if (dcmd == 2) {  // close object
                if (req.domain_obj < 256) {
                    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_domain_lock);
                    Service *o = sess->domain->objs[req.domain_obj];
                    sess->domain->objs[req.domain_obj] = NULL;
                    Service *last = service_release(o);
                    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_domain_lock);
                    if (last) last->on_close(last);
                }
                goto write_response;
            }
            req.ndomain_in = nin;
            for (int i = 0; i < nin; i++) req.domain_in_objs[i] = *(uint32_t *)(payload + 16 + dsize + 4 * i);
            payload += 16;
        }
        if (memcmp(payload, "SFCI", 4)) {
            LOG("[ipc] bad SFCI magic on %s (domain=%d):", sess->svc->name, sess->domain != NULL);
            for (int i = 0; i < 24; i++) LOG(" %08x", msg[i]);
            LOG("\n");
        }
        req.cmd = *(uint32_t *)(payload + 8);
        req.data = payload + 16;
        req.data_size = raw_words * 4 > 32 ? raw_words * 4 - 32 : 0;
        Service *target = sess->svc;
        if (sess->domain) {
            pthread_mutex_lock(&g_domain_lock);
            target = req.domain_obj < 256 ? sess->domain->objs[req.domain_obj] : NULL;
            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_domain_lock);
            if (!target) {
                LOG("[ipc] domain object %u missing on %s (cmd %u)\n", req.domain_obj, sess->svc->name, req.cmd);
                return 0xE401;
            }
        }
        target->handler(target, &req, &resp);
    } else if (req.type == 5 || req.type == 7) {  // control
        req.cmd = *(uint32_t *)(payload + 8);
        LOG("[ipc] control %u on %s (handle %x)\n", req.cmd, sess->svc->name, handle);
        switch (req.cmd) {
        case 0:  // ConvertCurrentObjectToDomain
            sess->domain = calloc(1, sizeof(Domain));
            sess->domain->objs[1] = sess->svc;
            resp_size(&resp, 4);
            *(uint32_t *)resp.data = 1;
            break;
        case 2: case 4: {  // CloneCurrentObject(Ex)
            uint32_t h = session_new(sess->svc);
            ((KSession *)handle_get(h))->domain = sess->domain;
            resp.move_handles[resp.nmove++] = h;
            break;
        }
        case 3:  // QueryPointerBufferSize
            *(uint16_t *)resp.data = 0x8000;
            resp_size(&resp, 4);
            break;
        default:
            LOG("[ipc] control cmd %u\n", req.cmd);
        }
    } else {
        LOG("[ipc] message type %u\n", req.type);
    }

write_response:;
    // returned objects: domain objects or new sessions
    uint32_t domain_out[8];
    int ndomain_out = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < resp.nobjects; i++) {
        if (dom) {
            pthread_mutex_lock(&g_domain_lock);
            int id = 1;
            while (id < 256 && sess->domain->objs[id]) id++;
            if (id == 256) FATAL("[ipc] domain of %s full (256 objects)\n", sess->svc->name);
            sess->domain->objs[id] = resp.objects[i];
            resp.objects[i]->refs++;
            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_domain_lock);
            domain_out[ndomain_out++] = id;
        } else {
            resp.move_handles[resp.nmove++] = session_new(resp.objects[i]);
        }
    }
    memset(msg, 0, 0x100);
    uint32_t *w = msg;
    int has_handles = resp.ncopy || resp.nmove;
    uint32_t payload_words = 4 + (resp.data_size + 3) / 4;   // SFCO header + data
    if (dom) payload_words += 4 + ndomain_out;
    uint32_t raw_size = payload_words + 4;  // + alignment padding
    w[0] = 0;  // type 0 response
    w[1] = raw_size | (has_handles ? 0x80000000u : 0);
    uint32_t *q = w + 2;
    if (has_handles) {
        *q++ = (resp.ncopy << 1) | (resp.nmove << 5);
        for (int i = 0; i < resp.ncopy; i++) *q++ = resp.copy_handles[i];
        for (int i = 0; i < resp.nmove; i++) *q++ = resp.move_handles[i];
    }
    uint32_t *out = (uint32_t *)(((uintptr_t)q + 15) & ~(uintptr_t)15);
    if (dom) {
        out[0] = ndomain_out;
        out += 4;
    }
    memcpy(out, "SFCO", 4);
    out[1] = 0;
    out[2] = resp.result;
    out[3] = 0;
    memcpy(out + 4, resp.data, resp.data_size);
    if (dom)
        for (int i = 0; i < ndomain_out; i++) out[4 + (resp.data_size + 3) / 4 + i] = domain_out[i];
    return 0;
}

```

`runtime/ipc.h`:

```h
// HIPC/CMIF message handling for HLE services.
#pragma once
#include "kernel.h"

typedef struct {
    uint64_t addr, size;
} IpcBuf;

typedef struct IpcReq {
    uint32_t type;      // 4 = request, 5 = control, 2 = close, 6/7 = with context
    uint32_t cmd;
    const uint8_t *data;  // payload after the SFCI header
    uint32_t data_size;
    uint64_t pid;
    uint32_t copy_handles[8], move_handles[8];
    int ncopy, nmove;
    IpcBuf x[8], a[8], b[8], c[8];
    int nx, na, nb, nc;
    uint32_t domain_obj;  // 0 if not a domain message
    uint32_t domain_in_objs[8];
    int ndomain_in;
} IpcReq;

typedef struct Service Service;

typedef struct IpcResp {
    uint32_t result;
    uint8_t data[0x200];
    uint32_t data_size;
    uint32_t copy_handles[8], move_handles[8];
    int ncopy, nmove;
    Service *objects[8];  // new service objects to return (move handle or domain object)
    int nobjects;
} IpcResp;

typedef void (*ServiceHandler)(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp);

struct Service {
    const char *name;
    ServiceHandler handler;
    void *state;
    int refs;                      // sessions + domain slots holding it
    void (*on_close)(Service *s);  // optional: the last of them closed (stop threads, free state)
};

typedef struct {
    Service *objs[256];
} Domain;

typedef struct {
    KObject obj;
    Service *svc;
    Domain *domain;  // shared by clones of a domain session
} KSession;

// payload helpers
#define IN(type, off) (*(const type *)(req->data + (off)))
#define OUT(type, off) (*(type *)(resp->data + (off)))
static inline void resp_size(IpcResp *resp, uint32_t n) { if (n > resp->data_size) resp->data_size = n; }

// Buffers may be sent as a pair (auto-select): use whichever one is non-empty.
static inline IpcBuf *out_buf(IpcReq *req, int i) {
    if (i < req->nb && req->b[i].size) return &req->b[i];
    if (i < req->nc && req->c[i].size) return &req->c[i];
    return i < req->nb ? &req->b[i] : i < req->nc ? &req->c[i] : NULL;
}
static inline IpcBuf *in_buf(IpcReq *req, int i) {
    if (i < req->na && req->a[i].size) return &req->a[i];
    if (i < req->nx && req->x[i].size) return &req->x[i];
    return i < req->na ? &req->a[i] : i < req->nx ? &req->x[i] : NULL;
}

Service *service_new(const char *name, ServiceHandler h, void *state);
Service *service_lookup(const char *name);  // from the registry (services/*.c)
void ipc_return_object(IpcResp *resp, Service *s);

typedef struct { const char *name; ServiceHandler handler; } ServiceDef;
#ifdef __APPLE__
#define SERVICE_SECTION "__DATA,__services"
#elif defined(__linux__)
#define SERVICE_SECTION "services"
#else
#define SERVICE_SECTION ".svc$m"  // between the .svc$a / .svc$z markers in runtime/ipc.c
#endif
#define SERVICE(sname, fn)                                                                  \
    static void fn(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp);                                 \
    __attribute__((used, section(SERVICE_SECTION))) static const ServiceDef                 \
        HLE_CAT(svc_def_, __LINE__) = {sname, fn};                                          \
    static void fn(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp)

```

`runtime/items.c`:

```c
// The game's items, for the give command and the overlay's Cheats tab: see runtime/items.h.
//
// The list: every actor of Actor/ActorInfo.product.sbyml (BYML) tagged CanGetPouch, by profile (weapons, bows,
// shields, arrows, armour, materials), leaving out the ones tagged Important (the Sheikah Slate, the Master Sword,
// quest items, Korok seeds), cooked dishes (CookResult: they need their effects) and rupees. Each has the name the
// game gives it, <actor>_Name in Message/Msg_<lang>.product.ssarc's ActorType/*.msbt inside Pack/Bootup_<lang>.pack;
// one without a name is left out, and of several actors with one name (armour's upgrade levels, dyes) the first by
// actor name stays.
//
// Adding: the pause menu data's item get (1.9.0 0x7000d921bc; x0 the pause menu data, x1 the item's name as a
// sead::SafeString, w2 its value, x3 its weapon modifier or NULL) is what picking an item up calls: a stack's value
// is how many, a weapon's its durability x 100 (a new one: generalLife x 100). The game thread calls it from
// rt_item_tick (tools/patches.py _item_tick), at the entry of Link's damage handling, which runs every frame in play,
// as picking an item up does.
#include <ctype.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "control.h"
#include "cpu.h"
#include "gamelib.h"
#include "hle.h"
#include "items.h"
#include "language.h"
#include "nvn/tegra.h"
#include "rt.h"
#include "services/archive.h"
#include "ui/i18n.h"

uint8_t *fs_game_file(const char *path, size_t *out_n);  // runtime/services/fs.c

// ---- BYML (little-endian "YB", version 2 and up): dictionaries, arrays, strings and numbers
typedef struct {
    const uint8_t *d;
    size_t n;
    uint32_t keys, strs;  // their string tables
} Byml;

static uint32_t rd32(const uint8_t *p) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, p, 4); return v; }
static char *copy(const char *s, size_t n) {
    char *o = malloc(n + 1);
    if (o) memcpy(o, s, n), o[n] = 0;
    return o;
}
static uint16_t rd16(const uint8_t *p) { uint16_t v; memcpy(&v, p, 2); return v; }

static const char *byml_str(const Byml *b, uint32_t table, uint32_t i) {
    if (!table || table + 8 > b->n || i >= (rd32(b->d + table) >> 8)) return NULL;
    uint32_t o = table + rd32(b->d + table + 4 + 4 * i);
    return o < b->n ? (const char *)b->d + o : NULL;
}
static uint32_t byml_count(const Byml *b, uint32_t node) { return node + 4 <= b->n ? rd32(b->d + node) >> 8 : 0; }
// Entry `key` of the dictionary at `node`: its type and value; false if it has none
static bool byml_get(const Byml *b, uint32_t node, const char *key, uint8_t *type, uint32_t *value) {
    if (node + 4 > b->n || b->d[node] != 0xc1) return false;
    uint32_t n = byml_count(b, node);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n && node + 12 + 8 * i <= b->n; i++) {
        const uint8_t *e = b->d + node + 4 + 8 * i;
        const char *k = byml_str(b, b->keys, rd32(e) & 0xffffff);
        if (k && !strcmp(k, key)) { *type = e[3], *value = rd32(e + 4); return true; }
    }
    return false;
}
static const char *byml_get_str(const Byml *b, uint32_t node, const char *key) {
    uint8_t t; uint32_t v;
    return byml_get(b, node, key, &t, &v) && t == 0xa0 ? byml_str(b, b->strs, v) : NULL;
}
static int byml_get_int(const Byml *b, uint32_t node, const char *key, int def) {
    uint8_t t; uint32_t v;
    return byml_get(b, node, key, &t, &v) && (t == 0xd1 || t == 0xd3) ? (int)v : def;
}

// ---- MSBT: the label's text, UTF-16 to UTF-8, control tags left out
static void utf8_put(char **o, char *end, uint32_t c) {
    char *p = *o;
    if (c < 0x80) { if (p + 1 < end) *p++ = (char)c; }
    else if (c < 0x800) { if (p + 2 < end) *p++ = (char)(0xc0 | c >> 6), *p++ = (char)(0x80 | (c & 63)); }
    else if (p + 3 < end) *p++ = (char)(0xe0 | c >> 12), *p++ = (char)(0x80 | ((c >> 6) & 63)), *p++ = (char)(0x80 | (c & 63));
    *o = p;
}

typedef struct { char *label, *text; } Msg;
static Msg *g_msgs;
static int g_nmsgs, g_capmsgs;

static void msbt_read(const uint8_t *d, size_t n) {
    if (n < 0x20 || memcmp(d, "MsgStdBn", 8) || d[8] != 0xff) return;  // (little-endian only, as the Switch's are)
    uint16_t nsec = rd16(d + 0xe);
    size_t off = 0x20, lbl = 0, txt = 0, txt_size = 0;
    for (int s = 0; s < nsec && off + 0x10 <= n; s++) {
        uint32_t size = rd32(d + off + 4);
        if (!memcmp(d + off, "LBL1", 4)) lbl = off + 0x10;
        if (!memcmp(d + off, "TXT2", 4)) txt = off + 0x10, txt_size = size;
        off = (off + 0x10 + size + 15) & ~(size_t)15;
    }
    if (!lbl || !txt || txt + 4 > n) return;
    uint32_t ntxt = rd32(d + txt), nb = rd32(d + lbl);
    for (uint32_t b = 0; b < nb && lbl + 12 + 8 * b <= n; b++) {
        uint32_t cnt = rd32(d + lbl + 4 + 8 * b);
        size_t p = lbl + rd32(d + lbl + 8 + 8 * b);
        for (uint32_t k = 0; k < cnt && p < n; k++) {
            uint8_t len = d[p];
            if (p + 1 + len + 4 > n) return;
            uint32_t idx = rd32(d + p + 1 + len);
            if (len > 5 && !memcmp(d + p + 1 + len - 5, "_Name", 5) && idx < ntxt) {
                size_t t0 = txt + rd32(d + txt + 4 + 4 * idx);
                size_t t1 = idx + 1 < ntxt ? txt + rd32(d + txt + 8 + 4 * idx) : txt + txt_size;
                char buf[160], *o = buf;
                for (size_t q = t0; q + 1 < t1 && q + 1 < n;) {
                    uint16_t c = rd16(d + q);
                    q += 2;
                    if (!c) break;
                    if (c == 0x0e) { if (q + 6 <= n) q += 6 + rd16(d + q + 4); continue; }  // (a tag: group, type, size, data)
                    if (c >= 0xd800 && c < 0xdc00 && q + 1 < n) {
                        uint16_t lo = rd16(d + q);
                        q += 2;
                        utf8_put(&o, buf + sizeof buf, 0x10000 + ((c - 0xd800) << 10) + (lo - 0xdc00));
                        continue;
                    }
                    utf8_put(&o, buf + sizeof buf, c);
                }
                while (o > buf && (o[-1] == ' ' || (o[-1] == 'x' && o - 1 > buf && o[-2] == ' '))) o--;  // ("... x ": a count's place)
                *o = 0;
                if (buf[0]) {
                    if (g_nmsgs == g_capmsgs) g_capmsgs = g_capmsgs ? g_capmsgs * 2 : 1024, g_msgs = realloc(g_msgs, sizeof *g_msgs * g_capmsgs);
                    g_msgs[g_nmsgs].label = copy((const char *)d + p + 1, len - 5);
                    g_msgs[g_nmsgs++].text = copy(buf, strlen(buf));
                }
            }
            p += 1 + len + 4;
        }
    }
}
static int msg_cmp(const void *a, const void *b) { return strcmp(((const Msg *)a)->label, ((const Msg *)b)->label); }
static const char *msg_name(const char *actor) {
    Msg k = {(char *)actor, NULL};
    Msg *m = bsearch(&k, g_msgs, g_nmsgs, sizeof *g_msgs, msg_cmp);
    return m ? m->text : NULL;
}

static void names_read(void) {
    const char *lang = language_text_folder();
    char path[64], inner[64];
    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "Pack/Bootup_%s.pack", lang);
    snprintf(inner, sizeof inner, "Message/Msg_%s.product.ssarc", lang);
    size_t pn = 0, mn = 0;
    uint8_t *pack = fs_game_file(path, &pn), *msg = NULL;
    uint32_t doff, s, e;
    if (pack && sarc_find(pack, pn, inner, &doff, &s, &e) >= 0) msg = yaz0_unpack(pack + doff + s, e - s, &mn);
    int nodes = msg ? sarc_count(msg, mn) : -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < nodes; i++) {
        const char *name; const uint8_t *data; size_t size;
        if (sarc_node(msg, mn, i, &name, &data, &size) && name && !strncmp(name, "ActorType/", 10)) msbt_read(data, size);
    }
    if (g_nmsgs) qsort(g_msgs, g_nmsgs, sizeof *g_msgs, msg_cmp);
    LOG("[items] %d names from %s\n", g_nmsgs, path);
    free(msg), free(pack);
}

// ---- the list
static GameItem *g_items;
static int g_nitems = -1;
static pthread_once_t g_once = PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT;

static uint32_t tag(const char *s) {  // (the tags are CRC-32s of their names)
    uint32_t c = 0xffffffff;
    for (; *s; s++) {
        c ^= (uint8_t)*s;
        for (int k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c >> 1 ^ (0xedb88320 & -(c & 1));
    }
    return ~c;
}
static bool has_tag(const Byml *b, uint32_t actor, uint32_t t) {
    uint8_t ty; uint32_t tags;
    if (!byml_get(b, actor, "tags", &ty, &tags) || ty != 0xc1) return false;
    uint32_t n = byml_count(b, tags);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n && tags + 12 + 8 * i <= b->n; i++)
        if (rd32(b->d + tags + 8 + 8 * i) == t) return true;
    return false;
}
static int item_cmp(const void *a, const void *b) {
    const GameItem *x = a, *y = b;
    if (x->cat != y->cat) return x->cat - y->cat;
    int c = strcmp(x->name, y->name);
    return c ? c : strcmp(x->actor, y->actor);
}

// An effect type ("ResistCold", "ResistColdAndResistAncient") as up to two ITEMFX_*; one the list lacks is left out
// (WakeWind, the Island Lobster Shirt's second: its description in the game tells of it)
static void effects(const char *type, unsigned char out[2]) {
    static const char *const ids[ITEMFX_COUNT] = {
        NULL, "AttackUp", "DefenseUp", "ClimbSpeed", "BeamPowerUp", "Quietness", "ResistAncient", "ResistBurn", "ResistCold",
        "ResistElectric", "ResistFreeze", "ResistHot", "ResistLightning", "SandMove", "SnowMove", "SwimSpeed",
        "ExGutsMaxUp", "Fireproof", "GutsRecover", "LifeMaxUp", "MovingSpeed",
    };
    int n = 0;
    for (const char *p = type; p && *p && n < 2;) {
        const char *and = strstr(p, "And");
        size_t len = and ? (size_t)(and - p) : strlen(p);
        for (int k = 1; k < ITEMFX_COUNT; k++)
            if (strlen(ids[k]) == len && !strncmp(p, ids[k], len)) out[n++] = (unsigned char)k;
        p = and ? and + 3 : NULL;
    }
}

static void list_read(void) {
    g_nitems = 0;
    size_t zn = 0, n = 0;
    uint8_t *z = fs_game_file("Actor/ActorInfo.product.sbyml", &zn), *d = z ? yaz0_unpack(z, zn, &n) : NULL;
    free(z);
    if (!d || n < 16 || memcmp(d, "YB", 2)) { LOG("[items] no ActorInfo\n"); free(d); return; }
    Byml b = {d, n, rd32(d + 4), rd32(d + 8)};
    uint8_t t; uint32_t actors;
    if (!byml_get(&b, rd32(d + 12), "Actors", &t, &actors) || t != 0xc0) { free(d); return; }
    names_read();
    static const struct { const char *profile; int cat; } profiles[] = {
        {"WeaponSmallSword", ITEMCAT_WEAPON}, {"WeaponLargeSword", ITEMCAT_WEAPON}, {"WeaponSpear", ITEMCAT_WEAPON},
        {"WeaponBow", ITEMCAT_BOW}, {"WeaponShield", ITEMCAT_SHIELD}, {"Bullet", ITEMCAT_ARROW},
        {"ArmorHead", ITEMCAT_ARMOR}, {"ArmorUpper", ITEMCAT_ARMOR}, {"ArmorLower", ITEMCAT_ARMOR}, {"Item", ITEMCAT_MATERIAL},
        // critters and fairies (Animal_Insect_*: bugs, lizards, frogs, fairies) are CapturedActors; CanGetPouch below
        // leaves out what the pouch can't hold
        {"CapturedActor", ITEMCAT_MATERIAL},
    };
    uint32_t can_get = tag("CanGetPouch"), important = tag("Important"), cooked = tag("CookResult"), rupee = tag("Rupee"),
             arrow = tag("Arrow");
    uint32_t na = byml_count(&b, actors);
    const uint8_t *types = d + actors + 4;
    uint32_t vals = actors + 4 + ((na + 3) & ~3u);
    g_items = calloc(na ? na : 1, sizeof *g_items);
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < na && vals + 4 * i + 4 <= n; i++) {
        if (types[i] != 0xc1) continue;
        uint32_t a = rd32(d + vals + 4 * i);
        const char *actor = byml_get_str(&b, a, "name"), *profile = byml_get_str(&b, a, "profile");
        if (!actor || !profile || !has_tag(&b, a, can_get) || has_tag(&b, a, important) || has_tag(&b, a, cooked) ||
            has_tag(&b, a, rupee))
            continue;
        // The One-Hit Obliterator belongs to one quest: outside it, Link can't put it away and it drains his hearts (#652)
        if (!strcmp(actor, "Weapon_Sword_502")) continue;
        int cat = -1;
        for (size_t p = 0; p < sizeof profiles / sizeof *profiles; p++)
            if (!strcmp(profile, profiles[p].profile)) cat = profiles[p].cat;
        if (cat < 0 || (cat == ITEMCAT_ARROW && !has_tag(&b, a, arrow))) continue;
        if (cat == ITEMCAT_MATERIAL && !strncmp(actor, "Obj_", 4) && strstr(actor, "Arrow")) cat = ITEMCAT_ARROW;  // (bundles: Obj_AncientArrow_C_01)
        const char *name = msg_name(actor);
        if (!name) continue;
        GameItem *it = &g_items[g_nitems++];
        it->actor = copy(actor, strlen(actor)), it->name = name, it->cat = cat;
        it->stack = cat == ITEMCAT_ARROW || cat == ITEMCAT_MATERIAL;
        it->value = cat <= ITEMCAT_SHIELD ? byml_get_int(&b, a, "generalLife", 1) * 100 : 1;
        it->attack = byml_get_int(&b, a, "attackPower", 0);
        it->durability = cat <= ITEMCAT_SHIELD ? byml_get_int(&b, a, "generalLife", 0) : 0;
        it->guard = byml_get_int(&b, a, "weaponCommonGuardPower", 0);
        it->defense = byml_get_int(&b, a, "armorDefenceAddLevel", 0);
        it->hearts = byml_get_int(&b, a, "cureItemHitPointRecover", 0);
        it->price = byml_get_int(&b, a, "itemSellingPrice", 0);
        effects(byml_get_str(&b, a, cat == ITEMCAT_ARMOR ? "armorEffectEffectType" : "cureItemEffectType"), it->effect);
    }
    qsort(g_items, g_nitems, sizeof *g_items, item_cmp);
    int w = 0;  // (one per name and category)
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nitems; i++)
        if (!w || g_items[w - 1].cat != g_items[i].cat || strcmp(g_items[w - 1].name, g_items[i].name)) g_items[w++] = g_items[i];
    g_nitems = w;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nitems; i++) ui_register_glyphs(g_items[i].name);
    LOG("[items] %d items can be added\n", g_nitems);
    free(d);
}

int items_count(void) { pthread_once(&g_once, list_read); return g_nitems; }
const GameItem *items_at(int i) { return i >= 0 && i < items_count() ? &g_items[i] : NULL; }

// ---- the item's picture in the pouch: UI/StockItem/<actor>.sbitemico, a Yaz0 BFRES whose BNTX holds one RGBA8
// texture (BRTI: format 0x0bXX at +0x1c, width and height at +0x24, GOBs per block (log2) at +0x34), block linear,
// its data 16 bytes into the BRTD section
static const uint8_t *find4(const uint8_t *p, const uint8_t *end, const char *magic) {
    for (; p + 4 <= end; p++)
        if (!memcmp(p, magic, 4)) return p;
    return NULL;
}
unsigned char *items_icon(int i, int *w, int *h) {
    const GameItem *it = items_at(i);
    if (!it) return NULL;
    char path[128];
    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "UI/StockItem/%s.sbitemico", it->actor);
    size_t zn = 0, n = 0;
    uint8_t *z = fs_game_file(path, &zn), *d = z ? yaz0_unpack(z, zn, &n) : NULL, *out = NULL;
    free(z);
    const uint8_t *end = d ? d + n : NULL, *k = d ? find4(d, end, "BNTX") : NULL;
    const uint8_t *r = k ? find4(k, end, "BRTI") : NULL, *t = k ? find4(k, end, "BRTD") : NULL;
    if (r && t && r + 0x38 <= end) {
        uint32_t fmt = rd32(r + 0x1c), iw = rd32(r + 0x24), ih = rd32(r + 0x28), bh = rd32(r + 0x34);
        uint64_t gob_rows = 8ull << (bh < 6 ? bh : 0), rows = (ih + gob_rows - 1) / gob_rows * gob_rows;
        uint64_t size = ((uint64_t)iw * 4 + 63) / 64 * 64 * rows;
        if ((fmt >> 8) == 0x0b && iw && ih && iw <= 512 && ih <= 512 && bh < 6 && (uint64_t)(end - t) >= 16 + size &&
            (out = malloc((size_t)iw * ih * 4))) {
            tegra_deswizzle(t + 16, out, iw, ih, 1, 4, bh, 0);
            *w = (int)iw, *h = (int)ih;
        }
    }
    free(d);
    return out;
}

bool items_available(void) {
    const GameLibTables *t = gamelib_tables();
    if (!t) return false;
    for (uint32_t k = 0; k < *t->nsites; k++)
        if (!strcmp(t->sites[k].name, "item_tick")) return true;
    return false;
}

// ---- requests, carried out on the game thread
typedef struct { char actor[64]; int item, value, times, asked; unsigned seq; bool stack; } Request;
static Request g_req[32];
static int g_nreq;
static atomic_int g_pending;
static unsigned g_seq;
static ItemResult g_result;
static pthread_mutex_t g_req_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

RT_ON_RESET(items_reset) {  // (what was asked for in the last boot isn't for this one)
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_req_lock);
    g_nreq = 0;
    atomic_store(&g_pending, 0);
    g_result = (ItemResult){g_seq, -1, 0, 0};
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_req_lock);
}

unsigned items_requested(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_req_lock);
    unsigned n = g_seq;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_req_lock);
    return n;
}

ItemResult items_last_result(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_req_lock);
    ItemResult r = g_result;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_req_lock);
    return r;
}

// How many entries the pouch has: the pause menu data's list of them at +0x78, its free entries at +0x90, 420 in all
// (seen comparing the object around item gets, 1.9.0). The item get adds nothing when the player has no free slot of
// that kind, and says nothing of it. -1: not those fields, this game version has them elsewhere.
static int pouch_entries(uint64_t pmdm) {
    uint32_t used = *(volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(pmdm + 0x78), free_ = *(volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(pmdm + 0x90);
    return used + free_ == 420 ? (int)used : -1;
}

bool items_request(int i, int count) {
    const GameItem *it = items_at(i);
    if (!it || count < 1) return false;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_req_lock);
    bool ok = g_nreq < (int)(sizeof g_req / sizeof *g_req);
    if (ok) {
        Request *r = &g_req[g_nreq++];
        snprintf(r->actor, sizeof r->actor, "%s", it->actor);
        r->item = i, r->seq = ++g_seq;
        r->value = it->stack ? (count > 999 ? 999 : count) : it->value;
        r->times = it->stack ? 1 : (count > ITEMS_MAX_EACH ? ITEMS_MAX_EACH : count);
        r->asked = it->stack ? r->value : r->times;
        r->stack = it->stack;
        atomic_store(&g_pending, g_nreq);
    }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_req_lock);
    return ok;
}

// The game thread, every frame in play (tools/patches.py _item_tick: at a function's entry, so only its arguments are
// live; the whole guest CPU state is put back afterwards). get: the item get; mgr: where the pause menu data's address
// is; sstr_vt: sead::SafeString's vtable. The name and its SafeString go on the guest stack below sp.
void rt_item_tick(Cpu *c, uint64_t get, uint64_t mgr, uint64_t sstr_vt) {
    if (!atomic_load_explicit(&g_pending, memory_order_relaxed)) return;
    Request req[32];
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_req_lock);
    int n = g_nreq;
    memcpy(req, g_req, sizeof *req * n);
    g_nreq = 0;
    atomic_store(&g_pending, 0);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_req_lock);
    uint64_t pmdm = *(volatile uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)mgr;
    if (!pmdm) return;
    Cpu *keep = malloc(sizeof *keep);
    if (!keep) return;
    memcpy(keep, c, sizeof *c);
    uint64_t buf = (c->sp - 0x100) & ~15ull;
    for (int r = 0; r < n; r++) {
        memcpy((void *)(uintptr_t)(buf + 0x20), req[r].actor, sizeof req[r].actor);
        *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)buf = sstr_vt;
        *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(buf + 8) = buf + 0x20;
        bool stack = req[r].stack;
        int added = stack ? req[r].asked : 0;  // (a stack: all of it at once)
        for (int k = 0; k < req[r].times; k++) {
            int before = pouch_entries(pmdm);
            c->sp = buf;
            c->x[0] = pmdm, c->x[1] = buf, c->x[2] = (uint32_t)req[r].value, c->x[3] = 0;
            guest_call(c, get);
            // (a stack may only grow an entry it has: there no new entry says nothing)
            if (!stack && before >= 0 && pouch_entries(pmdm) == before) break;
            if (!stack) added++;
        }
        LOG("[items] %s: value %d, %d of %d\n", req[r].actor, req[r].value, added, req[r].asked);
        pthread_mutex_lock(&g_req_lock);
        g_result = (ItemResult){req[r].seq, req[r].item, req[r].asked, added};
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_req_lock);
    }
    memcpy(c, keep, sizeof *c);
    free(keep);
}

// ---- give <actor> [count]
static bool has_text(const char *s, const char *t) {  // (ignoring case)
    size_t n = strlen(t);
    for (; *s; s++) {
        size_t k = 0;
        while (k < n && tolower((unsigned char)s[k]) == tolower((unsigned char)t[k])) k++;
        if (k == n) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

static void cmd_give(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    if (argc < 2 || argc > 3) { control_fail(r, "Usage: give <actor or part of a name> [count]"); return; }
    int count = argc == 3 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 1, i = 0, n = items_count();
    while (i < n && strcmp(g_items[i].actor, argv[1])) i++;
    if (i == n) {  // not an actor: the items whose name or actor has this in it. One is given, several are listed
        int found = 0, first = n;
        for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
            if (!has_text(g_items[k].name, argv[1]) && !has_text(g_items[k].actor, argv[1])) continue;
            if (!found++) first = k;
        }
        if (!found) { control_fail(r, "No item has this in its name or actor"); return; }
        if (found > 1) {
            // (the fields for scripts, the lines for the console, which prints them instead)
            char list[2048] = "";
            size_t at = 0;
            int shown = 0;
            for (int k = first; k < n && shown < 30; k++) {
                if (!has_text(g_items[k].name, argv[1]) && !has_text(g_items[k].actor, argv[1])) continue;
                control_text(r, "%s  %s", g_items[k].actor, g_items[k].name);
                if (at < sizeof list) at += (size_t)snprintf(list + at, sizeof list - at, "%s%s", shown ? " " : "", g_items[k].actor);
                shown++;
            }
            control_text(r, "%d items match: give one by its actor", found);
            control_field_int(r, "matches", found);
            control_field_str(r, "actors", list);
            return;
        }
        i = first;
    }
    if (!items_available()) { control_fail(r, "The game code has no item get"); return; }
    if (!items_request(i, count)) { control_fail(r, "Too many requests waiting"); return; }
    control_field_str(r, "name", g_items[i].name);
    control_field_int(r, "count", count);
    control_field_str(r, "applied", "next frame in play");
}

void control_items_init(void) {
    static const ControlCmd cmds[] = {
        {"give", "<actor or part of a name> [count]", "Put an item in the pouch, in play (several matches: lists them)", cmd_give},
    };
    control_register(cmds, (int)(sizeof cmds / sizeof *cmds));
}
```
