`runtime/memscan.c`:

```c
// Compare kernels for the optional development memory scanner. No guest pointers are retained.
#include "memscan.h"
#include <math.h>
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <string.h>

#if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__i386__)
#include <immintrin.h>
#define MS_X86 1
#define AVX2 __attribute__((target("avx2")))
#endif

typedef size_t (*Kernel)(const unsigned char *, size_t, const MsMatch *, uint32_t *, size_t, size_t *);

// memcpy permits raw snapshot storage without aliasing typed objects.
#define SCALAR(NAME, TYPE, LOW, HIGH) \
static size_t scalar_##NAME(const unsigned char *p, size_t n, const MsMatch *m, \
                           uint32_t *out, size_t max, size_t *used) { \
    const TYPE lo = (LOW), hi = (HIGH); \
    size_t count = 0, i = 0; \
    for (; i < n && count < max; i += sizeof(TYPE)) { \
        TYPE v; memcpy(&v, p + i, sizeof v); \
        if (v >= lo && v <= hi) out[count++] = (uint32_t)i; \
    } \
    *used = i; return count; \
}
SCALAR(u8, uint8_t, m->ulo, m->uhi)
SCALAR(u16, uint16_t, m->ulo, m->uhi)
SCALAR(u32, uint32_t, m->ulo, m->uhi)
SCALAR(u64, uint64_t, m->ulo, m->uhi)
SCALAR(s32, int32_t, m->slo, m->shi)
SCALAR(f32, float, m->flo, m->fhi)
SCALAR(f64, double, m->flo, m->fhi)
#undef SCALAR

static bool zero_scalar(const unsigned char *p, size_t n) {
    size_t i = 0;
    for (; n - i >= 8; i += 8) {
        uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, p + i, sizeof v);
        if (v) return false;
    }
    for (; i < n; i++) if (p[i]) return false;
    return true;
}

#ifdef MS_X86
static AVX2 bool zero_avx2(const unsigned char *p, size_t n) {
    size_t i = 0;
    for (; n - i >= 128; i += 128) {
        __m256i a = _mm256_or_si256(_mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i *)(p+i)),
                                  _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i *)(p+i+32)));
        __m256i b = _mm256_or_si256(_mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i *)(p+i+64)),
                                  _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i *)(p+i+96)));
        a = _mm256_or_si256(a, b);
        if (!_mm256_testz_si256(a, a)) return false;
    }
    for (; n - i >= 32; i += 32) {
        __m256i a = _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i *)(p+i));
        if (!_mm256_testz_si256(a, a)) return false;
    }
    return zero_scalar(p+i, n-i);
}

// Integer masks have one bit per byte. Keep the first bit of each matching lane.
// Clearing a complete lane avoids emitting a multi-byte integer more than once.
#define VECTOR(NAME, WIDTH, SETUP, MASK) \
static AVX2 size_t avx2_##NAME(const unsigned char *p, size_t n, const MsMatch *m, \
                             uint32_t *out, size_t max, size_t *used) { \
    SETUP; \
    size_t count = 0, i = 0; \
    for (; n - i >= 32; i += 32) { \
        unsigned bits = (MASK); \
        while (bits) { \
            unsigned bit = (unsigned)__builtin_ctz(bits); \
            size_t off = i + bit * (WIDTH); \
            out[count++] = (uint32_t)off; \
            if (count == max) { *used = off + sizeof_type_##NAME; return count; } \
            bits &= bits - 1; \
        } \
    } \
    size_t tail_used; \
    size_t tail = scalar_##NAME(p+i, n-i, m, out+count, max-count, &tail_used); \
    for (size_t j = 0; j < tail; j++) out[count+j] += (uint32_t)i; \
    *used = i + tail_used; return count + tail; \
}
#define LOAD _mm256_loadu_si256((const __m256i *)(p+i))
#define INT_SETUP(SUFFIX, TYPE, L, H, SIGN) \
    const __m256i sign = _mm256_set1_epi##SUFFIX(SIGN); \
    const __m256i lo = _mm256_xor_si256(_mm256_set1_epi##SUFFIX((TYPE)(L)), sign); \
    const __m256i hi = _mm256_xor_si256(_mm256_set1_epi##SUFFIX((TYPE)(H)), sign)
#define INT_MASK(SUFFIX, KEEP) \
    ((unsigned)~_mm256_movemask_epi8(_mm256_or_si256( \
        _mm256_cmpgt_epi##SUFFIX(lo, _mm256_xor_si256(LOAD, sign)), \
        _mm256_cmpgt_epi##SUFFIX(_mm256_xor_si256(LOAD, sign), hi))) & (KEEP))
enum { sizeof_type_u8=1, sizeof_type_u16=2, sizeof_type_u32=4, sizeof_type_u64=8,
       sizeof_type_s32=4, sizeof_type_f32=4, sizeof_type_f64=8 };
VECTOR(u8, 1, INT_SETUP(8, char, m->ulo, m->uhi, (char)0x80), INT_MASK(8, 0xffffffffu))
VECTOR(u16, 1, INT_SETUP(16, short, m->ulo, m->uhi, (short)0x8000), INT_MASK(16, 0x55555555u))
VECTOR(u32, 1, INT_SETUP(32, int, m->ulo, m->uhi, (int)0x80000000u), INT_MASK(32, 0x11111111u))
VECTOR(u64, 1, INT_SETUP(64x, long long, m->ulo, m->uhi, (long long)0x8000000000000000ull), INT_MASK(64, 0x01010101u))
VECTOR(s32, 1, INT_SETUP(32, int, m->slo, m->shi, 0), INT_MASK(32, 0x11111111u))
VECTOR(f32, 4,
       const __m256 lo = _mm256_set1_ps((float)m->flo); const __m256 hi = _mm256_set1_ps((float)m->fhi),
       (unsigned)_mm256_movemask_ps(_mm256_and_ps(
           _mm256_cmp_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps((const float *)(p+i)), lo, _CMP_GE_OQ),
           _mm256_cmp_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps((const float *)(p+i)), hi, _CMP_LE_OQ))))
VECTOR(f64, 8,
       const __m256d lo = _mm256_set1_pd(m->flo); const __m256d hi = _mm256_set1_pd(m->fhi),
       (unsigned)_mm256_movemask_pd(_mm256_and_pd(
           _mm256_cmp_pd(_mm256_loadu_pd((const double *)(p+i)), lo, _CMP_GE_OQ),
           _mm256_cmp_pd(_mm256_loadu_pd((const double *)(p+i)), hi, _CMP_LE_OQ))))
#undef VECTOR
#undef LOAD
#undef INT_SETUP
#undef INT_MASK

static bool have_avx2(void) {
    // 0 unknown, 1 scalar, 2 AVX2. Concurrent first calls are safe and equivalent.
    static atomic_int choice;
    int c = atomic_load_explicit(&choice, memory_order_relaxed);
    if (!c) {
        c = __builtin_cpu_supports("avx2") ? 2 : 1;
        atomic_store_explicit(&choice, c, memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    return c == 2;
}
#endif

size_t ms_scan(const void *p, size_t n, const MsMatch *match, bool skip_zero,
               uint32_t *out, size_t max, MsStats *st) {
    if (!max || !n) return 0;
    MsMatch m = *match;
    static const Kernel scalar[] = { scalar_u8, scalar_u16, scalar_u32, scalar_u64,
                                     scalar_s32, scalar_f32, scalar_f64 };
    if ((unsigned)m.type > MS_F64) return 0;
    if (m.type <= MS_U64) {
        static const uint64_t limits[] = { UINT8_MAX, UINT16_MAX, UINT32_MAX, UINT64_MAX };
        if (m.ulo > m.uhi || m.ulo > limits[m.type]) return 0;
        if (m.uhi > limits[m.type]) m.uhi = limits[m.type];
    } else if (m.type == MS_S32) {
        if (m.slo > m.shi || m.slo > INT32_MAX || m.shi < INT32_MIN) return 0;
        if (m.slo < INT32_MIN) m.slo = INT32_MIN;
        if (m.shi > INT32_MAX) m.shi = INT32_MAX;
    } else {
        if (!(m.flo <= m.fhi)) return 0;
        if (m.type == MS_F32) {
            float lo = (float)m.flo, hi = (float)m.fhi;
            if ((double)lo > m.flo) lo = nextafterf(lo, -INFINITY);
            if ((double)hi < m.fhi) hi = nextafterf(hi, INFINITY);
            m.flo = lo; m.fhi = hi;
        }
    }
    Kernel kernel = scalar[m.type];
    bool (*zero)(const unsigned char *, size_t) = zero_scalar;
#ifdef MS_X86
    if (have_avx2()) {
        static const Kernel vector[] = { avx2_u8, avx2_u16, avx2_u32, avx2_u64,
                                         avx2_s32, avx2_f32, avx2_f64 };
        kernel = vector[m.type]; zero = zero_avx2;
    }
#endif
    size_t count = 0;
    for (size_t page = 0; page < n && count < max;) {
        size_t bytes = n - page < 4096 ? n - page : 4096;
        const unsigned char *src = (const unsigned char *)p + page;
        if (skip_zero && zero(src, bytes)) {
            if (st) st->zero_bytes += bytes;
        } else {
            size_t used;
            size_t got = kernel(src, bytes, &m, out+count, max-count, &used);
            for (size_t j = 0; j < got; j++) out[count+j] += (uint32_t)page;
            count += got;
            if (st) st->compared += used;
        }
        page += bytes;
    }
    return count;
}

```

`runtime/memscan.h`:

```h
// (test and development only) The fast parts of the control endpoint's memory scan (runtime/control_mem.c):
// the compare kernels (runtime/memscan.c) and the OS helpers (runtime/memscan_os.c).
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

// ---- compare kernels (runtime/memscan.c)
enum { MS_U8, MS_U16, MS_U32, MS_U64, MS_S32, MS_F32, MS_F64 };  // same order as control_mem.c's types

// What a value must be to match: lo <= v <= hi, in the type's own domain (integers exact when lo == hi; floats with
// a tolerance give lo = target - tol, hi = target + tol). NaN never matches.
typedef struct {
    int type;               // MS_*
    uint64_t ulo, uhi;      // MS_U8..MS_U64
    int64_t slo, shi;       // MS_S32
    double flo, fhi;        // MS_F32 / MS_F64
} MsMatch;

typedef struct {
    uint64_t zero_bytes;    // bytes skipped as all-zero 4 KB pages
    uint64_t compared;      // bytes compared
} MsStats;

// Compare the naturally aligned values in [p, p + n) (p aligned to the type's width; n a multiple of it). Writes the
// byte offsets (from p) of matches to out, at most max of them, and returns how many it wrote. With skip_zero, a
// 4 KB page (relative to p, which callers align to 4 KB) that is all zero is skipped without comparing (callers pass
// skip_zero only when 0 cannot match). Uses AVX2 where the CPU has it, else plain C; both give identical results.
size_t ms_scan(const void *p, size_t n, const MsMatch *m, bool skip_zero, uint32_t *out, size_t max, MsStats *st);

// ---- OS helpers (runtime/memscan_os.c)
// Which of the npages 4 KB pages from addr (4 KB aligned) are resident in RAM: resident[i] = 1 or 0. Returns false
// when the OS can't say (then the caller treats every page as resident). On Windows a page trimmed out of the working
// set is not resident but still holds data, so skipping non-resident pages can miss values.
bool ms_resident(uint64_t addr, size_t npages, uint8_t *resident);

// Run fn(p, n, ctx) over memory that may become inaccessible while it runs, without crashing: on Windows under SEH
// (__try), elsewhere by copying through the OS first (fn then sees a copy). Returns false if the access faulted;
// *ret gets fn's result otherwise.
typedef size_t (*MsFn)(const void *p, size_t n, void *ctx);
bool ms_guarded(const void *p, size_t n, MsFn fn, void *ctx, size_t *ret);

```

`runtime/memscan_os.c`:

```c
// (test and development only) Residency queries never touch guest pages. Guarded reads tolerate unload races.
#ifndef _GNU_SOURCE
#define _GNU_SOURCE
#endif
#include "memscan.h"

#include <string.h>

#ifdef _WIN32
#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#include <windows.h>
#include <psapi.h>

bool ms_resident(uint64_t addr, size_t npages, uint8_t *resident) {
    PSAPI_WORKING_SET_EX_INFORMATION pages[4096];
    if (npages > (UINT64_MAX - addr) / 4096) return false;
    for (size_t base = 0; base < npages;) {
        size_t count = npages - base;
        if (count > 4096) count = 4096;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            pages[i].VirtualAddress = (void *)(uintptr_t)(addr + (base + i) * 4096);
            pages[i].VirtualAttributes.Flags = 0;
        }
        if (!K32QueryWorkingSetEx(GetCurrentProcess(), pages, (DWORD)(count * sizeof *pages))) return false;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++) resident[base + i] = pages[i].VirtualAttributes.Valid ? 1 : 0;
        base += count;
    }
    return true;
}

bool ms_guarded(const void *p, size_t n, MsFn fn, void *ctx, size_t *ret) {
    // Clang's x64 SEH scope encloses the call instruction, so callee faults unwind into this handler too.
    // The runtime's vectored lazy-commit handler runs first: callers must exclude uncommitted guest pages.
    __try {
        *ret = fn(p, n, ctx);
    } __except ((GetExceptionCode() == EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION ||
                 GetExceptionCode() == EXCEPTION_IN_PAGE_ERROR) ?
                EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER : EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH) {
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}

#else
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#ifdef __APPLE__
#include <mach/mach.h>
#include <mach/mach_vm.h>
#else
#include <sys/uio.h>
#endif

bool ms_resident(uint64_t addr, size_t npages, uint8_t *resident) {
    if (!npages) return true;
    long page_size = sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);
    if (page_size < 4096 || page_size % 4096 || addr % 4096 ||
        npages > (UINTPTR_MAX - addr) / 4096) return false;
    uint64_t native = (uint64_t)page_size;
    // macOS can use 16 KB pages. Translate their residency bits back to the caller's 4 KB pages.
    for (size_t base = 0; base < npages;) {
        size_t count = npages - base;
        if (count > 4096) count = 4096;
        uint64_t start = addr + base * 4096, aligned = start - start % native;
        size_t bytes = (size_t)(start - aligned) + count * 4096;
#ifdef __APPLE__
        char vec[4097];
#else
        unsigned char vec[4097];
#endif
        if (mincore((void *)(uintptr_t)aligned, bytes, vec)) return false;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < count; i++)
            resident[base + i] = (uint8_t)(vec[(start - aligned + i * 4096) / native] & 1);
        base += count;
    }
    return true;
}

// The snapshot buffer of each thread that calls ms_guarded, allocated on its first call and freed when it exits.
// A 1 MB _Thread_local array would sit in the static TLS of every thread in the process, which glibc carves out of
// each thread's stack: a thread created with a 1 MB stack (the Vulkan recorder, record.c rec_init) then failed.
#define MS_COPY_MAX (1024 * 1024)
static pthread_key_t copy_key;
static bool copy_key_ok;
static pthread_once_t copy_once = PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT;
static void copy_key_init(void) { copy_key_ok = pthread_key_create(&copy_key, free) == 0; }

bool ms_guarded(const void *p, size_t n, MsFn fn, void *ctx, size_t *ret) {
    // Unix callers pass at most 1 MB. One snapshot preserves fn's length and byte-offset semantics.
    // Each worker owns its buffer; the callback must not recursively call ms_guarded on this thread.
    if (n > MS_COPY_MAX) return false;
    pthread_once(&copy_once, copy_key_init);
    if (!copy_key_ok) return false;
    unsigned char *copy = pthread_getspecific(copy_key);
    if (!copy) {
        copy = malloc(MS_COPY_MAX);  // (malloc aligns for any type)
        if (!copy) return false;
        if (pthread_setspecific(copy_key, copy)) { free(copy); return false; }
    }
    if (n) {
#ifdef __APPLE__
        mach_vm_size_t got = 0;
        if (mach_vm_read_overwrite(mach_task_self(), (mach_vm_address_t)(uintptr_t)p, n,
                                  (mach_vm_address_t)(uintptr_t)copy, &got) != KERN_SUCCESS || got != n)
            return false;
#else
        struct iovec local = {copy, n}, remote = {(void *)p, n};
        if (process_vm_readv(getpid(), &local, 1, &remote, 1, 0) != (ssize_t)n) {
            extern uint64_t g_mem_direct_lo, g_mem_direct_hi;  // (control_mem.h: the heap's dma-buf mapping)
            uint64_t a = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)p;
            if (a < g_mem_direct_lo || a + n > g_mem_direct_hi) return false;
            memcpy(copy, p, n);
        }
#endif
    }
    *ret = fn(copy, n, ctx);
    return true;
}
#endif

```

`runtime/menu_wrap.c`:

```c
// Controls > Menus wrap around: pressing past the last button of a menu goes to the first, and back.
//
// The game's menus (the title menu, the System tab, the Adventure Log, Options, shops...) move their focus with one
// routine: the focused button's neighbour link for that direction, else the nearest focusable button roughly that
// way (tools/patches.py _menu_wrap: the end of that search). At the end of a list it finds none and the focus stays.
// Then this returns the button farthest the other way, in the same column (up / down) or row (left / right): nothing
// lies the pressed way, so every candidate is the other way. The candidates are the search's own: the focusable
// buttons (their isFocusable, vtable +0x28, for the screen's layer) of the control's active layers. Off: the game's
// result, untouched. Screens that switch pages at a list's edge (the inventory's categories) do it elsewhere and keep
// doing it (user play test 2026-11-11: the inventory still changes category at the grid's edge).
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "game_sites.h"
#include "hle.h"
#include "settings.h"

static bool in_guest(uint64_t p) { return p >= GUEST_LO && p < GUEST_HI - 0x100; }
static bool ptr(uint64_t p) { return in_guest(p) && !(p & 7); }

static uint64_t call(Cpu *c, uint64_t fn, uint64_t x0, uint64_t x1) {
    Cpu saved = *c;
    c->x[0] = x0, c->x[1] = x1;
    guest_call(c, fn);
    uint64_t r = c->x[0];
    *c = saved;
    return r;
}

// A button's centre on screen: its pane's global matrix translation (what the search compares)
static bool centre(uint64_t button, float *x, float *y) {
    uint64_t owner = LD64(button + 0x18), pane = ptr(owner) ? LD64(owner + 0x60) : 0;
    if (!ptr(pane)) return false;
    memcpy(x, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(pane + 0x7c), 4);
    memcpy(y, (const void *)(uintptr_t)(pane + 0x8c), 4);
    return true;
}

// found: the search's result; control: the control it searched for (its focused button at +0x48, its screen's
// layout at +0x20 -> +0x80); dir: 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right
uint64_t rt_menu_wrap(Cpu *c, uint64_t found, uint64_t control, uint32_t dir) {
    if (found || !g_settings.menu_wrap || dir > 3 || !g_site.ui_control_layer) return found;
    uint64_t cur = LD64(control + 0x48), owner = LD64(control + 0x20), screen = ptr(owner) ? LD64(owner + 0x80) : 0;
    uint64_t mgr = ptr(screen) ? LD64(screen + 0x28) : 0;
    float cx, cy;
    if (!ptr(cur) || !ptr(mgr) || !centre(cur, &cx, &cy)) return found;
    uint32_t layer = (uint32_t)call(c, g_site.ui_control_layer, screen, 0);
    const int8_t *active = (const int8_t *)(uintptr_t)LD64(mgr + 0x40);  // (per layer: negative = off)
    int count = (int)LD32(mgr + 0x28), end = (int)LD32(mgr + 0x38), i = 0;
    if (!in_guest((uint64_t)(uintptr_t)active) || count <= 0 || count > 4096) return found;  // (1.9.0: 99 layers)
    while (i < count && active[i] < 0) i++;
    while (end < count && active[end] < 0) end++;
    uint64_t best = 0;
    float best_score = -1e30f;
    for (; i != end && i < count; i++) {
        if (active[i] < 0) continue;
        uint64_t list = LD64(LD64(mgr + 0x30) + 8ull * i);
        if (!ptr(list)) continue;
        int64_t ofs = (int32_t)LD32(list + 0x9c);  // (the buttons' list node inside each button)
        uint64_t head = list + 0x88, node = LD64(list + 0x90);
        for (int n = 0; node != head && ptr(node) && n < 512; n++, node = LD64(node + 8)) {
            uint64_t b = node - ofs;
            if (b == cur || !ptr(LD64(b)) || !(call(c, LD64(LD64(b) + 0x28), b, layer) & 1)) continue;
            float x, y;
            if (!centre(b, &x, &y)) continue;
            float dx = x - cx, dy = y - cy, ax = dx < 0 ? -dx : dx, ay = dy < 0 ? -dy : dy;
            float along = dir < 2 ? ay : ax, across = dir < 2 ? ax : ay;
            if (along <= across) continue;  // (the same column / row: mostly along the pressed axis)
            float score = along - 3 * across;
            if (score > best_score) best_score = score, best = b;
        }
    }
    return best;
}

```

```c
// ---- bits ----

typedef struct { uint64_t lo, hi; } Bits128;

static inline uint64_t load64(const uint8_t *p) {
    uint64_t v = 0;
    for (int i = 7; i >= 0; i--) v = v << 8 | p[i];
    return v;
}

// n (<= 32) bits at pos; bits past 127 read as zero.
static inline uint32_t rbits(const Bits128 *b, int pos, int n) {
    if (n == 0 || pos >= 128) return 0;
    uint64_t v;
    if (pos >= 64) v = b->hi >> (pos - 64);
    else if (pos == 0) v = b->lo;
    else v = b->lo >> pos | b->hi << (64 - pos);
    return (uint32_t)(v & ((1ull << n) - 1));
}

static inline uint64_t bitrev64(uint64_t v) {
    v = (v >> 1 & 0x5555555555555555ull) | (v & 0x5555555555555555ull) << 1;
    v = (v >> 2 & 0x3333333333333333ull) | (v & 0x3333333333333333ull) << 2;
    v = (v >> 4 & 0x0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0Full) | (v & 0x0F0F0F0F0F0F0F0Full) << 4;
    v = (v >> 8 & 0x00FF00FF00FF00FFull) | (v & 0x00FF00FF00FF00FFull) << 8;
    v = (v >> 16 & 0x0000FFFF0000FFFFull) | (v & 0x0000FFFF0000FFFFull) << 16;
    return v >> 32 | v << 32;
}

// ---- integer sequence encoding ----

static int ise_bitcount(int count, int q) {
    int n = count * q_bits[q];
    if (q_trits[q]) n += (8 * count + 4) / 5;
    if (q_quints[q]) n += (7 * count + 2) / 3;
    return n;
}

static void trits_of(uint32_t T, int t[5]) {
    uint32_t C;
    if ((T >> 2 & 7) == 7) {
        C = (T >> 5 & 7) << 2 | (T & 3);
        t[4] = t[3] = 2;
    } else {
        C = T & 0x1F;
        if ((T >> 5 & 3) == 3) { t[4] = 2; t[3] = T >> 7 & 1; }
        else { t[4] = T >> 7 & 1; t[3] = T >> 5 & 3; }
    }
    if ((C & 3) == 3) {
        t[2] = 2; t[1] = C >> 4 & 1;
        t[0] = (C >> 3 & 1) << 1 | ((C >> 2 & 1) & ~(C >> 3) & 1);
    } else if ((C >> 2 & 3) == 3) {
        t[2] = 2; t[1] = 2; t[0] = C & 3;
    } else {
        t[2] = C >> 4 & 1; t[1] = C >> 2 & 3;
        t[0] = (C >> 1 & 1) << 1 | ((C & 1) & ~(C >> 1) & 1);
    }
}

static void quints_of(uint32_t Q, int q[3]) {
    if ((Q >> 1 & 3) == 3 && (Q >> 5 & 3) == 0) {
        uint32_t q0 = Q & 1;
        q[2] = (int)(q0 << 2 | ((Q >> 4 & 1) & ~q0 & 1) << 1 | ((Q >> 3 & 1) & ~q0 & 1));
        q[1] = q[0] = 4;
        return;
    }
    uint32_t C;
    if ((Q >> 1 & 3) == 3) { q[2] = 4; C = (Q >> 3 & 3) << 3 | (~(Q >> 5) & 3) << 1 | (Q & 1); }
    else { q[2] = Q >> 5 & 3; C = Q & 0x1F; }
    if ((C & 7) == 5) { q[1] = 4; q[0] = C >> 3 & 3; }
    else { q[1] = C >> 3 & 3; q[0] = C & 7; }
}

// Decodes count raw ISE values (tq << bits | bits) starting at bit pos.
static void ise_decode(const Bits128 *b, int pos, int count, int q, uint8_t *out) {
    int nb = q_bits[q];
    if (q_trits[q]) {
        static const uint8_t tb[5] = {2, 2, 1, 2, 1}, ts[5] = {0, 2, 4, 5, 7};
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i += 5) {
            uint32_t m[5], T = 0;
            int k = 0, t[5];
            for (; k < 5 && i + k < count; k++) {
                m[k] = rbits(b, pos, nb); pos += nb;
                T |= rbits(b, pos, tb[k]) << ts[k]; pos += tb[k];
            }
            trits_of(T, t);
            for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) out[i + j] = (uint8_t)((uint32_t)t[j] << nb | m[j]);
        }
    } else if (q_quints[q]) {
        static const uint8_t qb[3] = {3, 2, 2}, qs[3] = {0, 3, 5};
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i += 3) {
            uint32_t m[3], Q = 0;
            int k = 0, v[3];
            for (; k < 3 && i + k < count; k++) {
                m[k] = rbits(b, pos, nb); pos += nb;
                Q |= rbits(b, pos, qb[k]) << qs[k]; pos += qb[k];
            }
            quints_of(Q, v);
            for (int j = 0; j < k; j++) out[i + j] = (uint8_t)((uint32_t)v[j] << nb | m[j]);
        }
    } else {
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++, pos += nb) out[i] = (uint8_t)rbits(b, pos, nb);
    }
}

// ---- block mode ----

typedef struct { int wx, wy, dual, quant, wbits; } BlockMode;

static bool block_mode_2d(uint32_t m, uint32_t bw, uint32_t bh, BlockMode *bm) {
    uint32_t r = m >> 4 & 1, h = m >> 9 & 1, d = m >> 10 & 1, a = m >> 5 & 3;
    int wx, wy;
    if (m & 3) {
        r |= (m & 3) << 1;
        uint32_t b = m >> 7 & 3;
        switch (m >> 2 & 3) {
        case 0: wx = b + 4; wy = a + 2; break;
        case 1: wx = b + 8; wy = a + 2; break;
        case 2: wx = a + 2; wy = b + 8; break;
        default:
            b &= 1;
            if (m & 0x100) { wx = b + 2; wy = a + 2; }
            else { wx = a + 2; wy = b + 6; }
            break;
        }
    } else {
        r |= (m >> 2 & 3) << 1;
        if ((m >> 2 & 3) == 0) return false;
        uint32_t b = m >> 9 & 3;
        switch (m >> 7 & 3) {
        case 0: wx = 12; wy = a + 2; break;
        case 1: wx = a + 2; wy = 12; break;
        case 2: wx = a + 6; wy = b + 6; d = 0; h = 0; break;
        default:
            if (a == 0) { wx = 6; wy = 10; }
            else if (a == 1) { wx = 10; wy = 6; }
            else return false;
            break;
        }
    }
    int count = wx * wy * (int)(d + 1);
    bm->wx = wx; bm->wy = wy; bm->dual = (int)d;
    bm->quant = (int)(r - 2 + 6 * h);
    bm->wbits = ise_bitcount(count, bm->quant);
    return count <= 64 && bm->wbits >= 24 && bm->wbits <= 96 && wx <= (int)bw && wy <= (int)bh;
}

// ---- partitions ----

static uint32_t hash52(uint32_t p) {
    p ^= p >> 15; p -= p << 17; p += p << 7; p += p << 4;
    p ^= p >> 5;  p += p << 16; p ^= p >> 7; p ^= p >> 3;
    p ^= p << 6;  p ^= p >> 17;
    return p;
}

typedef struct { int s[8]; uint32_t r[4]; int count; } PartSel;

static void part_init(PartSel *ps, int seed, int count) {
    seed += (count - 1) * 1024;
    uint32_t rnum = hash52((uint32_t)seed);
    int s[8];
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) { int v = (int)(rnum >> (4 * i) & 0xF); s[i] = v * v; }
    int sh1, sh2;
    if (seed & 1) { sh1 = seed & 2 ? 4 : 5; sh2 = count == 3 ? 6 : 5; }
    else { sh1 = count == 3 ? 6 : 5; sh2 = seed & 2 ? 4 : 5; }
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) ps->s[i] = s[i] >> (i & 1 ? sh2 : sh1);
    ps->r[0] = rnum >> 14; ps->r[1] = rnum >> 10; ps->r[2] = rnum >> 6; ps->r[3] = rnum >> 2;
    ps->count = count;
}

static inline int part_of(const PartSel *ps, int x, int y) {
    // z = 0 for 2D, so seeds 9..12 drop out
    int a = (int)((uint32_t)(ps->s[0] * x + ps->s[1] * y) + ps->r[0]) & 0x3F;
    int b = (int)((uint32_t)(ps->s[2] * x + ps->s[3] * y) + ps->r[1]) & 0x3F;
    int c = ps->count >= 3 ? (int)((uint32_t)(ps->s[4] * x + ps->s[5] * y) + ps->r[2]) & 0x3F : 0;
    int d = ps->count >= 4 ? (int)((uint32_t)(ps->s[6] * x + ps->s[7] * y) + ps->r[3]) & 0x3F : 0;
    if (a >= b && a >= c && a >= d) return 0;
    if (b >= c && b >= d) return 1;
    if (c >= d) return 2;
    return 3;
}

// ---- colour endpoints ----

static inline int clamp255(int v) { return v < 0 ? 0 : v > 255 ? 255 : v; }

// e[0..3] endpoint 0, e[4..7] endpoint 1 (8-bit). Returns false for an HDR mode.
static bool unpack_endpoints(int cem, const uint8_t *v, int e0[4], int e1[4]) {
    switch (cem) {
    case 0:  // L direct
        e0[0] = e0[1] = e0[2] = v[0]; e1[0] = e1[1] = e1[2] = v[1];
        e0[3] = e1[3] = 255;
        return true;
    case 1: {  // L delta
        int l0 = v[0] >> 2 | (v[1] & 0xC0);
        int l1 = l0 + (v[1] & 0x3F);
        if (l1 > 255) l1 = 255;
        e0[0] = e0[1] = e0[2] = l0; e1[0] = e1[1] = e1[2] = l1;
        e0[3] = e1[3] = 255;
        return true;
    }
    case 4:  // LA direct
        e0[0] = e0[1] = e0[2] = v[0]; e1[0] = e1[1] = e1[2] = v[1];
        e0[3] = v[2]; e1[3] = v[3];
        return true;
    case 5: {  // LA delta
        int l0 = v[0], l1 = v[1], a0 = v[2], a1 = v[3];
        l0 |= (l1 & 0x80) << 1; a0 |= (a1 & 0x80) << 1;
        l1 &= 0x7F; a1 &= 0x7F;
        if (l1 & 0x40) l1 -= 0x80;
        if (a1 & 0x40) a1 -= 0x80;
        l0 >>= 1; a0 >>= 1; l1 >>= 1; a1 >>= 1;  // arithmetic shift of the signed deltas
        l1 = clamp255(l1 + l0); a1 = clamp255(a1 + a0);
        e0[0] = e0[1] = e0[2] = l0; e1[0] = e1[1] = e1[2] = l1;
        e0[3] = a0; e1[3] = a1;
        return true;
    }
    case 6:  // RGB scale
    case 10: {  // RGB scale + two alphas
        int s = v[3];
        for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++) { e1[c] = v[c]; e0[c] = v[c] * s >> 8; }
        if (cem == 6) e0[3] = e1[3] = 255;
        else { e0[3] = v[4]; e1[3] = v[5]; }
        return true;
    }
    case 8:  // RGB(A) direct
    case 12: {
        int a[4] = {v[0], v[2], v[4], cem == 12 ? v[6] : 0};
        int b[4] = {v[1], v[3], v[5], cem == 12 ? v[7] : 0};
        if (a[0] + a[1] + a[2] > b[0] + b[1] + b[2]) {  // blue contraction: swap + uncontract
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) { e0[c] = b[c]; e1[c] = a[c]; }
            e0[0] = (e0[0] + e0[2]) >> 1; e0[1] = (e0[1] + e0[2]) >> 1;
            e1[0] = (e1[0] + e1[2]) >> 1; e1[1] = (e1[1] + e1[2]) >> 1;
        } else {
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) { e0[c] = a[c]; e1[c] = b[c]; }
        }
        if (cem == 8) e0[3] = e1[3] = 255;
        return true;
    }
    case 9:  // RGB(A) base + delta
    case 13: {
        int n = cem == 13 ? 4 : 3;
        int a[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0}, b[4] = {0, 0, 0, 0};
        for (int c = 0; c < n; c++) {
            int base = v[2 * c], delta = v[2 * c + 1];
            a[c] = base >> 1 | (delta & 0x80);
            b[c] = delta >> 1 & 0x3F;
            if (b[c] & 0x20) b[c] -= 0x40;
        }
        int sum = b[0] + b[1] + b[2];
        for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) b[c] += a[c];
        if (sum < 0) {  // swap + uncontract
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) { e0[c] = b[c]; e1[c] = a[c]; }
            e0[0] = (e0[0] + e0[2]) >> 1; e0[1] = (e0[1] + e0[2]) >> 1;
            e1[0] = (e1[0] + e1[2]) >> 1; e1[1] = (e1[1] + e1[2]) >> 1;
        } else {
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) { e0[c] = a[c]; e1[c] = b[c]; }
        }
        for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) { e0[c] = clamp255(e0[c]); e1[c] = clamp255(e1[c]); }
        if (cem == 9) e0[3] = e1[3] = 255;
        return true;
    }
    default:  // 2, 3, 7, 11, 14, 15: HDR
        return false;
    }
}

// ---- block ----

static void fill_error(uint8_t *out, int texels) {
    for (int i = 0; i < texels; i++) {
        out[4 * i + 0] = 0xFF; out[4 * i + 1] = 0x00; out[4 * i + 2] = 0xFF; out[4 * i + 3] = 0xFF;
    }
}

bool astc_decode_block(const uint8_t block[16], uint32_t bw, uint32_t bh, bool srgb, uint8_t *out) {
    if (bw < 4 || bh < 4 || bw > 12 || bh > 12) return false;  // not an ASTC 2D footprint
    int texels = (int)(bw * bh);
    Bits128 b = {load64(block), load64(block + 8)};
    uint32_t mode = (uint32_t)(b.lo & 0x7FF);

    if ((mode & 0x1FF) == 0x1FC) {  // void extent
        if (mode & 0x200) goto error;           // HDR (fp16) constant: error in LDR
        if ((b.lo >> 10 & 3) != 3) goto error;  // reserved bits
        uint32_t s0 = rbits(&b, 12, 13), s1 = rbits(&b, 25, 13);
        uint32_t t0 = rbits(&b, 38, 13), t1 = rbits(&b, 51, 13);
        bool all_ones = s0 == 0x1FFF && s1 == 0x1FFF && t0 == 0x1FFF && t1 == 0x1FFF;
        if ((s0 >= s1 || t0 >= t1) && !all_ones) goto error;
        uint8_t c[4] = {block[9], block[11], block[13], block[15]};  // top 8 bits of the UNORM16s
        for (int i = 0; i < texels; i++) memcpy(out + 4 * i, c, 4);
        return true;
    }

    BlockMode bm;
    if (!block_mode_2d(mode, bw, bh, &bm)) goto error;
    int pcount = (int)(b.lo >> 11 & 3) + 1;
    int wcount = bm.wx * bm.wy;

    // Weights, read backwards from the top of the block.
    uint8_t raw[64];
    Bits128 rev = {bitrev64(b.hi), bitrev64(b.lo)};
    ise_decode(&rev, 0, wcount << bm.dual, bm.quant, raw);
    if (bm.dual && pcount == 4) goto error;

    const uint8_t *wt = wunq_data + wunq_off[bm.quant];
    uint8_t grid[2][80];
    memset(grid, 0, sizeof grid);
    if (bm.dual) {
        for (int i = 0; i < wcount; i++) { grid[0][i] = wt[raw[2 * i]]; grid[1][i] = wt[raw[2 * i + 1]]; }
    } else {
        for (int i = 0; i < wcount; i++) grid[0][i] = wt[raw[i]];
    }

    // Colour endpoint modes.
    int cem[4];
    int below = 128 - bm.wbits, high = 0;
    if (pcount == 1) {
        cem[0] = (int)(b.lo >> 13 & 0xF);
    } else {
        high = 3 * pcount - 4;
        below -= high;
        uint32_t enc = (uint32_t)(b.lo >> 23 & 0x3F) | rbits(&b, below, high) << 6;
        uint32_t base = enc & 3;
        if (base == 0) {
            for (int i = 0; i < pcount; i++) cem[i] = (int)(enc >> 2 & 0xF);
            below += high;
            high = 0;
        } else {
            base--;
            for (int i = 0; i < pcount; i++) cem[i] = (int)(((enc >> (2 + i) & 1) + base) << 2);
            for (int i = 0; i < pcount; i++) cem[i] |= (int)(enc >> (2 + pcount + 2 * i) & 3);
        }
    }
    int ccount = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < pcount; i++) ccount += ((cem[i] >> 2) + 1) * 2;
    if (ccount > 18) goto error;
    int cbits = (pcount == 1 ? 111 : 99) - bm.wbits - high - (bm.dual ? 2 : 0);
    if (cbits < 0) cbits = 0;
    int cq = -1;
    for (int q = 20; q >= 0; q--) {
        if (ise_bitcount(ccount, q) <= cbits) { cq = q; break; }
    }
    if (cq < QUANT_6) goto error;
    uint8_t cv[18];
    ise_decode(&b, pcount == 1 ? 17 : 29, ccount, cq, cv);
    if (cq != QUANT_256) {
        const uint8_t *ct = cunq_data + cunq_off[cq - QUANT_6];
        for (int i = 0; i < ccount; i++) cv[i] = ct[cv[i]];
    }
    int ccs = bm.dual ? (int)rbits(&b, below - 2, 2) : -1;

    // Endpoints, expanded to 16 bits.
    int ep[4][2][4];
    for (int p = 0, k = 0; p < pcount; p++) {
        int *e0 = ep[p][0], *e1 = ep[p][1];
        if (!unpack_endpoints(cem[p], cv + k, e0, e1)) {
            static const int magenta[4] = {0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0xFF};
            memcpy(e0, magenta, sizeof magenta);
            memcpy(e1, magenta, sizeof magenta);
        }
        k += ((cem[p] >> 2) + 1) * 2;
        for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
            e0[c] = srgb ? e0[c] << 8 | 0x80 : e0[c] * 257;
            e1[c] = srgb ? e1[c] << 8 | 0x80 : e1[c] * 257;
        }
    }

    // Weight grid -> texel weights (bilinear infill), per axis.
    int xi[12], xf[12], yi[12], yf[12];
    for (uint32_t x = 0; x < bw; x++) {
        int v = (int)(((1024 + bw / 2) / (bw - 1)) * x * (uint32_t)(bm.wx - 1) + 32) >> 6;
        xi[x] = v >> 4; xf[x] = v & 0xF;
    }
    for (uint32_t y = 0; y < bh; y++) {
        int v = (int)(((1024 + bh / 2) / (bh - 1)) * y * (uint32_t)(bm.wy - 1) + 32) >> 6;
        yi[y] = (v >> 4) * bm.wx; yf[y] = v & 0xF;
    }

    PartSel ps = {0};
    if (pcount > 1) part_init(&ps, (int)(b.lo >> 13 & 0x3FF), pcount);
    int small = texels < 32;

    uint8_t *o = out;
    for (uint32_t y = 0; y < bh; y++) {
        for (uint32_t x = 0; x < bw; x++, o += 4) {
            int fs = xf[x], ft = yf[y];
            int w11 = (fs * ft + 8) >> 4, w10 = fs - w11, w01 = ft - w11, w00 = 16 - fs - ft + w11;
            int i0 = yi[y] + xi[x];
            int w[2];
            for (int pl = 0; pl <= bm.dual; pl++) {
                const uint8_t *g = grid[pl];
                w[pl] = (g[i0] * w00 + g[i0 + 1] * w10 + g[i0 + bm.wx] * w01 + g[i0 + bm.wx + 1] * w11 + 8) >> 4;
            }
            int p = pcount > 1 ? part_of(&ps, small ? (int)x << 1 : (int)x, small ? (int)y << 1 : (int)y) : 0;
            const int *e0 = ep[p][0], *e1 = ep[p][1];
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
                int wc = c == ccs ? w[1] : w[0];
                o[c] = (uint8_t)((e0[c] * (64 - wc) + e1[c] * wc + 32) >> 14);  // >> 6, then top 8 bits
            }
        }
    }
    return true;

error:
    fill_error(out, texels);
    return false;
}

void astc_decode_ldr(const uint8_t *blocks, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t bw, uint32_t bh,
                     bool srgb, uint8_t *rgba_out) {
    if (bw < 4 || bh < 4 || bw > 12 || bh > 12) return;
    uint32_t bx = (width + bw - 1) / bw, by = (height + bh - 1) / bh;
    uint8_t tmp[12 * 12 * 4];
    for (uint32_t j = 0; j < by; j++) {
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < bx; i++) {
            const uint8_t *src = blocks + 16 * ((size_t)j * bx + i);
            uint32_t x0 = i * bw, y0 = j * bh;
            uint32_t cw = width - x0 < bw ? width - x0 : bw, ch = height - y0 < bh ? height - y0 : bh;
            // decode in place when the block's rows are contiguous in the output
            uint8_t *dst = width == bw && ch == bh ? rgba_out + (size_t)y0 * width * 4 : tmp;
            astc_decode_block(src, bw, bh, srgb, dst);
            if (dst == tmp) {
                for (uint32_t y = 0; y < ch; y++)
                    memcpy(rgba_out + ((size_t)(y0 + y) * width + x0) * 4, tmp + y * bw * 4, cw * 4);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`runtime/nvn/astc.h`:

```h
// ASTC LDR decoder (2D blocks) to RGBA8, for GPUs without native ASTC (desktop NVIDIA / AMD).
// Bit-exact with ARM astcenc's 8-bit (decode_unorm8) decode, -dl (srgb = false) / -ds (srgb = true).
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

// blocks: row-major 16-byte blocks covering ceil(width/bw) x ceil(height/bh).
// rgba_out: width*height*4 bytes, tightly packed rows. Values are the 8-bit UNORM results (no sRGB
// -> linear conversion; srgb only selects the sRGB endpoint expansion, which changes rounding).
// Error / illegal blocks and HDR content decode to magenta (FF 00 FF FF).
void astc_decode_ldr(const uint8_t *blocks, uint32_t width, uint32_t height, uint32_t bw, uint32_t bh,
                     bool srgb, uint8_t *rgba_out);

// One block -> bw*bh*4 bytes (rows of bw texels). Returns false for an error block (output magenta).
bool astc_decode_block(const uint8_t block[16], uint32_t bw, uint32_t bh, bool srgb, uint8_t *rgba_out);
```

`runtime/nvn/cmdbuf.c`:

```c
// NVN command buffers: commands are recorded as CmdRec records in host memory; the guest-provided command
// memory still drives the game's own memory management and out-of-memory callbacks (see below).
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "ksync.h"
#include "nvn.h"

#define JUMP_RESERVE (sizeof(CmdRec) + 8)

// What the game sees and where the records go are kept apart. The game sizes command memory for the GPU commands
// real NVN writes, and the records here are larger: BOTW 1.8.2 measures each display list by recording it once
// ("calc resource"), then allocates exactly that much from the model's heap, which the resource size table sized for
// real NVN; with record sizes the heap runs out and the lists get no memory pool.
// - Guest side: command memory size, used and free, and the out-of-memory callback, count cmd_cost bytes per
//   command, an estimate of what NVN writes for it (kept at or under the real size: memory the game allocates from
//   an estimate that is too small is only accounting, the records do not live there).
// - Host side: records go to shadow storage keyed by the guest memory they are accounted to: the chunk while it is
//   being recorded into, then the part of it that was used. When the game writes commands over that memory again,
//   what was recorded there is dead (on hardware it is overwritten): the lists the first bytes go over at once, the
//   others as the recording reaches them. The memory the game adds is often far more than it records there (BOTW
//   gives each deferred lighting composite's material list a 0x200-byte window, records the 0x18 bytes it measured
//   and packs the next list right after); killing the whole window lost the lists packed there before, which the
//   frame still calls (the composites' material ID, and with it the lighting). Dead blocks are reused three frames later,
//   not at once: the command buffer that recorded there may still chain on from them. Memory added without a guest
//   chunk (a null pool) gets shadow storage of its own.
// - Lists in a memory pool die with it (nvnMemoryPoolFinalize: cmdbuf_pool_gone): on hardware their commands were in
//   that memory. Without this, every list of every model ever unloaded stayed (issue #74: +6-10k shadows a load).
// - A shadow's storage starts small and grows a block at a time: the memory the game adds is often far more than it
//   records there (BOTW adds hundreds of KB where it records a few hundred bytes).
// A command handle is the host address of a list's first record.
static uint32_t cmd_cost(uint32_t op, uint32_t extra) { (void)op; return 8 + ((extra + 3) & ~3u); }

typedef struct { uint8_t *mem; uint64_t size; uint64_t frame; } HBlock;
typedef struct Shadow {
    uint64_t lo, hi;  // the guest memory it stands for (written so far); lo == hi == 0: none
    uint64_t win;     // end of the memory the game added there (0: none)
    uint64_t free_to; // claims below this go over no other live shadow (shadow_claim takes no lock)
    HBlock *blocks;
    int nblocks, cap;
    int users;        // command buffers recording into it
    bool dead;        // overlapped: out of the live list (freed when its last user leaves)
} Shadow;

static Shadow **g_live;  // shadows of guest memory, sorted by lo, never overlapping
static int g_nlive, g_caplive;
static HBlock *g_free;   // blocks ready for reuse
static int g_nfree, g_capfree;
static uint64_t g_free_bytes;
#define FREE_BUDGET (64ull << 20)  // dead blocks past this go back to the C heap
static HBlock *g_grave;  // dead blocks, oldest first, until three frames have passed
static int g_ngrave, g_capgrave;
static KMutex g_shadow_lock = KMUTEX_INIT;
static NvnCmdBuf *g_command_buffers;
uint64_t renderer_present_count(void);

static void push_block(HBlock **v, int *n, int *cap, HBlock b) {
    if (*n == *cap) {
        *cap = *cap ? *cap * 2 : 256;
        *v = realloc(*v, *cap * sizeof **v);
    }
    (*v)[(*n)++] = b;
}

static void block_release(HBlock b) {  // (lock held)
    b.frame = renderer_present_count();
    push_block(&g_grave, &g_ngrave, &g_capgrave, b);
}

static HBlock block_get(uint64_t want) {  // (lock held) a free block that fits without wasting much, or a new one
    uint64_t now = renderer_present_count();
    static int stats = -1;
    static uint64_t stats_at;
    if (stats < 0) stats = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_CMD_STATS") != NULL;
    if (stats && now >= stats_at) {  // (test) what the command records hold, every 600 frames
        uint64_t live = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < g_nlive; i++)
            for (int j = 0; j < g_live[i]->nblocks; j++) live += g_live[i]->blocks[j].size;
        LOG("[cmdbuf] frame %llu: %d lists' shadows, %llu MB of records; %d free blocks, %llu MB\n",
            (unsigned long long)now, g_nlive, (unsigned long long)(live >> 20), g_nfree,
            (unsigned long long)(g_free_bytes >> 20));
        stats_at = now + 600;
    }
    int k = 0;
    for (; k < g_ngrave && now - g_grave[k].frame >= 3; k++) {
        if (g_free_bytes + g_grave[k].size > FREE_BUDGET) { free(g_grave[k].mem); continue; }
        g_free_bytes += g_grave[k].size;
        push_block(&g_free, &g_nfree, &g_capfree, g_grave[k]);
    }
    if (k) memmove(g_grave, g_grave + k, (g_ngrave -= k) * sizeof *g_grave);
    for (int i = g_nfree - 1; i >= 0; i--)
        if (g_free[i].size >= want && g_free[i].size <= want * 4) {
            HBlock b = g_free[i];
            g_free[i] = g_free[--g_nfree];
            g_free_bytes -= b.size;
            return b;
        }
    want = (want + 0xFF) & ~0xFFull;
    HBlock b = {malloc(want), want, 0};
    if (!b.mem) FATAL("nvn: out of host memory for command records (%llu bytes)\n", (unsigned long long)want);
    return b;
}

static void shadow_kill(Shadow *sh) {  // (lock held; already out of the live list) its records are dead
    for (int i = 0; i < sh->nblocks; i++) block_release(sh->blocks[i]);
    sh->nblocks = 0;
    sh->dead = true;
    if (!sh->users) { free(sh->blocks); free(sh); }
}

static void shadow_unuse(Shadow *sh) {  // (lock held)
    if (!--sh->users && sh->dead) { free(sh->blocks); free(sh); }
}

static int live_index(uint64_t lo) {  // (lock held) the first live shadow not wholly before lo
    int a = 0, b = g_nlive;
    while (a < b) {
        int m = (a + b) / 2;
        if (g_live[m]->hi <= lo && g_live[m]->lo < lo) a = m + 1; else b = m;
    }
    return a;
}

// A command buffer moves from shadow `old` (NULL: none yet), having used `used` guest bytes there, to the shadow
// for guest memory [lo, hi): the same one when the game adds exactly that range again, unless that is the one
// being recorded into (`recording`: its blocks still hold the start of the list); otherwise a new one, and the
// shadows its first bytes go over die (shadow_claim: the others once written over). What `old` stands for shrinks
// to the part used first.
static Shadow *shadow_switch(Shadow *old, uint64_t used, bool recording, uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi) {
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    if (old && !old->dead && old->lo < old->hi && old->lo + used < old->hi) old->hi = old->lo + used;
    Shadow *sh = NULL;
    if (lo < hi) {
        int a = live_index(lo);
        Shadow *same = a < g_nlive && g_live[a]->lo == lo && g_live[a]->win == hi ? g_live[a] : NULL;
        if (same && (same->users == (same == old)) && !(recording && same == old)) sh = same;
        else {
            int end = a;
            while (end < g_nlive && g_live[end]->lo <= lo) end++;
            for (int i = a; i < end; i++) shadow_kill(g_live[i]);
            if (g_nlive - (end - a) + 1 > g_caplive) {
                g_caplive = g_caplive ? g_caplive * 2 : 1024;
                g_live = realloc(g_live, g_caplive * sizeof *g_live);
            }
            memmove(g_live + a + 1, g_live + end, (g_nlive - end) * sizeof *g_live);
            g_nlive += 1 - (end - a);
            sh = calloc(1, sizeof *sh);
            sh->lo = sh->hi = lo;
            sh->win = hi;
            sh->free_to = a + 1 < g_nlive && g_live[a + 1]->lo < hi ? g_live[a + 1]->lo : hi;
            g_live[a] = sh;
            if (a > 0 && g_live[a - 1]->free_to > lo) g_live[a - 1]->free_to = lo;
        }
    } else {
        sh = calloc(1, sizeof *sh);
    }
    sh->users++;
    if (old) shadow_unuse(old);
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
    return sh;
}

// The command buffer recording into `sh` has written its guest memory up to `end`: lists recorded there before die.
static void shadow_claim(Shadow *sh, uint64_t end) {
    if (end > sh->win) end = sh->win;  // (recording goes on past the window when the game adds no more: accounting only)
    if (end <= sh->hi || sh->dead) return;
    if (end <= sh->free_to) { sh->hi = end; return; }
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    if (!sh->dead) {
        int i = live_index(sh->lo);
        while (i < g_nlive && g_live[i] != sh) i++;
        if (i < g_nlive) {
            int last = i + 1;
            while (last < g_nlive && g_live[last]->lo < end) last++;
            for (int k = i + 1; k < last; k++) shadow_kill(g_live[k]);
            memmove(g_live + i + 1, g_live + last, (g_nlive - last) * sizeof *g_live);
            g_nlive -= last - (i + 1);
            sh->hi = end;
            sh->free_to = i + 1 < g_nlive && g_live[i + 1]->lo < sh->win ? g_live[i + 1]->lo : sh->win;
        }
    }
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
}

static void shadow_leave(Shadow *sh, uint64_t used) {  // (a command buffer is finalized)
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    if (!sh->dead && sh->lo < sh->hi && sh->lo + used < sh->hi) sh->hi = sh->lo + used;
    shadow_unuse(sh);
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
}

// A memory pool is finalized: the lists recorded in its memory [lo, hi) are dead.
void cmdbuf_pool_gone(uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi) {
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    int a = live_index(lo), end = a;
    while (end < g_nlive && g_live[end]->lo < hi) end++;
    for (int i = a; i < end; i++) shadow_kill(g_live[i]);
    memmove(g_live + a, g_live + end, (g_nlive - end) * sizeof *g_live);
    g_nlive -= end - a;
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
}

// Block i of a shadow, at least `want` bytes (blocks past the one in use hold dead records).
static HBlock shadow_block(Shadow *sh, int i, uint64_t want) {
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    if (i < sh->nblocks && sh->blocks[i].size < want) {
        block_release(sh->blocks[i]);
        sh->blocks[i] = block_get(want);
    }
    while (sh->nblocks <= i) {
        if (sh->nblocks == sh->cap) {
            sh->cap = sh->cap ? sh->cap * 2 : 4;
            sh->blocks = realloc(sh->blocks, sh->cap * sizeof *sh->blocks);
        }
        HBlock nb = block_get(want);  // (before the count goes up: the stats line reads the blocks)
        sh->blocks[sh->nblocks++] = nb;
    }
    HBlock b = sh->blocks[i];
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
    return b;
}

RT_ON_RESET(cmdbuf_shadow_reset) {  // (reboot: every list is dead; command buffers were guest objects)
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    while (g_command_buffers) {
        NvnCmdBuf *cb = g_command_buffers;
        g_command_buffers = cb->registry_next;
        free(cb);
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nlive; i++) {
        for (int k = 0; k < g_live[i]->nblocks; k++) free(g_live[i]->blocks[k].mem);
        free(g_live[i]->blocks);
        free(g_live[i]);
    }
    g_nlive = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_ngrave; i++) free(g_grave[i].mem);
    g_ngrave = 0;
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
}

static NvnCmdBuf *cb_of(uint64_t guest) { return HOST(NvnCmdBuf, guest); }

NVN(nvnCommandBufferInitialize) {
    NvnCmdBuf *cb = calloc(1, sizeof *cb);
    cb->guest = A(0);
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    cb->registry_next = g_command_buffers; g_command_buffers = cb;
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
    SET_HOST(A(0), cb);
    RET(1);
}
NVN(nvnCommandBufferFinalize) {
    NvnCmdBuf *cb = cb_of(A(0));
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    NvnCmdBuf **link = &g_command_buffers;
    while (*link && *link != cb) link = &(*link)->registry_next;
    if (*link) *link = cb->registry_next;
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
    if (cb && cb->shadow) shadow_leave(cb->shadow, cb->gused);
    free(cb);
    SET_HOST(A(0), 0);
}
NVN(nvnCommandBufferSetDebugLabel) { (void)c; }

static CmdRec *raw_rec(uint64_t at, uint32_t op, uint32_t size) {
    CmdRec *r = (CmdRec *)(uintptr_t)at;
    memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
    r->op = op;
    r->size = size;
    return r;
}

// Record into block i of the command buffer's shadow, chaining the list being recorded on to it.
static void use_block(NvnCmdBuf *cb, int i, uint64_t want) {
    HBlock b = shadow_block(cb->shadow, i, want);
    uint64_t h = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)b.mem;
    if (cb->recording && cb->mem) {  // (rec_cost always leaves JUMP_RESERVE free for this)
        CmdRec *j = raw_rec(cb->mem + cb->used, CMD_JUMP, sizeof(CmdRec));
        j->x[0] = h;
    }
    cb->block = i;
    cb->mem = h;
    cb->size = b.size;
    cb->used = 0;
}

static void use_guest_chunk(NvnCmdBuf *cb, uint64_t gmem, uint64_t gsize) {
    cb->shadow = shadow_switch(cb->shadow, cb->gused, cb->recording, gmem, gmem ? gmem + gsize : 0);
    cb->gmem = gmem;
    cb->gsize = gsize;
    cb->gused = 0;
    uint64_t want = gsize * 8;  // (records take several times the GPU bytes; more blocks chain on when needed, each
    use_block(cb, 0, want < 0x400 ? 0x400 : want > 0x4000 ? 0x4000 : want);  // twice the last: start small)
}

NVN(nvnCommandBufferAddCommandMemory) {  // (cmd, pool, offset, size)
    NvnCmdBuf *cb = cb_of(A(0));
    NvnPool *pool = A(1) ? HOST(NvnPool, A(1)) : NULL;
    if (!pool) {
        static int logged;
        if (logged++ < 4) LOG("[nvn] AddCommandMemory(%llx) without a memory pool (offset %llx, size %llx)\n",
                              (unsigned long long)A(0), (unsigned long long)A(2), (unsigned long long)A(3));
    }
    use_guest_chunk(cb, pool ? pool->storage + A(2) : 0, A(3));
}
NVN(nvnCommandBufferAddControlMemory) { (void)c; }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetCommandMemorySize) { RET(cb_of(A(0))->gsize); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetCommandMemoryUsed) { RET(cb_of(A(0))->gused); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetCommandMemoryFree) {
    NvnCmdBuf *cb = cb_of(A(0));
    RET(cb->gsize > cb->gused ? cb->gsize - cb->gused : 0);
}
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetControlMemorySize) { RET(0x10000); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetControlMemoryUsed) { RET(0); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetControlMemoryFree) { RET(0x10000); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferSetMemoryCallback) { cb_of(A(0))->callback = A(1); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetMemoryCallback) { RET(cb_of(A(0))->callback); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferSetMemoryCallbackData) { cb_of(A(0))->callback_data = A(1); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferGetMemoryCallbackData) { RET(cb_of(A(0))->callback_data); }
NVN(nvnCommandBufferSetCommandMemoryCallbackEnabled) { (void)c; }

// Append a host record without touching guest command-memory accounting.
static CmdRec *host_rec(NvnCmdBuf *cb, uint32_t op, uint32_t extra) {
    uint32_t size = (uint32_t)((sizeof(CmdRec) + extra + 7) & ~7u);
    if (cb->used + size + JUMP_RESERVE > cb->size) {
        uint64_t want = size + JUMP_RESERVE;
        use_block(cb, cb->block + 1, want > cb->size * 2 ? want : cb->size * 2);
    }
    CmdRec *r = raw_rec(cb->mem + cb->used, op, size);
    cb->used += size;
    return r;
}
// Reserve a record costing `cost` guest bytes. May call back into the guest for more memory, so callers snapshot
// their arguments first. When the game adds no more (BOTW gives some command buffers a callback that is a bare
// ret), recording goes on past the guest chunk: only the accounting is over, the records have room.
static CmdRec *rec_cost(Cpu *c, NvnCmdBuf *cb, uint32_t op, uint32_t extra, uint32_t cost) {
    for (int tries = 0; !cb->shadow || cb->gused + cost > cb->gsize; tries++) {
        if (!cb->callback || tries == 2) {
            if (!cb->shadow) use_guest_chunk(cb, 0, 0);  // never given memory: the records still need a home
            break;
        }
        uint64_t saved[8];
        memcpy(saved, c->x, sizeof saved);
        c->x[0] = cb->guest;
        c->x[1] = 0;  // NVN_COMMAND_BUFFER_MEMORY_EVENT_OUT_OF_COMMAND_MEMORY
        c->x[2] = cost;
        c->x[3] = cb->callback_data;
        guest_call(c, cb->callback);
        memcpy(c->x, saved, sizeof saved);
    }
    cb->gused += cost;
    shadow_claim(cb->shadow, cb->gmem + cb->gused);
    return host_rec(cb, op, extra);
}
bool nvn_ui_scope(uint64_t commands, unsigned kind) {
    // The native screen can be called before its context is ready. Never dereference a candidate host pointer.
    kmutex_lock(&g_shadow_lock);
    NvnCmdBuf *cb = g_command_buffers;
    while (cb && cb->guest != commands) cb = cb->registry_next;
    kmutex_unlock(&g_shadow_lock);
    if (!cb || !cb->recording || !cb->shadow || !cb->mem) return false;
    // A host marker never allocates guest memory or invokes a guest out-of-memory callback.
    CmdRec *r = host_rec(cb, CMD_UI_SCOPE, 0);
    r->x[0] = kind;
    return true;
}

static CmdRec *rec(Cpu *c, NvnCmdBuf *cb, uint32_t op, uint32_t extra) {
    return rec_cost(c, cb, op, extra, cmd_cost(op, extra));
}

bool nvn_timeline(void);
#define TL(fmt, ...) do { if (nvn_timeline()) LOG("[tl] %.3f %x " fmt "\n", plat_now_ns() / 1e6, kernel_current_thread_handle(), ##__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
NVN(nvnCommandBufferBeginRecording) {
    NvnCmdBuf *cb = cb_of(A(0));
    TL("record %llx (lr %llx)", (unsigned long long)A(0), (unsigned long long)c->x[30]);
    cb->recording = true;
    rec_cost(c, cb, CMD_BARRIER, 0, 0);  // makes sure memory exists; the list starts here
    cb->start = cb->mem + cb->used - sizeof(CmdRec);
}
NVN(nvnCommandBufferEndRecording) {
    NvnCmdBuf *cb = cb_of(A(0));
    rec_cost(c, cb, CMD_END, 0, 0);
    cb->recording = false;
    TL("recorded %llx", (unsigned long long)A(0));
    RET(cb->start);
}
NVN(nvnCommandBufferIsRecording) { RET(cb_of(A(0))->recording); }

// ---- generic recorders
typedef struct { uint64_t x[8]; float f[4]; } Snap;
static Snap snap(Cpu *c) {
    Snap s;
    memcpy(s.x, c->x, sizeof s.x);
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) s.f[i] = *(float *)&c->v[i];
    return s;
}
static CmdRec *record(Cpu *c, uint32_t op, uint32_t extra, Snap *s) {
    CmdRec *r = rec(c, cb_of(s->x[0]), op, extra);
    memcpy(r->x, s->x + 1, sizeof r->x);
    memcpy(r->f, s->f, sizeof r->f);
    return r;
}
// record with a copy of `len` bytes from the guest pointer in argument `arg`
static CmdRec *record_copy(Cpu *c, uint32_t op, int arg, uint32_t len) {
    Snap s = snap(c);
    CmdRec *r = record(c, op, len, &s);
    if (s.x[arg] && len) memcpy(r->extra, (void *)(uintptr_t)s.x[arg], len);
    return r;
}
#define PLAIN(name, op) NVN(name) { Snap s = snap(c); record(c, op, 0, &s); }

// ---- state binding
NVN(nvnCommandBufferBindProgram) {
    Snap s = snap(c);
    CmdRec *r = record(c, CMD_BIND_PROGRAM, 0, &s);
    r->x[0] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)HOST(NvnProgram, s.x[1]);  // host program
}

    CmdRec *r = record(c, CMD_BIND_VERTEX_BUFFERS, 16, &s);
    r->x[0] = s.x[1]; r->x[1] = 1;
    memcpy(r->extra, &s.x[2], 16);
}

NVN(nvnCommandBufferBindImage) {

    CmdRec *r = record(c, CMD_BIND_IMAGES, 8, &s);
    r->x[0] = s.x[1]; r->x[1] = s.x[2]; r->x[2] = 1;
    memcpy(r->extra, &s.x[3], 8);
}

// SetRenderTargets(cmd, n, colors[], colorViews[], depth, depthView)
// extra: { u64 tex[8]; NvnTextureView views[8]; u8 has_view[8]; u64 depth; NvnTextureView dview; u8 has_dview }
typedef struct {
    uint64_t tex[8];
    NvnTextureView views[8];
    uint8_t has_view[8];
    uint64_t depth;
    NvnTextureView dview;
    uint8_t has_dview;
} RtRec;
// Textures in records are host textures, taken when recorded (nvn_texture_host): on hardware a list holds the
// texture's address and shape as they were then. One the game finalizes later (BOTW does, between frames, for render
// targets its display lists keep using) still names its memory: the renderer keeps one image per memory and shape.
NVN(nvnCommandBufferSetRenderTargets) {
    Snap s = snap(c);
    int n = (int)s.x[1];
    if (n > 8) n = 8;
    RtRec rt = {0};
    const uint64_t *colors = (const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)s.x[2], *views = (const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)s.x[3];
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        rt.tex[i] = colors ? (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)nvn_texture_host(colors[i]) : 0;
        if (views && views[i]) { rt.has_view[i] = 1; memcpy(&rt.views[i], (void *)(uintptr_t)views[i], sizeof(NvnTextureView)); }
    }
    rt.depth = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)nvn_texture_host(s.x[4]);
    if (s.x[5]) { rt.has_dview = 1; memcpy(&rt.dview, (void *)(uintptr_t)s.x[5], sizeof(NvnTextureView)); }
    CmdRec *r = record(c, CMD_SET_RENDER_TARGETS, sizeof rt, &s);
    r->x[0] = (uint64_t)n;
    memcpy(r->extra, &rt, sizeof rt);
}

// ClearTexture(cmd, texture, view, region, color, mask)
typedef struct { uint64_t tex; NvnTextureView view; uint8_t has_view; int32_t region[6]; float color[4]; } ClearTexRec;
static void clear_texture(Cpu *c, int kind) {
    Snap s = snap(c);
    ClearTexRec ct = {0};
    ct.tex = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)nvn_texture_host(s.x[1]);
    if (s.x[2]) { ct.has_view = 1; memcpy(&ct.view, (void *)(uintptr_t)s.x[2], sizeof ct.view); }
    if (s.x[3]) memcpy(ct.region, (void *)(uintptr_t)s.x[3], sizeof ct.region);
    if (s.x[4]) memcpy(ct.color, (void *)(uintptr_t)s.x[4], 16);
    CmdRec *r = record(c, CMD_CLEAR_TEXTURE, sizeof ct, &s);
    r->x[6] = (uint64_t)kind;
    memcpy(r->extra, &ct, sizeof ct);
}
NVN(nvnCommandBufferClearTexture) { clear_texture(c, 0); }

// DiscardColor(cmdbuf, index): the target's contents become undefined. On the Switch a discarded (compressed)
// target reads back cleared; areas the game then leaves undrawn (e.g. a pit after a floor tile falls away) stay
// black there. Treated as a clear to (0,0,0,0) (SAVAGEWIND_KEEP_DISCARD=1: old no-op behaviour).
NVN(nvnCommandBufferDiscardColor) {
    static int keep = -1, logged;
    if (keep < 0) keep = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_KEEP_DISCARD") != NULL;
    if (logged < 5) { logged++; LOG("[nvn] DiscardColor index %llu%s\n", (unsigned long long)c->x[1], keep ? " (kept)" : " -> clear"); }
    if (keep) return;
    Snap s = snap(c);
    CmdRec *r = record(c, CMD_CLEAR_COLOR, 16, &s);
    memset(r->extra, 0, 16);
    r->x[2] = 0xF;  // all channels
    r->x[5] = 0;    // float clear
}

// Debug: SAVAGEWIND_TRACE_COUNT=<n> logs the guest call chain of indexed draws with n indices.
static void trace_draw(Cpu *c, uint64_t count) {
    static long want = -2;
    if (want == -2) want = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TRACE_COUNT") ? atol(getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TRACE_COUNT")) : -1;
    if (want < 0 || (long)count != want) return;
    static int n;
    if (n++ > 40) return;
    LOG("[trace] draw count %llu lr %llx chain:", (unsigned long long)count, (unsigned long long)c->x[30]);
    uint64_t fp = c->x[29];
    for (int i = 0; i < 14 && fp >= 0x7000000000ull && fp < 0x8000000000ull && (fp & 7) == 0; i++) {
        uint64_t next = *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)fp, lr = *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(fp + 8);
        LOG(" %llx", (unsigned long long)lr);
        if (next <= fp) break;
        fp = next;
    }
    LOG("\n");
}

// ---- copies
typedef struct { uint64_t tex; NvnTextureView view; uint8_t has_view; int32_t region[6]; } TexRef;
static void tex_ref(TexRef *t, uint64_t tex, uint64_t view, uint64_t region) {
    t->tex = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)nvn_texture_host(tex);
    if (view) { t->has_view = 1; memcpy(&t->view, (void *)(uintptr_t)view, sizeof t->view); }
    if (region) memcpy(t->region, (void *)(uintptr_t)region, sizeof t->region);
}

    memcpy(r->extra, &t, sizeof t);
}
```

`runtime/nvn/formats.c`:

```c
// NVNformat -> block size and kind.
#include "tegra.h"

#define C(bpb) {bpb, 1, 1, FMT_COLOR, 0}
#define B(bpb, w, h) {bpb, w, h, FMT_COMPRESSED, 0}

static const FormatInfo formats[] = {
    [0x00] = C(0),
    [0x01] = C(1), [0x02] = C(1), [0x03] = C(1), [0x04] = C(1),                 // R8
    [0x05] = C(2), [0x06] = C(2), [0x07] = C(2), [0x08] = C(2), [0x09] = C(2),  // R16
    [0x0A] = C(4), [0x0B] = C(4), [0x0C] = C(4),                                // R32
    [0x0D] = C(2), [0x0E] = C(2), [0x0F] = C(2), [0x10] = C(2),                 // RG8
    [0x11] = C(4), [0x12] = C(4), [0x13] = C(4), [0x14] = C(4), [0x15] = C(4),  // RG16
    [0x16] = C(8), [0x17] = C(8), [0x18] = C(8),                                // RG32
    [0x19] = C(3), [0x1A] = C(3), [0x1B] = C(3), [0x1C] = C(3),                 // RGB8
    [0x1D] = C(6), [0x1E] = C(6), [0x1F] = C(6), [0x20] = C(6), [0x21] = C(6),  // RGB16
    [0x22] = C(12), [0x23] = C(12), [0x24] = C(12),                             // RGB32
    [0x25] = C(4), [0x26] = C(4), [0x27] = C(4), [0x28] = C(4),                 // RGBA8
    [0x29] = C(8), [0x2A] = C(8), [0x2B] = C(8), [0x2C] = C(8), [0x2D] = C(8),  // RGBA16
    [0x2E] = C(16), [0x2F] = C(16), [0x30] = C(16),                             // RGBA32
    [0x31] = {1, 1, 1, FMT_STENCIL, 0},
    [0x32] = {2, 1, 1, FMT_DEPTH, 0},
    [0x33] = {4, 1, 1, FMT_DEPTH, 0},
    [0x34] = {4, 1, 1, FMT_DEPTH, 0},
    [0x35] = {4, 1, 1, FMT_DEPTH_STENCIL, 0},
    [0x36] = {8, 1, 1, FMT_DEPTH_STENCIL, 0},
    [0x37] = C(4), [0x38] = C(4),                                               // RGBX8/RGBA8 sRGB
    [0x39] = C(2), [0x3A] = C(2), [0x3B] = C(2), [0x3C] = C(2),                 // RGBA4, RGB5, RGB5A1, RGB565
    [0x3D] = C(4), [0x3E] = C(4), [0x3F] = C(4), [0x40] = C(4),                 // RGB10A2(UI), R11G11B10F, RGB9E5
    [0x41] = B(8, 4, 4), [0x42] = B(8, 4, 4), [0x43] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x44] = B(16, 4, 4),
    [0x45] = B(8, 4, 4), [0x46] = B(8, 4, 4), [0x47] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x48] = B(16, 4, 4),
    [0x49] = B(8, 4, 4), [0x4A] = B(8, 4, 4), [0x4B] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x4C] = B(16, 4, 4),
    [0x4D] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x4E] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x4F] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x50] = B(16, 4, 4),
    // integer-to-float vertex formats
    [0x51] = C(1), [0x52] = C(1), [0x53] = C(2), [0x54] = C(2), [0x55] = C(4), [0x56] = C(4),
    [0x57] = C(2), [0x58] = C(2), [0x59] = C(4), [0x5A] = C(4), [0x5B] = C(8), [0x5C] = C(8),
    [0x5D] = C(3), [0x5E] = C(3), [0x5F] = C(6), [0x60] = C(6), [0x61] = C(12), [0x62] = C(12),
    [0x63] = C(4), [0x64] = C(4), [0x65] = C(8), [0x66] = C(8), [0x67] = C(16), [0x68] = C(16),
    [0x69] = C(4), [0x6A] = C(4), [0x6B] = C(4), [0x6C] = C(4),
    [0x6D] = C(4), [0x6E] = C(4), [0x6F] = C(4), [0x70] = C(4),                 // RGBX8
    [0x71] = C(8), [0x72] = C(8), [0x73] = C(8), [0x74] = C(8), [0x75] = C(8),  // RGBX16
    [0x76] = C(16), [0x77] = C(16), [0x78] = C(16),                             // RGBX32
    // ASTC (linear then sRGB)
    [0x79] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x7A] = B(16, 5, 4), [0x7B] = B(16, 5, 5), [0x7C] = B(16, 6, 5),
    [0x7D] = B(16, 6, 6), [0x7E] = B(16, 8, 5), [0x7F] = B(16, 8, 6), [0x80] = B(16, 8, 8),
    [0x81] = B(16, 10, 5), [0x82] = B(16, 10, 6), [0x83] = B(16, 10, 8), [0x84] = B(16, 10, 10),
    [0x85] = B(16, 12, 10), [0x86] = B(16, 12, 12),
    [0x87] = B(16, 4, 4), [0x88] = B(16, 5, 4), [0x89] = B(16, 5, 5), [0x8A] = B(16, 6, 5),
    [0x8B] = B(16, 6, 6), [0x8C] = B(16, 8, 5), [0x8D] = B(16, 8, 6), [0x8E] = B(16, 8, 8),
    [0x8F] = B(16, 10, 5), [0x90] = B(16, 10, 6), [0x91] = B(16, 10, 8), [0x92] = B(16, 10, 10),
    [0x93] = B(16, 12, 10), [0x94] = B(16, 12, 12),
    [0x95] = C(2), [0x96] = C(2), [0x97] = C(2),                                 // BGR5, BGR5A1, A1BGR5
    [0x98] = C(4), [0x99] = C(4), [0x9A] = C(4), [0x9B] = C(4),                  // BGRX8, BGRA8 (+sRGB)
};

const FormatInfo *nvn_format_info(uint32_t f) {
    static const FormatInfo unknown = {4, 1, 1, FMT_COLOR, 0};
    if (f >= sizeof formats / sizeof *formats || !formats[f].bpb) return &unknown;
    return &formats[f];
}
```
