`runtime/services/save_convert.h`:

```h
// Import of Wii U / Cemu saves (runtime/services/save_convert.c), the C version of tools/botw_save_convert.py (which
// stays as its reference and test oracle: tools/test_save_convert.py compares the two file by file).
//
// A save is a folder of small binary files; the Wii U's are big endian, the Switch's little endian, and each game
// revision has its own flag list. The flag list (name hash, type, length, default) comes from the player's own
// Pack/Bootup.pack, so nothing of the game is embedded. Everything here is SDL-free and has no state of its own: the
// start screen's Saves tab (runtime/ui/saves_tab.mm) calls it from a worker thread.
//
// An import is: sc_format_load -> sc_convert into a new staging folder (the saves stay as they are) -> the player
// confirms -> sc_stage_install, which moves the current save folder to a dated backup folder and puts the staged one
// in its place. Nothing the player had is deleted, and a failure at any step leaves the saves as they were.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <time.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    SC_OK = 0,
    SC_NO_SAVE,       // no BotW save in the folder (no numbered folder with a game_data.sav)
    SC_SWITCH_SAVE,   // the save is already in the Switch byte order: nothing to convert
    SC_BAD_SAVE,      // a save file is damaged or incomplete (detail: which)
    SC_NO_BOOTUP,     // Pack/Bootup.pack can't be opened
    SC_BAD_BOOTUP,    // Pack/Bootup.pack can't be read or lacks the flag tables (detail: why)
    SC_IO,            // a file or folder couldn't be read, written or moved (detail: which and why)
    SC_LINKED,        // the save folder is a link: moving it would move the link
    SC_MOVED,         // sc_stage_install stopped halfway and could not undo it: the saves are in the backup (detail: it)
    SC_SEARCH_LIMIT,  // the folder search ran out of time or visits: choose a closer folder
    SC_CANCELLED,     // the caller requested cancellation before installation
    SC_IN_USE,        // a running game holds the save folder's lock (see sc_lock_take): close it first
    SC_WIIU_SAVE,     // the save is already in the Wii U byte order: nothing to convert
} ScCode;

// One converted flag file: what it held and what became of it
typedef struct {
    char file[64];                    // "0/game_data.sav", "0/caption.sav", "option.sav"
    uint32_t src_rev, dst_rev;        // the game revision in the file's header, before and after
    uint32_t kept, defaulted, dropped, resized;  // flags carried over / not in the save (default) / not in the game /
                                                 // carried over with another length (resized flags count in kept too)
} ScFlagFile;

typedef struct {
    ScCode code;
    char detail[1200];                // English, for the log and the message's variable part: a path or a reason
    char root[1100];                  // the profile folder the slots were found in
    char **slots;                     // the slot folders converted ("0", "1", ...)
    int nslots;
    ScFlagFile *files;
    int nfiles;
    uint32_t kept, defaulted, dropped, resized;  // the sums over files
    int n_tracker, n_album, n_pict;   // Hero's Path blocks, album and compendium pictures
    int n_written;                    // files written (the staging folder; a backup: the files copied)
    int warnings;                     // things that didn't stop the import (install: files not carried over)
} ScReport;

void sc_report_free(ScReport *r);

// ---- the game's flag tables
typedef struct ScFormat ScFormat;
// Reads GameData/gamedata.ssarc and savedataformat.ssarc of a Pack/Bootup.pack. SC_NO_BOOTUP / SC_BAD_BOOTUP.
ScCode sc_format_load(const char *bootup_path, ScFormat **out, ScReport *r);
void sc_format_free(ScFormat *f);
uint32_t sc_format_revision(const ScFormat *f);

// ---- converting
enum {
    SC_ALLOW_SWITCH = 1,  // (tests) a little-endian source is converted for its revision instead of refused
    SC_TO_WIIU      = 2,  // converts to Wii U (big-endian) directly into stage_dir (no save_0 wrapping)
};

// The profile folder in dir: dir itself if it holds numbered slot folders with a game_data.sav, else the first folder
// below it (up to 10 levels, in name order) that does; one in the Wii U's byte order is preferred to any other. SC_NO_SAVE
// otherwise; SC_SEARCH_LIMIT if the four-second or 100,000-folder budget is exhausted.
ScCode sc_find_profile(const char *dir, char *root, size_t cap);

typedef struct ScStage ScStage;
// Optional cooperative cancellation, checked during the search and between files. The callback must be thread-safe.
typedef struct { bool (*requested)(void *); void *data; } ScCancel;
// Converts the profile found in src into the NEW folder stage_dir (it must not exist): stage_dir/save_0/<slot>/...,
// option.sav, tracker/, album/, pict_book/, for the Switch byte order and the revision of fmt. The Hero's Path, album
// and compendium pictures are always taken. On failure everything it made is removed again (*stage is NULL).
ScCode sc_convert(const char *src, const char *stage_dir, const ScFormat *fmt, unsigned flags, ScStage **stage,
                  ScReport *r);
ScCode sc_convert_cancel(const char *src, const char *stage_dir, const ScFormat *fmt, unsigned flags,
                         const ScCancel *cancel, ScStage **stage, ScReport *r);
// Puts the staged folder in place of save_dir: save_dir (if there) is first moved whole to backup_dir (which must not
// exist; its parent folders are made), then stage_dir becomes save_dir, and what the old one held besides save_0
// (sdcard, ...) is copied over. If the second step fails the first is undone. Consumes the stage only on success.
// After SC_MOVED, use sc_stage_keep to preserve the new saves for recovery; other failures can discard the stage.
ScCode sc_stage_install(ScStage *stage, const char *save_dir, const char *backup_dir, ScReport *r);
// Moves the staged export folder to dst_dir: creates dst_dir and its subfolders if needed, moves or copies staged files
// to dst_dir, and preserves any existing files in dst_dir with a dated .bak suffix. Frees stage.
ScCode sc_stage_export(ScStage *stage, const char *dst_dir, ScReport *r);
// Converts the Switch profile found in src_dir (or src_dir/save_0) into dst_dir, in the Wii U's big-endian byte order.
// Existing files in dst_dir are preserved with a dated .bak suffix.
ScCode sc_export(const char *src_dir, const char *dst_dir, const ScFormat *fmt, const ScCancel *cancel, ScReport *r);
// Removes the files and folders the conversion made (and only those) and frees the stage.
void sc_stage_discard(ScStage *stage);
// Frees the stage without removing its files: keep the new saves for recovery after SC_MOVED.
void sc_stage_keep(ScStage *stage);

typedef struct { char imported[1100], backup[1100]; } ScRecovery;  // empty when none; backup can be absent
// Removes dated save-import-* folders beside save_dir, except keep_dir (a live or unconfirmed stage, or NULL).
// If save_dir is missing, keeps ALL of them and reports the newest import and backup folders for manual recovery.
// Does not follow links. Call only while no other job can create, install or discard a stage.
ScCode sc_cleanup_stages(const char *save_dir, const char *keep_dir, ScRecovery *recovery, ScReport *r);

// ---- backups
// A dated folder name that doesn't exist yet: <save_dir>-backups/save-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS (a -2, -3... if taken), and
// the staging folder's: <save_dir>-import-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.
void sc_backup_path(const char *save_dir, char *out, size_t cap);
void sc_stage_path(const char *save_dir, char *out, size_t cap);
void sc_stage_export_path(const char *save_dir, char *out, size_t cap);
// Copies save_dir whole into the new folder backup_dir (made, with its parents). SC_NO_SAVE: nothing to copy. On
// failure the copy made so far is removed again.
ScCode sc_backup(const char *save_dir, const char *backup_dir, ScReport *r);

// ---- the lock on the save folder
// While a game runs it holds the lock of its save folder: the file <save_dir>.lock, next to the folder. sc_backup and
// sc_stage_install take it for their run and fail with SC_IN_USE when somebody else has it. The operating system drops
// a lock when its process ends, so a crashed game leaves none behind.
typedef struct ScLock ScLock;
typedef enum {
    SC_LOCK_OK,           // taken: *out is the lock (sc_lock_take)
    SC_LOCK_BUSY,         // another process holds it
    SC_LOCK_UNAVAILABLE,  // the lock file can't be made or locked (read-only folder...): nothing to wait for, *out is NULL
} ScLockResult;
ScLockResult sc_lock_take(const char *save_dir, ScLock **out);
void sc_lock_drop(ScLock *lock);  // NULL is fine

// ---- looking at a save folder (<save>/save_0)
typedef struct {
    char name[16];          // the slot folder
    int number;
    time_t saved;           // when the game wrote it: the modification time of caption.sav (else game_data.sav)
    int64_t play_seconds;   // from caption.sav's PlayTime flag when it has one, else -1
    bool has_picture;       // <slot>/caption.jpg
} ScSlot;
// The slots of save_0_dir, by number; the count (0: none, or the folder isn't there). Free the list with free().
int sc_list_slots(const char *save_0_dir, ScSlot **out);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

`runtime/services/save_profiles.c`:

```c
// Save profiles: see save_profiles.h. The comments say where a choice comes from rather than what a line does.
#include "save_profiles.h"

#include <ctype.h>
#include <dirent.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "../platform.h"  // (Windows: mkdir with a mode)
#include "../settings.h"
#include "save_convert.h"
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <sys/statvfs.h>
#endif

#define PATH_CAP 1100
#define PROFILES_DIR "save-profiles"
#define ACTIVE_FILE "save_profile.txt"
#define TMP_MAX_AGE (24 * 60 * 60)

static __thread char g_detail[PATH_CAP + 128];
const char *sp_detail(void) { return g_detail; }

static SpCode fail(SpCode c, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
static SpCode fail(SpCode c, const char *fmt, ...) {
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    vsnprintf(g_detail, sizeof g_detail, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
    return c;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ small helpers
static bool is_dir(const char *p) {
    struct stat st;
    return stat(p, &st) == 0 && S_ISDIR(st.st_mode);
}

static bool is_link(const char *path) {  // symlink or junction, a broken one too
#ifdef _WIN32
    DWORD a = GetFileAttributesA(path);
    return a != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES && (a & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT);
#else
    struct stat st;
    return lstat(path, &st) == 0 && S_ISLNK(st.st_mode);
#endif
}

// root + "/" + rest; root NULL or "" gives rest alone (the working directory is the data root)
static bool join(char *out, size_t cap, const char *root, const char *rest) {
    int n = root && *root ? snprintf(out, cap, "%s/%s", root, rest) : snprintf(out, cap, "%s", rest);
    return n > 0 && (size_t)n < cap;
}

static bool fold_eq(const char *a, const char *b) {
    for (; *a && *b; a++, b++)
        if (tolower((unsigned char)*a) != tolower((unsigned char)*b)) return false;
    return !*a && !*b;
}

static bool is_default_name(const char *name) { return !name || !*name || fold_eq(name, SP_DEFAULT_NAME); }

static void mkdir_one(const char *p, bool *ok) {
    if (!is_dir(p) && mkdir(p, 0755) != 0 && !is_dir(p)) *ok = false;
}

// <root>/save-profiles, made when missing
static bool profiles_dir(const char *root, char *out, size_t cap, bool make) {
    if (!join(out, cap, root, PROFILES_DIR)) return false;
    if (!make) return true;
    bool ok = true;
    mkdir_one(out, &ok);
    return ok;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ names
static const char *const RESERVED[] = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL", "CLOCK$", "CONIN$", "CONOUT$"};

// Windows treats these as devices in any case and with any extension: "nul", "NUL.txt", "com1.save"
static bool windows_device(const char *name) {
    char base[SP_NAME_MAX + 1];
    snprintf(base, sizeof base, "%s", name);
    char *dot = strchr(base, '.');
    if (dot) *dot = 0;
    size_t n = strlen(base);
    while (n && base[n - 1] == ' ') base[--n] = 0;  // ("nul .txt" is still the device)
    for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof RESERVED / sizeof *RESERVED; i++)
        if (fold_eq(base, RESERVED[i])) return true;
    bool numbered = n == 4 && base[3] >= '1' && base[3] <= '9';  // COM1..COM9, LPT1..LPT9
    base[3] = 0;
    return numbered && (fold_eq(base, "COM") || fold_eq(base, "LPT"));
}

SpCode sp_validate_name(const char *name) {
    if (!name) return SP_NAME_EMPTY;
    size_t n = strlen(name);
    if (n == 0) return SP_NAME_EMPTY;
    if (n > SP_NAME_MAX) return SP_NAME_LONG;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        unsigned char c = (unsigned char)name[i];
        if (!(c < 128 && (isalnum(c) || c == ' ' || c == '-' || c == '_' || c == '.' || c == '(' || c == ')')))
            return SP_NAME_CHARS;
    }
    if (name[0] == ' ' || name[n - 1] == ' ') return n == strspn(name, " ") ? SP_NAME_EMPTY : SP_NAME_CHARS;
    if (name[0] == '.' || name[n - 1] == '.' || strstr(name, "..")) return SP_NAME_CHARS;
    if (fold_eq(name, SP_DEFAULT_NAME) || windows_device(name)) return SP_NAME_RESERVED;
    return SP_OK;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ where things are
bool sp_save_dir(const char *root, const char *name, char *out, size_t cap) {
    if (is_default_name(name)) {
        if (g_settings.save_dir[0]) return snprintf(out, cap, "%s", g_settings.save_dir) < (int)cap;
        return join(out, cap, root, "save");
    }
    if (sp_validate_name(name) != SP_OK) return false;
    char rel[PATH_CAP];
    return snprintf(rel, sizeof rel, PROFILES_DIR "/%s/save", name) < (int)sizeof rel && join(out, cap, root, rel);
}

static bool profile_dir(const char *root, const char *name, char *out, size_t cap) {
    char rel[PATH_CAP];
    return snprintf(rel, sizeof rel, PROFILES_DIR "/%s", name) < (int)sizeof rel && join(out, cap, root, rel);
}

static int cmp_name(const void *a, const void *b) {
    const char *x = *(char *const *)a, *y = *(char *const *)b;
    for (; *x && *y; x++, y++) {
        int d = tolower((unsigned char)*x) - tolower((unsigned char)*y);
        if (d) return d;
    }
    int d = (unsigned char)*x - (unsigned char)*y;
    return d ? d : strcmp(*(char *const *)a, *(char *const *)b);
}

// The valid profile names in save-profiles, sorted. Free with names_free.
static char **names_list(const char *root, int *n) {
    char dir[PATH_CAP];
    *n = 0;
    if (!profiles_dir(root, dir, sizeof dir, false)) return NULL;
    DIR *d = opendir(dir);
    if (!d) return NULL;
    char **v = NULL;
    int cnt = 0, cap = 0;
    struct dirent *e;
    while ((e = readdir(d))) {
        char p[PATH_CAP];
        if (sp_validate_name(e->d_name) != SP_OK || snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s/%s", dir, e->d_name) >= (int)sizeof p ||
            !is_dir(p))
            continue;
        if (cnt == cap) {
            char **nv = realloc(v, (cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 8) * sizeof *v);
            if (!nv) break;
            v = nv;
        }
        if (!(v[cnt] = strdup(e->d_name))) break;
        cnt++;
    }
    closedir(d);
    if (cnt > 1) qsort(v, cnt, sizeof *v, cmp_name);
    *n = cnt;
    return v;
}

static void names_free(char **v, int n) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) free(v[i]);
    free(v);
}

// The folder name a profile has now, in the list's own spelling: the name looked up without regard to case. NULL: none.
static char *find_profile(const char *root, const char *name) {
    if (is_default_name(name)) return strdup(SP_DEFAULT_NAME);
    int n;
    char **v = names_list(root, &n);
    char *found = NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < n && !found; i++)
        if (fold_eq(v[i], name)) found = strdup(v[i]);
    names_free(v, n);
    return found;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the active profile
static void read_active_file(const char *root, char *name, size_t cap) {
    char path[PATH_CAP], buf[SP_NAME_MAX + 8] = {0};
    snprintf(name, cap, "%s", SP_DEFAULT_NAME);
    if (!join(path, sizeof path, root, ACTIVE_FILE)) return;
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    size_t got = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf - 1, f);
    fclose(f);
    buf[got] = 0;
    buf[strcspn(buf, "\r\n")] = 0;
    if (sp_validate_name(buf) != SP_OK) return;
    char *real = find_profile(root, buf);  // (a profile deleted by hand: Default)
    if (real) snprintf(name, cap, "%s", real);
    free(real);
}

void sp_active(const char *root, char *name, size_t cap) { read_active_file(root, name, cap); }

bool sp_override_active(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR");
    return e && *e;
}

void sp_active_save_dir(const char *root, char *out, size_t cap) {
    const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR");  // (tests: a scratch copy; wins, as it always did)
    if (e && *e) {
        snprintf(out, cap, "%s", e);
        return;
    }
    char name[SP_NAME_MAX + 1];
    sp_active(root, name, sizeof name);
    if (!sp_save_dir(root, name, out, cap)) {
        if (g_settings.save_dir[0]) snprintf(out, cap, "%s", g_settings.save_dir);
        else snprintf(out, cap, "%s", "save");
    }
}

static char g_session[PATH_CAP];

void sp_session_begin(void) {
    sp_active_save_dir(NULL, g_session, sizeof g_session);
    char name[SP_NAME_MAX + 1];
    sp_active(NULL, name, sizeof name);
    if (!sp_override_active() && !is_default_name(name)) fprintf(stderr, "[saves] profile: %s (%s)\n", name, g_session);
}

const char *sp_session_save_dir(void) {
    if (!g_session[0]) sp_active_save_dir(NULL, g_session, sizeof g_session);
    return g_session;
}

// The name is written whole by a rename: a power cut leaves the old name or the new one, never half
static SpCode write_active(const char *root, const char *name) {
    char path[PATH_CAP], tmp[PATH_CAP + 8];
    if (!join(path, sizeof path, root, ACTIVE_FILE)) return fail(SP_IO, "path too long");
    snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s.tmp", path);
    FILE *f = fopen(tmp, "wb");
    if (!f) return fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", tmp, strerror(errno));
    bool ok = fprintf(f, "%s\n", name) > 0;
    ok = fclose(f) == 0 && ok;
    if (ok) {
#ifdef _WIN32
        ok = MoveFileExA(tmp, path, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH) != 0;
#else
        ok = rename(tmp, path) == 0;
#endif
    }
    if (!ok) {
        int err = errno;
        remove(tmp);
        return fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", path, strerror(err));
    }
    return SP_OK;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ listing
int sp_list(const char *root, SpProfile **out) {
    char active[SP_NAME_MAX + 1];
    sp_active(root, active, sizeof active);
    int n;
    char **names = names_list(root, &n);
    SpProfile *v = calloc((size_t)n + 1, sizeof *v);
    *out = v;
    if (!v) { names_free(names, n); return 0; }
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) {
        SpProfile *p = &v[i];
        snprintf(p->name, sizeof p->name, "%s", i ? names[i - 1] : SP_DEFAULT_NAME);
        p->is_default = i == 0;
        p->active = !strcmp(p->name, active);
        char dir[PATH_CAP], s0[PATH_CAP + 8];
        ScSlot *slots = NULL;
        if (sp_save_dir(root, p->name, dir, sizeof dir) && snprintf(s0, sizeof s0, "%s/save_0", dir) < (int)sizeof s0)
            p->slots = sc_list_slots(s0, &slots);
        for (int k = 0; k < p->slots; k++)
            if (slots[k].saved > p->saved) p->saved = slots[k].saved;
        free(slots);
    }
    names_free(names, n);
    return n + 1;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ locks and sizes
// A running game holds <save>.lock: the profile is in use when somebody else has it. A lock file that can't be made
// protects nothing (read-only folder) and doesn't stop the player.
static bool in_use(const char *save_dir) {
    ScLock *l = NULL;
    bool busy = sc_lock_take(save_dir, &l) == SC_LOCK_BUSY;
    sc_lock_drop(l);
    return busy;
}

static uint64_t tree_bytes(const char *dir, int depth) {
    if (depth > 16 || is_link(dir)) return 0;
    DIR *d = opendir(dir);
    if (!d) return 0;
    uint64_t total = 0;
    struct dirent *e;
    while ((e = readdir(d))) {
        char p[PATH_CAP];
        struct stat st;
        if (!strcmp(e->d_name, ".") || !strcmp(e->d_name, "..") || snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s/%s", dir, e->d_name) >= (int)sizeof p ||
            stat(p, &st) != 0)
            continue;
        if (S_ISDIR(st.st_mode)) total += tree_bytes(p, depth + 1);
        else if (S_ISREG(st.st_mode)) total += (uint64_t)st.st_size;
    }
    closedir(d);
    return total;
}

static uint64_t os_free_space(const char *dir) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    ULARGE_INTEGER avail;
    return GetDiskFreeSpaceExA(dir, &avail, NULL, NULL) ? avail.QuadPart : UINT64_MAX;
#else
    struct statvfs sv;
    return statvfs(dir, &sv) == 0 ? (uint64_t)sv.f_bavail * sv.f_frsize : UINT64_MAX;
#endif
}
uint64_t (*sp_free_space_hook)(const char *dir) = os_free_space;

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ removing
// rm -rf that never goes through a link (a junction in a profile would otherwise be followed out of it)
static bool remove_tree(const char *dir, int depth) {
    if (depth > 32 || is_link(dir)) return false;
    DIR *d = opendir(dir);
    if (!d) return false;
    bool ok = true;
    struct dirent *e;
    while (ok && (e = readdir(d))) {
        char p[PATH_CAP];
        if (!strcmp(e->d_name, ".") || !strcmp(e->d_name, "..")) continue;
        if (snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s/%s", dir, e->d_name) >= (int)sizeof p) ok = false;
        else if (is_link(p)) {
#ifdef _WIN32
            ok = remove(p) == 0 || RemoveDirectoryA(p);  // (the link itself, never what it points to)
#else
            ok = remove(p) == 0;
#endif
        } else if (is_dir(p)) ok = remove_tree(p, depth + 1);
        else ok = remove(p) == 0;
    }
    closedir(d);
    return ok && rmdir(dir) == 0;
}

static void tmp_name(const char *root, const char *what, char *out, size_t cap) {
    static unsigned counter;
    char rel[PATH_CAP];
    snprintf(rel, sizeof rel, PROFILES_DIR "/.%s-%lx-%u", what, (unsigned long)time(NULL), ++counter);
    join(out, cap, root, rel);
}

void sp_cleanup(const char *root) {
    char dir[PATH_CAP];
    if (!profiles_dir(root, dir, sizeof dir, false)) return;
    DIR *d = opendir(dir);
    if (!d) return;
    char *doomed[64];
    int n = 0;
    struct dirent *e;
    time_t now = time(NULL);
    while (n < 64 && (e = readdir(d))) {
        char p[PATH_CAP];
        struct stat st;
        bool deleting = !strncmp(e->d_name, ".deleting-", 10), tmp = !strncmp(e->d_name, ".tmp-", 5);
        if (!(deleting || tmp) || snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s/%s", dir, e->d_name) >= (int)sizeof p || stat(p, &st) != 0)
            continue;
        if (deleting || now - st.st_mtime > TMP_MAX_AGE) doomed[n++] = strdup(p);
    }
    closedir(d);
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        if (doomed[i]) remove_tree(doomed[i], 0);
        free(doomed[i]);
    }
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ changing
SpCode sp_set_active(const char *root, const char *name) {
    char *real = find_profile(root, name);
    if (!real) return fail(SP_NOT_FOUND, "%s", name ? name : "");
    char dir[PATH_CAP];
    SpCode c = SP_OK;
    if (!sp_save_dir(root, real, dir, sizeof dir)) c = fail(SP_IO, "path too long");
    else if (in_use(dir)) c = fail(SP_IN_USE, "%s", dir);  // (a running game: starting into it would save from both)
    else c = write_active(root, real);
    free(real);
    return c;
}

// Checks the new name is valid and free; nothing else
static SpCode check_new(const char *root, const char *name) {
    SpCode c = sp_validate_name(name);
    if (c != SP_OK) return fail(c, "%s", name ? name : "");
    char *other = find_profile(root, name);
    if (other) {
        free(other);
        return fail(SP_EXISTS, "%s", name);
    }
    return SP_OK;
}

SpCode sp_create(const char *root, const char *name) {
    SpCode c = check_new(root, name);
    if (c != SP_OK) return c;
    char top[PATH_CAP], dir[PATH_CAP], save[PATH_CAP];
    if (!profiles_dir(root, top, sizeof top, true)) return fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", top, strerror(errno));
    if (!profile_dir(root, name, dir, sizeof dir) || !sp_save_dir(root, name, save, sizeof save)) return fail(SP_IO, "path too long");
    if (mkdir(dir, 0755) != 0) return fail(errno == EEXIST ? SP_EXISTS : SP_IO, "%s: %s", dir, strerror(errno));  // (atomic: two at once can't both win)
    if (mkdir(save, 0755) != 0) {
        int err = errno;
        rmdir(dir);
        return fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", save, strerror(err));
    }
    return SP_OK;
}

SpCode sp_copy(const char *root, const char *from, const char *to, uint64_t *bytes) {
    if (bytes) *bytes = 0;
    char *src_name = find_profile(root, from);
    if (!src_name) return fail(SP_NOT_FOUND, "%s", from ? from : "");
    SpCode c = check_new(root, to);
    char src[PATH_CAP], top[PATH_CAP], tmp[PATH_CAP], tmp_save[PATH_CAP + 8], dst[PATH_CAP];
    if (c == SP_OK && !sp_save_dir(root, src_name, src, sizeof src)) c = fail(SP_IO, "path too long");
    free(src_name);
    if (c != SP_OK) return c;
    if (!profiles_dir(root, top, sizeof top, true)) return fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", top, strerror(errno));
    tmp_name(root, "tmp", tmp, sizeof tmp);
    if (!profile_dir(root, to, dst, sizeof dst) || snprintf(tmp_save, sizeof tmp_save, "%s/save", tmp) >= (int)sizeof tmp_save)
        return fail(SP_IO, "path too long");

    uint64_t size = is_dir(src) ? tree_bytes(src, 0) : 0;
    uint64_t need = size + size / 16 + (1u << 20);  // a margin for folder entries and the next save
    uint64_t have = sp_free_space_hook ? sp_free_space_hook(top) : UINT64_MAX;
    if (have < need) return fail(SP_NO_SPACE, "%llu bytes needed, %llu free", (unsigned long long)need, (unsigned long long)have);

    if (mkdir(tmp, 0755) != 0) return fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", tmp, strerror(errno));
    if (is_dir(src)) {
        ScReport r = {0};
        ScCode sc = sc_backup(src, tmp_save, &r);  // (takes the source's lock; removes what it copied again on failure)
        if (sc != SC_OK) {
            c = sc == SC_IN_USE ? SP_IN_USE : SP_IO;
            fail(c, "%s", r.detail);
            sc_report_free(&r);
            remove_tree(tmp, 0);
            return c;
        }
        sc_report_free(&r);
    } else if (mkdir(tmp_save, 0755) != 0) {  // (no save folder yet: the copy of nothing is an empty profile)
        c = fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", tmp_save, strerror(errno));
        remove_tree(tmp, 0);
        return c;
    }
    // renaming onto an existing folder would replace an empty one on Linux, so look again right before
    char *late = find_profile(root, to);
    if (late) {
        free(late);
        remove_tree(tmp, 0);
        return fail(SP_EXISTS, "%s", to);
    }
    if (rename(tmp, dst) != 0) {
        c = fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", dst, strerror(errno));
        remove_tree(tmp, 0);
        return c;
    }
    if (bytes) *bytes = size;
    return SP_OK;
}

// The profile `name` as a folder that may be renamed or deleted: not Default, not the active one, not in use
static SpCode check_changeable(const char *root, const char *name, char **real) {
    *real = NULL;
    if (is_default_name(name)) return fail(SP_IS_DEFAULT, "%s", SP_DEFAULT_NAME);
    *real = find_profile(root, name);
    if (!*real) return fail(SP_NOT_FOUND, "%s", name);
    char active[SP_NAME_MAX + 1], save[PATH_CAP];
    sp_active(root, active, sizeof active);
    SpCode c = SP_OK;
    if (!strcmp(*real, active)) c = fail(SP_IS_ACTIVE, "%s", *real);
    else if (!sp_save_dir(root, *real, save, sizeof save)) c = fail(SP_IO, "path too long");
    else if (in_use(save)) c = fail(SP_IN_USE, "%s", save);
    if (c != SP_OK) free(*real), *real = NULL;
    return c;
}

SpCode sp_rename(const char *root, const char *from, const char *to) {
    char *real;
    SpCode c = check_changeable(root, from, &real);
    if (c != SP_OK) return c;
    char a[PATH_CAP], b[PATH_CAP];
    if (sp_validate_name(to) != SP_OK) c = fail(sp_validate_name(to), "%s", to ? to : "");
    else if (!profile_dir(root, real, a, sizeof a) || !profile_dir(root, to, b, sizeof b)) c = fail(SP_IO, "path too long");
    else if (!fold_eq(real, to)) {  // (only the case of the letters changing is a rename of the same folder: allowed)
        char *other = find_profile(root, to);
        if (other) free(other), c = fail(SP_EXISTS, "%s", to);
    }
    if (c == SP_OK && rename(a, b) != 0) c = fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", a, strerror(errno));
    free(real);
    return c;
}

SpCode sp_delete(const char *root, const char *name) {
    char *real;
    SpCode c = check_changeable(root, name, &real);
    if (c != SP_OK) return c;
    char dir[PATH_CAP], gone[PATH_CAP];
    if (!profile_dir(root, real, dir, sizeof dir)) c = fail(SP_IO, "path too long");
    else if (is_link(dir)) c = fail(SP_LINKED, "%s", dir);
    else {
        tmp_name(root, "deleting", gone, sizeof gone);
        if (rename(dir, gone) != 0) c = fail(SP_IO, "%s: %s", dir, strerror(errno));  // (nothing changed; Windows: a program has it open)
        else if (!remove_tree(gone, 0)) c = fail(SP_IO, "%s: could not be removed completely (sp_cleanup finishes it)", gone);
    }
    free(real);
    return c;
}

```

`runtime/services/save_profiles.h`:

```h
// Save profiles (runtime/services/save_profiles.c): several complete save folders side by side, one of them active.
//
// A profile is a whole save root, the same layout the game has always used: <save root>/save_0/{0..5,tracker,option.sav}.
// The player's existing `save` folder is the profile called "Default" and is never moved or renamed, so an install
// that has never heard of profiles keeps working with no action. The others live in `save-profiles/<name>/save`:
//
//   <data root>/save                          the Default profile (as before)
//   <data root>/save.lock, save-backups/      its lock and its backups (as before, see save_convert.h)
//   <data root>/save-profiles/<name>/save     every other profile, with its own save.lock and save-backups beside it
//   <data root>/save_profile.txt              the active profile's name (one line); missing or unknown = Default
//
// Which profile is active is one small file of its own rather than a key in savagewind.ini: it is read before and
// independently of the settings, a half-written ini can't lose it, and it is written whole by a rename.
//
// SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR (tests, scratch runs) still wins over everything: when it is set the active profile is ignored.
//
// Like save_convert.h this is SDL-free and has no state of its own except the per-boot session path below. Every
// function that changes a profile takes the game's lock on it (sc_lock_take), so a profile in use by a running Savage
// Wind is never switched to, copied, renamed or deleted from under it. `root` is the data root, NULL or "" for the
// working directory (which rt_paths_init makes the data root).
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <time.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    SP_OK = 0,
    SP_NAME_EMPTY,     // no name, or only spaces
    SP_NAME_LONG,      // longer than SP_NAME_MAX
    SP_NAME_CHARS,     // a character other than letters, digits, space, - _ . ( ), a leading / trailing dot or space, or ".."
    SP_NAME_RESERVED,  // "Default", or a name Windows reserves for devices (CON, NUL, COM1, ...)
    SP_EXISTS,         // a profile with that name exists (upper / lower case don't count)
    SP_NOT_FOUND,      // no such profile
    SP_IS_DEFAULT,     // the Default profile can't be renamed or deleted
    SP_IS_ACTIVE,      // the active profile can't be renamed or deleted: switch to another first
    SP_IN_USE,         // a running game holds the profile's lock
    SP_NO_SPACE,       // not enough free space for the copy
    SP_LINKED,         // the profile folder is a link: deleting it would not stay inside Savage Wind's folder
    SP_IO,             // a file or folder couldn't be read, written or moved (see sp_detail)
} SpCode;

enum { SP_NAME_MAX = 32 };  // (short: the data root, the name and save_0/tracker/... have to fit Windows' 260 characters)
#define SP_DEFAULT_NAME "Default"

// Why the last failing call failed, in English, for the log (a path and the system's reason). Per thread.
const char *sp_detail(void);

// ---- names
// SP_OK, or SP_NAME_*. Name rules: 1..SP_NAME_MAX characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 space - _ . ( ); no leading or trailing
// space or dot, no "..", not a Windows device name (with or without an extension), not "Default" in any case. That keeps
// a name a single plain folder name on Windows and Linux, with no separator, drive or parent reference possible.
SpCode sp_validate_name(const char *name);

// ---- looking
typedef struct {
    char name[SP_NAME_MAX + 1];
    bool is_default;
    bool active;
    int slots;        // slot folders in it
    time_t saved;     // when the newest slot was saved (the game's file times), 0: none
} SpProfile;
// Default first, then the others by name (upper / lower case alike). Folders whose name isn't a valid profile name, and
// the temporary ones the copy and delete make (a leading dot), are not listed. The count; free the list with free().
int sp_list(const char *root, SpProfile **out);
// The profile's save root (the folder with save_0 in it), as game and Saves tab use it. false: invalid name.
// NULL, "" and "Default" give <root>/save.
bool sp_save_dir(const char *root, const char *name, char *out, size_t cap);
// The active profile's name: from save_profile.txt, "Default" when the file is missing or names a profile that is gone.
void sp_active(const char *root, char *name, size_t cap);
bool sp_override_active(void);  // SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR is set: profiles don't apply
// The save root to use now: SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR if set, else the active profile's.
void sp_active_save_dir(const char *root, char *out, size_t cap);

// ---- the game's session
// main.c calls sp_session_begin() once per boot, after the start screen (where the player may have switched profile),
// and the lock, the game's file system and the log all use sp_session_save_dir() from then on: one answer for the
// whole boot, even if save_profile.txt changes meanwhile. Without a session it is sp_active_save_dir(NULL, ...).
void sp_session_begin(void);
const char *sp_session_save_dir(void);

// ---- changing
SpCode sp_set_active(const char *root, const char *name);       // SP_NOT_FOUND, SP_IN_USE (a game runs in it)
SpCode sp_create(const char *root, const char *name);           // an empty profile
// A complete copy of profile `from` as the new profile `to`: made under a temporary name and renamed into place only
// when whole, so a failure (no space, a file in use, a power cut) leaves no half profile. `from` can be Default.
// SP_NO_SPACE before anything is copied when the drive is too full. *bytes: the size copied (may be NULL).
SpCode sp_copy(const char *root, const char *from, const char *to, uint64_t *bytes);
SpCode sp_rename(const char *root, const char *from, const char *to);
// Deletes the profile whole. Refuses Default, the active profile, a profile in use and a linked folder. The folder
// is renamed out of the list first, so an interrupted delete never leaves a half profile showing.
SpCode sp_delete(const char *root, const char *name);
// Removes what a crash left: temporary copies older than a day and half-deleted profiles. Call from a worker.
void sp_cleanup(const char *root);

// Free bytes where `dir` is; tests replace it to fake a full disk. Default: the operating system's answer (UINT64_MAX
// when it can't tell, which skips the check).
extern uint64_t (*sp_free_space_hook)(const char *dir);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

```

`runtime/services/test_warp.c`:

```c
// (test only, never a player feature) Start the game somewhere else: values of game_data.sav rewritten as the game
// reads the file, which itself stays as it is. With a scratch save folder (SAVAGEWIND_SAVE_DIR) and "Continue", a
// scripted test run loads straight into another region, at another hour or in other weather.
//
//   SAVAGEWIND_TEST_WARP=<place> | <x>,<y>,<z>[,<map type>/<map name>]   where Link appears (PlayerSavePos and the
//       map it is on; for MainField the section, e.g. D-6, follows from x and z). Places: see warp_places below.
//       A warp also hands Link the paraglider (IsGet_PlayerStole2), which opens the Great Plateau.
//   SAVAGEWIND_TEST_TIME=<hour 0-24>         the hour of the day, held there: the game takes no time of day from
//                                            the save on Continue (WM_Time is ignored), so test_warp_frame writes
//                                            both WM_Time buffers and stops TimeMgr's native clock
//   SAVAGEWIND_TEST_WEATHER=<n>              every forecast (climateWeather*): 0 clear, 1 cloudy, 2 rain,
//                                            3 heavy rain, 4 snow, 5 heavy snow, 6 thunderstorm, 7 thunder rain
//                                            (the weather at load does not follow them either)
//   SAVAGEWIND_TEST_FLAGS=<name>=<value>[,...]  any other s32 / bool (integer) or f32 (with a '.') value
//
// game_data.sav: a 0xC-byte header, then 8-byte entries (crc32 of the flag name, 32-bit value). Vectors, arrays and
// strings are runs of entries with the same hash (x, y, z / one per element / 4 characters each).
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../control_mem.h"
#include "../game_sites.h"
#include "../hle.h"

typedef struct { const char *name; float x, y, z; const char *map_type, *map_name; } WarpPlace;
// Positions are the game's own start positions near each place (Map/MainField/Static.smubin and
// Map/MainFieldDungeon/Static.smubin in Bootup.pack: StartPos entries).
static const WarpPlace warp_places[] = {
    {"plateau", -1041.6f, 250.2f, 1812.1f},          // the Great Plateau, outside the Shrine of Resurrection
    {"kakariko", 1811.7f, 218.5f, 982.6f},           // Kakariko Village (HorseGate)
    {"stable", 384.8f, 121.7f, 1035.6f},             // Riverside Stable (OldKorok_RiversideStable)
    {"hateno", 3437.5f, 235.9f, 2101.5f},            // Hateno Village, goddess statue (GoddessHateno)
    {"castle", -254.0f, 140.6f, -544.6f},            // Hyrule Castle, front (HyruleCastleExit)
    {"castle_in", -156.6f, 144.2f, -1159.3f},        // inside Hyrule Castle, by its shrine (StartPos_CDungeon089)
    {"desert", -3196.0f, 129.4f, 2549.3f},           // Gerudo Desert, Kara Kara Bazaar (Oasis001)
    {"gerudo", -3784.7f, 149.1f, 2864.5f},           // Gerudo Town gate (Gerudo001)
    {"hebra", -2165.2f, 529.2f, -2029.5f},           // Hebra, on top of its tower (StartPos_Tower01)
    {"zora", 3315.6f, 255.6f, -501.0f},              // Zora's Domain, goddess statue (GoddessZora)
    {"goron", 1719.0f, 498.9f, -2456.2f},            // Goron City (GoddessGoron)
    {"rito", -3607.2f, 286.3f, -1805.5f},            // Rito Village (GoddessRito)
    {"korok", 418.1f, 258.5f, -2177.6f},             // Korok Forest (GoddessKorok)
    {"ruta", 48.0f, 6.3f, 3.0f, "MainFieldDungeon", "RemainsWater"},     // inside Divine Beast Vah Ruta (Entrance_1)
    {"rudania", 0.0f, 16.8f, 69.5f, "MainFieldDungeon", "RemainsFire"},  // inside Divine Beast Vah Rudania
};

static uint32_t crc32_of(const char *s) {
    uint32_t c = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
    for (; *s; s++) {
        c ^= (uint8_t)*s;
        for (int k = 0; k < 8; k++) c = c >> 1 ^ (0xEDB88320u & -(c & 1));
    }
    return ~c;
}

// Every entry of `name` from the first, in order: n values (u32 bits) copied in; returns how many entries matched.
static int set_entries(uint8_t *d, uint64_t size, const char *name, const uint32_t *v, int n, bool repeat_last) {
    uint32_t h = crc32_of(name);
    int k = 0;
    for (uint64_t o = 0xC; o + 8 <= size; o += 8) {
        if (*(uint32_t *)(d + o) != h) continue;
        if (k < n) *(uint32_t *)(d + o + 4) = v[k];
        else if (repeat_last && n) *(uint32_t *)(d + o + 4) = v[n - 1];
        k++;
    }
    if (!k) LOG("[warp] %s is not in the save\n", name);
    return k;
}
static void set_f32(uint8_t *d, uint64_t size, const char *name, const float *f, int n) {
    uint32_t v[4];
    memcpy(v, f, (size_t)n * 4);
    set_entries(d, size, name, v, n, false);
}
static void set_u32(uint8_t *d, uint64_t size, const char *name, uint32_t v) { set_entries(d, size, name, &v, 1, false); }
static void set_str(uint8_t *d, uint64_t size, const char *name, const char *s) {
    uint32_t v[16] = {0};  // (string_data: 32 bytes, 8 entries)
    strncpy((char *)v, s, sizeof v - 1);
    set_entries(d, size, name, v, 16, false);
}

bool test_warp_active(void) {
    return getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_WARP") || getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_TIME") || getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_WEATHER") ||
           getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_FLAGS");
}

void test_warp_patch(uint8_t *d, uint64_t size) {
    const char *w = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_WARP");
    if (w && *w) {
        WarpPlace p = {0};
        bool found = false;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof warp_places / sizeof warp_places[0]; i++)
            if (!strcmp(w, warp_places[i].name)) { p = warp_places[i]; found = true; }
        static char type[32], name[32];
        if (!found && sscanf(w, "%f,%f,%f", &p.x, &p.y, &p.z) == 3) {
            found = true;
            const char *m = strchr(w, '/') ? strrchr(w, ',') : NULL;  // ",<map type>/<map name>" after the third number
            if (m && sscanf(m + 1, "%31[^/]/%31s", type, name) == 2) { p.map_type = type; p.map_name = name; }
        }
        if (!found) {
            LOG("[warp] unknown place '%s'; places:", w);
            for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof warp_places / sizeof warp_places[0]; i++) LOG(" %s", warp_places[i].name);
            LOG("\n");
        } else {
            char section[8];
            if (!p.map_type) {  // MainField sections: 1000 x 1000, columns A-J from x = -5000, rows 1-8 from z = -4000
                int col = (int)((p.x + 5000.0f) / 1000.0f), row = (int)((p.z + 4000.0f) / 1000.0f) + 1;
                snprintf(section, sizeof section, "%c-%d", 'A' + (col < 0 ? 0 : col > 9 ? 9 : col), row < 1 ? 1 : row > 8 ? 8 : row);
                p.map_type = "MainField";
                p.map_name = section;
            }
            float pos[3] = {p.x, p.y, p.z};
            set_f32(d, size, "PlayerSavePos", pos, 3);
            set_str(d, size, "PlayerSavePosMapType", p.map_type);
            set_str(d, size, "PlayerSavePosMapName", p.map_name);
            set_u32(d, size, "IsGet_PlayerStole2", 1);
            LOG("[warp] Link starts at %.1f, %.1f, %.1f on %s/%s\n", p.x, p.y, p.z, p.map_type, p.map_name);
        }
    }
    const char *t = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_TIME");
    if (t && *t) {
        float wm = (float)atof(t) * 15.0f;
        set_f32(d, size, "WM_Time", &wm, 1);
        LOG("[warp] hour %s (WM_Time %.1f)\n", t, wm);
    }
    const char *wx = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_WEATHER");
    if (wx && *wx) {
        uint32_t v = (uint32_t)atoi(wx);
        set_entries(d, size, "climateWeather", &v, 1, true);
        set_entries(d, size, "climateWeather2", &v, 1, true);
        set_entries(d, size, "climateWeather3", &v, 1, true);
        LOG("[warp] weather %u in every forecast\n", v);
    }
    const char *fl = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_FLAGS");
    for (const char *s = fl; s && *s;) {
        char name[128], val[64];
        if (sscanf(s, "%127[^=]=%63[^,]", name, val) != 2) break;
        if (strchr(val, '.')) { float f = (float)atof(val); set_f32(d, size, name, &f, 1); }
        else set_u32(d, size, name, (uint32_t)strtol(val, NULL, 0));
        LOG("[warp] %s = %s\n", name, val);
        s = strchr(s, ',');
        if (s) s++;
    }
}

// TimeMgr's time of day, 0..360 = 24 h (NULL until the world exists). ksys::world::Manager [world_mgr]
// (+0x5c0 count, +0x5c8 its managers; [0] = TimeMgr, the time at +0xb8), as SAVAGEWIND_CLOCK_PROBE reads it
// (runtime/hle/framepace.c).
static float *time_of_day(void) {
    if (!g_site.world_mgr) return NULL;
    uint64_t wm = *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)g_site.world_mgr;
    if (!wm || !*(uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x5c0)) return NULL;
    uint64_t mgrs = *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x5c8), tm = mgrs ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)mgrs : 0;
    return tm ? (float *)(uintptr_t)(tm + 0xb8) : NULL;
}

// The requested held hour (-2: SAVAGEWIND_TEST_TIME not read yet, -1: not held).
static float held_tod = -2;
static uint64_t sampled_manager, game_data_site;
static uint64_t frozen_manager;
static float saved_speed, pending_tod = -1;

static uint64_t read_pointer(uint64_t addr) {
    uint64_t p = 0;
    return control_mem_peek(addr, &p, sizeof p) ? p : 0;
}

// TimeMgr::calc reloads WM_Time from GameDataMgr each update. Its vtable's calc slot starts with an ADRP/ADD
// reference to that singleton. Decode that reference rather than pinning a 1.9.0 address or changing the game
// library's site table. Require the whole load/branch sequence and a singleton in main's data segment.
static uint64_t time_data_site(uint64_t tm) {
    if (tm == sampled_manager && game_data_site) return game_data_site;
    uint64_t calc = read_pointer(read_pointer(tm) + 0x30);
    uint32_t code[32];
    if (calc < MAIN_BASE || calc >= g_site.main_data ||
        !control_mem_peek(calc, code, sizeof code)) return 0;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i + 3 < sizeof code / sizeof *code; i++) {
        if ((code[i] & 0x9f00001f) != 0x90000008 ||
            (code[i + 1] & 0xffc003ff) != 0x91000108 ||
            code[i + 2] != 0xf9400114 || (code[i + 3] & 0xff00001f) != 0xb5000014) continue;
        uint32_t imm = ((code[i] >> 5) & 0x7ffff) << 2 | ((code[i] >> 29) & 3);
        int64_t pages = (int64_t)(imm ^ 0x100000) - 0x100000;
        uint64_t site = ((calc + 4 * i) & ~0xfffull) + pages * 4096 + ((code[i + 1] >> 10) & 0xfff);
        if (site < g_site.main_data || site + 8 > g_site.main_end) continue;
        sampled_manager = tm;
        return game_data_site = site;
    }
    return 0;
}

// The pending-write buffer uses proxy flags (value at +0x10, primary flag at +8); the current-read buffer uses
// primary flags (value at +0x18, name hash at +0x1c). Verify each float getter and the primary's WM_Time hash.
static bool time_flags(float *now, uint64_t flags[2]) {
    uint64_t tm = (uintptr_t)now - 0xb8, site = time_data_site(tm);
    uint64_t mgr = site ? read_pointer(site) : 0;
    uint32_t handle;
    if (!mgr || !control_mem_peek(tm + 0xd4, &handle, sizeof handle) || handle == UINT32_MAX) return false;
    handle &= 0xffffff;
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
        uint64_t buffer = read_pointer(read_pointer(mgr + 0xbd8 + 8 * i));
        uint32_t count, hash;
        if (!buffer || !control_mem_peek(buffer + 0x28, &count, sizeof count) || handle >= count) return false;
        uint64_t array = read_pointer(buffer + 0x30);
        uint64_t flag = array ? read_pointer(array + 8 * handle) : 0;
        uint64_t getter = read_pointer(read_pointer(flag) + 0x88), primary = flag;
        uint32_t code[2], value_offset;
        if (!getter || !control_mem_peek(getter, code, sizeof code) || code[1] != 0xd65f03c0) return false;
        if (code[0] == 0xbd401800) value_offset = 0x18;  // ldr s0, [x0, #0x18]; ret
        else if (code[0] == 0xbd401000) {               // ldr s0, [x0, #0x10]; ret
            value_offset = 0x10;
            primary = read_pointer(flag + 8);
        } else return false;
        if (!primary || !control_mem_peek(primary + 0x1c, &hash, sizeof hash) || hash != crc32_of("WM_Time")) return false;
        flags[i] = flag + value_offset;
    }
    return true;
}

static bool write_time(float *now, float tod) {
    uint64_t flags[2];
    if (!time_flags(now, flags)) return false;
    // Updating just the display is lost on the next calc; updating only one buffer is lost on publication.
    if (!control_mem_poke(flags[0], &tod, sizeof tod) ||
        !control_mem_poke(flags[1], &tod, sizeof tod)) return false;
    // Before the paraglider, TimeMgr caps its clock at 11:00. Lift only that cached clock gate for this
    // explicit time override, so release can advance from any hour. The quest's game-data flag stays intact.
    uint8_t running = 1;
    if (!control_mem_poke((uintptr_t)now - 0xb8 + 0x14e, &running, sizeof running)) return false;
    *now = tod;
    return true;
}

static void read_test_time(void) {
    if (held_tod != -2) return;
    const char *t = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_TEST_TIME");
    held_tod = t && *t ? (float)atof(t) * 15.0f : -1;
}

// TimeMgr::calc advances WM_Time by (+0xc4 * frame delta), in both its normal and accelerated modes.
// Stop that native increment before publishing the held hour to both buffers, so every clock consumer sees
// the same value. Keep the original speed once per manager; repeated freeze/set commands must not save zero.
static void hold_time(float *now) {
    uint64_t tm = (uintptr_t)now - 0xb8;
    if (frozen_manager != tm) {
        float speed, stopped = 0;
        if (!control_mem_peek(tm + 0xc4, &speed, sizeof speed) ||
            !control_mem_poke(tm + 0xc4, &stopped, sizeof stopped)) return;
        if (!write_time(now, held_tod == 360 ? 0 : held_tod)) {
            control_mem_poke(tm + 0xc4, &speed, sizeof speed);
            return;  // The world may expose its TimeMgr before the game-data handles are ready.
        }
        saved_speed = speed;
        frozen_manager = tm;
    }
}

// A numeric hour changes the time, preserving whether the clock is running or held.
void test_warp_set_hour(float hour) {
    read_test_time();
    float tod = hour * 15.0f;
    if (held_tod >= 0) held_tod = tod;
    float *now = time_of_day();
    pending_tod = now ? -1 : tod;
    if (!now) return;
    if (held_tod >= 0) hold_time(now);
    if (!write_time(now, tod == 360 ? 0 : tod)) pending_tod = tod;
}

// Explicit hold for freeze, goto and test fixtures; a negative hour releases it.
void test_warp_hold_hour(float hour) {
    read_test_time();
    float *now = time_of_day();
    if (hour < 0) {
        if (held_tod >= 0 && now) {
            write_time(now, held_tod == 360 ? 0 : held_tod);
            uint64_t tm = (uintptr_t)now - 0xb8;
            if (frozen_manager == tm) control_mem_poke(tm + 0xc4, &saved_speed, sizeof saved_speed);
        }
        frozen_manager = 0;
        held_tod = -1;
    } else {
        held_tod = hour * 15.0f;
        pending_tod = -1;
        if (now) {
            hold_time(now);
            write_time(now, held_tod == 360 ? 0 : held_tod);
        }
    }
}

// The current hour of the day (0..24), or -1 before the world exists; *held says whether it is being held.
float test_warp_hour(bool *held) {
    read_test_time();
    if (held) *held = held_tod >= 0;
    float *now = time_of_day();
    if (!now) return -1.0f;
    return (held_tod >= 0 ? held_tod : *now) / 15.0f;
}

// Every presentation, before control_frame on both backends: attach a pending override to a newly loaded
// TimeMgr. Once held, its native clock stays stopped; no per-frame display write fights its calc or lights.
void test_warp_frame(uint64_t frame) {
    (void)frame;
    read_test_time();
    if (held_tod < 0 && pending_tod < 0) return;
    float *now = time_of_day();
    if (!now) { frozen_manager = 0; return; }
    if (held_tod >= 0) hold_time(now);
    else if (pending_tod >= 0 && !write_time(now, pending_tod == 360 ? 0 : pending_tod)) return;
    pending_tod = -1;
}

RT_ON_RESET(test_warp_reset) {
    held_tod = -2;
    sampled_manager = game_data_site = frozen_manager = 0;
    pending_tod = -1;
}
```

`runtime/services/time.c`:

```c
// time:u / time:a / time:s
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/time.h>
#include <time.h>

#include "../hle.h"
#include "../ipc.h"

static const uint8_t clock_uuid[16] = {0x4c, 0x41, 0x52, 0x65, 0x63, 0x6f, 0x6d, 0x70, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8};

static int64_t steady_seconds(void) { return (int64_t)(rt_ticks() / 19200000ull); }
static int64_t unix_now(void) { return (int64_t)time(NULL); }

static void write_system_context(uint8_t *p) {  // SystemClockContext (0x20)
    int64_t steady = steady_seconds();
    *(int64_t *)p = unix_now() - steady;
    *(int64_t *)(p + 8) = steady;
    memcpy(p + 0x10, clock_uuid, 16);
}

static void time_shmem_map(KSharedMem *s) {
    uint8_t *m = (uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)s->guest_addr;
    LOG("[time] shared memory mapped at %llx\n", (unsigned long long)s->guest_addr);
    // 0x00: LockFreeAtomicType<SteadyClockContext{u64 internal_offset, uuid}>
    *(uint32_t *)m = 0;
    *(uint64_t *)(m + 0x08) = 0;
    memcpy(m + 0x10, clock_uuid, 16);
    // 0x38 local system clock, 0x80 network system clock
    *(uint32_t *)(m + 0x38) = 0;
    write_system_context(m + 0x40);
    *(uint32_t *)(m + 0x80) = 0;
    write_system_context(m + 0x88);
    // 0xC8 automatic correction enabled
    *(uint32_t *)(m + 0xC8) = 0;
    m[0xCC] = 0;
}

static void system_clock(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp) {
    (void)s;
    switch (req->cmd) {
    case 0: OUT(int64_t, 0) = unix_now(); resp_size(resp, 8); break;  // GetCurrentTime
    case 2: write_system_context(resp->data); resp_size(resp, 0x20); break;  // GetSystemClockContext
    default: LOG("[time] ISystemClock cmd %u (ok)\n", req->cmd);
    }
}

static void steady_clock(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp) {
    (void)s;
    switch (req->cmd) {
    case 0:  // GetCurrentTimePoint
        OUT(int64_t, 0) = steady_seconds();
        memcpy(resp->data + 8, clock_uuid, 16);
        resp_size(resp, 0x18);
        break;
    default: OUT(int64_t, 0) = 0; resp_size(resp, 8); LOG("[time] ISteadyClock cmd %u (ok)\n", req->cmd);
    }
}

static void to_calendar(int64_t t, IpcResp *resp, int utc) {
    time_t tt = (time_t)t;
    struct tm tm;
    if (utc) gmtime_r(&tt, &tm); else localtime_r(&tt, &tm);
    uint8_t *o = resp->data;
    *(uint16_t *)o = (uint16_t)(tm.tm_year + 1900);
    o[2] = (uint8_t)(tm.tm_mon + 1); o[3] = (uint8_t)tm.tm_mday;
    o[4] = (uint8_t)tm.tm_hour; o[5] = (uint8_t)tm.tm_min; o[6] = (uint8_t)tm.tm_sec;
    *(uint32_t *)(o + 8) = (uint32_t)tm.tm_wday;
    *(uint32_t *)(o + 12) = (uint32_t)tm.tm_yday;
#ifdef _WIN32  // no tm_zone / tm_gmtoff: offset = local broken-down time read back as UTC, minus now
    struct tm g;
    gmtime_r(&tt, &g);
    long gmtoff = (long)difftime(_mkgmtime(&tm), _mkgmtime(&g));
    memcpy(o + 16, utc ? "UTC" : "LCL", 4);
#else
    long gmtoff = tm.tm_gmtoff;
    memcpy(o + 16, utc ? "UTC" : tm.tm_zone, 4);
#endif
    *(uint32_t *)(o + 24) = (uint32_t)tm.tm_isdst;
    *(int32_t *)(o + 28) = utc ? 0 : (int32_t)gmtoff;
    resp_size(resp, 0x20);
}

static void timezone_service(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp) {
    (void)s;
    switch (req->cmd) {
    case 0: memcpy(resp->data, "UTC", 4); resp_size(resp, 0x24); break;  // GetDeviceLocationName
    case 100: to_calendar(IN(int64_t, 0), resp, 1); break;  // ToCalendarTime(rule buffer)
    case 101: to_calendar(IN(int64_t, 0), resp, 0); break;  // ToCalendarTimeWithMyRule
    case 201: {  // ToPosixTimeWithMyRule -> count + buffer of posix times
        const uint8_t *in = req->data;
        struct tm tm = {0};
        tm.tm_year = *(uint16_t *)in - 1900; tm.tm_mon = in[2] - 1; tm.tm_mday = in[3];
        tm.tm_hour = in[4]; tm.tm_min = in[5]; tm.tm_sec = in[6]; tm.tm_isdst = -1;
        int64_t t = mktime(&tm);
        if (req->nc) *(int64_t *)(uintptr_t)req->c[0].addr = t;
        else if (req->nb) *(int64_t *)(uintptr_t)req->b[0].addr = t;
        OUT(uint32_t, 0) = 1;
        resp_size(resp, 4);
        break;
    }
    default: LOG("[time] ITimeZoneService cmd %u (ok)\n", req->cmd); resp_size(resp, 0x10);
    }
}

static uint32_t g_shmem_handle;
RT_ON_RESET(time_reset) { g_shmem_handle = 0; }

static void static_service(Service *s, IpcReq *req, IpcResp *resp) {
    (void)s;
    switch (req->cmd) {
    case 0: case 1: case 4: case 5:
        ipc_return_object(resp, service_new("ISystemClock", system_clock, NULL));
        break;
    case 2: ipc_return_object(resp, service_new("ISteadyClock", steady_clock, NULL)); break;
    case 3: ipc_return_object(resp, service_new("ITimeZoneService", timezone_service, NULL)); break;
    case 20: {  // GetSharedMemoryNativeHandle
        if (!g_shmem_handle) kernel_create_shared_memory(0x1000, time_shmem_map, &g_shmem_handle);
        resp->copy_handles[resp->ncopy++] = g_shmem_handle;
        break;
    }
    case 100: case 101: OUT(uint8_t, 0) = 0; resp_size(resp, 1); break;
    default: LOG("[time] IStaticService cmd %u (ok)\n", req->cmd); resp_size(resp, 0x10);
    }
}

SERVICE("time:u", time_u) { static_service(s, req, resp); }
SERVICE("time:a", time_a) { static_service(s, req, resp); }
SERVICE("time:s", time_s) { static_service(s, req, resp); }

// nn::time::StandardUserSystemClock::GetCurrentTime(PosixTime*): answered directly from the host clock. The SDK's
// shared-memory path aborts (svcBreak via nn::diag::Abort, result 0xcc74) if the local clock's source id ever
// differs from the steady clock's; that happened once in the room sweep on an autosave (entering Eagle's Tower) and
// could not be reproduced, so the date stamp no longer depends on it.
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn4time23StandardUserSystemClock14GetCurrentTimeEPNS0_9PosixTimeE", time_std_user_now) {
    static int n;
    if (n++ < 3) LOG("[time] StandardUserSystemClock::GetCurrentTime (host clock)\n");
    if (c->x[0]) *(int64_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[0] = unix_now();
    c->x[0] = 0;  // ResultSuccess
}
```

`runtime/settings.c`:

```c
#include "settings.h"
#include "gpu_select.h"

#include <math.h>

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "hle.h"

bool fsr3_upscaler_enabled(void);  // (nvn/output_scale.c: SAVAGEWIND_FSR3=0 hides FSR 3 / 4)

#define SETTINGS_FILE settings_file()

// SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS=<path>: another settings file (test runs never touch the player's savagewind.ini)
const char *settings_file(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS");
    return e && *e ? e : "savagewind.ini";
}

Settings g_settings = {

    .anisotropy = 1,  // (2x: the Original graphics preset)

    .render_scale = RSCALE_100,

    .pc_gyro = true,

    .stick_cam_x = STICK_CAM_DEFAULT,

    .stick_deadzone = {STICK_DEADZONE_DEFAULT, STICK_DEADZONE_DEFAULT},
    .fps_limit = FPS_DEFAULT,
    .precompile_shaders = true,

    .boot_picture = true,

    .async_shaders = true,
    .vsync = VSYNC_DEFAULT,
    .gpu = -1,
    .wide_view = true,
    .hud_edges = false,
    .hdr_peak_nits = 0,  // (not set yet: the first start reads the ICC peak, else 1000; then it is a normal setting)
    .hdr_game_nits = 203,  // (HGIG reference white)
    .hdr_ui_nits = 203,    // (the HUD/menu; HGIG reference white by default)
    .hdr_hue = 70,         // (RenoDX BOTW's default highlight hue/purity transfer)
    .hdr_blowout = 65,     // (RenoDX BOTW's default SDR highlight desaturation/purity)
    .hdr_sdr_blend = 18,   // (RenoDX BOTW's default extended-curve pivot, percent)
    .hdr_vanilla_saturation = 100,  // (the game's own saturation grade)
    .hdr_bloom = 100,      // (the game's own bloom)
    .hdr_clamp = 0,        // (BT.709, as the game's own grade)
    .hdr_tonemapper = 1,   // (RenoDX PsychoV, the BOTW mod's default and its "RenoDRT" label)
    .hdr_exposure = 100,   // (the mod's ColorGradeExposure default)
    .hdr_highlights = 50,  // (the mod's ColorGradeHighlights default)

    .hdr_flare = 0,        // (the mod's ColorGradeFlare default)
    .hdr_gamma = 0,        // (the mod's ToneMapGammaCorrection default)
    .hdr_look = {          // (Video > HDR preset 1..3; all three start as the mod's defaults)
        {1, 100, 50, 50, 50, 50, 50, 0, 70, 65, 18, 100, 100, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0},

    .fast_fma = true,
};

static const char *const k_vsync[VSYNC_COUNT] = {"on", "fast", "adaptive", "off"};  // (VSYNC_*: the ini's words)

// settings_version 2 (2026-10-19): the upscaler's mode, the window size and the 300% mouse default. Older files: their
// "resolution" (the internal resolution, removed) gives the upscaler's mode, and a mouse sensitivity at the old
// default (100%) becomes the new one.
// settings_version 3 (2026-10-20): the upscaler sets the 3D image's resolution (AMD FSR 1 renders it smaller). Before,
// "fsr1" (the default) only scaled the finished 1920x1080 image to a bigger window: older files load it as Off, so
// nobody drops below the window's resolution unasked, except version-1 files whose internal resolution was a share of
// the display (75%, 50%, 25%: they keep FSR 1 at the nearest mode).
// settings_version 4 (2026-11-01): "Asynchronous shaders" is on by default: with the shaders precompiled, the pipeline
// list pre-warmed at start and the cheap links done inline (exec.c link_now), a draw only skips a frame for a real
// shader compile, and the draws that must not be skipped (one-shot targets, texture arrays, compute) wait. Older files
// have the old default (off) written in them: version 3 files take the new default (a player who turned it on keeps
// it; one who left it off was on the default, since the menu wrote every key).
#define SETTINGS_VERSION 4
```
