`runtime/update_appimage.c`:

```c
// Updating a Linux AppImage (runtime/update_appimage.h).
#ifdef __linux__
#ifndef _GNU_SOURCE
#define _GNU_SOURCE  // (execvpe)
#endif
#include "update_appimage.h"
#include "platform.h"
#include "platform/sw_update_key.h"
#include "update_crypto.h"

#include <errno.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <strings.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/statvfs.h>
#include <sys/wait.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <fcntl.h>

#define REPO "Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp"
#define FEED_URL "https://api.github.com/repos/" REPO "/releases?per_page=30"
#define DOWNLOAD_PREFIX "https://github.com/" REPO "/releases/download/"
#define HEALTH_EXIT 73  // savagewind --update-health (runtime/main.c)

#if defined(__x86_64__)
#define ASSET_SUFFIX "-x86_64.AppImage"
#elif defined(__aarch64__)
#define ASSET_SUFFIX "-aarch64.AppImage"
#else
#define ASSET_SUFFIX "-unsupported.AppImage"
#endif

extern char **environ;

static bool fail(UpdateProblem *p, const char *code, const char *title, const char *fmt, ...) {
    snprintf(p->code, sizeof p->code, "%s", code);
    snprintf(p->title, sizeof p->title, "%s", title);
    va_list a;
    va_start(a, fmt);
    vsnprintf(p->what, sizeof p->what, fmt, a);
    va_end(a);
    fprintf(stderr, "[update] PROBLEM %s: %s | %s\n", p->code, p->title, p->what);
    return false;
}

// $APPIMAGE only when this program is the one inside it: the runtime sets $APPDIR to its mount, which this program then
// runs from. An AppImage launcher passes its own $APPIMAGE / $APPDIR on to the games it starts (Quiver Launcher before
// 3.3.3), and a source build started from such a terminal inherits them: "updating" would replace that other program.
static char g_self_image[1100];

static void appimage_find(void) {
    const char *a = getenv("APPIMAGE"), *d = getenv("APPDIR");
    if (!a || !*a) return;
    char exe[1100], appdir[1100], real[1100];
    if (!d || !realpath(d, appdir) || !plat_exe_path(exe, sizeof exe) || !uc_path_inside(exe, appdir)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[update] APPIMAGE=%s is another program's: this one is not an AppImage release\n", a);
        return;
    }
    // (the file itself: started through a symbolic link, the update replaces what it points to, not the link)
    snprintf(g_self_image, sizeof g_self_image, "%s", realpath(a, real) ? real : a);
}

const char *appimage_path(void) {
    static pthread_once_t once = PTHREAD_ONCE_INIT;
    pthread_once(&once, appimage_find);
    return g_self_image[0] ? g_self_image : NULL;
}

// The environment for another program. What the AppImage runtime set describes this mount, not the next program's.
// curl is the system's: libraries a launcher such as Steam injects aren't meant for it (no_ld).
static char **child_env(bool no_ld) {
    size_t n = 0;
    while (environ[n]) n++;
    char **e = (char **)calloc(n + 1, sizeof *e);
    size_t k = 0;
    static const char *const drop[] = {"APPDIR=", "APPIMAGE=", "ARGV0=", "OWD="}, *const ld[] = {"LD_LIBRARY_PATH=", "LD_PRELOAD="};
    for (size_t i = 0; e && i < n; i++) {
        bool skip = false;
        for (size_t d = 0; d < sizeof drop / sizeof *drop; d++) skip |= !strncmp(environ[i], drop[d], strlen(drop[d]));
        for (size_t d = 0; no_ld && d < sizeof ld / sizeof *ld; d++) skip |= !strncmp(environ[i], ld[d], strlen(ld[d]));
        if (!skip) e[k++] = environ[i];
    }
    return e;
}

// Runs argv (looked up in PATH), stdout into out if given; exit status, 127 if it can't start, -1 if it had to be stopped.
// While it runs, *watch_size (if given) follows the size of watch.
static int run(char *const argv[], const char *out, int timeout_s, bool no_ld, const char *watch, uint64_t watch_base,
               uint64_t watch_total, volatile float *progress, float from, float to) {
    char **env = child_env(no_ld);
    if (!env) return 127;
    pid_t pid = fork();
    if (pid < 0) {
        free(env);
        return 127;
    }
    if (!pid) {
        int fd = open(out ? out : "/dev/null", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, 0644);
        if (fd >= 0) dup2(fd, 1);
        int nul = open("/dev/null", O_WRONLY);
        if (nul >= 0) dup2(nul, 2);
        execvpe(argv[0], argv, env);
        _exit(127);
    }
    free(env);
    time_t t0 = time(NULL);
    for (;;) {
        int st;
        pid_t r = waitpid(pid, &st, WNOHANG);
        if (r == pid) return WIFEXITED(st) ? WEXITSTATUS(st) : -1;
        if (r < 0) return -1;
        if (timeout_s && time(NULL) - t0 > timeout_s) {
            kill(pid, SIGKILL);
            waitpid(pid, &st, 0);
            return -1;
        }
        if (watch && progress && watch_total) {
            struct stat s;
            if (stat(watch, &s) == 0) {
                float f = (float)(s.st_size + (long long)watch_base) / (float)watch_total;
                *progress = from + (to - from) * (f > 1 ? 1 : f);
            }
        }
        struct timespec ts = {0, 100000000};
        nanosleep(&ts, NULL);
    }
}

static bool curl_problem(int rc, UpdateProblem *p) {
    switch (rc) {
        case 127:
            return fail(p, "no_curl", "curl is not installed",
                        "Savage Wind uses your system's curl program to download updates and could not find it. Install "
                        "curl with your distribution's package manager, or get the new AppImage from the project's "
                        "GitHub releases page.");
        case 6:
            return fail(p, "no_internet", "No internet connection",
                        "Savage Wind could not find GitHub, where the updates are. Check that this device is connected "
                        "to the internet and try again. You can keep playing the version you have.");
        case 5:
            return fail(p, "proxy", "The proxy settings don't work",
                        "curl could not get out through the configured proxy. Check your proxy settings and try again.");
        case 7:
        case 52:
        case 55:
        case 56:
            return fail(p, "cannot_connect", "Can't connect to GitHub",
                        "The connection to GitHub failed or was cut. Your internet may be down, or a firewall or VPN may "
                        "be blocking it. Check them and try again. You can keep playing the version you have.");
        case -1:
        case 28:
            return fail(p, "timeout", "GitHub took too long to answer",
                        "The connection is very slow or GitHub is having problems. Try again in a moment. Whatever was "
                        "already downloaded is kept.");
        case 35:
        case 51:
        case 58:
        case 60:
        case 77:
        case 80:
            return fail(p, "tls", "The connection to GitHub isn't secure",
                        "GitHub's security certificate could not be verified, so nothing was downloaded. The usual cause "
                        "is a wrong date or time on this device: check it. (curl error %d)", rc);
        case 23:
            return fail(p, "disk_full", "The download could not be written",
                        "There may be no space left on the disk that holds the AppImage. Free some space and try again.");
        default:
            return fail(p, "network", "The connection failed",
                        "Something went wrong talking to GitHub (curl error %d). Check your connection and try again.", rc);
    }
}

static long header_number(const char *path, const char *name) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return -1;
    char line[512];
    long v = -1;
    size_t l = strlen(name);
    while (fgets(line, sizeof line, f))
        if (!strncasecmp(line, name, l) && line[l] == ':') v = strtol(line + l + 1, NULL, 10);
    fclose(f);
    return v;
}

static bool http_problem(long code, const char *headers, UpdateProblem *p) {
    if (code == 403 || code == 429) {
        long left = header_number(headers, "x-ratelimit-remaining"), reset = header_number(headers, "x-ratelimit-reset");
        if (left == 0 || code == 429) {
            long mins = reset > 0 ? (reset - (long)time(NULL)) / 60 + 1 : 60;
            if (mins < 1) mins = 1;
            return fail(p, "rate_limited", "GitHub asked to wait",
                        "This internet connection has made too many requests to GitHub for now. This resets by itself in "
                        "about %ld minute(s): try again then. You can keep playing the version you have.", mins);
        }
        return fail(p, "forbidden", "GitHub refused the request",
                    "GitHub did not allow this request (HTTP %ld). A VPN or a shared network can cause it. Try again later.", code);
    }
    if (code == 404)
        return fail(p, "not_found", "The update isn't on GitHub",
                    "The release or its download could not be found (HTTP 404). It may have just been replaced. Try again later.");
    if (code >= 500)
        return fail(p, "github_down", "GitHub is having problems",
                    "GitHub answered with an error of its own (HTTP %ld). Nothing is wrong on your side: try again in a few minutes.", code);
    return fail(p, "bad_response", "GitHub sent an unexpected answer", "Savage Wind received HTTP %ld. Try again later.", code);
}

static char *read_text(const char *path, size_t max, size_t *out_n) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return NULL;
    char *b = (char *)malloc(max + 1);
    size_t n = b ? fread(b, 1, max, f) : 0;
    fclose(f);
    if (!b) return NULL;
    b[n] = 0;
    if (out_n) *out_n = n;
    return b;
}

static const char *feed_url(void) {
#ifdef SW_UPDATE_TEST
    if (getenv("SW_UPDATE_TEST_FEED")) return getenv("SW_UPDATE_TEST_FEED");
#endif
    return FEED_URL;
}

bool appimage_find_update(const char *work, const char *current, UcRelease *out, bool *available, UpdateProblem *p) {
    *available = false;
    char body[1100], headers[1100], code_f[1100];
    snprintf(body, sizeof body, "%s/update-feed.json", work);
    snprintf(headers, sizeof headers, "%s/update-feed.headers", work);
    snprintf(code_f, sizeof code_f, "%s/update-feed.code", work);
    char *const argv[] = {"curl", "-sS", "-L", "--connect-timeout", "15", "--max-time", "45", "-A", "SavageWind-SWUpdate",
                          "-H", "Accept: application/vnd.github+json", "-D", headers, "-o", body, "-w", "%{http_code}",
                          (char *)feed_url(), NULL};
    int rc = run(argv, code_f, 60, true, NULL, 0, 0, NULL, 0, 0);
    bool ok = false;
    if (rc) curl_problem(rc, p);
    else {
        char *c = read_text(code_f, 16, NULL);
        long code = c ? strtol(c, NULL, 10) : 0;
        free(c);
        if (code != 200) http_problem(code, headers, p);
        else {
            char *json = read_text(body, 8u << 20, NULL);
            int unsig = 0;
            UcPick pick = json ? uc_pick_release(json, current, ASSET_SUFFIX, out, &unsig) : UC_PICK_BAD_JSON;
            free(json);
            if (unsig) fprintf(stderr, "[update] %d newer release(s) have no signature: passed over\n", unsig);
            if (pick == UC_PICK_BAD_JSON)
                fail(p, "bad_response", "GitHub sent an unexpected answer",
                     "The list of releases could not be read. A captive portal (hotel or airport Wi-Fi) can cause this. Try again later.");
            else {
                ok = true;
                *available = pick == UC_PICK_UPDATE;
#ifndef SW_UPDATE_TEST
                if (*available && (strncmp(out->zip_url, DOWNLOAD_PREFIX, sizeof DOWNLOAD_PREFIX - 1) ||
                                   strncmp(out->sig_url, DOWNLOAD_PREFIX, sizeof DOWNLOAD_PREFIX - 1))) {
                    *available = false;
                    ok = fail(p, "bad_response", "GitHub sent an unexpected answer",
                              "The download address is not where Savage Wind's releases are. Nothing was downloaded.");
                }
#endif
            }
        }
    }
    remove(body), remove(headers), remove(code_f);
    return ok;
}

static void hex32(const uint8_t b[32], char out[65]) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) sprintf(out + 2 * i, "%02x", b[i]);
    out[64] = 0;
}

static bool signature_ok(const uint8_t hash[32], const uint8_t sig[64]) {
#ifdef SW_UPDATE_TEST_PUBKEY
    uint8_t key[64];
    return uc_hex_decode(SW_UPDATE_TEST_PUBKEY, key, 64) && uc_p256_verify(hash, sig, key);
#else
    return uc_p256_verify(hash, sig, SW_UPDATE_PUBKEY);
#endif
}

static uint64_t file_size(const char *p) {
    struct stat s;
    return stat(p, &s) == 0 ? (uint64_t)s.st_size : 0;
}

static bool folder_of(const char *file, char *out, size_t n) {
    snprintf(out, n, "%s", file);
    char *s = strrchr(out, '/');
    if (!s) return false;
    if (s == out) s[1] = 0;
    else *s = 0;
    return true;
}

// The new file complete at part. false: p says why (what was downloaded stays, unless it's bad).
static bool download(const UcRelease *r, const char *part, volatile float *progress, UpdateProblem *p) {
    for (int attempt = 1;; attempt++) {
        uint64_t have = file_size(part);
        if (have > r->zip_size) remove(part), have = 0;
        if (have == r->zip_size) return true;
        char *const argv[] = {"curl", "-sS", "-L", "--fail", "-C", "-", "--connect-timeout", "15", "--speed-limit", "1024",
                              "--speed-time", "45", "-A", "SavageWind-SWUpdate", "-o", (char *)part, (char *)r->zip_url, NULL};
        int rc = run(argv, NULL, 0, true, part, 0, r->zip_size, progress, 0.0f, 0.8f);
        if (!rc && file_size(part) == r->zip_size) return true;
        if (rc == 33) {  // (the server can't continue from there: from the start)
            remove(part);
            continue;
        }
        if (rc == 22) return http_problem(404, "/nonexistent", p);
        bool passing = !rc || rc == 7 || rc == 18 || rc == 28 || rc == 52 || rc == 55 || rc == 56 || rc == -1;
        if (!passing) return curl_problem(rc, p);
        fprintf(stderr, "[update] download attempt %d stopped (curl %d)\n", attempt, rc);
        if (attempt >= 4)
            return fail(p, "download_interrupted", "The download keeps getting cut off",
                        "The connection dropped several times before the download finished. What was downloaded is kept: "
                        "try again to continue from there.");
        sleep(2);
    }
}

bool appimage_install(const char *work, const UcRelease *r, volatile float *progress, UpdateProblem *p) {
    const char *self = appimage_path();
    if (!self) return fail(p, "not_appimage", "This copy can't update itself", "Only the AppImage releases can update themselves.");
    char dir[1100], part[1200], sigf[1300], old[1200];
    if (!folder_of(self, dir, sizeof dir))
        return fail(p, "wrong_folder", "The AppImage's location isn't known", "Get the new AppImage from the project's GitHub releases page.");
    snprintf(part, sizeof part, "%s.part", self);
    snprintf(sigf, sizeof sigf, "%s/update.sig", work);
    snprintf(old, sizeof old, "%s.old", self);
    if (access(dir, W_OK))
        return fail(p, "read_only", "Savage Wind can't write in this folder",
                    "The system does not allow writing in:\n%s\n\nMove the AppImage somewhere in your home folder and try again.", dir);
    struct statvfs vfs;
    if (statvfs(dir, &vfs) == 0) {
        unsigned long long have = (unsigned long long)vfs.f_bavail * vfs.f_frsize, need = r->zip_size * 2 + (1ull << 28);
#ifdef SW_UPDATE_TEST
        if (getenv("SW_UPDATE_TEST_FREE_MB")) have = strtoull(getenv("SW_UPDATE_TEST_FREE_MB"), NULL, 10) << 20;
#endif
        if (have < need)
            return fail(p, "disk_full", "Not enough free disk space",
                        "The update needs about %.1f GB free on this disk and there are %.1f GB. Nothing was changed. Free some space and try again.",
                        need / 1073741824.0, have / 1073741824.0);
    }
    bool from_earlier = file_size(part) > 0;
    uint8_t hash[32];
    char hex[65];
    for (;;) {
        *progress = 0;
        if (!download(r, part, progress, p)) return false;
        *progress = 0.8f;
        if (!uc_sha256_file(part, hash)) {
            remove(part);
            return fail(p, "file_error", "The download could not be read", "The downloaded file disappeared or can't be opened. Try again.");
        }
        hex32(hash, hex);
        bool bad = file_size(part) != r->zip_size || (r->digest[0] && strcmp(hex, r->digest));
        if (!bad) break;
        remove(part);
        if (!from_earlier)
            return fail(p, "corrupt_download", "The download arrived damaged",
                        "The file does not match what GitHub says it should be, so it was deleted and nothing was installed. Try again to download it again.");
        fprintf(stderr, "[update] what was kept from an earlier download doesn't match the release: downloading it again\n");
        from_earlier = false;
    }
    *progress = 0.85f;
    char *const sig_argv[] = {"curl", "-sS", "-L", "--fail", "--connect-timeout", "15", "--max-time", "45", "-A", "SavageWind-SWUpdate",
                              "-o", sigf, (char *)r->sig_url, NULL};
    int rc = run(sig_argv, NULL, 60, true, NULL, 0, 0, NULL, 0, 0);
    if (rc) {
        remove(sigf);
        return rc == 22 ? http_problem(404, "/nonexistent", p) : curl_problem(rc, p);
    }
    char *sig_hex = read_text(sigf, 4096, NULL);
    remove(sigf);
    uint8_t sig[64];
    bool sig_read = false;
    if (sig_hex) {
        sig_hex[strcspn(sig_hex, "\r\n ")] = 0;
        sig_read = uc_hex_decode(sig_hex, sig, 64);
    }
    free(sig_hex);
    if (!sig_read || !signature_ok(hash, sig)) {
        remove(part);
        return fail(p, "bad_signature", "This update did not pass the security check",
                    "The download is not signed by the Savage Wind team, so it was deleted and NOT installed. Do not look for "
                    "this file elsewhere. Please report this on the project's GitHub page.");
    }
    fprintf(stderr, "[update] signature ok, sha256 %s\n", hex);

    *progress = 0.9f;
    if (chmod(part, 0755)) {
        remove(part);
        return fail(p, "file_error", "The new version could not be made runnable", "Reason: %s.", strerror(errno));
    }
    char *const health[] = {part, "--update-health", NULL};
    rc = run(health, NULL, 90, false, NULL, 0, 0, NULL, 0, 0);
    fprintf(stderr, "[update] health check: exit %d\n", rc);
#ifdef SW_UPDATE_TEST
    if (getenv("SW_UPDATE_TEST_SKIP_HEALTH")) rc = HEALTH_EXIT;
#endif
    if (rc != HEALTH_EXIT) {
        remove(part);
        return fail(p, "health_failed", "The new version did not start correctly",
                    "The new AppImage stopped with code %d, so it was not installed and your version was left as it was. If "
                    "this folder is on a drive mounted noexec, move the AppImage to your home folder. Otherwise please report this "
                    "on the project's GitHub page.", rc);
    }
    remove(old);
    if (link(self, old) == 0) {  // (the new file in place in one step: there is never a moment without an AppImage)
        if (rename(part, self)) {
            int e = errno;
            remove(old);
            remove(part);
            return fail(p, "file_error", "The AppImage could not be replaced", "Reason: %s. Your version was left as it was.", strerror(e));
        }
    } else {  // (a file system without hard links)
        if (rename(self, old)) {
            int e = errno;
            remove(part);
            return fail(p, "file_error", "The AppImage could not be replaced", "Reason: %s. Your version was left as it was.", strerror(e));
        }
        if (rename(part, self)) {
            int e = errno;
            rename(old, self);
            remove(part);
            return fail(p, "file_error", "The AppImage could not be replaced", "Reason: %s. Your version was left as it was.", strerror(e));
        }
    }
    *progress = 1;
    fprintf(stderr, "[update] installed %s\n", r->version);
    return true;
}

bool appimage_has_old(void) {
    const char *self = appimage_path();
    char old[1200];
    if (!self) return false;
    snprintf(old, sizeof old, "%s.old", self);
    return access(old, F_OK) == 0;
}

void appimage_remove_old(void) {
    const char *self = appimage_path();
    char old[1200];
    if (!self) return;
    snprintf(old, sizeof old, "%s.old", self);
    remove(old);
}

bool appimage_go_back(UpdateProblem *p) {
    const char *self = appimage_path();
    char old[1200];
    if (!self) return fail(p, "not_appimage", "This copy can't update itself", "Only the AppImage releases can update themselves.");
    snprintf(old, sizeof old, "%s.old", self);
    if (access(old, F_OK))
        return fail(p, "no_backup", "There is no earlier version to go back to",
                    "The previous version is only kept until an update finishes setting up.");
    if (rename(old, self)) return fail(p, "file_error", "The previous version could not be put back", "Reason: %s.", strerror(errno));
    return true;
}

void appimage_relaunch(UpdateProblem *p) {
    const char *self = appimage_path();
    if (!self) {
        fail(p, "not_appimage", "This copy can't update itself", "Only the AppImage releases can update themselves.");
        return;
    }
    char path[1100];
    snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s", self);
    char **env = child_env(false);
    char *const argv[] = {path, "--config", NULL};
    fprintf(stderr, "[update] starting the new version\n");
    fflush(NULL);
    if (env) execve(path, argv, env);
    int e = errno;
    free(env);
    fail(p, "relaunch", "The new version is installed but could not be started",
         "Reason: %s. Close this window and start Savage Wind again.", strerror(e));
}
#endif
```

`runtime/update_appimage.h`:

```h
// Updating a Linux AppImage (runtime/update_appimage.c): the new file replaces the old one in place, under the same
// name, so shortcuts and Steam entries keep working. Linux allows that while the program runs, so no separate updater
// is needed. Downloads with the system's curl, and checks the file against a signature before anything changes.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include "update_core.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef struct {
    char code[32];    // stable, for tests
    char title[200];  // what happened
    char what[900];   // what it means and what to do
} UpdateProblem;

// The running AppImage's file, NULL when not running from one
const char *appimage_path(void);
// work: a writable folder for temporary files. true: *available says if out holds a newer release.
bool appimage_find_update(const char *work, const char *current, UcRelease *out, bool *available, UpdateProblem *p);
// Downloads, checks, starts the new file once to see that it runs, and replaces the old one, kept as <file>.old until
// the new version has finished setting up. *progress goes 0..1 as it works.
bool appimage_install(const char *work, const UcRelease *r, volatile float *progress, UpdateProblem *p);
bool appimage_go_back(UpdateProblem *p);        // <file>.old back in place
bool appimage_has_old(void);
void appimage_remove_old(void);
// Replaces this process with the AppImage on disk, opening Savage Wind Configuration. Returns only if it couldn't.
void appimage_relaunch(UpdateProblem *p);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

`runtime/update_core.c`:

```c
// Plain logic of SW Update (runtime/update_core.h).
#include "update_core.h"
#include <ctype.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ versions
typedef struct { unsigned long n[3]; int pre_kind; unsigned long pre; } Ver;  // pre_kind: 0 alpha, 1 beta, 2 rc, 3 final

static bool ver_parse(const char *s, Ver *v) {
    if (!s) return false;
    if (*s == 'v' || *s == 'V') s++;
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        if (!isdigit((unsigned char)*s)) return false;
        char *e;
        v->n[i] = strtoul(s, &e, 10);
        s = e;
        if (i < 2) {
            if (*s != '.') return false;
            s++;
        }
    }
    v->pre_kind = 3, v->pre = 0;
    if (!*s) return true;
    if (*s != '-') return false;
    s++;
    static const char *const kinds[3] = {"alpha.", "beta.", "rc."};
    for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) {
        size_t l = strlen(kinds[k]);
        if (!strncmp(s, kinds[k], l)) {
            s += l;
            if (!isdigit((unsigned char)*s)) return false;
            char *e;
            v->pre = strtoul(s, &e, 10);
            v->pre_kind = k;
            return !*e;
        }
    }
    return false;
}

bool uc_version_valid(const char *v) {
    Ver t;
    return ver_parse(v, &t);
}

int uc_version_cmp(const char *a, const char *b) {
    Ver x, y;
    bool ox = ver_parse(a, &x), oy = ver_parse(b, &y);
    if (!ox || !oy) return ox - oy;  // (a version that can't be read is older than any that can)
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++)
        if (x.n[i] != y.n[i]) return x.n[i] < y.n[i] ? -1 : 1;
    if (x.pre_kind != y.pre_kind) return x.pre_kind < y.pre_kind ? -1 : 1;
    if (x.pre != y.pre) return x.pre < y.pre ? -1 : 1;
    return 0;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ JSON: just enough to read the list of releases
typedef struct { const char *p; bool bad; int depth; } J;

static void j_ws(J *j) {
    while (*j->p == ' ' || *j->p == '\t' || *j->p == '\n' || *j->p == '\r') j->p++;
}

// A string into out (cut to fit; out may be NULL). \uXXXX below 0x80 is kept, anything else becomes '?': no value read
// here (tags, names, URLs, digests) needs more.
static void j_string(J *j, char *out, size_t n) {
    size_t k = 0;
    j_ws(j);
    if (*j->p != '"') { j->bad = true; return; }
    j->p++;
    for (;;) {
        char c = *j->p;
        if (!c || (unsigned char)c < 0x20) { j->bad = true; return; }
        j->p++;
        if (c == '"') break;
        if (c == '\\') {
            char e = *j->p;
            if (!e) { j->bad = true; return; }
            j->p++;
            switch (e) {
                case 'n': c = '\n'; break;
                case 't': c = '\t'; break;
                case 'r': c = '\r'; break;
                case 'b': c = '\b'; break;
                case 'f': c = '\f'; break;
                case 'u': {
                    unsigned v = 0;
                    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
                        if (!isxdigit((unsigned char)j->p[i])) { j->bad = true; return; }
                        v = v * 16 + (unsigned)(isdigit((unsigned char)j->p[i]) ? j->p[i] - '0' : (tolower((unsigned char)j->p[i]) - 'a' + 10));
                    }
                    j->p += 4;
                    c = v < 0x80 ? (char)v : '?';
                    break;
                }
                default: c = e;
            }
        }
        if (out && k + 1 < n) out[k++] = c;
    }
    if (out && n) out[k] = 0;
}

static void j_skip(J *j);

static void j_skip_container(J *j, char close) {
    if (++j->depth > 64) { j->bad = true; return; }
    j->p++;
    j_ws(j);
    if (*j->p == close) { j->p++; j->depth--; return; }
    while (!j->bad) {
        if (close == '}') {
            j_string(j, NULL, 0);
            j_ws(j);
            if (*j->p != ':') { j->bad = true; return; }
            j->p++;
        }
        j_skip(j);
        j_ws(j);
        if (*j->p == ',') { j->p++; continue; }
        if (*j->p == close) { j->p++; j->depth--; return; }
        j->bad = true;
    }
}

static void j_skip(J *j) {
    j_ws(j);
    char c = *j->p;
    if (c == '"') j_string(j, NULL, 0);
    else if (c == '{') j_skip_container(j, '}');
    else if (c == '[') j_skip_container(j, ']');
    else if (c == 't' && !strncmp(j->p, "true", 4)) j->p += 4;
    else if (c == 'f' && !strncmp(j->p, "false", 5)) j->p += 5;
    else if (c == 'n' && !strncmp(j->p, "null", 4)) j->p += 4;
    else if (c == '-' || isdigit((unsigned char)c)) {
        j->p++;
        while (*j->p && strchr("0123456789.eE+-", *j->p)) j->p++;
    } else j->bad = true;
}

static bool ends_with(const char *s, const char *suffix) {
    size_t a = strlen(s), b = strlen(suffix);
    return a >= b && !strcmp(s + a - b, suffix);
}

static void j_string_or_skip(J *j, char *out, size_t n) {
    j_ws(j);
    if (*j->p == '"') j_string(j, out, n);
    else j_skip(j);
}

// One entry of "assets": this platform's file and its signature go into r
static void read_asset(J *j, UcRelease *r, const char *suffix) {
    char name[256] = "", url[1024] = "", digest[80] = "";
    uint64_t size = 0;
    j_ws(j);
    if (*j->p != '{') { j_skip(j); return; }
    j->p++;
    j_ws(j);
    if (*j->p == '}') { j->p++; return; }
    while (!j->bad) {
        char key[40];
        j_string(j, key, sizeof key);
        j_ws(j);
        if (*j->p != ':') { j->bad = true; return; }
        j->p++;
        if (!strcmp(key, "name")) j_string_or_skip(j, name, sizeof name);
        else if (!strcmp(key, "browser_download_url")) j_string_or_skip(j, url, sizeof url);
        else if (!strcmp(key, "digest")) j_string_or_skip(j, digest, sizeof digest);
        else if (!strcmp(key, "size")) {
            j_ws(j);
            size = strtoull(j->p, NULL, 10);
            j_skip(j);
        } else j_skip(j);
        j_ws(j);
        if (*j->p == ',') { j->p++; continue; }
        if (*j->p == '}') { j->p++; break; }
        j->bad = true;
    }
    char sig_suffix[64];
    snprintf(sig_suffix, sizeof sig_suffix, "%s.sig", suffix);
    if (ends_with(name, suffix)) {
        snprintf(r->zip_name, sizeof r->zip_name, "%s", name);
        snprintf(r->zip_url, sizeof r->zip_url, "%s", url);
        r->zip_size = size;
        r->digest[0] = 0;
        if (!strncmp(digest, "sha256:", 7) && strlen(digest) == 71) snprintf(r->digest, sizeof r->digest, "%s", digest + 7);
    } else if (ends_with(name, sig_suffix))
        snprintf(r->sig_url, sizeof r->sig_url, "%s", url);
}

static void read_release(J *j, UcRelease *r, bool *draft, const char *suffix) {
    memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
    *draft = false;
    j_ws(j);
    if (*j->p != '{') { j->bad = true; return; }
    j->p++;
    j_ws(j);
    if (*j->p == '}') { j->p++; return; }
    while (!j->bad) {
        char key[40];
        j_string(j, key, sizeof key);
        j_ws(j);
        if (*j->p != ':') { j->bad = true; return; }
        j->p++;
        j_ws(j);
        if (!strcmp(key, "tag_name")) j_string_or_skip(j, r->tag, sizeof r->tag);
        else if (!strcmp(key, "html_url")) j_string_or_skip(j, r->page_url, sizeof r->page_url);
        else if (!strcmp(key, "draft")) {
            *draft = !strncmp(j->p, "true", 4);
            j_skip(j);
        } else if (!strcmp(key, "assets") && *j->p == '[') {
            j->p++;
            j_ws(j);
            if (*j->p == ']') j->p++;
            else
                while (!j->bad) {
                    read_asset(j, r, suffix);
                    j_ws(j);
                    if (*j->p == ',') { j->p++; continue; }
                    if (*j->p == ']') { j->p++; break; }
                    j->bad = true;
                }
        } else j_skip(j);
        j_ws(j);
        if (*j->p == ',') { j->p++; continue; }
        if (*j->p == '}') { j->p++; break; }
        j->bad = true;
    }
}

UcPick uc_pick_release(const char *json, const char *current, const char *suffix, UcRelease *out, int *skipped_unsigned) {
    J j = {json, false, 0};
    j_ws(&j);
    if (*j.p != '[') return UC_PICK_BAD_JSON;
    j.p++;
    j_ws(&j);
    bool found = false;
    int unsigned_newer = 0;
    if (*j.p == ']') j.p++;
    else
        for (;;) {
            UcRelease r;
            bool draft;
            read_release(&j, &r, &draft, suffix);
            if (j.bad) return UC_PICK_BAD_JSON;
            if (!draft && uc_version_valid(r.tag) && uc_version_cmp(r.tag, current) > 0) {
                const char *v = r.tag[0] == 'v' || r.tag[0] == 'V' ? r.tag + 1 : r.tag;
                if (!r.zip_url[0] || !r.zip_size) {
                    // (no Windows zip in this one: another platform's release, nothing to say)
                } else if (!r.sig_url[0]) unsigned_newer++;
                else if (!found || uc_version_cmp(v, out->version) > 0) {
                    *out = r;
                    snprintf(out->version, sizeof out->version, "%s", v);
                    found = true;
                }
            }
            j_ws(&j);
            if (*j.p == ',') { j.p++; continue; }
            if (*j.p == ']') { j.p++; break; }
            return UC_PICK_BAD_JSON;
        }
    if (skipped_unsigned) *skipped_unsigned = unsigned_newer;
    return found ? UC_PICK_UPDATE : UC_PICK_CURRENT;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ paths and the manifest
bool uc_path_safe(const char *path) {
    if (!path || !*path || strlen(path) > 400) return false;
    const char *s = path;
    for (;;) {
        const char *e = s + strcspn(s, "/");
        size_t l = (size_t)(e - s);
        if (!l || (l == 1 && s[0] == '.') || (l == 2 && s[0] == '.' && s[1] == '.')) return false;
        if (s[l - 1] == '.' || s[l - 1] == ' ') return false;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < l; i++) {
            unsigned char c = (unsigned char)s[i];
            if (c < 0x20 || strchr("\\:*?\"<>|", c)) return false;
        }
        // (the name before its first dot: "nul.txt" is the NUL device too)
        size_t stem = strcspn(s, "./");
        char up[6] = "";
        if (stem <= 4) {
            for (size_t i = 0; i < stem; i++) up[i] = (char)toupper((unsigned char)s[i]);
            up[stem] = 0;
            static const char *const reserved[] = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL"};
            for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof reserved / sizeof *reserved; i++)
                if (!strcmp(up, reserved[i])) return false;
            if (stem == 4 && (!strncmp(up, "COM", 3) || !strncmp(up, "LPT", 3)) && up[3] >= '0' && up[3] <= '9') return false;
        }
        if (!*e) return true;
        s = e + 1;
    }
}

const char *uc_strip_top(const char *zip_path) {
    static const char top[] = "Savage Wind/";
    size_t l = sizeof top - 1;
    return !strncmp(zip_path, top, l) && zip_path[l] ? zip_path + l : NULL;
}

bool uc_hex_decode(const char *hex, uint8_t *out, size_t n) {
    if (strlen(hex) != n * 2) return false;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * 2; i++) {
        if (!isxdigit((unsigned char)hex[i])) return false;
        int c = tolower((unsigned char)hex[i]), v = isdigit(c) ? c - '0' : c - 'a' + 10;
        if (i & 1) out[i / 2] |= (uint8_t)v;
        else out[i / 2] = (uint8_t)(v << 4);
    }
    return true;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ launchers
// The launchers that install recomps from their GitHub releases and update them, and the sign each leaves (read from
// their sources, 2026-11):
//   Quiver Launcher (tgeorgiadis/quiver-launcher)   .quiver-version in the game's folder (install.rs VERSION_FILE)
//   GitHub Launcher (SirDiabo/N64RecompLauncher)    version.txt in the game's folder, with LastPlayed.txt or
//                                                   selected_executable.txt; Quiver's older versions wrote it too
//   RecompLauncher (elripalda/RecompLauncher)      RECOMPLAUNCHER=1 in every game it starts; its library is
//                                                   "Recomp Library" (C:\Recomp Library, ~/Games/Recomp Library)
// The folder above counts too, for a launcher that kept the zip's "Savage Wind/" - but a lone version.txt there doesn't:
// that is too common a name.
const char *uc_launcher_installed(const char *dir, const char *up, bool (*has)(const char *dir, const char *name),
                                  const char *recomplauncher) {
    if (recomplauncher && *recomplauncher && strcmp(recomplauncher, "0")) return "RecompLauncher";
    bool above = up && *up;
    if (has(dir, ".quiver-version") || (above && has(up, ".quiver-version"))) return "Quiver Launcher";
    if (has(dir, "version.txt") ||
        (above && has(up, "version.txt") && (has(up, "LastPlayed.txt") || has(up, "selected_executable.txt"))))
        return "GitHub Launcher";
    char low[1100];
    snprintf(low, sizeof low, "/%s/", dir);
    for (char *c = low; *c; c++) *c = *c == '\\' ? '/' : (char)tolower((unsigned char)*c);
    return strstr(low, "/recomp library/") ? "RecompLauncher" : NULL;
}

bool uc_path_inside(const char *exe, const char *appdir) {
    size_t n = strlen(appdir);
    while (n > 1 && appdir[n - 1] == '/') n--;  // ("/tmp/.mount_x/" and "/tmp/.mount_x" are the same folder)
    return n && !strncmp(exe, appdir, n) && exe[n] == '/';
}

void uc_manifest_free(UcManifest *m) {
    for (int i = 0; i < m->count; i++) free(m->files[i].path);
    free(m->files);
    m->files = NULL;
    m->count = 0;
}

bool uc_manifest_parse(const char *text, UcManifest *out, char *why, size_t why_size) {
    memset(out, 0, sizeof *out);
    int cap = 0, line_no = 0;
    bool header = false;
    for (const char *s = text; *s;) {
        const char *e = s + strcspn(s, "\n");
        size_t l = (size_t)(e - s);
        if (l && s[l - 1] == '\r') l--;
        line_no++;
        char line[1024];
        if (l >= sizeof line) { snprintf(why, why_size, "line %d is too long", line_no); goto bad; }
        memcpy(line, s, l);
        line[l] = 0;
        s = *e ? e + 1 : e;
        if (!l) continue;
        if (!header) {
            if (strcmp(line, "savagewind-update-manifest 1")) { snprintf(why, why_size, "not a file list of a known format"); goto bad; }
            header = true;
        } else if (!strncmp(line, "version ", 8)) {
            snprintf(out->version, sizeof out->version, "%s", line + 8);
        } else if (!strncmp(line, "f ", 2)) {
            char *hash = line + 2, *size_s = strchr(hash, ' ');
            if (!size_s) { snprintf(why, why_size, "line %d has no size", line_no); goto bad; }
            *size_s++ = 0;
            char *path = strchr(size_s, ' ');
            if (!path) { snprintf(why, why_size, "line %d has no path", line_no); goto bad; }
            *path++ = 0;
            uint8_t raw[32];
            char *end;
            uint64_t size = strtoull(size_s, &end, 10);
            if (!uc_hex_decode(hash, raw, 32) || *end || !isdigit((unsigned char)*size_s)) {
                snprintf(why, why_size, "line %d is malformed", line_no);
                goto bad;
            }
            if (!uc_path_safe(path)) { snprintf(why, why_size, "line %d names an unsafe path", line_no); goto bad; }
            if (uc_manifest_find(out, path)) { snprintf(why, why_size, "line %d repeats a file", line_no); goto bad; }
            if (out->count == cap) {
                cap = cap ? cap * 2 : 256;
                UcFile *nf = (UcFile *)realloc(out->files, (size_t)cap * sizeof *nf);
                if (!nf) { snprintf(why, why_size, "out of memory"); goto bad; }
                out->files = nf;
            }
            UcFile *f = &out->files[out->count];
            for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) f->sha256[i] = (char)tolower((unsigned char)hash[i]);
            f->sha256[64] = 0;
            f->size = size;
            f->path = strdup(path);
            if (!f->path) { snprintf(why, why_size, "out of memory"); goto bad; }
            out->count++;
        } else { snprintf(why, why_size, "line %d is not understood", line_no); goto bad; }
    }
    if (!header) { snprintf(why, why_size, "it is empty"); goto bad; }
    if (!uc_version_valid(out->version)) { snprintf(why, why_size, "it has no valid version"); goto bad; }
    if (!out->count) { snprintf(why, why_size, "it lists no files"); goto bad; }
    return true;
bad:
    uc_manifest_free(out);
    return false;
}

const UcFile *uc_manifest_find(const UcManifest *m, const char *path) {
    for (int i = 0; i < m->count; i++) {
        const char *a = m->files[i].path, *b = path;
        while (*a && tolower((unsigned char)*a) == tolower((unsigned char)*b)) a++, b++;
        if (!*a && !*b) return &m->files[i];
    }
    return NULL;
}
```

```h
// The parts of SW Update that are plain logic (runtime/update_core.c; tools/test_update_core.c tests them on any OS):
// release versions, choosing a release from GitHub's list, the release's file list (sw-manifest.txt), safe paths.

bool uc_version_valid(const char *v);
// <0, 0, >0 as a is older than, the same as or newer than b. A final version is newer than its own pre-releases.
```

`runtime/update_crypto.c`:

```c
// SHA-256 and ECDSA P-256 verification (runtime/update_crypto.h).
#include "update_crypto.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ SHA-256
static const uint32_t K[64] = {
    0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf, 0xe9b5dba5, 0x3956c25b, 0x59f111f1, 0x923f82a4, 0xab1c5ed5,
    0xd807aa98, 0x12835b01, 0x243185be, 0x550c7dc3, 0x72be5d74, 0x80deb1fe, 0x9bdc06a7, 0xc19bf174,
    0xe49b69c1, 0xefbe4786, 0x0fc19dc6, 0x240ca1cc, 0x2de92c6f, 0x4a7484aa, 0x5cb0a9dc, 0x76f988da,
    0x983e5152, 0xa831c66d, 0xb00327c8, 0xbf597fc7, 0xc6e00bf3, 0xd5a79147, 0x06ca6351, 0x14292967,
    0x27b70a85, 0x2e1b2138, 0x4d2c6dfc, 0x53380d13, 0x650a7354, 0x766a0abb, 0x81c2c92e, 0x92722c85,
    0xa2bfe8a1, 0xa81a664b, 0xc24b8b70, 0xc76c51a3, 0xd192e819, 0xd6990624, 0xf40e3585, 0x106aa070,
    0x19a4c116, 0x1e376c08, 0x2748774c, 0x34b0bcb5, 0x391c0cb3, 0x4ed8aa4a, 0x5b9cca4f, 0x682e6ff3,
    0x748f82ee, 0x78a5636f, 0x84c87814, 0x8cc70208, 0x90befffa, 0xa4506ceb, 0xbef9a3f7, 0xc67178f2,
};

#define ROR(x, n) (((x) >> (n)) | ((x) << (32 - (n))))

static void sha_block(uint32_t h[8], const uint8_t *p) {
    uint32_t w[64];
    for (int i = 0; i < 16; i++)
        w[i] = (uint32_t)p[i * 4] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[i * 4 + 1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[i * 4 + 2] << 8 | p[i * 4 + 3];
    for (int i = 16; i < 64; i++) {
        uint32_t s0 = ROR(w[i - 15], 7) ^ ROR(w[i - 15], 18) ^ (w[i - 15] >> 3);
        uint32_t s1 = ROR(w[i - 2], 17) ^ ROR(w[i - 2], 19) ^ (w[i - 2] >> 10);
        w[i] = w[i - 16] + s0 + w[i - 7] + s1;
    }
    uint32_t a = h[0], b = h[1], c = h[2], d = h[3], e = h[4], f = h[5], g = h[6], k = h[7];
    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
        uint32_t t1 = k + (ROR(e, 6) ^ ROR(e, 11) ^ ROR(e, 25)) + ((e & f) ^ (~e & g)) + K[i] + w[i];
        uint32_t t2 = (ROR(a, 2) ^ ROR(a, 13) ^ ROR(a, 22)) + ((a & b) ^ (a & c) ^ (b & c));
        k = g, g = f, f = e, e = d + t1, d = c, c = b, b = a, a = t1 + t2;
    }
    h[0] += a, h[1] += b, h[2] += c, h[3] += d, h[4] += e, h[5] += f, h[6] += g, h[7] += k;
}

void uc_sha256_init(UcSha256 *c) {
    static const uint32_t iv[8] = {0x6a09e667, 0xbb67ae85, 0x3c6ef372, 0xa54ff53a, 0x510e527f, 0x9b05688c, 0x1f83d9ab, 0x5be0cd19};
    memcpy(c->h, iv, sizeof iv);
    c->total = 0;
    c->used = 0;
}

void uc_sha256_update(UcSha256 *c, const void *data, size_t n) {
    const uint8_t *p = (const uint8_t *)data;
    c->total += n;
    while (n) {
        if (!c->used && n >= 64) {
            sha_block(c->h, p);
            p += 64, n -= 64;
            continue;
        }
        size_t k = 64 - c->used < n ? 64 - c->used : n;
        memcpy(c->buf + c->used, p, k);
        c->used += k, p += k, n -= k;
        if (c->used == 64) {
            sha_block(c->h, c->buf);
            c->used = 0;
        }
    }
}

void uc_sha256_final(UcSha256 *c, uint8_t out[32]) {
    uint64_t bits = c->total * 8;
    static const uint8_t one = 0x80, zero = 0;
    uc_sha256_update(c, &one, 1);
    while (c->used != 56) uc_sha256_update(c, &zero, 1);
    uint8_t len[8];
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) len[i] = (uint8_t)(bits >> (56 - i * 8));
    uc_sha256_update(c, len, 8);
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) out[i] = (uint8_t)(c->h[i / 4] >> (24 - (i % 4) * 8));
}

bool uc_sha256_file(const char *path, uint8_t out[32]) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return false;
    static __thread uint8_t buf[1 << 16];
    UcSha256 c;
    uc_sha256_init(&c);
    size_t n;
    while ((n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, f)) > 0) uc_sha256_update(&c, buf, n);
    bool ok = !ferror(f);
    fclose(f);
    if (ok) uc_sha256_final(&c, out);
    return ok;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ P-256
// Plain and slow on purpose: a modular product is 256 doublings and additions. A verification takes well under a second
// and happens once per update, and this is far easier to get right than a fast reduction.
typedef struct { uint32_t v[8]; } U;  // little-endian limbs

static const U P = {{0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF}};
static const U N = {{0xFC632551, 0xF3B9CAC2, 0xA7179E84, 0xBCE6FAAD, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF}};
static const U B = {{0x27D2604B, 0x3BCE3C3E, 0xCC53B0F6, 0x651D06B0, 0x769886BC, 0xB3EBBD55, 0xAA3A93E7, 0x5AC635D8}};
static const U GX = {{0xD898C296, 0xF4A13945, 0x2DEB33A0, 0x77037D81, 0x63A440F2, 0xF8BCE6E5, 0xE12C4247, 0x6B17D1F2}};
static const U GY = {{0x37BF51F5, 0xCBB64068, 0x6B315ECE, 0x2BCE3357, 0x7C0F9E16, 0x8EE7EB4A, 0xFE1A7F9B, 0x4FE342E2}};
static const U ONE = {{1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}};

static int u_cmp(const U *a, const U *b) {
    for (int i = 7; i >= 0; i--)
        if (a->v[i] != b->v[i]) return a->v[i] < b->v[i] ? -1 : 1;
    return 0;
}
static bool u_zero(const U *a) {
    uint32_t o = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) o |= a->v[i];
    return !o;
}
static uint32_t u_add(U *r, const U *a, const U *b) {
    uint64_t c = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        c += (uint64_t)a->v[i] + b->v[i];
        r->v[i] = (uint32_t)c;
        c >>= 32;
    }
    return (uint32_t)c;
}
static uint32_t u_sub(U *r, const U *a, const U *b) {
    int64_t c = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        c += (int64_t)a->v[i] - b->v[i];
        r->v[i] = (uint32_t)c;
        c >>= 32;
    }
    return (uint32_t)(c & 1);
}
static void add_mod(U *r, const U *a, const U *b, const U *m) {
    U t;
    uint32_t carry = u_add(&t, a, b);
    if (carry || u_cmp(&t, m) >= 0) u_sub(&t, &t, m);
    *r = t;
}
static void sub_mod(U *r, const U *a, const U *b, const U *m) {
    U t;
    if (u_sub(&t, a, b)) u_add(&t, &t, m);
    *r = t;
}
static void mul_mod(U *r, const U *a, const U *b, const U *m) {
    U t = {{0}};
    for (int i = 255; i >= 0; i--) {
        add_mod(&t, &t, &t, m);
        if (b->v[i / 32] >> (i % 32) & 1) add_mod(&t, &t, a, m);
    }
    *r = t;
}
static void inv_mod(U *r, const U *a, const U *m) {  // (m is prime: a^(m-2))
    U e, t = ONE, two = {{2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}};
    u_sub(&e, m, &two);
    for (int i = 255; i >= 0; i--) {
        mul_mod(&t, &t, &t, m);
        if (e.v[i / 32] >> (i % 32) & 1) mul_mod(&t, &t, a, m);
    }
    *r = t;
}

static void u_from_be(U *r, const uint8_t b[32]) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        const uint8_t *p = b + 28 - i * 4;
        r->v[i] = (uint32_t)p[0] << 24 | (uint32_t)p[1] << 16 | (uint32_t)p[2] << 8 | p[3];
    }
}

typedef struct { U x, y, z; } Pt;  // Jacobian; z == 0: the point at infinity

#define MUL(r, a, b) mul_mod(&(r), &(a), &(b), &P)
#define ADD(r, a, b) add_mod(&(r), &(a), &(b), &P)
#define SUB(r, a, b) sub_mod(&(r), &(a), &(b), &P)

static void pt_double(Pt *r, const Pt *a) {
    if (u_zero(&a->z) || u_zero(&a->y)) {
        memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        return;
    }
    U delta, gamma, beta, alpha, t1, t2, x3, y3, z3;
    MUL(delta, a->z, a->z);
    MUL(gamma, a->y, a->y);
    MUL(beta, a->x, gamma);
    SUB(t1, a->x, delta);
    ADD(t2, a->x, delta);
    MUL(alpha, t1, t2);
    ADD(t1, alpha, alpha);
    ADD(alpha, t1, alpha);  // 3 (x - delta)(x + delta), as a = -3
    MUL(x3, alpha, alpha);
    ADD(t1, beta, beta);
    ADD(t1, t1, t1);        // 4 beta
    ADD(t2, t1, t1);        // 8 beta
    SUB(x3, x3, t2);
    ADD(t2, a->y, a->z);
    MUL(z3, t2, t2);
    SUB(z3, z3, gamma);
    SUB(z3, z3, delta);
    SUB(t1, t1, x3);
    MUL(y3, alpha, t1);
    MUL(t2, gamma, gamma);
    ADD(t2, t2, t2);
    ADD(t2, t2, t2);
    ADD(t2, t2, t2);        // 8 gamma^2
    SUB(y3, y3, t2);
    r->x = x3, r->y = y3, r->z = z3;
}

static void pt_add(Pt *r, const Pt *a, const Pt *b) {
    if (u_zero(&a->z)) { *r = *b; return; }
    if (u_zero(&b->z)) { *r = *a; return; }
    U z1z1, z2z2, u1, u2, s1, s2, h, rr, hh, hhh, v, t, x3, y3, z3;
    MUL(z1z1, a->z, a->z);
    MUL(z2z2, b->z, b->z);
    MUL(u1, a->x, z2z2);
    MUL(u2, b->x, z1z1);
    MUL(t, b->z, z2z2);
    MUL(s1, a->y, t);
    MUL(t, a->z, z1z1);
    MUL(s2, b->y, t);
    SUB(h, u2, u1);
    SUB(rr, s2, s1);
    if (u_zero(&h)) {
        if (u_zero(&rr)) pt_double(r, a);
        else memset(r, 0, sizeof *r);
        return;
    }
    MUL(hh, h, h);
    MUL(hhh, h, hh);
    MUL(v, u1, hh);
    MUL(x3, rr, rr);
    SUB(x3, x3, hhh);
    SUB(x3, x3, v);
    SUB(x3, x3, v);
    SUB(t, v, x3);
    MUL(y3, rr, t);
    MUL(t, s1, hhh);
    SUB(y3, y3, t);
    MUL(t, a->z, b->z);
    MUL(z3, t, h);
    r->x = x3, r->y = y3, r->z = z3;
}

static void pt_mul(Pt *r, const Pt *a, const U *k) {
    Pt t;
    memset(&t, 0, sizeof t);
    for (int i = 255; i >= 0; i--) {
        pt_double(&t, &t);
        if (k->v[i / 32] >> (i % 32) & 1) pt_add(&t, &t, a);
    }
    *r = t;
}

static bool on_curve(const U *x, const U *y) {  // y^2 = x^3 - 3x + b
    U left, right, t;
    MUL(left, *y, *y);
    MUL(t, *x, *x);
    MUL(right, t, *x);
    ADD(t, *x, *x);
    ADD(t, t, *x);
    SUB(right, right, t);
    ADD(right, right, B);
    return !u_cmp(&left, &right);
}

bool uc_p256_verify(const uint8_t hash[32], const uint8_t sig[64], const uint8_t pub[64]) {
    U r, s, e, qx, qy;
    u_from_be(&r, sig);
    u_from_be(&s, sig + 32);
    u_from_be(&e, hash);
    u_from_be(&qx, pub);
    u_from_be(&qy, pub + 32);
    if (u_zero(&r) || u_zero(&s) || u_cmp(&r, &N) >= 0 || u_cmp(&s, &N) >= 0) return false;
    if (u_cmp(&qx, &P) >= 0 || u_cmp(&qy, &P) >= 0 || !on_curve(&qx, &qy)) return false;
    if (u_cmp(&e, &N) >= 0) u_sub(&e, &e, &N);
    U w, u1, u2;
    inv_mod(&w, &s, &N);
    mul_mod(&u1, &e, &w, &N);
    mul_mod(&u2, &r, &w, &N);
    Pt g = {GX, GY, ONE}, q = {qx, qy, ONE}, a, b, sum;
    pt_mul(&a, &g, &u1);
    pt_mul(&b, &q, &u2);
    pt_add(&sum, &a, &b);
    if (u_zero(&sum.z)) return false;
    U zi, zi2, x;
    inv_mod(&zi, &sum.z, &P);
    MUL(zi2, zi, zi);
    MUL(x, sum.x, zi2);
    if (u_cmp(&x, &N) >= 0) u_sub(&x, &x, &N);
    return !u_cmp(&x, &r);
}
```

`runtime/update_crypto.h`:

```h
// SHA-256 and ECDSA P-256 verification without any library (runtime/update_crypto.c), for updating an AppImage: it runs
// on many distributions and can count on none of their crypto libraries. Only checks public data, so nothing here
// needs to be constant time. SW Update on Windows uses Windows' own crypto instead.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef struct {
    uint32_t h[8];
    uint64_t total;
    uint8_t buf[64];
    size_t used;
} UcSha256;

void uc_sha256_init(UcSha256 *c);
void uc_sha256_update(UcSha256 *c, const void *data, size_t n);
void uc_sha256_final(UcSha256 *c, uint8_t out[32]);
bool uc_sha256_file(const char *path, uint8_t out[32]);  // false: it can't be read

// hash: the SHA-256 of what was signed; sig: r then s; pub: X then Y (all big-endian)
bool uc_p256_verify(const uint8_t hash[32], const uint8_t sig[64], const uint8_t pub[64]);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

`runtime/weather.c`:

```c
// Cheats > Weather in the Savage Wind overlay, and `weather` (settings.h weather): holds the weather the player picks,
// or keeps out rain or thunderstorms. No patch in the game's code: once a frame, ksys::world::Manager's current weather
// is replaced before the game reads it, the way the game's own setWeatherType does (mWeatherType at +0x7d1, its timer
// at +0x794). A cutscene's own weather (mWeatherSetForDemo at +0x7d6) is left alone, so story scenes keep theirs.
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "control.h"
#include "game_sites.h"
#include "hle.h"
#include "settings.h"

// The game's weather types: 0 clear, 1 cloudy, 2 rain, 3 heavy rain, 4 snow, 5 heavy snow, 6 thunderstorm,
// 7 thunder rain, 8 rain in sunshine. The setting: 0 the game's, 1 no rain, 2 no thunderstorms, 3 + n: n held.
static int logged;  // (changes written to the log this boot: the first few)

void weather_frame(void) {
    int w = g_settings.weather;
    if (w <= 0 || w >= WEATHER_COUNT || !g_site.world_mgr) return;
    uint64_t wm = *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)g_site.world_mgr;
    if (!wm || !*(uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x5c0)) return;  // (the world isn't up yet)
    if (*(volatile uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x7d6)) return;   // (a cutscene's weather)
    volatile uint8_t *now = (volatile uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x7d1);
    uint8_t cur = *now;
    int want = w >= 3 ? w - 3 : -1;
    if (w == 1 && (cur == 2 || cur == 3 || cur == 6 || cur == 7 || cur == 8)) want = 1;  // (rain of any kind: cloudy)
    if (w == 2 && cur == 6) want = 1;                                                    // (a dry storm: cloudy)
    if (w == 2 && cur == 7) want = 2;                                                    // (thunder rain: rain)
    if (want < 0) return;
    if (cur != want && logged < 20 && (cur != 255 || !logged)) {  // (255: none requested; held: rewritten each frame)
        LOG("[weather] %d -> %d (setting %d)\n", cur, want, w);
        logged++;
    }
    *now = (uint8_t)want;
    *(volatile int32_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x794) = 4;  // (as setWeatherType leaves it: the change is taken up)
}

// weather: show | <name>: game (the game's own again), no_rain, no_storms, or one weather held (settings.h names)
static void cmd_weather(int argc, char **argv, ControlReply *r) {
    static const char *const usage = "weather: use weather game, no_rain, no_storms, clear, cloudy, rain, heavy_rain, "
                                     "snow, heavy_snow, thunderstorm, thunder_rain or sun_shower";
    if (argc > 2) { control_fail(r, "%s", usage); return; }
    if (argc == 2) {
        int w = -1;
        for (int i = 0; i < WEATHER_COUNT; i++)
            if (!strcmp(argv[1], g_weather_keys[i])) w = i;
        if (w < 0) { control_fail(r, "%s", usage); return; }
        g_settings.weather = w;  // (weather_frame writes it from the next frame; as `set`, the ini isn't written)
        logged = 0;
    }
    int w = g_settings.weather >= 0 && g_settings.weather < WEATHER_COUNT ? g_settings.weather : 0;
    control_field_str(r, "weather", g_weather_keys[w]);
    control_text(r, "Weather: %s", w == 0 ? "the game's own" : g_weather_keys[w]);
    uint64_t wm = g_site.world_mgr ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)g_site.world_mgr : 0;
    if (wm && *(uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x5c0)) {
        uint8_t cur = *(volatile uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x7d1);
        if (cur < 9) {  // (the game's types, as g_weather_keys from 3 on)
            control_field_str(r, "now", g_weather_keys[3 + cur]);
            control_text(r, "Now: %s", g_weather_keys[3 + cur]);
        }
        if (*(volatile uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(wm + 0x7d6)) control_text(r, "A cutscene sets the weather now: it keeps it");
    } else if (argc == 2) control_text(r, "No world yet: it applies once one is loaded");
}

// (runtime/control_game.c: developer mode only - it writes the game's memory)
void weather_control_init(void) {
    static const ControlCmd cmds[] = {
        {"weather", "[game | no_rain | no_storms | clear | cloudy | rain | heavy_rain | snow | heavy_snow | thunderstorm | "
                    "thunder_rain | sun_shower]",
         "Cheat: show, hold or limit the weather (game: the game's own again)", cmd_weather, 0},
    };
    control_register(cmds, 1);
}

RT_ON_RESET(weather_reset) { logged = 0; }

```

`runtime/window_size.c`:

```c
// Window size (Video > Window size). The list (user, 2026-10-19), by shape: 16:9 640x360 .. 7680x4320, 21:9
// 1280x540 / 1708x720 / 1920x810 / 2134x900 / 2560x1080 / 3440x1440 / 3840x1600, 16:10 1280x800 / 1680x1050 /
// 1920x1200 / 2560x1600, 4:3 and 5:4 640x480 .. 1600x1200. Offered:
// those that fit on the window's display (its desktop size), and the desktop size itself; fullscreen also offers
// bigger ones the display has a mode for (GPU downsampling such as NVIDIA DSR adds them).
//   In a window: the window's inside is that size (in pixels), centred on its display.
//   Fullscreen: the desktop size is borderless fullscreen (no mode change); another size the display has a mode for
//   switches the display to it (exclusive fullscreen); any other (a 21:9 size on a 16:9 display) stays borderless and
//   the game image is that size, scaled to fit the screen (winsize_virtual; runtime/nvn/vulkan/device.c). Video >
//   Fullscreen mode can make it always borderless (no mode change) or always exclusive (the desktop's size too).
// Video > Monitor: the window goes to that display (made there at start; moved there when the setting changes);
// Automatic leaves it where it is. A display that isn't connected is Automatic until it is.
// Sizes are pixels; SDL's window sizes are pixels / the display's pixel density (1 on Windows).
#include "window_size.h"

#include <math.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include <SDL3/SDL.h>

#include "hle.h"
#include "settings.h"

static const WinSize k_sizes[] = {
    {640, 360}, {960, 540}, {1280, 720}, {1600, 900}, {1920, 1080}, {2560, 1440}, {3840, 2160},  // 16:9
    {5120, 2880}, {7680, 4320},
    {1280, 540}, {1708, 720}, {1920, 810}, {2134, 900}, {2560, 1080}, {3440, 1440}, {3840, 1600}, // 21:9
    {1280, 800}, {1680, 1050}, {1920, 1200}, {2560, 1600},                               // 16:10
    {640, 480}, {800, 600}, {1024, 768}, {1280, 1024}, {1600, 1200},                     // 4:3, 5:4
};
#define NSIZES (int)(sizeof k_sizes / sizeof k_sizes[0])

static pthread_mutex_t g_m = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static WinSize g_desk = {1920, 1080};  // the display's desktop size (a guess until a display is read)
static float g_density = 1;            // its pixel density (window size = pixels / density)
static WinSize g_modes[64];            // its fullscreen modes' sizes
static int g_nmodes;
static SDL_DisplayID g_display;
static WinSize g_virtual;              // fullscreen on a size the display has no mode for (0 x 0: none)
static float g_hz;                     // its refresh rate (0: not known)
static WinDisplay g_disp[WINDISPLAY_MAX];  // the displays connected (Video > Monitor)
static SDL_DisplayID g_disp_id[WINDISPLAY_MAX];
static int g_ndisp;

static bool same(WinSize a, WinSize b) { return a.w == b.w && a.h == b.h; }

// 0 16:9, 1 21:9, 2 16:10, 3 4:3, 4 5:4, 5 another shape
static int shape(int w, int h) {
    double r = h > 0 ? (double)w / h : 0;
    if (fabs(r - 16.0 / 9.0) < 0.02) return 0;
    if (r >= 2.3 && r <= 2.45) return 1;  // (64:27, 43:18 and 12:5 are all sold as 21:9)
    if (fabs(r - 1.6) < 0.02) return 2;
    if (fabs(r - 4.0 / 3.0) < 0.02) return 3;
    if (fabs(r - 1.25) < 0.02) return 4;
    return 5;
}

const char *winsize_aspect(int w, int h) {
    static const char *const names[] = {"16:9", "21:9", "16:10", "4:3", "5:4"};
    int s = shape(w, h);
    return s < 5 ? names[s] : NULL;
}

static int group(WinSize s) {  // (4:3 and 5:4 together)
    int k = shape(s.w, s.h);
    return k == 4 ? 3 : k == 5 ? 4 : k;
}

static int cmp(const void *a, const void *b) {
    const WinSize *x = a, *y = b;
    int gx = group(*x), gy = group(*y);
    if (gx != gy) return gx - gy;
    long long ax = (long long)x->w * x->h, ay = (long long)y->w * y->h;
    return ax < ay ? -1 : ax > ay ? 1 : x->w - y->w;
}

int winsize_list(WinSize *out, bool fullscreen) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    WinSize desk = g_desk, modes[64];
    int nm = g_nmodes;
    for (int i = 0; i < nm; i++) modes[i] = g_modes[i];
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    int n = 0;
    bool have_desk = false;
    for (int i = 0; i < NSIZES && n < WINSIZE_MAX - 1; i++) {
        WinSize s = k_sizes[i];
        bool ok = s.w <= desk.w && s.h <= desk.h;
        for (int m = 0; !ok && fullscreen && m < nm; m++) ok = same(s, modes[m]);
        if (!ok) continue;
        have_desk |= same(s, desk);
        out[n++] = s;
    }
    if (!have_desk) out[n++] = desk;
    qsort(out, (size_t)n, sizeof *out, cmp);
    for (int i = 1; i < n; i++)  // (the desktop's own size first)
        if (same(out[i], desk)) {
            for (; i > 0; i--) out[i] = out[i - 1];
            out[0] = desk;
            break;
        }
    return n;
}

float winsize_refresh_rate(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    float hz = g_hz;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    return hz;
}

WinSize winsize_desktop(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    WinSize d = g_desk;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    return d;
}

static WinSize resolve(WinSize want, bool fullscreen) {
    WinSize list[WINSIZE_MAX];
    int n = winsize_list(list, fullscreen);
    if (want.w <= 0 || want.h <= 0) {
        if (fullscreen) return winsize_desktop();
        want = (WinSize){1280, 720};
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        if (same(list[i], want)) return list[i];
    // not offered here (another display, or set for fullscreen only): the biggest of that shape that fits, else the
    // smallest 16:9 size, else the desktop
    int best = -1;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        if (group(list[i]) == group(want) && list[i].w <= want.w && list[i].h <= want.h &&
            (best < 0 || list[i].w * list[i].h > list[best].w * list[best].h))
            best = i;
    if (best < 0 && !fullscreen)
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
            if (group(list[i]) == 0 && (best < 0 || list[i].w * list[i].h < list[best].w * list[best].h)) best = i;
    return best >= 0 ? list[best] : winsize_desktop();
}

WinSize winsize_effective(bool fullscreen) {
    if (g_settings.window_w <= 0 || g_settings.window_h <= 0) return winsize_default(fullscreen);
    return resolve((WinSize){g_settings.window_w, g_settings.window_h}, fullscreen);
}

WinSize winsize_default(bool fullscreen) {
    WinSize s = {0, 0};
    if (!settings_handheld_size(&s.w, &s.h)) s.w = s.h = 0;  // (a handheld: its screen's own size)
    return resolve(s, fullscreen);
}

void winsize_name(WinSize s, const char *native, char *buf, int n) {
    const char *a = winsize_aspect(s.w, s.h);
    WinSize d = winsize_desktop();
    if (!native || !same(s, d)) native = NULL;
    if (a && native) snprintf(buf, (size_t)n, "%d x %d  (%s, %s)", s.w, s.h, a, native);
    else if (a || native) snprintf(buf, (size_t)n, "%d x %d  (%s)", s.w, s.h, a ? a : native);
    else snprintf(buf, (size_t)n, "%d x %d", s.w, s.h);
}

bool winsize_virtual(int *w, int *h) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    WinSize v = g_virtual;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    if (v.w <= 0) return false;
    *w = v.w, *h = v.h;
    return true;
}

int windisplay_list(WinDisplay *out) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    int n = g_ndisp;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) out[i] = g_disp[i];
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    return n;
}

int windisplay_current(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    int x = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_ndisp && !x; i++)
        if (g_disp_id[i] == g_display) x = i + 1;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    return x;
}

// The setting's display in the list (1..; 0: Automatic or not connected): the one of its name at its place, else the
// first of its name (the displays came in another order), else (no name: a hand-edited file) the one at its place.
// g_m held.
static int target_locked(void) {
    int want = g_settings.display;
    const char *name = g_settings.display_name;
    if (want <= 0) return 0;
    if (want <= g_ndisp && (!name[0] || !strcmp(g_disp[want - 1].name, name))) return want;
    for (int i = 0; name[0] && i < g_ndisp; i++)
        if (!strcmp(g_disp[i].name, name)) return i + 1;
    return 0;
}

int windisplay_target(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    int x = target_locked();
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    return x;
}

void windisplay_set(int n) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    if (n >= 1 && n <= g_ndisp) {
        g_settings.display = n;
        snprintf(g_settings.display_name, sizeof g_settings.display_name, "%s", g_disp[n - 1].name);
    } else {
        g_settings.display = 0, g_settings.display_name[0] = 0;
    }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
}

void windisplay_name(const WinDisplay *d, int n, const char *primary, char *buf, int len) {
    if (d->primary && primary) snprintf(buf, (size_t)len, "%d: %s  (%d x %d, %s)", n, d->name, d->w, d->h, primary);
    else snprintf(buf, (size_t)len, "%d: %s  (%d x %d)", n, d->name, d->w, d->h);
}

// The displays connected (read again every half second: one plugged in or out, or its desktop size changed)
static void read_displays(void) {
    static uint64_t at;
    uint64_t now = SDL_GetTicks();
    if (at && now - at < 500) return;
    at = now;
    WinDisplay l[WINDISPLAY_MAX];
    SDL_DisplayID ids[WINDISPLAY_MAX];
    int n = 0, count = 0;
    SDL_DisplayID *ds = SDL_GetDisplays(&count), primary = SDL_GetPrimaryDisplay();
    for (int i = 0; ds && i < count && n < WINDISPLAY_MAX; i++) {
        const SDL_DisplayMode *dm = SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode(ds[i]);
        const char *name = SDL_GetDisplayName(ds[i]);
        float density = dm && dm->pixel_density > 0 ? dm->pixel_density : 1;
        WinDisplay *d = &l[n];
        memset(d, 0, sizeof *d);
        snprintf(d->name, sizeof d->name, "%s", name && *name ? name : "Display");
        d->w = dm ? (int)lroundf(dm->w * density) : 0, d->h = dm ? (int)lroundf(dm->h * density) : 0;
        d->primary = ds[i] == primary;
        ids[n++] = ds[i];
    }
    SDL_free(ds);
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    bool same_list = n == g_ndisp;
    for (int i = 0; same_list && i < n; i++)
        same_list = ids[i] == g_disp_id[i] && !memcmp(&l[i], &g_disp[i], sizeof l[i]);
    g_ndisp = n;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) g_disp[i] = l[i], g_disp_id[i] = ids[i];
    int t = target_locked();
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    if (same_list) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        LOG("[window] display %d: %s %dx%d%s%s\n", i + 1, l[i].name, l[i].w, l[i].h, l[i].primary ? " (primary)" : "",
            t == i + 1 ? " (Video > Monitor)" : "");
    if (g_settings.display > 0 && !t)
        LOG("[window] Video > Monitor %d (%s) isn't connected: the window's own\n", g_settings.display,
            g_settings.display_name);
}

// The SDL display the setting picks (0: Automatic, or not connected)
static SDL_DisplayID target_display(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    int t = target_locked();
    SDL_DisplayID d = t ? g_disp_id[t - 1] : 0;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    return d;
}

unsigned winsize_start_display(void) { return (unsigned)target_display(); }

// The display's mode of that size with the highest refresh rate (NULL: none)
static bool find_mode(SDL_DisplayID d, WinSize s, SDL_DisplayMode *out) {
    int count = 0;
    SDL_DisplayMode **ms = SDL_GetFullscreenDisplayModes(d, &count);
    bool found = false;
    for (int i = 0; ms && i < count; i++) {
        WinSize m = {(int)lroundf(ms[i]->w * ms[i]->pixel_density), (int)lroundf(ms[i]->h * ms[i]->pixel_density)};
        if (same(m, s) && (!found || ms[i]->refresh_rate > out->refresh_rate)) *out = *ms[i], found = true;
    }
    SDL_free(ms);
    return found;
}

// Read display d (its desktop size, modes, refresh rate) when it isn't the one read last (0: the primary)
static void refresh_display(SDL_DisplayID d) {
    if (!d) d = SDL_GetPrimaryDisplay();
    const SDL_DisplayMode *dm = d ? SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode(d) : NULL;
    if (!dm) return;
    float density = dm->pixel_density > 0 ? dm->pixel_density : 1;
    WinSize desk = {(int)lroundf(dm->w * density), (int)lroundf(dm->h * density)};
    const SDL_DisplayMode *cur = SDL_GetCurrentDisplayMode(d);  // (exclusive fullscreen: the mode in use)
    float hz = cur && cur->refresh_rate > 0 ? cur->refresh_rate : dm->refresh_rate;
    SDL_DisplayMode max_mode;
    if (find_mode(d, desk, &max_mode) && max_mode.refresh_rate > hz) {
        // If the monitor supports a higher refresh rate for its desktop resolution
        // (e.g. Windows 11 Dynamic Refresh Rate / power savings reporting 60 Hz while the panel is 165 Hz),
        // adopt the true panel refresh rate unless locked in exclusive fullscreen at another rate.
        if (!cur || cur == dm) hz = max_mode.refresh_rate;
    }
    settings_fps_for_display(hz);  // (Frame rate > Match display)
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    g_hz = hz;
    bool known = d == g_display && same(desk, g_desk);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    if (known) return;
    WinSize modes[64];
    int nm = 0, count = 0;
    SDL_DisplayMode **ms = SDL_GetFullscreenDisplayModes(d, &count);
    for (int i = 0; ms && i < count && nm < 64; i++) {
        WinSize s = {(int)lroundf(ms[i]->w * ms[i]->pixel_density), (int)lroundf(ms[i]->h * ms[i]->pixel_density)};
        bool dup = false;
        for (int k = 0; k < nm && !dup; k++) dup = same(modes[k], s);
        if (!dup) modes[nm++] = s;
    }
    SDL_free(ms);
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    g_display = d, g_desk = desk, g_density = density, g_nmodes = nm;
    for (int i = 0; i < nm; i++) g_modes[i] = modes[i];
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
    WinSize list[WINSIZE_MAX];
    char buf[512];
    int len = 0, n = winsize_list(list, true);
    for (int i = 0; i < n && len < (int)sizeof buf - 16; i++) len += snprintf(buf + len, sizeof buf - len, " %dx%d", list[i].w, list[i].h);
    LOG("[window] display %u: desktop %dx%d (density %.2f, %.2f Hz), %d fullscreen sizes; offered:%s\n", (unsigned)d,
        desk.w, desk.h, density, hz, nm, buf);
}

void winsize_refresh(void *win) {
    read_displays();
    // (no window yet: the display it will be made on)
    refresh_display(win ? SDL_GetDisplayForWindow((SDL_Window *)win) : target_display());
}

void winsize_apply(void *win) {
    SDL_Window *w = (SDL_Window *)win;
    if (!w) return;
    static bool first = true;
    // test windows (SAVAGEWIND_WINDOW / SAVAGEWIND_HIDDEN) keep their size and display at start and are never made
    // fullscreen
    bool test = getenv("SAVAGEWIND_WINDOW") || getenv("SAVAGEWIND_HIDDEN");
    bool keep_size = first && getenv("SAVAGEWIND_WINDOW");
    first = false;
    read_displays();
    bool fs = g_settings.fullscreen && !test;
    // Steam's Gaming Mode on a handheld: gamescope's game display can be another shape than the screen (1920x1080 on a
    // Deck's 1280x800: bars), and fullscreen takes that size. A plain window of the size set fills the screen instead.
    const char *cd = getenv("XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP");
    int hw, hh;
    if (fs && settings_handheld_size(&hw, &hh) && (getenv("GAMESCOPE_WAYLAND_DISPLAY") || (cd && !strcmp(cd, "gamescope")))) {
        fs = false;
        static bool logged;
        if (!logged) LOG("[window] gamescope: a window, not fullscreen\n"), logged = true;
    }
    // Video > Monitor: to that display first (out of fullscreen for the move: a fullscreen window keeps its display)
    SDL_DisplayID to = test ? 0 : target_display(), d = SDL_GetDisplayForWindow(w);
    if (to && to != d) {
        if (SDL_GetWindowFlags(w) & SDL_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN) {
            SDL_SetWindowFullscreen(w, false);
            SDL_SyncWindow(w);
        }
        if (SDL_GetWindowFlags(w) & SDL_WINDOW_MAXIMIZED) SDL_RestoreWindow(w);
        SDL_SetWindowPosition(w, (int)SDL_WINDOWPOS_CENTERED_DISPLAY(to), (int)SDL_WINDOWPOS_CENTERED_DISPLAY(to));
        SDL_SyncWindow(w);
        d = SDL_GetDisplayForWindow(w);
        LOG("[window] to display %u (Video > Monitor)%s\n", (unsigned)to, d == to ? "" : ": it stayed where it was");
    }
    refresh_display(d);
    WinSize s = winsize_effective(fs), desk = winsize_desktop(), virt = {0, 0};
    if (fs) {
        // Video > Fullscreen mode: a display mode for a size other than the desktop's (Automatic), for every size
        // (Exclusive), or for none (Borderless: another size is the image scaled to the screen)
        int fm = g_settings.fullscreen_mode;
        SDL_DisplayMode mode;
        bool has_mode = find_mode(d, s, &mode);
        const SDL_DisplayMode *dm = d ? SDL_GetDesktopDisplayMode(d) : NULL;
        bool higher_hz = has_mode && dm && (mode.refresh_rate > dm->refresh_rate + 1.0f);
        bool want_mode = fm == FSMODE_EXCLUSIVE || (fm != FSMODE_BORDERLESS && (!same(s, desk) || higher_hz));
        bool exclusive = want_mode && has_mode;
        if (!same(s, desk) && !exclusive) virt = s;
        SDL_SetWindowFullscreenMode(w, exclusive ? &mode : NULL);  // (NULL: borderless, the desktop's size)
        SDL_SetWindowFullscreen(w, true);
        if (exclusive) {
            float mode_hz = mode.refresh_rate > 0 ? mode.refresh_rate : winsize_refresh_rate();
            pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
            g_hz = mode_hz;
            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
            settings_fps_for_display(mode_hz);
            LOG("[window] fullscreen %dx%d (display mode, %.2f Hz)\n", s.w, s.h, mode.refresh_rate);
        } else {
            LOG("[window] fullscreen %dx%d (%s)\n", s.w, s.h, virt.w ? "borderless, image scaled to the screen" : "borderless");
        }
    } else {
        SDL_SetWindowFullscreen(w, false);
        if (!keep_size) {
            if (SDL_GetWindowFlags(w) & SDL_WINDOW_MAXIMIZED) SDL_RestoreWindow(w);
            pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
            float density = g_density;
            pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
            SDL_SetWindowSize(w, (int)lroundf(s.w / density), (int)lroundf(s.h / density));
            // centred in the usable area (not under the taskbar); the title bar stays on screen when it doesn't fit
            SDL_Rect u;
            if (d && SDL_GetDisplayUsableBounds(d, &u)) {
                int top = 0, x = u.x + (u.w - (int)lroundf(s.w / density)) / 2,
                    y = u.y + (u.h - (int)lroundf(s.h / density)) / 2;
                SDL_GetWindowBordersSize(w, &top, NULL, NULL, NULL);
                if (y < u.y + top) y = u.y + top;
                if (x < u.x) x = u.x;
                SDL_SetWindowPosition(w, x, y);
            }
            LOG("[window] window %dx%d\n", s.w, s.h);
        }
    }
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_m);
    g_virtual = virt;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_m);
}
```

`runtime/window_size.h`:

```h
// Window size (Video > Window size, runtime/window_size.c): the sizes offered, the window and fullscreen mode they
// give, and the image size in fullscreen when the display has no mode of that size.
#pragma once
#include <stdbool.h>

typedef struct { int w, h; } WinSize;
enum { WINSIZE_MAX = 48 };

// The sizes offered: the desktop's own size first, then the others grouped by shape (16:9, 21:9, 16:10, 4:3 / 5:4,
// then any other the desktop has): those of the list that fit on the window's display. Fullscreen also offers bigger
// sizes the display has a mode for (GPU downsampling such as NVIDIA DSR). Any thread.
int winsize_list(WinSize *out, bool fullscreen);
// The size the setting gives (g_settings.window_w / window_h; unset: 1280 x 720 in a window, the desktop in
// fullscreen), one of the sizes offered. Any thread.
WinSize winsize_effective(bool fullscreen);
WinSize winsize_default(bool fullscreen);  // (the setting unset)
WinSize winsize_desktop(void);
// The window's display's refresh rate, Hz (0: not known yet). Any thread.
float winsize_refresh_rate(void);
// "1920 x 1080  (16:9)"; the desktop's size with `native` (the word, translated; NULL: none) too:
// "1920 x 1080  (16:9, native)"
void winsize_name(WinSize s, const char *native, char *buf, int n);
// "16:9", "21:9", "16:10", "4:3", "5:4", or NULL for another shape
const char *winsize_aspect(int w, int h);
// Fullscreen on a size the display has no mode for: the game image is that size, scaled to fit the screen (true, and
// the size). Any thread.
bool winsize_virtual(int *w, int *h);

// Video > Monitor: the displays connected, in SDL's order (the setting's display n is the list's n - 1). Any thread.
enum { WINDISPLAY_MAX = 8 };
typedef struct { char name[64]; int w, h; bool primary; } WinDisplay;
int windisplay_list(WinDisplay *out);
int windisplay_current(void);  // the window's display: its number in the list (1..; 0: not known)
int windisplay_target(void);   // the display the setting picks (1..; 0: Automatic, or that display isn't connected)
void windisplay_set(int n);    // the setting: 0 Automatic, n the list's n-th display (by its name too)
// "2: DELL U2723QE  (3840 x 2160, primary)"
void windisplay_name(const WinDisplay *d, int n, const char *primary, char *buf, int len);

// Main thread (the window loop): read the window's display again when it changed; apply the setting to the window
// (and move it to the display the setting picks). winsize_start_display: the display to make the window on (an
// SDL_DisplayID; 0 the primary), after winsize_refresh(NULL).
void winsize_refresh(void *sdl_window);
void winsize_apply(void *sdl_window);
unsigned winsize_start_display(void);
```
