```py
class SiteError(Exception):
    pass


def supported_version(build_id):
    """The VERSIONS entry of a main module build id (64 hex digits or the first 16), or None."""
    for v in VERSIONS:
        if v.build_id and build_id[:16] == v.build_id:
            return v
    return None


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ instructions

def sext(v, bits):
    return v - (1 << bits) if v & (1 << (bits - 1)) else v


def is_adrp(w):
    return (w & 0x9F000000) == 0x90000000


def adrp_page(w, pc):
    return (pc & ~0xFFF) + (sext(((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2 | ((w >> 29) & 3), 21) << 12)


def lo12(w):
    """(scaled low 12 bits, base register) of an ADD (immediate, 64-bit) or an LDR / STR (unsigned offset); else None"""
    if (w & 0xFFC00000) == 0x91000000:  # add xd, xn, #imm
        return (w >> 10) & 0xFFF, (w >> 5) & 31
    if (w & 0x3B000000) == 0x39000000:  # ldr / str (immediate, unsigned offset), integer or SIMD&FP
        scale = (w >> 30) & 3
        if w & 0x04000000 and (w >> 23) & 1:  # (a 128-bit SIMD&FP register)
            scale = 4
        return ((w >> 10) & 0xFFF) << scale, (w >> 5) & 31
    return None


def imm_value(w):
    """The immediate of an LDR / STR (unsigned offset, scaled), an ADD / SUB / CMP (immediate) or a MOVZ; else None"""
    if (w & 0x3B000000) == 0x39000000:
        return lo12(w)[0]
    if (w & 0x1F000000) == 0x11000000:
        return ((w >> 10) & 0xFFF) << (12 if (w >> 22) & 1 else 0)
    if (w & 0x7F800000) == 0x52800000:  # movz (32 / 64-bit)
        return ((w >> 5) & 0xFFFF) << (16 * ((w >> 21) & 3))
    return None


def mask(w, adrp_regs):
    """The bits of instruction w a pattern keeps (adrp_regs: registers an ADRP earlier in the pattern set)."""
    if (w & 0x7C000000) == 0x14000000:  # b, bl
        return 0xFC000000
    if (w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000 or (w & 0x7E000000) == 0x34000000:  # b.cond; cbz, cbnz
        return 0xFF00001F
    if (w & 0x7E000000) == 0x36000000:  # tbz, tbnz
        return 0xFFF8001F
    if (w & 0x1F000000) == 0x10000000:  # adr, adrp
        return 0x9F00001F
    if (w & 0x3B000000) == 0x18000000:  # ldr (literal)
        return 0xFF00001F
    lo = lo12(w)
    if lo and lo[1] in adrp_regs:
        return 0xFFC003FF
    return 0xFFFFFFFF


def make_pattern(words):
    """A pattern string for these instruction words: each word as hex, or value/mask where bits are masked."""
    out, adrp_regs = [], set()
    for w in words:
        m = mask(w, adrp_regs)
        if is_adrp(w):
            adrp_regs.add(w & 31)
        else:  # (most instructions write their bits 0-4 register: it holds no page any more)
            adrp_regs.discard(w & 31)
        out.append(f'{w:08x}' if m == 0xFFFFFFFF else f'{w & m:08x}/{m:08x}')
    return ' '.join(out)


def parse_pattern(p):
    words = []
    for t in p.split():
        v, _, m = t.partition('/')
        words.append((int(v, 16), int(m, 16) if m else 0xFFFFFFFF))
    return words


def compile_pattern(p):
    parts = []
    for v, m in parse_pattern(p):
        for i in range(4):
            vb, mb = (v >> 8 * i) & 0xFF, (m >> 8 * i) & 0xFF
            if mb == 0xFF:
                parts.append(re.escape(bytes([vb])))
            elif mb == 0:
                parts.append(b'.')
            else:
                parts.append(b'[' + b''.join(re.escape(bytes([b])) for b in range(256) if b & mb == vb & mb) + b']')
    return re.compile(b''.join(parts), re.DOTALL)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ a main module

class Main:
    def __init__(self, nso, base=MAIN_BASE):
        self.nso, self.base = nso, base
        self.text_off, self.text_size = nso.text
        self.text = bytes(nso.image[self.text_off:self.text_off + self.text_size])

    def word(self, a):
        return struct.unpack_from('<I', self.nso.image, a - self.base)[0]

    def find(self, pattern, limit=2):
        """Addresses (word-aligned, in .text) where the pattern matches; at most `limit`."""
        rx, out, pos = compile_pattern(pattern), [], 0
        while len(out) < limit:
            m = rx.search(self.text, pos)
            if not m:
                break
            if m.start() % 4:
                pos = m.start() + 1
                continue
            out.append(self.base + self.text_off + m.start())
            pos = m.start() + 4
        return out

    def target(self, kind, a):
        """What the site of this kind at instruction a is (see the module docstring)."""
        w = self.word(a)
        if kind == 'code':
            return a
        if kind == 'call':
            if (w & 0x7C000000) != 0x14000000:
                raise SiteError(f'{a:#x} is not a branch ({w:08x})')
            return a + sext(w & 0x3FFFFFF, 26) * 4
        if kind == 'imm':
            v = imm_value(w)
            if v is None:
                raise SiteError(f'{a:#x} has no immediate ({w:08x})')
            return v
        if is_adrp(w):
            v = adrp_page(w, a)
        else:
            lo = lo12(w)
            if not lo:
                raise SiteError(f'{a:#x} does not complete an address ({w:08x})')
            for b in range(a - 4, a - 4 * 33, -4):  # its ADRP
                pw = self.word(b)
                if is_adrp(pw) and (pw & 31) == lo[1]:
                    v = adrp_page(pw, b) + lo[0]
                    break
            else:
                raise SiteError(f'{a:#x}: no ADRP for x{lo[1]} above it')
        if kind == 'got':
            return self.base + struct.unpack_from('<Q', self.nso.image, v - self.base)[0]
        return v

    def locate(self, s):
        """(address, or None when the pattern doesn't find exactly one place; how many places it matches) of a site"""
        if s.kind == 'data':
            return self.base + self.nso.data[0], 1
        if s.kind == 'end':
            return self.base + self.nso.size, 1
        hits = []
        for p, at in s.pattern if isinstance(s.pattern, list) else [(s.pattern, s.at)] if s.pattern else []:
            hits = self.find(p)
            if len(hits) == 1:
                return self.target(s.kind, hits[0] + 4 * at), 1
        return None, len(hits)

    def text_words(self, a, n):
        return [self.word(a + 4 * i) for i in range(n)]

    def function_of(self, a):
        """(start, end) of the function holding a, from the module's unwind info (None: none there)."""
        import bisect
        from analyze import eh_frame_extents
        if not hasattr(self, 'fdes'):
            self.fdes = sorted((self.base + s, self.base + e) for s, e in eh_frame_extents(self.nso) if e > s)
        i = bisect.bisect_right(self.fdes, (a, 1 << 64)) - 1
        return self.fdes[i] if i >= 0 and a < self.fdes[i][1] else None

    def pattern_for(self, a, kind='code', shortest=8, longest=24):
        """A pattern that finds only a: (pattern, at). It stays inside a's function (the code around it may change
        on its own), starts as close above a as it can - at the ADRP for a ref or got site, whose address bits it
        masks then - and has `shortest` words at least (or the whole function): short ones are likelier to find
        another place in a new build."""
        f0, f1 = self.function_of(a) or (a - 64, a + 128)
        first = 0
        if kind in ('ref', 'got') and not is_adrp(self.word(a)):
            reg = lo12(self.word(a))[1]
            first = next(i for i in range(1, 33) if is_adrp(self.word(a - 4 * i)) and self.word(a - 4 * i) & 31 == reg)
        for back in range(first, (a - f0) // 4 + 1):
            s = a - 4 * back
            room = (f1 - s) // 4
            for n in range(min(max(shortest, back + 1), room), min(longest, room) + 1):
                p = make_pattern(self.text_words(s, n))
                if self.find(p) == [s]:
                    return p, back
        raise SiteError(f'no pattern inside its function finds only {a:#x}')


def common_pattern(ma, a, mb, b, kind='code', shortest=8, longest=32):
    """A pattern that finds only a in main module ma and only b in mb, the same code in two versions: the bits both
    keep (and make_pattern keeps). For an imm site the immediate itself is always masked. (pattern, at)"""
    fa, fb = ma.function_of(a) or (a - 64, a + 128), mb.function_of(b) or (b - 64, b + 128)
    first = 0
    if kind in ('ref', 'got') and not is_adrp(ma.word(a)):
        reg = lo12(ma.word(a))[1]
        first = next(i for i in range(1, 33) if is_adrp(ma.word(a - 4 * i)) and ma.word(a - 4 * i) & 31 == reg)
    for back in range(first, min(a - fa[0], b - fb[0]) // 4 + 1):
        sa, sb = a - 4 * back, b - 4 * back
        room = min(fa[1] - sa, fb[1] - sb) // 4
        for n in range(min(max(shortest, back + 1), room), min(longest, room) + 1):
            out = []
            for i, ((va, ka), (vb, kb)) in enumerate(zip(parse_pattern(make_pattern(ma.text_words(sa, n))),
                                                         parse_pattern(make_pattern(mb.text_words(sb, n))))):
                k = ka & kb & ~(va ^ vb) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                if kind == 'imm' and i == back:
                    k &= 0xFFE0001F if (va & 0x7F800000) == 0x52800000 else 0xFFC003FF
                out.append(f'{va & k:08x}' if k == 0xFFFFFFFF else f'{va & k:08x}/{k:08x}')
            p = ' '.join(out)
            if ma.find(p) == [sa] and mb.find(p) == [sb]:
                return p, back
    raise SiteError(f'no pattern inside both functions finds only {a:#x} and {b:#x}')


def resolve(main, known=None, log=None):
    """{site name: address} for this main module. known: the addresses listed for its build (or None)."""
    out, problems = {}, []
    for s in SITES:
        try:
            found, hits = main.locate(s)
        except SiteError as e:
            problems.append(f'{s.name}: {e}')
            continue
        # This experiment changes native object routing. A stale KNOWN address
        # must never turn it on after a failed signature check.
        if s.name in OPT_TWO_SITES and (found is None or
                                      (known and s.name in known and found != known[s.name])):
            if log:
                log(f'game_sites: {s.name}: spike signature did not match')
            continue
        k = (known or {}).get(s.name)
        if found is not None and k is not None and found != k:
            raise SiteError(f'{s.name}: the pattern finds {found:#x}, the table says {k:#x}')
        if found is None and k is None:
            if s.name in OPTIONAL:
                continue
            problems.append(f'{s.name}: the pattern matches {hits} places' + (' or more' if hits > 1 else ''))
            continue
        if found is None and log:
            log(f'game_sites: {s.name}: the pattern matches {hits} places; {k:#x} from the table')
        out[s.name] = found if found is not None else k
    if problems:
        raise SiteError('; '.join(problems))
    for g in OPTIONAL_GROUPS:
        missing = [n for n in g if n not in out]
        if not missing:
            continue
        if log:
            log(f'game_sites: {", ".join(missing)} not found: {", ".join(g)} left out')
        for n in g:
            out.pop(n, None)
    return out


def for_module(nso, base, allow_unsupported=False, log=None):
    """(version name, sites) for the main module nso at base. Refuses a build that VERSIONS doesn't support, unless
    allow_unsupported (bringing up a new version: its sites must then all be found by pattern)."""
    v = supported_version(nso.build_id)
    if not v or not v.supported:
        what = f'version {v.name}, not supported yet' if v else 'not a version Savage Wind knows'
        if not allow_unsupported:
            raise SiteError(f'main module build {nso.build_id[:16]}: {what}')
        if log:
            log(f'game_sites: main module build {nso.build_id[:16]}: {what}; sites by pattern only')
    name = v.name if v else nso.build_id[:16]
    return name, resolve(Main(nso, base), KNOWN.get(name) if v and v.supported else None, log)


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 3 or sys.argv[1] not in ('find', 'pattern', 'common'):
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    from nso import Nso
    m = Main(Nso(sys.argv[2]))
    if sys.argv[1] == 'common':
        mb, a, b = Main(Nso(sys.argv[4])), int(sys.argv[3], 16), int(sys.argv[5], 16)
        kind = sys.argv[6] if len(sys.argv) > 6 else 'code'
        p, at = common_pattern(m, a, mb, b, kind)
        print(f"    Site('<name>', '{kind}', '{p}', {at}),  # -> {m.target(kind, a):#x} / {mb.target(kind, b):#x}")
        return
    if sys.argv[1] == 'pattern':
        a = int(sys.argv[3], 16)
        kind = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 'code'
        p, at = m.pattern_for(a, kind)
        print(f"    Site('<name>', '{kind}', '{p}', {at}),  # -> {m.target(kind, a):#x}")
        return
    v = supported_version(m.nso.build_id)
    known = KNOWN.get(v.name, {}) if v else {}
    print(f'main module build {m.nso.build_id[:16]}: ' + (f'version {v.name}' + ('' if v.supported else
          ' (not supported yet)') if v else 'not in VERSIONS'))
    bad = 0
    for s in SITES:
        try:
            found, hits = m.locate(s)
        except SiteError as e:
            found, hits = None, str(e)
        k = known.get(s.name)
        state = (f'{hits} matches' if found is None else
                 'ok' if k == found else 'new' if k is None else f'TABLE SAYS {k:#x}')
        bad += state not in ('ok', 'new')
        print(f"        '{s.name}': {found:#x},  # {state}" if found is not None else
              f"        # '{s.name}': {state}" + (f' (table {k:#x})' if k is not None else ''))
    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/game_slot.sh`:

```sh
# Sourced by the test scripts before they start ./build/savagewind: a new test copy of the game starts only while the
# Mac has at least 10 GB free (each copy takes ~2 GB; too many at once ran it out of memory). Launches are taken one
# at a time and the next waits ~20 s, so the copy just started has grown before memory is measured again.
# SAVAGEWIND_MIN_FREE_GB (default 10), SAVAGEWIND_SLOT_DIR.
GAME_MIN_FREE_GB=${SAVAGEWIND_MIN_FREE_GB:-10}
GAME_SLOT_DIR=${SAVAGEWIND_SLOT_DIR:-$HOME/.cache/savagewind_test_slots}
mkdir -p "$GAME_SLOT_DIR"
game_free_gb() {  # free + inactive + speculative + purgeable pages (what macOS can hand out without swapping)
    vm_stat | awk '/page size of/ {ps = $8} /Pages (free|inactive|speculative|purgeable):/ {gsub("\\.", "", $NF); n += $NF}
                   END {printf "%d", n * ps / 1073741824}'
}
L="$GAME_SLOT_DIR/launch"
until mkdir "$L" 2>/dev/null; do
    if ! kill -0 "$(cat "$L/pid" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$(find "$L" -maxdepth 0 -mmin +2 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        rm -rf "$L"  # (stale: holder gone for 2+ minutes)
    fi
    sleep 2
done
echo $$ > "$L/pid"
until [ "$(game_free_gb)" -ge "$GAME_MIN_FREE_GB" ]; do sleep 5; done
( sleep 20; rm -rf "$L" ) >/dev/null 2>&1 &
GAME_SLOT=  # (nothing to release at exit)
# test runs never write the player's savagewind.ini: a scratch copy unless the caller gave SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS
if [ -z "$SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS" ]; then
    mkdir -p build/test_ini
    SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS="build/test_ini/settings_$$.ini"
    cp savagewind.ini "$SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS" 2>/dev/null || : > "$SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS"
    export SAVAGEWIND_SETTINGS
fi

```

`tools/gamelib_entry.c`:

```c
// Entry of the game code library (runtime/gamelib.h), compiled into it with the generated code: the module layout,
// function tables and the game version's sites (the generated layout.c), found by name when the app loads the library.
// Everything else in it stays hidden.
#include "gamelib.h"

extern const GameLibModule game_modules[];
extern const uint32_t game_module_count;
extern const char game_version[];
extern const GameLibSite game_sites[];
extern const uint32_t game_site_count;

// simd.h: the compatible target's fma mode, set by the runtime through the tables (exact until then)
#ifndef _WIN32
__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))
#endif
int simd_fma_unfused;

GAMELIB_EXPORT const GameLibTables *swgame_tables(void) {
    static const GameLibTables t = {GAMELIB_ABI, GAMELIB_ID, game_modules, &game_module_count,
                                    game_version, game_sites, &game_site_count, &simd_fma_unfused};
    return &t;
}

```

`tools/gen.py`:

```py
"""Generate C for a whole NSO module.

Usage: gen.py <name> <nso> <layout.txt> <outdir> [--hle hle_symbols.txt] [--chunk N] [--simd asm|c]
       gen.py layout <exefs> <outdir>
       gen.py all <exefs> <outdir> [--hle hle_symbols.txt] [--simd asm|c]

The module's guest address comes from layout.txt, which `gen.py layout` writes (with layout.c) from the exefs
(tools/layout.py). `all` does that and then generates every module into <outdir>/<name>, with --hle for all of them
but main (`make gen`).

The main module has to be a game version Savage Wind supports (tools/game_sites.py VERSIONS): its sites are looked
up there, for tools/patches.py and for the runtime (layout.c). --any-version takes any main module whose sites the
patterns all find (bringing up a new version); --no-sites generates without sites or patches (the made-up modules
of tools/test_layout.py).

--simd: FP/SIMD/CRC32 as AArch64 inline asm (default on arm64 hosts) or portable C (default elsewhere).

--locals: each function keeps its most used registers (tools/regs.py) and its flags (tools/flags.py) in C locals
instead of the Cpu, so clang can hold them in host registers (docs/RECOMP-LOCALS.md). --reg-locals N: how many
registers (default 6); --no-callee-saved-trust: reload X19-X29 and SP after every call too. The Makefile's
RECOMP_LOCALS=1 (the default) passes --locals, and the start screen's build (runtime/gamebuild.c) the same.
"""
import argparse
import bisect
import faulthandler
import os
import platform
import re
import shutil
import struct
import sys
import time
from collections import Counter

import capstone
import unicorn as uc
from unicorn import arm64_const as A

import flags
import game_sites
import layout
import patches
import regs
from analyze import eh_frame_extents, eh_frame_functions
from lifter import Insn, Lifter, Unsupported, bits, emit_asm_batch, hx, sext
from nso import Nso, R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT, R_AARCH64_RELATIVE, header

SCRATCH_MEM = 0x7300000000
# An instruction's C reads the flags (Module._reads_flags; from PR #324 by Hiorac)
FLAG_READ = re.compile(r'\b(?:COND_|FLAG_)|\b(?:adc|sbc|adcs|sbcs)\d+\(|c->nzcv(?! =)')


def sext26(w):
    v = w & 0x03FFFFFF
    return v - 0x04000000 if v & 0x02000000 else v


def fname(a):
    return f'f_{a:x}'


SETJMP_SYMS = ('setjmp', '_setjmp', '__setjmp')


def setjmp_call(t, ret):
    """A call to the guest setjmp. The recompiled code can't resume in the middle of a function, where the guest
    longjmp returns to, so the call gets a host setjmp in the C function of the caller (runtime/hle/setjmp.c):
    the guest longjmp (HLE) restores the registers the guest setjmp saved and jumps back here with x0 set."""
    return (f'{{ jmp_buf *hb_ = rt_setjmp_slot(c, c->x[0]); '
            f'if (!setjmp(*hb_)) {{ c->x[30] = {hx(ret)}; {fname(t)}(c); }} }}')


def sanitize(sym):
    return 'hle_' + re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_]', '_', sym)


class Locals:
    """gen.py --locals: registers per function in locals (tools/regs.py), and the registers a call leaves alone."""

    def __init__(self, n=regs.LOCALS, callee_saved=True):
        self.n = n
        self.kept = regs.CALLEE_SAVED if callee_saved else frozenset()


class Module:
    def __init__(self, name, path, base, simd='asm', locals_=None):
        self.name = name
        self.nso = Nso(path)
        self.base = base
        n = self.nso
        self.lo = base + n.text[0]
        self.hi = base + n.text[0] + n.text[1]
        self.words = struct.unpack(f'<{n.text[1] // 4}I', bytes(n.image[n.text[0]:n.text[0] + n.text[1]]))
        self.lifter = Lifter(base, simd)
        self.cache = {}
        self.stats = Counter()
        self.mu = None
        self.cs = None  # (capstone, made on first use: writes_gpr)
        # the functions as compiled: discovery may split one into several C functions, a jump table spans all of it
        self.fdes = sorted((base + a, base + b) for a, b in eh_frame_extents(n) if b > a)
        self.fde_starts = [a for a, _ in self.fdes]
        self.jt_cache = {}
        self.setjmps = self.setjmp_targets()
        self.sites, self.patches = {}, {}  # (main: tools/game_sites.py, tools/patches.py)
        self.locals = locals_  # Locals, or None: registers and flags stay in the Cpu
        self.entry_flags = {}  # (_entry_flags)

    def in_text(self, a):
        return self.lo <= a < self.hi and a % 4 == 0

    def fde(self, a):
        """(start, end) of the eh_frame function holding a, or None (code without unwind info)."""
        i = bisect.bisect_right(self.fde_starts, a) - 1
        if i >= 0 and a < self.fdes[i][1]:
            return self.fdes[i]
        return None

    def word(self, a):
        return self.words[(a - self.lo) // 4]

    def setjmp_targets(self):
        """Addresses whose call is a call to setjmp: the function itself (a module defining it) and the PLT stubs
        bound to it (adrp x16; ldr x17, [x16, #o]; add x16, x16, #o; br x17 through a JUMP_SLOT slot of it)."""
        n, b = self.nso, self.base
        out = {b + v for s, info, shndx, v, size in n.syms if shndx and s in SETJMP_SYMS}
        slots = {b + off for off, typ, si, add in n.relocs
                 if typ == R_AARCH64_JUMP_SLOT and si < len(n.syms) and n.syms[si][0] in SETJMP_SYMS}
        if not slots:
            return out
        for a in range(self.lo, self.hi - 12, 4):
            w = self.word(a)
            if (w & 0x9F00001F) != 0x90000010 or self.word(a + 12) != 0xD61F0220:  # adrp x16 ... br x17
                continue
            ld = self.word(a + 4)
            if (ld & 0xFFC003FF) != 0xF9400211:  # ldr x17, [x16, #imm]
                continue
            page = sext(((w >> 29) & 3) | ((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2, 21) << 12
            if (a & ~0xFFF) + page + ((ld >> 10) & 0xFFF) * 8 in slots:
                out.add(a)
        return out

    def lift(self, a):
        ins = self.cache.get(a)
        if ins is None:
            try:
                ins = self.lifter.lift(self.word(a), a)
            except Unsupported as e:
                self.stats['unsupported'] += 1
                ins = Insn('trap', f'rt_udf(c, {hx(a)}); /* {e} */')
            self.cache[a] = ins
        return ins

    def boundaries(self):
        n, b = self.nso, self.base
        starts = set()
        for a in eh_frame_functions(n):
            starts.add(b + a)
        for name, info, shndx, value, size in n.syms:
            if shndx and (info & 0xF) == 2:
                starts.add(b + value)
        for off, typ, sym, add in n.relocs:
            if typ == R_AARCH64_RELATIVE:
                starts.add(b + add)
        starts = sorted(a for a in starts if self.in_text(a))
        return starts

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ jump tables

    def emu(self):
        if self.mu is None:
            mu = uc.Uc(uc.UC_ARCH_ARM64, uc.UC_MODE_ARM)
            n = self.nso
            mu.mem_map(self.base, len(n.image))
            mu.mem_write(self.base, bytes(n.image))
            mu.mem_map(SCRATCH_MEM, 0x100000)
            mu.reg_write(A.UC_ARM64_REG_CPACR_EL1, 0x300000)

            # a load before the index is set (often the one that fetches the index) can go through a register
            # nothing set: it reads zeros instead of stopping the emulation
            def zero_page(mu, access, addr, size, value, data):
                try:
                    mu.mem_map(addr & ~0xFFF, 0x1000)
                except uc.UcError:
                    return False
                return True
            mu.hook_add(uc.UC_HOOK_MEM_READ_UNMAPPED | uc.UC_HOOK_MEM_WRITE_UNMAPPED, zero_page)
            self.mu = mu
        return self.mu

    def jump_table(self, br_pc, entry, end):
        """Resolve `br xN` targets from a bounds-checked jump table, or None. The table's base, its index
        math and its targets can be anywhere in the function the br belongs to (its eh_frame range), also
        outside the piece entry..end that discovery made of it; code without an FDE is just entry..end."""
        lo, hi = self.fde(br_pc) or (entry, end)
        key = (br_pc, lo, hi)
        if key not in self.jt_cache:  # (discovery scans a piece again each time it is split)
            r = self._jump_table_fallthrough(br_pc, lo, hi)
            if r is None:
                r = self._jump_table_taken(br_pc, lo, hi)
            self.jt_cache[key] = r
        return self.jt_cache[key]

    def _index_regs(self, start, at, idx):
        """The index register plus registers holding the same value in start..at: sources it was
        copied/masked from, and copies of those (the table lookup sometimes recomputes the index
        from another copy after the bounds check)."""
        def copy_src(w):
            if (w & 0x7F800000) == 0x12000000:  # AND (imm)
                return bits(w, 5, 5)
            if (w & 0x7FE0FFE0) == 0x2A0003E0:  # MOV (ORR with zr)
                return bits(w, 16, 5)
            if (w & 0x7F800000) in (0x53000000, 0x13000000):  # UBFM/SBFM (uxtb, uxth, sxtw...)
                return bits(w, 5, 5)
            return None
        regs = {idx}
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            for a in range(start, at, 4):
                w = self.word(a)
                rd, src = w & 31, copy_src(w)
                if src is None or src >= 31 or rd >= 31:
                    continue
                for x, y in ((rd, src), (src, rd)):
                    if x in regs and y not in regs:
                        regs.add(y)
                        changed = True
        return sorted(regs)

    def _set_index(self, mu, regs, i):
        for r in regs:
            mu.reg_write(A.UC_ARM64_REG_X0 + r if r < 29 else A.UC_ARM64_REG_X29, i)

    def _sets_flags(self, a):
        ins = self.lift(a)
        if ins.kind == 'asm':
            return ins.asm.flags
        return ins.kind == 'op' and re.search(r'\b(adds|subs|adcs|sbcs|logic)\d+\(|nzcv', ins.code) is not None

    # Whether code reads the flags it is entered with (from PR #324 by Hiorac, "Recompiled code: flags in a local where
    # only the function can see them"). gen.py --locals uses it to publish the flags before a call only to a callee
    # that reads them, and at a tail exit only when the code jumped to may read them before it sets them.
    def _reads_flags(self, a):
        ins = self.lift(a)
        text = ins.cond if ins.kind == 'bcond' else ins.code if ins.kind == 'op' else ''
        return FLAG_READ.search(text) is not None

    def _entry_flags(self, a, unknown, depth=4):
        """Does the code at a read the flags before setting them? A call or a return ends the search with no: the
        AArch64 calling convention keeps no flags across them. unknown: the answer where the code can't be followed."""
        key = a, unknown, depth
        if key not in self.entry_flags:
            self.entry_flags[key] = self._find_flag_use(a, unknown, depth)
        return self.entry_flags[key]

    def _find_flag_use(self, a, unknown, depth):
        for _ in range(32):
            if not self.in_text(a) or a in self.patches:
                return unknown
            if self._reads_flags(a):
                return True
            if self._sets_flags(a):
                return False
            ins = self.lift(a)
            if ins.kind in ('bl', 'blr', 'ret', 'trap'):
                return False
            if ins.kind == 'br' or ins.kind == 'asm':
                return unknown
            if ins.kind == 'b':
                a = ins.target
                continue
            if ins.kind == 'bcond':  # (cbz, tbz: a flag test is a read, above)
                if depth == 0 or self._entry_flags(ins.target, unknown, depth - 1):
                    return True if depth else unknown
            a += 4
        return unknown

    def _guard_cmp(self, guard, lo):
        """The `cmp idx, #imm` that sets the flags a bounds check at guard tests, or None. Only straight-line
        code without other flag writes may come in between (cbz/tbz included: the compiler interleaves them)."""
        a = guard - 4
        while a >= lo and guard - a <= 4 * 12:
            w = self.word(a)
            if (w & 0x7F80001F) == 0x7100001F:  # SUBS (imm) with Rd = zr, i.e. CMP #imm
                return None if bits(w, 22, 1) else a
            if self.lift(a).kind not in ('op', 'asm', 'bcond') or self._sets_flags(a):
                return None
            a -= 4
        return None

    def _emulate_table(self, br_pc, lo, hi, start, set_at, idx_regs, count):
        """Run start..br once per index value (set in idx_regs on reaching set_at) and collect the br
        targets, which must lie in lo..hi. The window is straight-line code where a conditional branch falls
        through (the in-bounds path). First replays the address materialization (ADRP/ADR/ADD-imm) from the
        function entry lo, so table bases computed before loops or branches are known."""
        mu = self.emu()
        rn = bits(self.word(br_pc), 5, 5)
        targets = []
        try:
            for r in range(29):
                mu.reg_write(A.UC_ARM64_REG_X0 + r, SCRATCH_MEM + 0x80000)
            mu.reg_write(A.UC_ARM64_REG_SP, SCRATCH_MEM + 0x80000)
            for a in range(lo, start, 4):
                w = self.word(a)
                if (w & 0x1F000000) == 0x10000000 or (w & 0xFF800000) == 0x91000000:
                    mu.emu_start(a, 0, count=1)
            ctx = mu.context_save()  # (the replay doesn't depend on the index: once per table)
            for i in range(count):
                mu.context_restore(ctx)
                for a in range(start, br_pc, 4):
                    if a == set_at:
                        self._set_index(mu, idx_regs, i)
                    k = self.lift(a).kind
                    if k == 'bcond':
                        continue
                    if k not in ('op', 'asm'):
                        return None
                    mu.emu_start(a, 0, count=1)  # (single steps: Unicorn's `until` is unreliable mid translation block)
                t = mu.reg_read(A.UC_ARM64_REG_X0 + rn if rn < 29 else
                                (A.UC_ARM64_REG_X29 if rn == 29 else A.UC_ARM64_REG_X30))
                if not (lo <= t < hi) or t % 4:
                    return None
                targets.append(t)
        except uc.UcError:
            return None
        if count > 1 and len(set(targets)) == 1:  # (the index set wasn't the one the table is read with)
            return None
        return sorted(set(targets))

    def _jump_table_taken(self, br_pc, lo, hi):
        """Form: cmp idx, #N ; b.ls/b.lo table ... table: <address math> ; br"""
        # start of the block holding the br
        s = br_pc
        while s - 4 >= lo and br_pc - (s - 4) <= 4 * 12 and self.lift(s - 4).kind in ('op', 'asm'):
            s -= 4
        for g in range(lo, hi, 4):
            w = self.word(g)
            if (w & 0xFF000010) != 0x54000000 or bits(w, 0, 4) not in (9, 3):
                continue
            t = g + sext(bits(w, 5, 19), 19) * 4
            if t != s:
                continue
            cmp = self._guard_cmp(g, lo)
            if cmp is None:
                continue
            limit = bits(self.word(cmp), 10, 12)
            count = limit + 1 if bits(w, 0, 4) == 9 else limit
            if count <= 0 or count > 4096:
                continue
            return self._emulate_table(br_pc, lo, hi, s, s, [bits(self.word(cmp), 5, 5)], count)
        return None

    def _jump_table_fallthrough(self, br_pc, lo, hi):
        """Form: cmp idx, #N ; b.hi/b.hs default ; <address math> ; br"""
        # find the guarding b.hi / b.hs, scanning backwards
        a = br_pc - 4
        guard = None
        while a >= lo and br_pc - a <= 4 * 32:
            w = self.word(a)
            if (w & 0xFF000010) == 0x54000000 and bits(w, 0, 4) in (8, 2):
                guard = a
                break
            if self.lift(a).kind not in ('op', 'asm', 'bcond'):
                return None
            a -= 4
        if guard is None:
            return None
        cmp = self._guard_cmp(guard, lo)
        if cmp is None:
            return None
        w = self.word(cmp)
        limit = bits(w, 10, 12)
        count = limit + 1 if bits(self.word(guard), 0, 4) == 8 else limit
        if count <= 0 or count > 4096:
            return None
        # window start: back from cmp to the first control-flow instruction
        start = cmp
        while start - 4 >= lo and cmp - (start - 4) <= 4 * 12 and self.lift(start - 4).kind in ('op', 'asm'):
            start -= 4
        return self._emulate_table(br_pc, lo, hi, start, cmp, self._index_regs(start, cmp, bits(w, 5, 5)), count)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ functions

    def writes_gpr(self, a, rn):
        """True if the instruction at a writes general register rn (Xn or Wn). Its low 5 bits don't tell: they are
        also the register a store stores (`stp s9, s8, [sp, #0x80]`) and FP/SIMD destinations."""
        if self.cs is None:
            self.cs = capstone.Cs(capstone.CS_ARCH_ARM64, capstone.CS_MODE_ARM)
            self.cs.detail = True
        ins = next(self.cs.disasm(struct.pack('<I', self.word(a)), a), None)
        if ins is None:
            return True  # (undecoded: stop there, as for a write)
        return any(ins.reg_name(r) in (f'x{rn}', f'w{rn}') for r in ins.regs_access()[1])

    def computed_target(self, br_pc, entry):
        """True if the br register comes from address arithmetic (a table) rather than a load."""
        rn = bits(self.word(br_pc), 5, 5)
        a = br_pc - 4
        while a >= entry and br_pc - a <= 4 * 16:
            w = self.word(a)
            if self.lift(a).kind not in ('op', 'asm'):
                return False
            if self.writes_gpr(a, rn):
                if (w & 0x1F000000) == 0x0B000000:  # ADD/SUB (shifted or extended register)
                    return True
                if (w & 0x9F000000) == 0x10000000:  # ADR
                    return True
                return False
            a -= 4
        return False

    def scan(self, entry, end):
        """Collect labels and external entries referenced by a function."""
        labels, ext, tables = {entry}, set(), {}
        terminated = False
        for a in range(entry, end, 4):
            ins = self.lift(a)
            if ins.kind in ('b', 'bcond'):
                t = ins.target
                if entry <= t < end:
                    labels.add(t)
                elif self.in_text(t):
                    ext.add(t)
            elif ins.kind == 'bl':
                if self.in_text(ins.target):
                    ext.add(ins.target)
            elif ins.kind == 'br':
                jt = self.jump_table(a, entry, end)
                if jt:
                    tables[a] = jt
                    # (a target outside this piece of a split function is a boundary, reached by a tail call)
                    for t in jt:
                        (labels if entry <= t < end else ext).add(t)
                elif self.computed_target(a, (self.fde(a) or (entry,))[0]):
                    # unresolved table jump: allow jumping to any instruction of the function
                    tables[a] = 'all'
            terminated = ins.kind in ('b', 'br', 'ret', 'trap')
        if not terminated and end < self.hi:
            ext.add(end)
        return labels, ext, tables

    def render_single(self, ins, a, jump, refs):
        """C for one lifted instruction (no batching); used for patch variants."""
        k = ins.kind
        if k == 'asm':
            return [emit_asm_batch([ins.asm])]
        if k in ('op', 'trap'):
            return [ins.code]
        if k == 'b':
            return [jump(ins.target)]
        if k == 'bcond':
            return [f'if ({ins.cond}) {{ {jump(ins.target)} }}']
        if k == 'bl':
            t = ins.target
            if t in self.setjmps:
                refs.add(t)
                return [setjmp_call(t, a + 4)]
            if self.in_text(t):
                refs.add(t)
                return [f'c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {fname(t)}(c);']
            return [f'c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; c->pc = {hx(t)}; rt_dispatch(c);']
        if k == 'blr':
            return [f'c->pc = {ins.target}; c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; rt_dispatch(c);']
        if k == 'br':
            return [f'c->pc = {ins.target}; __attribute__((musttail)) return rt_dispatch(c);']
        if k == 'ret':
            return ['return;']
        raise Unsupported(k)

    def emit_function(self, entry, end, labels, tables, hle):
        if entry in hle:
            self._refs = set()
            return [f'void {fname(entry)}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    {sanitize(hle[entry])}(c);', '}']
        # Jump tables are emulated (jump_table), so their cases are known; one whose emulation missed some still
        # reaches the right instruction through the all-instruction fallback: a label on every instruction and a
        # switch over all of them. With an unresolved table ('all') that is the function's normal path. Otherwise
        # it lives in a cold copy of the function (<name>_r), entered on a miss only: in the function itself it
        # split every instruction into its own block and made LLVM's register coalescer take minutes per function.
        refs = set()
        if not tables or 'all' in tables.values():
            out = self._emit_body(entry, end, labels, tables, refs, 'plain')
        else:
            out = [f'static void {fname(entry)}_r(Cpu *c);']
            out += self._emit_body(entry, end, labels, tables, refs, 'fast')
            out += self._emit_body(entry, end, labels, tables, refs, 'resume')
        self._refs = refs
        return out

    def _flow(self, entry, end, tables):
        """Successors of each instruction of entry..end inside it (gen.py --locals). Index n = (end - entry) / 4 stands
        for falling through into the next function and has none. A patch site goes on to the next instruction and to
        the labels its C jumps to."""
        def idx(t):
            return [(t - entry) // 4] if entry <= t < end else []

        succ = []
        for i, a in enumerate(range(entry, end, 4)):
            ins = self.lift(a)
            k = ins.kind
            if a in self.patches:
                text = self.patches[a](self, a)
                succ.append([i + 1] + [t for g in re.findall(r'goto L_([0-9a-f]+);', text) for t in idx(int(g, 16))])
            elif k in ('op', 'asm', 'bl', 'blr'):
                succ.append([i + 1])
            elif k == 'b':
                succ.append(idx(ins.target))
            elif k == 'bcond':
                succ.append(idx(ins.target) + [i + 1])
            elif k == 'br':
                jt = tables.get(a)
                succ.append([t for x in jt for t in idx(x)] if jt and jt != 'all' else [])
            else:  # ret, trap
                succ.append([])
        succ.append([])
        return succ

    def _flag_plan(self, entry, end, tables, succ):
        """tools/flags.py plan of entry..end over the flow succ (_flow)."""
        n = (end - entry) // 4
        # (a fall into the next function, or a tail branch, publishes only if the code there can read them first)
        mems, effects, exits = set(), [], {n} if end >= self.hi or self._entry_flags(end, True) else set()
        for i, a in enumerate(range(entry, end, 4)):
            ins = self.lift(a)
            k = ins.kind
            if a in self.patches:
                mems.add(i)
                exits.add(i)   # (its C sees the Cpu's flags: they are published before it)
                effects.append((False, None))
                continue
            if k in ('bl', 'blr'):
                mems.add(i)
                if k == 'bl' and self._entry_flags(ins.target, False):
                    exits.add(i)   # (a callee that reads the flags it is handed: none in BOTW 1.9.0, AAPCS64 has none)
            elif k in ('b', 'bcond') and not entry <= ins.target < end:
                if not self.in_text(ins.target) or self._entry_flags(ins.target, True):
                    exits.add(i)
            elif k == 'br':
                exits.add(i)   # through rt_dispatch, a table's miss or its cases outside the function
            effects.append(flags.effect(ins.cond if k == 'bcond' else ins.code or ''))
        effects.append((False, None))
        return flags.plan(effects, succ, mems, exits)

    def _emit_body(self, entry, end, labels, tables, refs, mode):
        """One C function for entry..end. mode: 'plain' (the all-instruction fallback inside when it has tables),
        'fast' (a table miss goes on in <name>_r) or 'resume' (<name>_r: from c->pc, through that fallback)."""
        if mode == 'resume':
            # (optnone: optimized, its switch made the copy as slow to build as the function used to be, and it is
            # never run in practice. Unoptimized, its frame can reach ~250 KB: guest threads have 256 MB host stacks)
            head = f'__attribute__((cold, noinline, optnone)) static void {fname(entry)}_r(Cpu *c) {{'
            out = [head, '    goto L_dispatch;']
        else:
            out = [f'void {fname(entry)}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    FN_ENTER({hx(entry)});']
        all_labels = mode == 'resume' or (mode == 'plain' and bool(tables))
        # Registers and flags in locals (tools/regs.py, tools/flags.py; gen.py --locals): not where the all-instruction
        # fallback switches on c->pc to any instruction, nor around FP/SIMD inline asm, which works on the Cpu.
        local = (self.locals is not None and not all_labels
                 and not any(self.lift(a).kind == 'asm' for a in range(entry, end, 4)))
        spill, reload, reload_call = (regs.SPILL, regs.RELOAD, regs.RELOAD_CALL) if local else ('', '', '')
        opaque, end_opaque = (regs.OPAQUE, regs.END) if local else ('', '')
        succ = self._flow(entry, end, tables) if local else None
        fp = self._flag_plan(entry, end, tables, succ) if local else None
        fl = fp is not None and fp.used

        def fx(i, code):
            return fp.rewrite(i, code) if fl else code

        def publish(i):
            return fp.publish(i) if fl else ''

        def fload(i):
            return fp.reload(i) if fl else ''

        body = []  # (instruction index, or None for a label or an asm batch, line)
        batch = []

        def emit(i, line):
            body.append((i, line))

        def flush():
            if batch:
                emit(None, '    ' + emit_asm_batch(batch))
                batch.clear()

        def jump(t, i):
            if entry <= t < end:
                if local and t <= entry + 4 * i:
                    # A backward branch closes a loop. Guest spin waits poll memory with plain loads (`ldr w8, [x9];
                    # cmp w8, #1; b.eq`), which the hardware keeps fresh but C does not: with the registers in locals
                    # nothing in such a loop stores any more, and clang hoists the load and spins forever. Without
                    # locals the loop's own stores to the Cpu kept the load inside. The barrier keeps every load in
                    # its loop; locals are not memory, so they stay in registers.
                    return f'__asm__ volatile("" ::: "memory"); goto L_{t:x};'
                return f'goto L_{t:x};'
            if not self.in_text(t):
                return f'{publish(i)}{spill}c->pc = {hx(t)}; __attribute__((musttail)) return rt_dispatch(c);'
            refs.add(t)
            return f'{publish(i)}{spill}__attribute__((musttail)) return {fname(t)}(c);'

        if all_labels:
            labels = set(range(entry, end, 4))
        miss = f'__attribute__((musttail)) return {fname(entry)}_r(c);' if mode == 'fast' else 'goto L_dispatch;'
        last = None
        for i, a in enumerate(range(entry, end, 4)):
            ins = self.lift(a)
            if a in labels:
                flush()
                emit(None, f'L_{a:x}:;')
            if a in self.patches:  # hand-written replacement for one instruction (tools/patches.py)
                flush()
                text = self.patches[a](self, a)
                if local:
                    # it calls into the runtime with c, which may read and write any register: it runs on the Cpu,
                    # after a spill and with the flags published, and every register is loaded again after it,
                    # also where it jumps to a label
                    text = re.sub(r'goto (L_[0-9a-f]+);', lambda g: f'{{{reload}{fload(i)} goto {g.group(1)}; }}', text)
                    text = f'{spill}{publish(i)}{opaque}{text}{end_opaque}{reload}{fload(i)}'
                emit(i, '    ' + text)
                last = 'op'
                continue
            k = ins.kind
            if k == 'asm':
                if len(batch) >= 24:
                    flush()
                batch.append(ins.asm)
                try:
                    emit_asm_batch(batch)
                except Unsupported:
                    batch.pop()
                    flush()
                    batch.append(ins.asm)
                last = k
                continue
            flush()
            if k == 'op':
                code = fx(i, ins.code)
                emit(i, f'    {spill}{code}{reload}' if local and regs.ESCAPE.search(code) else '    ' + code)
            elif k == 'trap':
                emit(i, f'    {spill}{ins.code}')
            elif k == 'b':
                emit(i, '    ' + jump(ins.target, i))
            elif k == 'bcond':
                emit(i, f'    if ({fx(i, ins.cond)}) {{ {jump(ins.target, i)} }}')
            elif k == 'bl':
                t = ins.target
                if t in self.setjmps:
                    refs.add(t)
                    # (the longjmp lands in it with the registers the setjmp saved in the Cpu: all are loaded again)
                    emit(i, f'    {spill}{opaque}{setjmp_call(t, a + 4)}{end_opaque}{reload}{fload(i)}')
                elif self.in_text(t):
                    refs.add(t)
                    emit(i, f'    c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {publish(i)}{spill}{fname(t)}(c);{reload_call}{fload(i)}')
                else:
                    emit(i, f'    c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}c->pc = {hx(t)}; rt_dispatch(c);{reload_call}'
                            f'{fload(i)}')
            elif k == 'blr':
                emit(i, f'    c->pc = {ins.target}; c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}rt_dispatch(c);{reload_call}'
                        f'{fload(i)}')
            elif k == 'br':
                jt = tables.get(a)
                if jt == 'all':
                    emit(i, f'    c->pc = {ins.target}; goto L_dispatch;')
                    continue
                if jt:
                    cases = ' '.join(f'case {hx(t)}: {jump(t, i)}' for t in jt)
                    emit(i, f'    switch ({ins.target}) {{ {cases} default: break; }}')
                    emit(i, f'    {publish(i)}{spill}c->pc = {ins.target}; {miss}')
                    continue
                emit(i, f'    {publish(i)}{spill}c->pc = {ins.target}; __attribute__((musttail)) return rt_dispatch(c);')
            elif k == 'ret':
                emit(i, f'    {spill}return;')
            last = k
        flush()
        n = (end - entry) // 4
        if last not in ('b', 'br', 'ret', 'trap'):
            emit(n, '    ' + jump(end, n) if end < self.hi else f'    {spill}rt_udf(c, {hx(end)});')
        if local:
            texts = [''] * (n + 1)
            for i, line in body:
                if i is not None:
                    texts[i] += line
            clean = {i for i, a in enumerate(range(entry, end, 4))
                     if a in self.patches or self.lift(a).kind in ('bl', 'blr') or regs.RELOAD in texts[i]}
            rp = regs.plan(texts, succ, clean, self.locals.n, self.locals.kept)
            if fl:
                out.append('    ' + fp.decl())
                self.stats['local_flag_functions'] += 1
                self.stats['flag_reads_direct'] += sum(1 for k in fp.reader if k and k != 'nz')
                self.stats['flag_reads_packed'] += sum(1 for k in fp.reader if k == 'nz')
                self.stats['flag_reads_after_call'] += fp.after_call
                self.stats['flag_publishing_exits'] += sum(1 for k in fp.exit if k)
                self.stats['flag_loads_after_call'] += sum(fp.load)
            if rp.regs:
                out.append('    ' + rp.decl())
                self.stats['local_reg_functions'] += 1
                self.stats['reg_spills'] += sum(len(s) for s in rp.spill)
            out += [line if i is None else rp.resolve(i, line) for i, line in body]
        else:
            out += [line for _, line in body]
        if all_labels:
            out.append('L_dispatch:')
            cases = ' '.join(f'case {hx(t)}: goto L_{t:x};' for t in range(entry, end, 4))
            out.append(f'    switch (c->pc) {{ {cases} default: break; }}')
            out.append('    __attribute__((musttail)) return rt_dispatch(c);')
        out.append('}')
        return out


def single_with_locals(code, loc=None):
    """C body of a function made of one lifted instruction's C (code) and a tail exit, with the registers and flags
    in locals as gen.py --locals makes them (tools/test_lift.py, tools/test_simd.py --locals). The exit publishes the
    flags and spills the registers, so the Cpu after it is what the instruction alone leaves."""
    loc = loc or Locals()
    fp = flags.plan([flags.effect(code), (False, None)], [[1], []], set(), {1})
    body = fp.rewrite(0, code) if fp.used else code
    clean = set()
    if regs.ESCAPE.search(body):
        body = f'{regs.SPILL}{body}{regs.RELOAD}'
        clean.add(0)
    tail = (fp.publish(1) if fp.used else '') + regs.SPILL
    rp = regs.plan([body, tail], [[1], []], clean, loc.n, loc.kept)
    decl = (fp.decl() + ' ' if fp.used else '') + (rp.decl() + ' ' if rp.regs else '')
    return f'{decl}{rp.resolve(0, body)} {rp.resolve(1, tail)}'


def write_if_changed(path, text):
    """Leaves unchanged chunks untouched so make only recompiles what a patch affected."""
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            if f.read() == text:
                return
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    with open(path, 'w') as f:
        f.write(text)


def discover(m, starts):
    """Partition text into functions: address -> (end, labels, jump tables). Returns (entries, rounds)."""
    # Partition text into functions; any branch/call target outside its function becomes a new
    # boundary (splitting the containing function) until a fixpoint is reached.
    start_set = set(starts)
    for i, w in enumerate(m.words):
        if (w & 0xFC000000) == 0x94000000:
            t = m.lo + i * 4 + sext26(w) * 4
            if m.in_text(t):
                start_set.add(t)
    # Code addresses materialized in registers (callbacks, vtables built at runtime): ADR, or
    # ADRP followed shortly by ADD on the same register. One inside the function that takes it is a label
    # there instead, a jump table's base: as a boundary it would split the function away from its table.
    def own_label(pc, t):
        f = m.fde(pc)
        return f is not None and f[0] < t < f[1]

    adrp_regs = {}
    for i, w in enumerate(m.words):
        pc = m.lo + i * 4
        if (w & 0x9F000000) == 0x10000000:  # ADR
            imm = ((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2 | ((w >> 29) & 3)
            if imm & (1 << 20):
                imm -= 1 << 21
            if m.in_text(pc + imm) and not own_label(pc, pc + imm):
                start_set.add(pc + imm)
        elif (w & 0x9F000000) == 0x90000000:  # ADRP
            imm = ((w >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2 | ((w >> 29) & 3)
            if imm & (1 << 20):
                imm -= 1 << 21
            adrp_regs[w & 31] = ((pc & ~0xFFF) + (imm << 12), i)
        elif (w & 0xFFC00000) == 0x91000000:  # ADD (imm, 64-bit, no shift)
            rn, rd = (w >> 5) & 31, w & 31
            if rn in adrp_regs and i - adrp_regs[rn][1] <= 8:
                t = adrp_regs[rn][0] + ((w >> 10) & 0xFFF)
                if m.in_text(t) and not own_label(pc, t):
                    start_set.add(t)
    scanned = {}
    rounds = 0
    while True:
        rounds += 1
        order = sorted(start_set)
        new = set()
        for i, a in enumerate(order):
            end = order[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(order) else m.hi
            key = (a, end)
            if key not in scanned:
                scanned[key] = m.scan(a, end)
            new |= scanned[key][1] - start_set
        if not new:
            break
        start_set |= new
    entries = {}
    for i, a in enumerate(order):
        end = order[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(order) else m.hi
        labels, ext, tables = scanned[(a, end)]
        entries[a] = (end, labels, tables)
        # indirect branches of the final functions: jump tables resolved, all-labels fallback, plain dispatch
        for t in tables.values():
            m.stats['br_all_labels' if t == 'all' else 'jumptables'] += 1
        m.stats['br_dispatch'] += sum(m.lift(x).kind == 'br' for x in range(a, end, 4)) - len(tables)
    return entries, rounds


def main_sites(nso, base, opts):
    """(version, sites) of a main module (tools/game_sites.py); none with --no-sites"""
    if opts.no_sites:
        return '', {}
    return game_sites.for_module(nso, base, opts.any_version, lambda s: print(s, file=sys.stderr))


def generate(name, nso, base, outdir, opts, sites=None):
    t0 = time.time()
    loc = Locals(opts.reg_locals, not opts.no_callee_saved_trust) if opts.locals and opts.reg_locals >= 0 else None
    m = Module(name, nso, base, opts.simd, loc)
    if name == 'main':
        m.sites = sites if sites is not None else main_sites(m.nso, base, opts)[1]
        m.patches = patches.table(m.sites) if m.sites else {}
    starts = m.boundaries()
    hle = {}
    if opts.hle and os.path.exists(opts.hle):
        want = {l.strip() for l in open(opts.hle) if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')}
        for sym, info, shndx, value, size in m.nso.syms:
            if shndx and sym in want:
                hle[base + value] = sym

    entries, rounds = discover(m, starts)
    print(f'{name}: {len(starts)} boundaries, {len(entries)} functions, {rounds} rounds, {dict(m.stats)}, '
          f'{time.time() - t0:.0f}s', file=sys.stderr)

    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
    order = sorted(entries)
    if opts.limit:
        order = order[:opts.limit]
    nchunks = 0
    ci = 0
    pending = None  # (address, lines, refs) of a big function that starts the next file
    while ci < len(order) or pending:
        body, refs, size, fns = [], set(), 0, []
        while (pending or ci < len(order)) and len(fns) < opts.chunk and size < opts.chunk_bytes:
            if pending:
                a, lines, r = pending
                pending = None
            else:
                a = order[ci]
                ci += 1
                end, labels, tables = entries[a]
                lines = m.emit_function(a, end, labels, tables, hle)
                r = getattr(m, '_refs', set())
                m._refs = set()
            n = sum(len(l) + 1 for l in lines)
            if n > opts.big_fn and fns:  # (a big function gets a file of its own: they compile in parallel)
                pending = (a, lines, r)
                break
            body += lines
            size += n
            fns.append(a)
            refs |= r
            if n > opts.big_fn:
                break
        path = os.path.join(outdir, f'{name}_{nchunks:03d}.c')
        text = ['#include "cpu.h"\n' + ('#include "simd.h"\n' if m.lifter.sc else '')]
        if any('rt_setjmp_slot(' in l for l in body):
            text += ['#include <setjmp.h>\njmp_buf *rt_setjmp_slot(Cpu *c, uint64_t gbuf);\n']
        text += [f'void {fname(r)}(Cpu *c);\n' for r in sorted(refs)]
        text += [f'void {sanitize(hle[a])}(Cpu *c);\n' for a in sorted(set(hle) & set(fns))]
        text += ['\n'.join(body), '\n']
        write_if_changed(path, ''.join(text))
        nchunks += 1
        # (the start screen's setup reads these for its progress bar: runtime/gamebuild.c)
        print(f'{name}: progress {ci}/{len(order)} files {nchunks}', file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    for fn in os.listdir(outdir):  # an earlier run's extra chunks
        mm = re.fullmatch(re.escape(name) + r'_(\d{3})\.c', fn)
        if mm and int(mm.group(1)) >= nchunks:
            os.remove(os.path.join(outdir, fn))
    import io
    with io.StringIO() as f:
        f.write('#include "cpu.h"\n')
        for a in order:
            f.write(f'void {fname(a)}(Cpu *c);\n')
        # (a module without functions still gets its arrays: C has no empty initializer)
        f.write(f'const uint64_t {name}_fn_addrs[] = {{\n')
        f.write(',\n'.join(hx(a) for a in order) or '0')
        f.write('};\n')
        f.write(f'const GuestFn {name}_fn_ptrs[] = {{\n')
        f.write(',\n'.join(fname(a) for a in order) or '0')
        f.write('};\n')
        f.write(f'const uint64_t {name}_fn_count = {len(order)};\n')
        write_if_changed(os.path.join(outdir, f'{name}_table.c'), f.getvalue())
    if loc:
        st = {k: v for k, v in sorted(m.stats.items()) if k.startswith(('local_', 'flag_', 'reg_'))}
        print(f'{name}: locals {st}', file=sys.stderr)
    print(f'{name}: wrote {nchunks} chunks, {time.time() - t0:.0f}s total', file=sys.stderr)


def main():
    # a crash in native code (Unicorn, capstone, Python itself) leaves the Python stack in the log instead of nothing
    # (the setup copies the end of this log into savagewind.log: runtime/gamebuild.c). Not on Windows: there it also
    # writes a "Windows fatal exception: access violation" stack for each fault Unicorn raises and handles itself (a
    # dozen or more in a run that works), which reads like the crash; a real one still shows as the exit status.
    if sys.platform != 'win32':
        try:  # (only the Python stack: 3.14's C stack, without symbols, would push it out of the lines the setup keeps)
            faulthandler.enable(**({'c_stack': False} if sys.version_info >= (3, 14) else {}))
        except (AttributeError, RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError):  # (no stderr to write to)
            pass
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(usage=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument('name')  # a module (main, subsdk0..9, sdk), or layout / all
    ap.add_argument('input')  # its NSO; layout / all: the exefs folder
    ap.add_argument('paths', nargs='+')  # <layout.txt> <outdir>; layout / all: <outdir>
    ap.add_argument('--hle')
    ap.add_argument('--chunk', type=int, default=1500)  # functions per file at most
    ap.add_argument('--chunk-bytes', type=int, default=1500000)  # and about this much C (even compile times)
    ap.add_argument('--big-fn', type=int, default=100000)  # bytes of C from which a function gets its own file
    ap.add_argument('--limit', type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument('--any-version', action='store_true')  # (a main module of a version not supported yet)
    ap.add_argument('--no-sites', action='store_true')  # (made-up modules, tools/test_layout.py: no sites, no patches)
    ap.add_argument('--simd', choices=('asm', 'c'),
                    default='asm' if platform.machine().lower() in ('arm64', 'aarch64') else 'c')
    ap.add_argument('--locals', action='store_true')  # registers and flags in C locals (tools/regs.py, tools/flags.py)
    ap.add_argument('--reg-locals', type=int, default=regs.LOCALS)  # (with --locals) registers per function
    ap.add_argument('--no-callee-saved-trust', action='store_true')  # (with --locals) reload X19-X29, SP after calls
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if len(args.paths) != (1 if args.name in ('layout', 'all') else 2):
        ap.error('wrong number of arguments')

    try:
        if args.name in ('layout', 'all'):
            exefs, outdir = args.input, args.paths[0]
            lay = layout.checked(exefs)
            layout.show(lay)
            main_base = next(b for n, b, *_ in lay if n == 'main')
            version, sites = main_sites(Nso(os.path.join(exefs, 'main')), main_base, args)
            print(f'  game version {version}, {len(sites)} sites')
            layout.write(lay, outdir, (version, sites))
            if args.name == 'all':
                present = {n for n, *_ in lay}
                for n in layout.LOAD_ORDER:  # a module gone from the exefs: its old C would still be built in
                    if n not in present and os.path.isdir(os.path.join(outdir, n)):
                        shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(outdir, n))
                hle = args.hle
                for n, base, size, build_id in lay:
                    args.hle = hle if n != 'main' else None
                    generate(n, os.path.join(exefs, n), base, os.path.join(outdir, n), args,
                             sites if n == 'main' else None)
            return
        lay = {n: (b, i) for n, b, s, i in layout.read(args.paths[0])}
        if args.name not in lay:
            raise layout.LayoutError(f'{args.paths[0]} has no module {args.name}')
        base, build_id = lay[args.name]
        if header(args.input)['build_id'] != build_id:
            raise layout.LayoutError(f'{args.input} is not the {args.name} that {args.paths[0]} was made from')
        generate(args.name, args.input, base, args.paths[1], args)
    except (layout.LayoutError, game_sites.SiteError) as e:
        sys.exit(f'gen.py: {e}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

```

`tools/gen_launch_flags.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Launch options: the table of environment flags the start screen suggests (runtime/launch_flags_table.c).

Scans runtime/ for every "SAVAGEWIND_*" name the code passes to getenv() or to a helper such as env_int(), works out
what kind of value each takes, and joins that with tools/launch_flags_curated.txt (which flags can't be added from the
start screen, which are suggested first, and what each does in one line).

usage: tools/gen_launch_flags.py           write runtime/launch_flags_table.c
       tools/gen_launch_flags.py --check   exit 1 if the checked-in table is stale (make test-launch-flags)
       tools/gen_launch_flags.py --list    print the table as text

Kinds, from how the code reads the flag:
  switch  every read only asks "is it set?": any value turns it on, so it can only be turned off by removing it
  number  some read parses a number (atoi, env_int, ...): 0 can turn it off
  text    anything else (a path, a name, a mode word)
"""
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime', 'launch_flags_table.c')
CURATED = os.path.join(ROOT, 'tools', 'launch_flags_curated.txt')
SCAN_EXT = ('.c', '.h', '.cpp', '.m', '.mm')
SKIP = {'launch_flags_table.c'}  # (this table itself)

NAME = r'SAVAGEWIND_[A-Z0-9_]+'
LITERAL = re.compile(r'[(,]\s*"(' + NAME + r')"')
NUMERIC = re.compile(r'\b(atoi|atol|atoll|atof|strtol|strtoul|strtoll|strtoull|strtod|sscanf|env_int|env_factor|env_float|env_long)\b')
TEXTUSE = re.compile(r'\b(strcmp|strncmp|strcasecmp|strstr|strchr|strdup|snprintf|sprintf|fopen|open|stat|memcmp)\b')
# a read that only asks whether the flag is set
SWITCH_USES = [
    r'getenv\(\s*"{n}"\s*\)\s*(!=|==)\s*NULL',
    r'!\s*getenv\(\s*"{n}"\s*\)',
    r'\(\s*getenv\(\s*"{n}"\s*\)\s*[)&|?]',
    r'getenv\(\s*"{n}"\s*\)\s*(&&|\|\||\?)',
    r'\bENV\(\s*"{n}"\s*\)\s*(!=|==)\s*NULL',
]
DEV_WORDS = {'DUMP', 'DUMPS', 'DUMPWB', 'TRACE', 'LOG', 'PROF', 'GPUPROF', 'FNPROF', 'SHOT', 'DEBUG', 'DBG', 'TEST', 'SAMPLE',
             'WATCH', 'VERIFY', 'STATS', 'CSV', 'PROBE', 'TIMELINE', 'AT', 'VIEW', 'CHECKPOINTS', 'VALIDATION', 'COUNTER',
             'SCRIPT', 'SOLO', 'WAV', 'SCAN', 'REPORT', 'TEXDUMP', 'SCREENSHOT', 'SCREENSHOTS', 'DEV', 'CONTROL', 'CLOCK',
             'REBOOT', 'WINDOW', 'OPT', 'SEED', 'GLYPH', 'ONESHOT'}


def scan():
    names = {}  # name -> list of source lines that mention it as a literal
    for base, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime')):
        for f in sorted(files):
            if not f.endswith(SCAN_EXT) or f in SKIP:
                continue
            with open(os.path.join(base, f), encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as fh:
                for line in fh:
                    stripped = line.lstrip()
                    if stripped.startswith('//'):
                        continue
                    for m in LITERAL.finditer(line):
                        names.setdefault(m.group(1), []).append(line)
    return names


def kind_of(name, lines):
    if any(NUMERIC.search(l) for l in lines):
        return 'number'
    uses = [re.compile(p.format(n=name)) for p in SWITCH_USES]
    if all(any(u.search(l) for u in uses) and not TEXTUSE.search(l) for l in lines):
        return 'switch'
    return 'text'


def curated():
    out = {}
    with open(CURATED, encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        for n, line in enumerate(fh, 1):
            line = line.rstrip('\n')
            if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith('#'):
                continue
            head, _, rest = line.partition('|')
            parts = head.split()
            example, _, desc = rest.partition('|')
            if len(parts) != 2 or parts[0] not in ('internal', 'launcher', 'build', 'play') or not desc.strip():
                sys.exit('%s:%d: expected "group NAME | example | description"' % (CURATED, n))
            if parts[1] in out:
                sys.exit('%s:%d: %s is listed twice' % (CURATED, n, parts[1]))
            if '\u2014' in desc or '\u2013' in desc or ' - ' in desc:
                sys.exit('%s:%d: no dashes in descriptions' % (CURATED, n))
            out[parts[1]] = (parts[0], example.strip(), desc.strip())
    return out


def group_of(name, cur):
    if name in cur:
        return cur[name][0]
    words = set(name[len('SAVAGEWIND_'):].split('_'))
    return 'dev' if words & DEV_WORDS else 'other'


def cstr(s):
    return '"' + s.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"') + '"'


def build():
    found = scan()
    cur = curated()
    for n, (g, _, _) in cur.items():
        if g == 'play' and n not in found:
            sys.exit('%s lists %s as a play flag, but runtime/ no longer reads it' % (CURATED, n))
    rows = []
    for name in sorted(set(found) | set(cur)):
        g = group_of(name, cur)
        kind = kind_of(name, found[name]) if name in found else 'text'
        example, desc = (cur[name][1], cur[name][2]) if name in cur else ('', '')
        rows.append((name, kind, g, example, desc))
    lines = ['// Generated by tools/gen_launch_flags.py from runtime/ and tools/launch_flags_curated.txt. Do not edit by hand.',
             '// (make test-launch-flags fails when this is stale.)',
             '#include "launch_flags.h"', '',
             'const LfInfo LF_TABLE[] = {']
    for name, kind, g, example, desc in rows:
        lines.append('    {%s, LF_KIND_%s, LF_GROUP_%s, %s, %s},' % (cstr(name), kind.upper(), g.upper(), cstr(example), cstr(desc)))
    lines += ['};', 'const int LF_TABLE_N = %d;' % len(rows), '']
    return '\n'.join(lines), rows


def main():
    text, rows = build()
    if '--list' in sys.argv:
        for r in rows:
            print('%-8s %-8s %s' % (r[2], r[1], r[0]))
        return 0
    if '--check' in sys.argv:
        try:
            with open(OUT, encoding='utf-8') as fh:
                have = fh.read()
        except OSError:
            have = ''
        if have != text:
            print('runtime/launch_flags_table.c is stale: run python3 tools/gen_launch_flags.py', file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print('launch flag table is up to date (%d names)' % len(rows))
        return 0
    with open(OUT, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as fh:
        fh.write(text)
    print('wrote %s (%d names)' % (os.path.relpath(OUT, ROOT), len(rows)))
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

```

`tools/gen_place_table.py`:

```py
"""The place names of Discord Rich Presence, from your own game files: writes runtime/game_place_table.inc.

    python tools/gen_place_table.py extracted/romfs/Pack [runtime/game_place_table.inc]

The Makefile runs it: the table is the game's own text, so it is never committed. From Pack/Bootup.pack: the map's labels (Map/MainField/Location.smubin),
the places with an icon and the small landmarks (LocationMarker, LocationPointer in Map/MainField/Static.smubin), and
the tower regions (Ecosystem/MapTower.sbeco). From each language's Pack/Bootup_<language>.pack: their names.
"""
import os
import struct
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from botw_save_convert import Byml, sarc_files, yaz0_decompress

# How far from its point a name holds, by kind. The closest name relative to its radius wins, so a village's wide
# radius beats a hill's next to it, and a stable's short one only holds at the stable.
TOWN_ICONS = ('Village', 'Castle')  # inside these, their name beats any label nearby
MARKER_RADIUS = {'Village': 320, 'Castle': 420, 'Hatago': 130, 'CheckPoint': 170, 'Labo': 90, 'StartPoint': 120}
POINTER_RADIUS = 90
LABEL_RADIUS = {2: 750, 4: 380, 8: 210}  # by ShowLevel: the map's biggest labels are 2
LABEL_REGION_TYPE = 6  # (Eldin, Hebra...: the region line already says it)

# Each language's text the game has no message for: main menu, exploring, inside a shrine, Divine Beast, inside, and a
# shrine with no name of its own (Discord refuses a line of one character: 試練の祠, not 祠)
TEXTS = {
    'USen': ('In the main menu', 'Exploring', 'Inside a shrine', 'Divine Beast', 'Interior', 'Shrine'),
    'EUen': ('In the main menu', 'Exploring', 'Inside a shrine', 'Divine Beast', 'Interior', 'Shrine'),
    'USes': ('En el menú principal', 'Explorando', 'Interior de santuario', 'Bestia Divina', 'Interior', 'Santuario'),
    'EUes': ('En el menú principal', 'Explorando', 'Interior de santuario', 'Bestia Divina', 'Interior', 'Santuario'),
    'USfr': ('Au menu principal', 'Exploration', 'Dans un sanctuaire', 'Créature divine', 'Intérieur', 'Sanctuaire'),
    'EUfr': ('Au menu principal', 'Exploration', 'Dans un sanctuaire', 'Créature divine', 'Intérieur', 'Sanctuaire'),
    'EUde': ('Im Hauptmenü', 'Auf Erkundung', 'In einem Schrein', 'Titan', 'Innenraum', 'Schrein'),
    'EUit': ('Nel menu principale', 'In esplorazione', 'In un sacrario', 'Colosso sacro', 'Interno', 'Sacrario'),
    'EUnl': ('In het hoofdmenu', 'Op verkenning', 'In een tempel', 'Goddelijk beest', 'Interieur', 'Tempel'),
    'EUru': ('В главном меню', 'Исследует мир', 'В святилище', 'Чудище', 'Внутри', 'Святилище'),
    'USpt': ('No menu principal', 'Explorando', 'Em um santuário', 'Fera Divina', 'Interior', 'Santuário'),
    'JPja': ('メインメニュー', '探索中', '祠の中', '神獣', '屋内', '試練の祠'),
    'KRko': ('메인 메뉴', '탐험 중', '사당 내부', '신수', '실내', '사당'),
    'CNzh': ('主菜单', '探索中', '神庙内', '神兽', '室内', '神庙'),
    'TWzh': ('主選單', '探索中', '神廟內', '神獸', '室內', '神廟'),
    'THth': ('เมนูหลัก', 'กำลังสำรวจ', 'ภายในเทวสถาน', 'อสูรเทพ', 'ภายใน', 'เทวสถาน'),
}
LANGUAGES = list(TEXTS)

WORLD_X, WORLD_Z = 10000, 8000  # x -5000..5000, z -4000..4000
CELL = 100  # the region grid: 100 x 80 cells


def clean_text(s):
    """A message without its control tags (0x0e group tag size, then size bytes of data) and final NUL."""
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(s):
        if s[i] == '\x0e':
            i += 4 + ord(s[i + 3]) // 2
        elif s[i] == '\0':
            break
        elif s[i] == '\n':  # (a long name, broken to fit the map: a space, except between CJK characters)
            if out and out[-1] < '⺀':
                out.append(' ')
            i += 1
        else:
            out.append(s[i])
            i += 1
    return ''.join(out)


def msbt_texts(d):
    """{label: text} of an MSBT file."""
    if d[:8] != b'MsgStdBn':
        raise ValueError('not an MSBT file')
    nsec, = struct.unpack_from('<H', d, 0xE)
    sec, o = {}, 0x20
    for _ in range(nsec):
        size, = struct.unpack_from('<I', d, o + 4)
        sec[d[o:o + 4]] = d[o + 16:o + 16 + size]
        o = (o + 16 + size + 15) & ~15
    lbl, txt = sec[b'LBL1'], sec[b'TXT2']
    nbuckets, = struct.unpack_from('<I', lbl, 0)
    ntxt, = struct.unpack_from('<I', txt, 0)
    out = {}
    for b in range(nbuckets):
        n, off = struct.unpack_from('<II', lbl, 4 + 8 * b)
        for _ in range(n):
            ln = lbl[off]
            name = lbl[off + 1:off + 1 + ln].decode()
            idx, = struct.unpack_from('<I', lbl, off + 1 + ln)
            off += ln + 5
            start, = struct.unpack_from('<I', txt, 4 + 4 * idx)
            end = struct.unpack_from('<I', txt, 8 + 4 * idx)[0] if idx + 1 < ntxt else len(txt)
            out[name] = clean_text(txt[start:end].decode('utf-16le', 'replace'))
    return out


def tower_grid(d):
    """The tower area id at (x, z), from MapTower.sbeco: a row of runs (u16 area, u16 length) per 2 units of z, offsets
    to them in u16s."""
    magic, nrows, row_h, _ = struct.unpack_from('<4I', d, 0)
    if magic != 0x00112233:
        raise ValueError('not an ecosystem file')
    rows = 0x10 + 4 * nrows

    def area(x, z):
        row = min(max(int((z + WORLD_Z / 2) / row_h), 0), nrows - 1)
        o = rows + 2 * struct.unpack_from('<I', d, 0x10 + 4 * row)[0]
        left = min(max(int(x + WORLD_X / 2), 0), WORLD_X - 1)
        while True:
            a, n = struct.unpack_from('<HH', d, o)
            if left < n:
                return a
            left -= n
            o += 4
    return area


def region_name(tower):
    """"Torre del lago" -> "Lago"; "Torre de Hebra" -> "Hebra"; "Lake Tower" -> "Lake". Other languages build the name in
    too many ways (Hebra-Turm, Turm der Ebene): there it stays the tower's."""
    if tower.endswith(' Tower'):
        return tower[:-len(' Tower')]
    for p in ('Torre de las ', 'Torre de la ', 'Torre del ', 'Torre de '):
        if tower.startswith(p):
            s = tower[len(p):]
            return s[0].upper() + s[1:]
    return tower


def beast_name(name, word):
    """"Bestia divina Vah Ruta" -> "Vah Ruta"; the second line already says what it is."""
    return name[len(word) + 1:] if name.lower().startswith(word.lower() + ' ') else name


def c_str(s):
    return '"' + s.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"') + '"'


def c_row(texts):
    if min(len(t) for t in texts) < 2:
        sys.exit(f'a line of one character: {texts}')
    return '{' + ', '.join(c_str(t) for t in texts) + '}'


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    pack = sys.argv[1]
    out = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'runtime', 'game_place_table.inc')
    boot = sarc_files(open(os.path.join(pack, 'Bootup.pack'), 'rb').read())

    def byml(name):
        b = Byml(yaz0_decompress(boot[name]))
        return b._node(b.root)

    def location_names(region):
        lang = sarc_files(open(os.path.join(pack, f'Bootup_{region}.pack'), 'rb').read())
        msgs = sarc_files(yaz0_decompress(lang[f'Message/Msg_{region}.product.ssarc']))
        return msbt_texts(msgs['StaticMsg/LocationMarker.msbt'])

    texts = [location_names(language) for language in LANGUAGES]
    names = texts[0]

    def in_all(msg):
        return [t[msg] for t in texts]

    static = byml('Map/MainField/Static.smubin')
    places = []
    for m in static['LocationMarker']:
        r = MARKER_RADIUS.get(m.get('Icon'))
        if r and m.get('MessageID') in names:
            places.append((m['Translate']['X'], m['Translate']['Z'], r, m['MessageID'], m.get('Icon') in TOWN_ICONS))
    for p in static['LocationPointer']:
        if p.get('MessageID') in names:
            places.append((p['Translate']['X'], p['Translate']['Z'], POINTER_RADIUS, p['MessageID'], False))
    for l in byml('Map/MainField/Location.smubin'):
        if l['Type'] != LABEL_REGION_TYPE and l['MessageID'] in names:
            places.append((l['Translate']['X'], l['Translate']['Z'], LABEL_RADIUS[l['ShowLevel']], l['MessageID'], False))

    # The regions: each area of the grid is named by the tower that stands in it
    area = tower_grid(yaz0_decompress(boot['Ecosystem/MapTower.sbeco']))
    regions = {}
    for m in static['LocationMarker']:
        if m.get('Icon') == 'Tower':
            regions[area(m['Translate']['X'], m['Translate']['Z'])] = m['MessageID']
    if len(regions) != 15:
        sys.exit(f'{len(regions)} regions found, 15 towers expected')
    ids = sorted(regions)
    grid = []
    for row in range(WORLD_Z // CELL):
        z = -WORLD_Z / 2 + (row + 0.5) * CELL
        cells = [area(-WORLD_X / 2 + (col + 0.5) * CELL, z) for col in range(WORLD_X // CELL)]
        grid.append(''.join(chr(ord('a') + ids.index(a)) if a in regions else '.' for a in cells))

    # The interiors, by pack. The add-on content's shrines (120...) have no name in the game's own message files.
    interiors = []
    for k in range(120):
        interiors.append((f'Dungeon{k:03}', in_all(f'Dungeon{k:03}'), 'SHRINE'))
    for k in range(120, 137):
        interiors.append((f'Dungeon{k:03}', [TEXTS[language][5] for language in LANGUAGES], 'SHRINE'))
    for pack_name in ('RemainsWater', 'RemainsFire', 'RemainsWind', 'RemainsElectric'):
        interiors.append((pack_name, [beast_name(t[pack_name], TEXTS[language][3]) for language, t in zip(LANGUAGES, texts)], 'BEAST'))
    interiors.append(('FinalTrial', in_all('FinalTrial'), 'TRIAL'))

    with open(out, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        f.write('// Made by tools/gen_place_table.py from the game files: do not edit.\n')
        f.write('static const char *const place_languages[PLACE_LANGUAGES] = {' + ', '.join(c_str(l) for l in LANGUAGES) + '};\n\n')
        f.write('// main menu, exploring, inside a shrine, Divine Beast, inside\n')
        f.write('static const char *const place_texts[PLACE_LANGUAGES][5] = {\n')
        for language in LANGUAGES:
            f.write(f'    {c_row(TEXTS[language][:5])},\n')
        f.write('};\n\nstatic const PlaceEntry place_table[] = {\n')
        for x, z, r, msg, town in sorted(places, key=lambda p: (p[0], p[1])):
            f.write(f'    {{{x:.0f}, {z:.0f}, {r}, {str(town).lower()}, {c_row(in_all(msg))}}},\n')
        f.write('};\n\nstatic const char *const region_names[][PLACE_LANGUAGES] = {\n')
        for i in ids:
            f.write(f'    {c_row([region_name(t) for t in in_all(regions[i])])},\n')
        f.write('};\n\n// A row per 100 units of z from -4000, a cell per 100 of x from -5000: a letter of region_names, . none\n')
        f.write(f'static const char region_grid[{len(grid)}][{len(grid[0]) + 1}] = {{\n')
        for g in grid:
            f.write(f'    "{g}",\n')
        f.write('};\n\nstatic const InteriorEntry interior_table[] = {\n')
        for pack_name, row, kind in interiors:
            f.write(f'    {{{c_str(pack_name)}, {c_row(row)}, INTERIOR_{kind}}},\n')
        f.write('};\n')
    print(f'{len(places)} places, {len(ids)} regions, {len(interiors)} interiors -> {out}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
