`tools/gen_places.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regenerate runtime/control_places_data.inc, the table behind `goto shrine 5`, `goto korok H23`, `goto stable ...`.

The coordinates are the game's own world coordinates (the same frame as `pos`), taken from the data behind the ZeldaMods
object map (https://objmap.zeldamods.org, https://github.com/zeldamods/objmap):
  game_files/map_summary/MainField/static.json   shrines, towers, villages, stables, Koroks (marker positions)
  game_files/text/StaticMsg/*.json               English names
  radar.zeldamods.org /objs/MainField/           the LocationTag object of each marker (the marker icons float above the
                                                 ground, the tag sits where the place really is)

Where the game has a start position for a place (shrine entrances, towers, goddess statues, ...) that is used instead, because
it is a spot Link can stand on (tools/places_startpos.json, see tools/dump_startpos.py).

Run it when you want newer data; it needs network access and only the Python standard library:
  python3 tools/gen_places.py [--out runtime/control_places_data.inc]
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

GAME_FILES = "https://objmap.zeldamods.org/game_files"
RADAR = "https://radar.zeldamods.org"

# The game's own start positions (tools/places_startpos.json, made by tools/dump_startpos.py from your game files) are where
# Link really stands, so they win over the map data for every place that has one. Key of the place -> name of the StartPos.
START_OF = {
    "ForestHatago": "OldKorok_ForestStable",
    "NorthHatelHatago": "OldKorok_WetlandsStable",
    "RiverSideHatago": "OldKorok_RiversideStable",
    "FaronHatago000": "Hatago_Ch",
    "TamourHatago": "HigakkareBF_Goal",
    "Gerudo": "Gerudo001",
    "Goron": "GoddessGoron",
    "Hateno": "GoddessHateno",
    "Kakariko": "GoddessKakariko",
    "Cokiri": "GoddessKorok",
    "Taura": "GoddessUotori",
    "Rito": "GoddessRito",
    "UMiiVillage": "GoddessIchikara",
    "WhiteZora": "GoddessZora",
    "AncientLabo": "WarpAkkareLabo",
    "ValleyVillage": "ParashawlTalk",
    "HatenoLabo": "WarpHatenoLabo",
    "HyruleCastle": "HyruleCastleExit",
    "Oasis": "Oasis001",
}
START_OF.update({"Dungeon%03d" % n: "StartPos_CDungeon%03d" % n for n in range(120)})  # (the DLC shrines have none)
START_OF.update({"Tower%02d" % n: "StartPos_Tower%02d" % n for n in range(1, 16)})
START_NAMES = set(START_OF.values())
START_FILE = Path(__file__).with_name("places_startpos.json")
# Places with no start position of the game (the DLC shrines, a few landmarks): the map marker floats, sometimes 100 above the
# ground. tools/places_measured.json holds the height Link really stood at after `goto` dropped him from the marker
# (measured in a running game with tools/check_places.py, plus 1), so these places get the same small lift as the rest.
MEASURED_FILE = Path(__file__).with_name("places_measured.json")
START_MAX_OFF = 450.0  # a start position further than this from the map data's idea of the place is some other spot


def fetch_json(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "swr-gen-places"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        return json.load(r)


def location_tag(message_id):
    """Position of the LocationTag with this message id, or None."""
    url = RADAR + "/objs/MainField/?q=" + urllib.parse.quote(message_id)
    for o in fetch_json(url):
        if o.get("name") == "LocationTag" and o.get("messageid") == message_id:
            return o["pos"]
    return None


def c_str(s):
    return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'


def grid_key(name):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"([A-Z])-(\d+)", name)
    return (m.group(1), int(m.group(2))) if m else (name, 0)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="runtime/control_places_data.inc")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    markers = fetch_json(GAME_FILES + "/map_summary/MainField/static.json")["markers"]
    loc_names = fetch_json(GAME_FILES + "/text/StaticMsg/LocationMarker.json")
    dungeon_names = fetch_json(GAME_FILES + "/text/StaticMsg/Dungeon.json")

    # Each entry: kind, number (0 = assigned by order), key, name, sub, position, source of the position
    entries = []

    def add(kind, number, key, name, sub, pos, ground_tag):
        entries.append({"kind": kind, "number": number, "key": key, "name": name, "sub": sub, "pos": pos, "tag": ground_tag})

    # Everything that has a message id also has a LocationTag in the world; fetch them all in parallel.
    ids = [m["MessageID"] for k in ("Dungeon", "Place", "Labo") for m in markers[k]]
    ids += [m["MessageID"] for m in markers["Tower"]]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as pool:
        tags = dict(zip(ids, pool.map(location_tag, ids)))

    def position(m, prefer_tag):
        t = tags.get(m["MessageID"]) if prefer_tag else None
        tr = m["Translate"]
        return (t, True) if t else ([tr["X"], tr["Y"], tr["Z"]], False)

    for m in markers["Dungeon"]:
        mid = m["MessageID"]
        n = int(mid.replace("Dungeon", ""))
        pos, tag = position(m, True)
        add("shrine", n, mid, dungeon_names[mid], dungeon_names.get(mid + "_sub", ""), pos, tag)
    for m in markers["Tower"]:
        # The tower's marker sits on the top platform, its tag at the foot inside the tower: use the marker.
        pos, tag = position(m, False)
        add("tower", int(m["MessageID"].replace("Tower", "")), m["MessageID"], loc_names[m["MessageID"]], "", pos, tag)
    for m in markers["Place"]:
        pos, tag = position(m, True)
        kind = {"Hatago": "stable", "Village": "village"}.get(m["Icon"], "landmark")
        add(kind, 0, m["MessageID"], loc_names[m["MessageID"]], "", pos, tag)
    for m in markers["Labo"]:
        pos, tag = position(m, True)
        add("landmark", 0, m["MessageID"], loc_names[m["MessageID"]], "", pos, tag)

    # Koroks: the game's ids (A01 ... Z99) are unique; number them in map grid order, then id
    for m in sorted(markers["Korok"], key=lambda k: (grid_key(k["map_name"]), k["id"])):
        tr = m["Translate"]
        add("korok", 0, m["id"], m["id"], m["map_name"], [tr["X"], tr["Y"], tr["Z"]], False)

    order = ["shrine", "tower", "stable", "village", "landmark", "korok"]
    out = []
    for kind in order:
        group = [e for e in entries if e["kind"] == kind]
        if kind in ("stable", "village", "landmark"):
            group.sort(key=lambda e: e["name"].lower())
        elif kind in ("shrine", "tower"):
            group.sort(key=lambda e: e["number"])
        for i, e in enumerate(group, 1):
            e["number"] = e["number"] if kind in ("shrine", "tower") else i
            out.append(e)

    # The game's own start positions replace the map data where there are any.
    starts = json.load(open(START_FILE)) if START_FILE.exists() else {}
    used = 0
    for e in out:
        s = starts.get(START_OF.get(e["key"], ""))
        if not s:
            continue
        off = ((s[0] - e["pos"][0]) ** 2 + (s[2] - e["pos"][2]) ** 2) ** 0.5
        if off > START_MAX_OFF:
            print("warning: %s: start position %s is %.0f away from the map data, not used" % (e["key"], START_OF[e["key"]], off), file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        e["pos"], e["tag"], e["ground"] = list(s), True, True
        used += 1
    print("start positions of the game used for %d places" % used, file=sys.stderr)

    measured = json.load(open(MEASURED_FILE)) if MEASURED_FILE.exists() else {}
    for e in out:
        m = measured.get(e["key"])
        if m and not e.get("ground"):
            e["pos"], e["ground"] = [e["pos"][0], m["y"], e["pos"][2]], True
    print("measured ground height used for %d places" % sum(1 for e in out if e["key"] in measured and e.get("ground")), file=sys.stderr)

    missing = [e["key"] for e in out if e["kind"] in ("shrine", "stable", "village") and not e["tag"]]
    if missing:
        print("warning: no LocationTag for", ", ".join(missing), "(marker position used, it floats above the ground)", file=sys.stderr)

    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
        f.write("// Generated by tools/gen_places.py, do not edit.\n")
        f.write("// Game world coordinates (the frame of `pos`) from the ZeldaMods object map data (https://objmap.zeldamods.org).\n")
        f.write("// PLACE(kind, number, key, name, sub, x, y, z, ground)\n")
        for e in out:
            x, y, z = e["pos"]
            f.write("PLACE(PLACE_%s, %d, %s, %s, %s, %.2ff, %.2ff, %.2ff, %s)\n" % (
                e["kind"].upper(), e["number"], c_str(e["key"]), c_str(e["name"]), c_str(e["sub"]), x, y, z,
                "true" if e.get("ground") else "false"))
    counts = {k: sum(1 for e in out if e["kind"] == k) for k in order}
    print("wrote %s: %s" % (args.out, counts))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`tools/ghidra/README.md`:

```md
# Ghidra queries

Savage Wind keeps one analyzed Ghidra project of the game's `main` module next to the repository
(`../ghidra/`, never inside it) and queries it from the command line with `gq.py`. The analysis runs
once; every query opens the project read-only, so nothing in it changes.

## Setup (once)

- Ghidra 12.1.2 with the [Switch Loader](https://github.com/Adubbz/Ghidra-Switch-Loader) extension
  built for that exact version (`SwitchLoader-1.6.1-...-Ghidra_12.1.2.zip`, unzipped into
  `<ghidra>/Ghidra/Extensions/`). Extensions only load in the Ghidra version they were built for.
- A JDK 21 or newer.
- Import and analyze the 1.9.0 `extracted/exefs/main`, then `sdk` and `subsdk0` the same way (about 22,
  6 and 3 minutes on 8 threads of a Ryzen 5 5600X):

  ```
  GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM=12G <ghidra>/support/analyzeHeadless <repo>/../ghidra botw_1.9.0 \
      -import <repo>/extracted/exefs/main -max-cpu 8 -log <repo>/../ghidra/analyze190_main.log
  ```

  `gq.py` opens `botw_1.9.0` by default, the supported version. An older `botw_1.8.2` project can be
  kept next to it and queried with `SW_GHIDRA_NAME=botw_1.8.2`.

- Point `gq.py` at the installation, through the environment or a git-ignored
  `tools/ghidra/gq.local.json`:

  ```json
  {"GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR": "E:/tools/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC",
   "JAVA_HOME": "C:/Program Files/Eclipse Adoptium/jdk-21.0.12.101-hotspot"}
  ```

## Use

```
python tools/ghidra/gq.py summary
python tools/ghidra/gq.py decompile 0x70001234a0        # a runtime address of main works too
python tools/ghidra/gq.py xrefs nvnBootstrapLoader
python tools/ghidra/gq.py strings "Actor/.*bactorpack" 20
```

Each call starts Ghidra headless (about half a minute), so pass several addresses to one
`decompile` or `xrefs` call when possible. The project cannot be queried while the analysis that
writes it is still running.

The Switch Loader maps `main` at `0x7100000000`; the generator and runtime use `0x7000000000`.
`gq.py` moves runtime addresses of `main` (`0x7000000000..0x7003ffffff`) to Ghidra's base and says
so on stderr. Output is printed, not stored: it is derived from the game's code and must stay out
of the repository.

## Working rule

Every claim about what a function does cites its evidence: the address, the relevant pseudocode
or instructions, and the callers that support the reading. Names given to functions (in notes,
patches or the runtime) say where they came from (a string reference, a zeldaret 1.5.0 match, a
call pattern).

```

`tools/ghidra/SWQuery.java`:

```java
// Savage Wind: read-only queries against an analyzed Ghidra program, driven by tools/ghidra/gq.py.
//
// The only script argument is a request file: line 1 is the output path, line 2 the command, every
// further line one argument (a file instead of command-line arguments keeps regexes and C++ names
// intact through analyzeHeadless.bat on Windows). Nothing in the program is modified.
//@category SavageWind

import java.io.FileOutputStream;
import java.io.OutputStreamWriter;
import java.io.PrintWriter;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Paths;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.TreeSet;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

import ghidra.app.decompiler.DecompInterface;
import ghidra.app.decompiler.DecompileResults;
import ghidra.app.script.GhidraScript;
import ghidra.program.model.address.Address;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.Data;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.DataIterator;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.Function;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.FunctionIterator;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.Instruction;
import ghidra.program.model.listing.Listing;
import ghidra.program.model.mem.MemoryBlock;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.Reference;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.Symbol;
import ghidra.program.model.symbol.SymbolIterator;

public class SWQuery extends GhidraScript {
    private static final int MAX_REFS = 500;
    private PrintWriter out;
    private DecompInterface decomp;

    @Override
    public void run() throws Exception {
        List<String> req = Files.readAllLines(Paths.get(getScriptArgs()[0]), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
        out = new PrintWriter(new OutputStreamWriter(new FileOutputStream(req.get(0)), StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        try {
            String cmd = req.get(1);
            List<String> args = req.subList(2, req.size());
            switch (cmd) {
                case "decompile": for (String s : args) decompile(s); break;
                case "xrefs": for (String s : args) xrefs(s); break;
                case "callees": for (String s : args) callees(s); break;
                case "disasm": disasm(args.get(0), args.size() > 1 ? Integer.parseInt(args.get(1)) : 40); break;
                case "data": data(args.get(0), args.size() > 1 ? Integer.parseInt(args.get(1)) : 4); break;
                case "strings": strings(args.get(0), args.size() > 1 ? Integer.parseInt(args.get(1)) : 100); break;
                case "symbols": symbols(args.get(0), args.size() > 1 ? Integer.parseInt(args.get(1)) : 100); break;
                case "functions": functions(); break;
                case "summary": summary(); break;
                default: out.println("unknown command: " + cmd);
            }
        } finally {
            if (decomp != null) {
                decomp.dispose();
            }
            out.close();
        }
    }

    /** An address ("0x7100123450") or a symbol name; null (with a message) when it resolves to nothing. */
    private Address resolve(String s) {
        if (s.matches("(?i)(0x)?[0-9a-f]+")) {
            return toAddr(s.toLowerCase().startsWith("0x") ? s.substring(2) : s);
        }
        // A qualified name ("nn::fs::MountRom") is looked up by its last part, then matched in full; the
        // leading namespaces Ghidra adds (such as <EXTERNAL>::) may be left out.
        String last = s.contains("::") ? s.substring(s.lastIndexOf("::") + 2) : s;
        SymbolIterator it = currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getSymbols(last);
        while (it.hasNext()) {
            Symbol sym = it.next();
            String full = sym.getName(true);
            if (full.equals(s) || full.endsWith("::" + s) || !s.contains("::")) {
                return sym.getAddress();
            }
        }
        out.println("?? no symbol named " + s);
        return null;
    }

    private Function functionAt(String s) {
        Address a = resolve(s);
        if (a == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Function f = getFunctionContaining(a);
        if (f == null) {
            out.println("?? no function contains " + a);
        }
        return f;
    }

    private String where(Address a) {
        Function f = getFunctionContaining(a);
        return f == null ? "(no function)" : f.getName(true) + "+0x" + Long.toHexString(a.subtract(f.getEntryPoint()));
    }

    private void header(Function f) {
        out.printf("== %s @ %s  (%d bytes, %d callers, %d callees)%n", f.getName(true), f.getEntryPoint(),
                f.getBody().getNumAddresses(), f.getCallingFunctions(monitor).size(), f.getCalledFunctions(monitor).size());
    }

    private void decompile(String s) throws Exception {
        Function f = functionAt(s);
        if (f == null) {
            return;
        }
        if (decomp == null) {
            decomp = new DecompInterface();
            decomp.openProgram(currentProgram);
        }
        header(f);
        DecompileResults r = decomp.decompileFunction(f, 180, monitor);
        if (r.decompileCompleted()) {
            out.println(r.getDecompiledFunction().getC());
        } else {
            out.println("?? decompilation failed: " + r.getErrorMessage());
        }
    }

    private void xrefs(String s) {
        Address a = resolve(s);
        if (a == null) {
            return;
        }
        Function f = getFunctionAt(a);
        out.printf("== references to %s%s%n", a, f != null ? " (" + f.getName(true) + ")" : "");
        int n = 0;
        for (Reference r : getReferencesTo(a)) {
            if (n++ >= MAX_REFS) {
                out.println("   ... (more than " + MAX_REFS + ")");
                break;
            }
            out.printf("   %s  %-16s %s%n", r.getFromAddress(), r.getReferenceType(), where(r.getFromAddress()));
        }
    }

    private void callees(String s) {
        Function f = functionAt(s);
        if (f == null) {
            return;
        }
        header(f);
        Set<String> lines = new TreeSet<>();
        for (Function c : f.getCalledFunctions(monitor)) {
            lines.add(String.format("   %s  %s", c.getEntryPoint(), c.getName(true)));
        }
        lines.forEach(out::println);
    }

    private void disasm(String s, int count) {
        Address a = resolve(s);
        if (a == null) {
            return;
        }
        Listing listing = currentProgram.getListing();
        Instruction ins = listing.getInstructionContaining(a);
        if (ins == null) {
            ins = listing.getInstructionAfter(a);
        }
        out.println("== " + where(a));
        for (int i = 0; i < count && ins != null; i++, ins = ins.getNext()) {
            out.printf("   %s  %s%n", ins.getAddress(), ins);
        }
    }

    /** count 64-bit words from an address, each with the symbol or function it points to (pointers, GOT slots). */
    private void data(String s, int count) throws Exception {
        Address a = resolve(s);
        if (a == null) {
            return;
        }
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++, a = a.add(8)) {
            long v = getLong(a);
            Address target = toAddr(v);
            Symbol sym = getSymbolAt(a);
            String to = "";
            if (currentProgram.getMemory().contains(target)) {
                Symbol ts = getSymbolAt(target);
                to = " -> " + (ts != null ? ts.getName(true) : where(target));
            }
            out.printf("%s  %016x%s%s%n", a, v, sym != null ? "  [" + sym.getName(true) + "]" : "", to);
        }
    }

    private void strings(String regex, int max) {
        Pattern p = Pattern.compile(regex);
        DataIterator it = currentProgram.getListing().getDefinedData(true);
        int n = 0;
        while (it.hasNext() && n < max && !monitor.isCancelled()) {
            Data d = it.next();
            if (!d.hasStringValue()) {
                continue;
            }
            String v = String.valueOf(d.getValue());
            if (!p.matcher(v).find()) {
                continue;
            }
            n++;
            List<String> users = new ArrayList<>();
            for (Reference r : getReferencesTo(d.getAddress())) {
                if (users.size() >= 5) {
                    users.add("...");
                    break;
                }
                users.add(where(r.getFromAddress()));
            }
            out.printf("%s  \"%s\"  <- %s%n", d.getAddress(), v.replace("\n", "\\n"), users.isEmpty() ? "(no references)" : String.join(", ", users));
        }
    }

    private void symbols(String regex, int max) {
        Pattern p = Pattern.compile(regex);
        SymbolIterator it = currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getAllSymbols(true);
        int n = 0;
        while (it.hasNext() && n < max && !monitor.isCancelled()) {
            Symbol sym = it.next();
            String name = sym.getName(true);
            if (p.matcher(name).find()) {
                n++;
                out.printf("%s  %-10s %s%n", sym.getAddress(), sym.getSymbolType(), name);
            }
        }
    }

    private void functions() {
        out.println("entry\tname\tbytes\treferences\tthunk");
        FunctionIterator it = currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctions(true);
        while (it.hasNext() && !monitor.isCancelled()) {
            Function f = it.next();
            out.printf("%s\t%s\t%d\t%d\t%s%n", f.getEntryPoint(), f.getName(true), f.getBody().getNumAddresses(),
                    currentProgram.getReferenceManager().getReferenceCountTo(f.getEntryPoint()), f.isThunk());
        }
    }

    private void summary() {
        out.println("program   " + currentProgram.getName());
        out.println("language  " + currentProgram.getLanguageID() + " / " + currentProgram.getCompilerSpec().getCompilerSpecID());
        out.println("base      " + currentProgram.getImageBase());
        out.println("functions " + currentProgram.getFunctionManager().getFunctionCount());
        out.println("symbols   " + currentProgram.getSymbolTable().getNumSymbols());
        for (MemoryBlock b : currentProgram.getMemory().getBlocks()) {
            out.printf("block     %-12s %s-%s %s%n", b.getName(), b.getStart(), b.getEnd(),
                    (b.isRead() ? "r" : "-") + (b.isWrite() ? "w" : "-") + (b.isExecute() ? "x" : "-"));
        }
    }
}

```

`tools/ghidra/gq.py`:

```py
"""Query the analyzed Ghidra project of the game's main module (read-only).

Usage: gq.py <command> [args...]

  summary                     program, language, memory blocks, counts
  decompile <addr|name>...    pseudocode of the functions containing these addresses
  xrefs <addr|name>...        references to an address (callers of a function)
  callees <addr|name>...      functions called from a function
  disasm <addr|name> [n]      n instructions from an address (default 40)
  strings <regex> [max]       defined strings matching a regex, with the functions using them
  symbols <regex> [max]       symbols whose qualified name matches a regex
  functions                   every function as TSV (entry, name, bytes, references, thunk)

Addresses can be given as Ghidra addresses (main loads at 0x7100000000 there) or as runtime
addresses of main (0x70xxxxxxxx, the base Savage Wind's generator and runtime use); runtime ones
are moved to Ghidra's base. Output goes to stdout, never into the repository: it is derived from
the game's code.

Paths come from the environment or from tools/ghidra/gq.local.json (git-ignored):
  GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR   extracted Ghidra release (with the Switch loader extension installed)
  JAVA_HOME            JDK 21+
  SW_GHIDRA_PROJECT    directory holding <name>.gpr (default: ../ghidra next to the repository)
  SW_GHIDRA_NAME       project name (default botw_1.9.0, the supported version; botw_1.8.2 is kept)
  SW_GHIDRA_PROGRAM    program inside the project (default main)
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(HERE))
RUNTIME_MAIN = (0x7000000000, 0x7004000000)  # runtime/rt.h MAIN_BASE .. SDK_BASE
GHIDRA_SHIFT = 0x7100000000 - 0x7000000000   # the Switch loader's base for main


def setting(name, default=None):
    local = os.path.join(HERE, 'gq.local.json')
    cfg = json.load(open(local)) if os.path.exists(local) else {}
    return os.environ.get(name) or cfg.get(name) or default


def to_ghidra(arg):
    if re.fullmatch(r'(?i)0x[0-9a-f]+', arg):
        v = int(arg, 16)
        if RUNTIME_MAIN[0] <= v < RUNTIME_MAIN[1]:
            print(f'(runtime {arg} -> ghidra {v + GHIDRA_SHIFT:#x})', file=sys.stderr)
            return hex(v + GHIDRA_SHIFT)
    return arg


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2 or sys.argv[1] in ('-h', '--help'):
        print(__doc__)
        return 0
    ghidra = setting('GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR')
    if not ghidra:
        sys.exit('set GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR (or put it in tools/ghidra/gq.local.json)')
    project = setting('SW_GHIDRA_PROJECT', os.path.join(os.path.dirname(REPO), 'ghidra'))
    name = setting('SW_GHIDRA_NAME', 'botw_1.9.0')
    program = setting('SW_GHIDRA_PROGRAM', 'main')
    env = dict(os.environ)
    if setting('JAVA_HOME'):
        env['JAVA_HOME'] = setting('JAVA_HOME')
        env['PATH'] = os.path.join(env['JAVA_HOME'], 'bin') + os.pathsep + env.get('PATH', '')
    env.setdefault('GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM', '8G')

    cmd, args = sys.argv[1], [to_ghidra(a) for a in sys.argv[2:]]
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='swgq-') as tmp:
        result, request = os.path.join(tmp, 'result.txt'), os.path.join(tmp, 'request.txt')
        with open(request, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write('\n'.join([result, cmd] + args) + '\n')
        launcher = os.path.join(ghidra, 'support', 'analyzeHeadless' + ('.bat' if os.name == 'nt' else ''))
        proc = subprocess.run([launcher, project, name, '-process', program, '-noanalysis', '-readOnly',
                               '-scriptPath', HERE, '-postScript', 'SWQuery.java', request],
                              env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace')
        if os.path.exists(result):
            sys.stdout.write(open(result, encoding='utf-8').read())
            return 0
        log = (proc.stdout + proc.stderr).splitlines()
        errors = [l for l in log if re.search(r'ERROR|Exception|Unable to lock|LockException', l)]
        print('\n'.join((errors or log)[-25:]), file=sys.stderr)
        if any('lock' in l.lower() for l in errors):
            print('(the project is open elsewhere, for example while the analysis is still running)', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

`tools/i18n_check.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Menu translations (runtime/ui/i18n.mm): lists the texts each runtime/ui/i18n/<lang>.inc lacks.

The keys are the English texts themselves. This collects the string literals of the menu sources (adjacent literals
joined, as the compiler does) that read like text shown to the player - not IDs ("##..."), paths, environment variable
names or log messages - and compares them with each table's T("English", "...") entries.

An entry with an empty translation, T("...", ""), keeps the English text (names, units). The ones that read like a
phrase are listed as left in English: usually a text added without its translation (only listed, not an error).

usage: tools/i18n_check.py [lang ...]           report missing, unused, left-in-English entries (all tables by default)
       tools/i18n_check.py --missing <lang>     print the missing keys as T("...", "") lines
"""
import glob
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
# (console.mm is left out: the console is English, like the command names and replies it shows)
SOURCES = sorted(p for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime/ui/*.mm')) if not p.endswith('console.mm')) + [
    os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime/language.c'),
    os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime/hle/bindings.c'),
    os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime/launch_flags.c'),
]
SKIP_LINE = re.compile(r'\b(said|LOG|_Static_assert|static_assert|fprintf|printf|getenv|strcmp|strncmp|memcmp|strstr|fopen|file_exists|mkdir|unlink|rt_resource|rt_remove_game_file|'
                       r'PushID|BeginChild|BeginTable|BeginPopup|OpenPopup|IsPopupOpen|InvisibleButton|GetID|Begin)\s*\(|'
                       r'#include|#define|SAVAGEWIND_|//')


def literals(text):
    """(line, string) for every string literal; adjacent literals (only whitespace / comments between) joined."""
    out, i, n, line = [], 0, len(text), 1
    pending, pend_line, last_end = None, 0, -1
    while i < n:
        c = text[i]
        if c == '\n':
            line += 1
        if text.startswith('//', i):
            j = text.find('\n', i)
            i = n if j < 0 else j
            continue
        if text.startswith('/*', i):
            j = text.find('*/', i + 2)
            line += text.count('\n', i, j)
            i = n if j < 0 else j + 2
            continue
        if c == "'":
            i += 3 if text[i + 1] != '\\' else 4
            continue
        if c == '"':
            j, buf = i + 1, []
            while j < n and text[j] != '"':
                if text[j] == '\\':
                    e = text[j + 1]
                    buf.append({'n': '\n', 't': '\t', '"': '"', '\\': '\\', "'": "'", '0': '\0'}.get(e, '\\' + e))
                    j += 2
                else:
                    buf.append(text[j])
                    j += 1
            s = ''.join(buf)
            between = text[last_end:i] if pending is not None else ''
            if pending is not None and re.fullmatch(r'\s*', between):
                pending += s
            else:
                if pending is not None:
                    out.append((pend_line, pending))
                pending, pend_line = s, line
            last_end = j + 1
            i = j + 1
            continue
        i += 1
    if pending is not None:
        out.append((pend_line, pending))
    return out


def looks_like_text(s, in_tr=False):
    if not re.search(r'[A-Za-z]{2}', s) or s.startswith('##') or '###' in s:
        return False
    if re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z]+(_[A-Za-z0-9]+)+', s):  # layout pane names (W_Base_00)
        return False
    if in_tr and '/' not in s and '\\' not in s:  # (a word passed to tr() is text, however short)
        return True
    if re.fullmatch(r'(?:\\x[0-9a-fA-F]{2})+', s):  # encoded icon glyphs, not words
        return False
    if re.fullmatch(r'[\w./\\:%-]+\.(ttf|ttc|otf|bfttf|bffnt|sbfarc|pack|bin|txt|ini|png|dll|so|dylib|nso|npdm|mp4|webm)', s):
        return False
    if re.fullmatch(r'[a-z0-9_./-]+', s):  # identifiers, ini keys, folder names
        return False
    if re.fullmatch(r'[A-Z]{2}[a-z]{2}', s):  # region languages (USen)
        return False
    if s.startswith(('/', 'C:', 'file:')) or 'SAVAGEWIND' in s:
        return False
    return True


def in_log_call(lines, i):
    """line i continues a LOG / fprintf / printf call begun on a line above, still open there"""
    start = i
    while start > 0 and i - start < 6 and lines[start - 1].rstrip() and lines[start - 1].rstrip()[-1] not in ';{}':
        start -= 1
        if re.match(r'\s*(LOG|fprintf|printf)\s*\(', lines[start]):
            code = re.sub(r'"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"', '""', ''.join(lines[start:i]))
            return code.count('(') > code.count(')')
    return False


def keys():
    found = {}
    for path in SOURCES:
        text = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
        lines = text.split('\n')
        for ln, s in literals(text):
            src = lines[ln - 1] if ln - 1 < len(lines) else ''
            if 'i18n-skip' in src or SKIP_LINE.search(src.split('"')[0]) or in_log_call(lines, ln - 1) or \
                    not looks_like_text(s, 'tr(' in src):
                continue
            found.setdefault(s, f'{os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)}:{ln}')
    # the colour presets' names (runtime/color_grade.c g_color_presets: shown through tr() by both menus)
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime/color_grade.c')
    text = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    for m in re.finditer(r'^\s*\{"([^"]+)", -?\d', text, re.M):
        found.setdefault(m.group(1), f'{os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)}:{text[:m.start()].count(chr(10)) + 1}')
    return found


def table(lang):
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime/ui/i18n', lang + '.inc')
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return {}
    text = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    lits = literals(text)
    # T("en", "tr"): literals come in pairs, in order
    entries = {}
    for k in range(0, len(lits) - 1, 2):
        entries[lits[k][1]] = lits[k + 1][1]
    return entries


def is_sentence(s):
    """reads like a phrase to translate, not a name or unit: three words or more, two of them lowercase"""
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]{2,}', s)
    return len(words) >= 3 and sum(w.islower() for w in words) >= 2


def c_quote(s):
    return '"' + s.replace('\\', '\\\\').replace('"', '\\"').replace('\n', '\\n').replace('\t', '\\t') + '"'


def main():
    want = keys()
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if args[:1] == ['--missing']:
        have = table(args[1])
        for k, where in want.items():
            if k not in have:
                print(f'T({c_quote(k)}, "")  // {where}')
        return
    langs = args or sorted(os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(p))[0] for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime/ui/i18n/*.inc')))
    print(f'{len(want)} menu texts')
    bad = False
    for lang in langs:
        have = table(lang)
        missing = [k for k in want if k not in have]
        unused = [k for k in have if k not in want]
        english = [k for k in want if have.get(k) == '' and is_sentence(k)]
        print(f'{lang}: {len(have)} entries, {len(missing)} missing, {len(unused)} unused, '
              f'{len(english)} left in English')
        for k in missing[:20]:
            print(f'  missing: {k[:90]!r}  ({want[k]})')
        for k in unused[:20]:
            print(f'  unused:  {k[:90]!r}')
        for k in english[:20]:
            print(f'  english: {k[:90]!r}  ({want[k]})')
        bad |= bool(missing)
    sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

`tools/layout.py`:

```py
"""Guest addresses of the exefs modules: the one place that decides them.

The Switch loader puts a process's modules back to back in load order (rtld, main, subsdk0..9, sdk), each one as
big as its image (text, rodata, data + bss) rounded up to a 4 KiB page, from a 2 MiB-aligned start. Savage Wind does
the same without rtld, whose work the runtime does itself (runtime/loader.c, runtime/main.c), so main starts the
module area at MAIN_BASE and the modules may be any size the area holds.

The generated code has these addresses baked in, so everything else follows what this computes:
- `gen.py layout` / `gen.py all` write it next to the generated code: layout.txt (read back by gen.py for each
  module and by the start screen's build, runtime/gamebuild.c) and layout.c, compiled into the game code library;
- runtime/loader.c loads each module where the library's layout says (runtime/gamelib.h);
- sw_probe.py reports it.

Usage: layout.py <exefs_dir> [outdir]   (prints the layout; with outdir it also writes layout.txt and layout.c)
"""
import os
import sys

from nso import header

MODULES_LO = 0x7000000000  # runtime/rt.h MAIN_BASE (2 MiB aligned)
MODULES_HI = 0x7080000000  # runtime/rt.h MODULES_END: the loader refuses a module past it
PAGE = 0x1000
LOAD_ORDER = ['main'] + [f'subsdk{i}' for i in range(10)] + ['sdk']


class LayoutError(Exception):
    pass


def image_size(h):
    """Bytes a module takes in memory (nso.header): its segments' furthest end, page-rounded."""
    end = max(h['text'][0] + h['text'][1], h['rodata'][0] + h['rodata'][1], h['data'][0] + h['data'][1] + h['bss'])
    return (end + PAGE - 1) & ~(PAGE - 1)


# The subsdk modules each known game version has, by its main module's build id (the first 8 bytes, as
# runtime/game_versions.h lists them). Another subsdk in such an ExeFS isn't the game's: a mod or a mod loader copied
# there (#165). It is left out, and runtime/loader.c skips it the same way.
GAME_SUBSDKS = {
    'de0b6ac4efc1dda7': ['subsdk0'],  # 1.8.2
    'cd57b23fa4bbad65': ['subsdk0'],  # 1.9.0
}


def foreign(exefs):
    """The subsdk modules in an exefs folder that aren't its known game version's (none for an unknown version)."""
    main = os.path.join(exefs, 'main')
    known = GAME_SUBSDKS.get(header(main)['build_id'][:16]) if os.path.isfile(main) else None
    if known is None:
        return []
    return [n for n in LOAD_ORDER if n.startswith('subsdk') and n not in known and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(exefs, n))]


def compute(exefs):
    """[(name, base, size, build_id)] of the modules in an exefs folder, in load order."""
    out, base = [], MODULES_LO
    skip = foreign(exefs)
    for name in skip:
        print(f"layout: {name} is not one of the game's modules (a mod?): left out", file=sys.stderr)
    for name in LOAD_ORDER:
        path = os.path.join(exefs, name)
        if os.path.isfile(path) and name not in skip:
            h = header(path)
            out.append((name, base, image_size(h), h['build_id']))
            base += out[-1][2]
    return out


def problems(layout):
    """Why the runtime could not load this layout (empty: it can)."""
    names = [m[0] for m in layout]
    why = [f'no {n} module' for n in ('main', 'sdk') if n not in names]
    end = layout[-1][1] + layout[-1][2] if layout else MODULES_LO
    if end > MODULES_HI:
        why.append(f'the modules end at {end:#x}, past {MODULES_HI:#x} (MODULES_END in runtime/rt.h)')
    return why


def checked(exefs):
    """compute(), or LayoutError if the runtime could not load it."""
    layout = compute(exefs)
    why = problems(layout)
    if why:
        raise LayoutError(f'{exefs}: ' + '; '.join(why))
    return layout


def text(layout):
    return ('# module layout (tools/layout.py), load order: name, guest base, image size, NSO build id\n' +
            ''.join(f'{n} {b:#x} {s:#x} {i}\n' for n, b, s, i in layout))


def read(path):
    """The layout from a layout.txt."""
    out = []
    for line in open(path):
        if line.strip() and not line.startswith('#'):
            n, b, s, i = line.split()
            out.append((n, int(b, 16), int(s, 16), i))
    return out


def c_source(layout, game=None):
    """layout.c: the layout inside the game code library, with each module's function table, and the game version
    with its main module's sites (game: (version, {name: address}), tools/game_sites.py) (runtime/gamelib.h)."""
    lines = ['// Module layout of this game code (tools/layout.py). Generated.\n#include "gamelib.h"\n\n']
    for n, *_ in layout:
        lines.append(f'extern const uint64_t {n}_fn_addrs[], {n}_fn_count;\nextern const GuestFn {n}_fn_ptrs[];\n')
    lines.append('\nconst GameLibModule game_modules[] = {\n')
    for n, b, s, i in layout:
        lines.append(f'    {{"{n}", {b:#x}ull, {s:#x}ull, "{i}", {n}_fn_addrs, {n}_fn_ptrs, &{n}_fn_count}},\n')
    lines.append(f'}};\nconst uint32_t game_module_count = {len(layout)};\n')
    version, sites = game or ('', {})
    lines.append(f'\nconst char game_version[] = "{version}";\nconst GameLibSite game_sites[] = {{\n')
    lines += [f'    {{"{n}", {a:#x}ull}},\n' for n, a in sorted(sites.items())] or ['    {0, 0},\n']
    lines.append(f'}};\nconst uint32_t game_site_count = {len(sites)};\n')
    return ''.join(lines)


def write_if_changed(path, s):  # (an unchanged file keeps its date: make doesn't recompile it)
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            if f.read() == s:
                return
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    with open(path, 'w') as f:
        f.write(s)


def write(layout, outdir, game=None):
    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
    write_if_changed(os.path.join(outdir, 'layout.txt'), text(layout))
    write_if_changed(os.path.join(outdir, 'layout.c'), c_source(layout, game))


def show(layout):
    for n, b, s, i in layout:
        print(f'  {n:8s} {b:#x}-{b + s:#x}  {s / 2**20:7.1f} MiB  build {i[:16]}')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    if len(sys.argv) not in (2, 3):
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    lay = compute(sys.argv[1])
    show(lay)
    why = problems(lay)
    if why:
        sys.exit('layout: ' + '; '.join(why))
    if len(sys.argv) == 3:
        write(lay, sys.argv[2])

```

`tools/lifter.py`:

```py
"""AArch64 -> C static recompiler.

Integer, memory, and control flow are translated to C. FP/SIMD instructions (and CRC32) are
either re-emitted as inline assembly (simd='asm', AArch64 hosts), with guest V registers
loaded from / stored to the Cpu struct around each batch, so their semantics are
bit-exact by construction, or lowered to portable C (simd='c', tools/simd_c.py + runtime/simd.h).
"""
import struct

# Cpu struct offsets (must match runtime/cpu.h)
OFF_X = 0
OFF_SP = 256
OFF_PC = 264
OFF_NZCV = 272
OFF_V = 512

COND_NAMES = ['eq', 'ne', 'cs', 'cc', 'mi', 'pl', 'vs', 'vc', 'hi', 'ls', 'ge', 'lt', 'gt', 'le', 'al', 'nv']
SCRATCH = [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17]


class Unsupported(Exception):
    pass


def bits(w, lo, n):
    return (w >> lo) & ((1 << n) - 1)


def sext(v, n):
    return v - (1 << n) if v & (1 << (n - 1)) else v


def ones(n):
    return (1 << n) - 1


def ror(v, r, size):
    r %= size
    return ((v >> r) | (v << (size - r))) & ones(size) if r else v


def replicate(v, esize, size):
    out = 0
    for i in range(0, size, esize):
        out |= v << i
    return out


def decode_bit_masks(N, imms, immr, size, immediate):
    x = (N << 6) | (~imms & 0x3F)
    if x == 0:
        raise Unsupported('reserved bitmask')
    length = x.bit_length() - 1
    if length < 1:
        raise Unsupported('reserved bitmask')
    levels = ones(length)
    if immediate and (imms & levels) == levels:
        raise Unsupported('reserved bitmask')
    S = imms & levels
    R = immr & levels
    diff = (S - R) & 0x3F
    esize = 1 << length
    d = diff & ones(length)
    welem = ones(S + 1)
    telem = ones(d + 1)
    wmask = replicate(ror(welem, R, esize), esize, size)
    tmask = replicate(telem, esize, size)
    return wmask, tmask


def hx(v):
    return f'0x{v:x}ull'


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- register helpers

def X(r):
    return '0ull' if r == 31 else f'c->x[{r}]'


def XS(r):
    return 'c->sp' if r == 31 else f'c->x[{r}]'


def W(r):
    return '0u' if r == 31 else f'(uint32_t)c->x[{r}]'


def WS(r):
    return '(uint32_t)c->sp' if r == 31 else f'(uint32_t)c->x[{r}]'


def R(sf, r, sp=False):
    if sf:
        return XS(r) if sp else X(r)
    return WS(r) if sp else W(r)


def set_reg(sf, r, expr, sp=False):
    """Statement writing expr to Rd (zero-extending 32-bit results)."""
    if r == 31 and not sp:
        return f'(void)({expr});'
    dst = 'c->sp' if r == 31 else f'c->x[{r}]'
    if sf:
        return f'{dst} = (uint64_t)({expr});'
    return f'{dst} = (uint32_t)({expr});'


def shift_expr(sf, val, typ, amt):
    if amt == 0 and typ != 3:
        return val
    if typ == 0:
        return f'({val} << {amt})'
    if typ == 1:
        return f'({val} >> {amt})'
    if typ == 2:
        return f'(uint64_t)((int64_t){val} >> {amt})' if sf else f'(uint32_t)((int32_t){val} >> {amt})'
    return f'ROR{64 if sf else 32}({val}, {amt})'


def extend_expr(r, option, shift):
    base = X(r)
    e = {
        0: f'(uint64_t)(uint8_t){base}',
        1: f'(uint64_t)(uint16_t){base}',
        2: f'(uint64_t)(uint32_t){base}',
        3: base,
        4: f'(uint64_t)(int64_t)(int8_t){base}',
        5: f'(uint64_t)(int64_t)(int16_t){base}',
        6: f'(uint64_t)(int64_t)(int32_t){base}',
        7: base,
    }[option]
    return f'({e} << {shift})' if shift else e


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- instruction classes

class Insn:
    """Result of lifting one instruction."""
    __slots__ = ('kind', 'code', 'target', 'cond', 'asm')

    def __init__(self, kind, code='', target=None, cond=None, asm=None):
        self.kind = kind      # 'op', 'asm', 'b', 'bcond', 'bl', 'blr', 'br', 'ret', 'trap'
        self.code = code      # C statements (for 'op'), or condition expr for 'bcond'
        self.target = target  # branch target (int) or register expr
        self.cond = cond
        self.asm = asm        # AsmInsn for 'asm'


class AsmInsn:
    """An FP/SIMD instruction to pass through as inline asm."""
    __slots__ = ('word', 'vregs', 'gprs', 'flags', 'consts')

    def __init__(self, word, vregs, gprs, flags=False, consts=None):
        self.word = word
        self.vregs = vregs    # set of V register numbers touched
        self.gprs = gprs      # list of (bit position, guest reg or 'sp')
        self.flags = flags
        self.consts = consts or []  # list of (bit position, constant) loaded into scratch


def is_fp_simd_dp(w):
    return bits(w, 25, 3) == 0b111


def is_ldst(w):
    return bits(w, 25, 1) == 0 and bits(w, 27, 1) == 1


class Lifter:
    def __init__(self, base, simd='asm'):
        self.base = base  # absolute load address of the module (guest == host)
        if simd not in ('asm', 'c'):
            raise ValueError(f'simd={simd!r}')
        self.sc = None
        if simd == 'c':
            from simd_c import SimdC
            self.sc = SimdC()

    def lift(self, w, pc):
        """pc is absolute. Returns an Insn."""
        op0 = bits(w, 25, 4)
        if (op0 & 0b1110) == 0b1000:
            return self.dp_imm(w, pc)
        if (op0 & 0b1110) == 0b1010:
            return self.branch_sys(w, pc)
        if (op0 & 0b0101) == 0b0100:
            return self.ldst(w, pc)
        if (op0 & 0b0111) == 0b0101:
            return self.dp_reg(w, pc)
        if (op0 & 0b0111) == 0b0111:
            return self.fp_simd(w, pc)
        # padding, trap words (e7ffdefe), header data: trap if ever executed
        return Insn('trap', f'rt_udf(c, {hx(pc)});')

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ data processing (imm)

    def dp_imm(self, w, pc):
        op = bits(w, 23, 3)
        sf = bits(w, 31, 1)
        rd, rn = bits(w, 0, 5), bits(w, 5, 5)
        if op in (0, 1):  # PC-relative
            imm = sext((bits(w, 5, 19) << 2) | bits(w, 29, 2), 21)
            if bits(w, 31, 1):
                val = (pc & ~0xFFF) + (imm << 12)
            else:
                val = pc + imm
            return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rd, hx(val & ones(64))))
        if op == 2:  # add/sub imm
            opc, S, sh = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 29, 1), bits(w, 22, 1)
            imm = bits(w, 10, 12) << (12 if sh else 0)
            a = R(sf, rn, sp=True)
            if S:
                fn = ('subs' if opc else 'adds') + ('64' if sf else '32')
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{fn}(c, {a}, {hx(imm)})'))
            return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{a} {"-" if opc else "+"} {hx(imm)}', sp=True))
        if op == 4:  # logical imm
            opc, N = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 22, 1)
            if not sf and N:
                raise Unsupported('logical imm N=1 32-bit')
            size = 64 if sf else 32
            imm, _ = decode_bit_masks(N, bits(w, 10, 6), bits(w, 16, 6), size, True)
            a = R(sf, rn)
            if opc == 0:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{a} & {hx(imm)}', sp=True))
            if opc == 1:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{a} | {hx(imm)}', sp=True))
            if opc == 2:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{a} ^ {hx(imm)}', sp=True))
            return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'logic{size}(c, {a} & {hx(imm)})'))
        if op == 5:  # move wide
            opc, hw = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 21, 2)
            if not sf and hw > 1:
                raise Unsupported('movw hw')
            imm = bits(w, 5, 16) << (hw * 16)
            if opc == 0:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, hx(~imm & ones(64 if sf else 32))))
            if opc == 2:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, hx(imm)))
            if opc == 3:
                mask = ~(0xFFFF << (hw * 16)) & ones(64)
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'({X(rd)} & {hx(mask)}) | {hx(imm)}'))
            raise Unsupported('movw opc')
        if op == 6:  # bitfield
            opc, N = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 22, 1)
            immr, imms = bits(w, 16, 6), bits(w, 10, 6)
            size = 64 if sf else 32
            if N != sf:
                raise Unsupported('bitfield N')
            wmask, tmask = decode_bit_masks(N, imms, immr, size, False)
            src = R(sf, rn)
            rot = f'ROR{size}({src}, {immr})' if immr else src
            if opc == 2:  # UBFM
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{rot} & {hx(wmask & tmask)}'))
            if opc == 0:  # SBFM
                top = f'(uint{size}_t)(-(int{size}_t)(({src} >> {imms}) & 1))'
                return Insn('op', set_reg(
                    sf, rd, f'({top} & {hx(~tmask & ones(size))}) | ({rot} & {hx(wmask & tmask)})'))
            if opc == 1:  # BFM
                dst = R(sf, rd)
                bot = f'(({dst} & {hx(~wmask & ones(size))}) | ({rot} & {hx(wmask)}))'
                return Insn('op', set_reg(
                    sf, rd, f'({dst} & {hx(~tmask & ones(size))}) | ({bot} & {hx(tmask)})'))
            raise Unsupported('bitfield opc')
        if op == 7:  # EXTR
            rm, lsb = bits(w, 16, 5), bits(w, 10, 6)
            size = 64 if sf else 32
            if lsb == 0:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, R(sf, rm)))
            return Insn('op', set_reg(
                sf, rd, f'({R(sf, rm)} >> {lsb}) | ((uint{size}_t){R(sf, rn)} << {size - lsb})'))
        raise Unsupported(f'dp_imm {w:08x}')

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ branches / system

    def branch_sys(self, w, pc):
        if bits(w, 26, 5) == 0b00101:  # B / BL
            t = (pc + sext(bits(w, 0, 26), 26) * 4) & ones(64)
            return Insn('bl' if bits(w, 31, 1) else 'b', target=t)
        if bits(w, 25, 7) == 0b0101010 and not bits(w, 4, 1):  # B.cond
            t = pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 19), 19) * 4
            cond = bits(w, 0, 4)
            if cond >= 14:
                return Insn('b', target=t)
            return Insn('bcond', target=t, cond=f'COND_{COND_NAMES[cond].upper()}(c)')
        if bits(w, 25, 6) == 0b011010:  # CBZ/CBNZ
            sf, nz, rt = bits(w, 31, 1), bits(w, 24, 1), bits(w, 0, 5)
            t = pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 19), 19) * 4
            return Insn('bcond', target=t, cond=f'{R(sf, rt)} {"!=" if nz else "=="} 0')
        if bits(w, 25, 6) == 0b011011:  # TBZ/TBNZ
            b = (bits(w, 31, 1) << 5) | bits(w, 19, 5)
            nz, rt = bits(w, 24, 1), bits(w, 0, 5)
            t = pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 14), 14) * 4
            return Insn('bcond', target=t, cond=f'(({X(rt)} >> {b}) & 1) {"!=" if nz else "=="} 0')
        if bits(w, 25, 7) == 0b1101011:  # branch register
            opc, rn = bits(w, 21, 4), bits(w, 5, 5)
            if bits(w, 16, 5) != 31 or bits(w, 10, 6) or bits(w, 0, 5):
                raise Unsupported('branch reg variant')
            if opc == 0:
                return Insn('br', target=X(rn))
            if opc == 1:
                return Insn('blr', target=X(rn))
            if opc == 2:
                return Insn('ret')
            raise Unsupported('branch reg opc')
        if bits(w, 24, 8) == 0b11010100:  # exception generation
            opc, ll, imm = bits(w, 21, 3), bits(w, 0, 5), bits(w, 5, 16)
            if opc == 0 and ll == 1:
                return Insn('op', f'rt_svc(c, {imm}, {hx(pc)});')
            if opc == 1 and ll == 0:
                return Insn('trap', f'rt_brk(c, {imm}, {hx(pc)});')
            raise Unsupported('exception')
        if bits(w, 22, 10) == 0b1101010100:
            return self.system(w, pc)
        raise Unsupported(f'branch_sys {w:08x}')

    def system(self, w, pc):
        L = bits(w, 21, 1)
        op0, op1, crn, crm, op2, rt = (bits(w, 19, 2), bits(w, 16, 3), bits(w, 12, 4),
                                       bits(w, 8, 4), bits(w, 5, 3), bits(w, 0, 5))
        if op0 == 0 and not L:
            if crn == 2 and op1 == 3 and rt == 31:  # hints
                return Insn('op', '/* hint */')
            if crn == 3 and op1 == 3 and rt == 31:  # barriers
                if op2 == 2:
                    return Insn('op', 'c->excl_addr = ~0ull;')
                return Insn('op', '__atomic_thread_fence(__ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);')
            raise Unsupported(f'pstate/system {w:08x}')
        if op0 == 1:  # SYS
            if not L and op1 == 3 and crn == 7 and crm == 4 and op2 == 1:  # DC ZVA
                return Insn('op', f'memset((void*)(uintptr_t)({X(rt)} & ~63ull), 0, 64);')
            return Insn('op', '/* cache maintenance */')
        key = (op0, op1, crn, crm, op2)
        if L:  # MRS
            src = {
                (3, 3, 13, 0, 3): 'c->tpidrro',
                (3, 3, 13, 0, 2): 'c->tpidr',
                (3, 3, 14, 0, 0): '19200000ull',
                (3, 3, 14, 0, 1): 'rt_ticks()',
                (3, 3, 14, 0, 2): 'rt_ticks()',
                (3, 3, 4, 2, 0): 'c->nzcv',
                (3, 3, 4, 4, 0): 'c->fpcr' if self.sc else 'rt_get_fpcr()',
                (3, 3, 4, 4, 1): 'c->fpsr' if self.sc else 'rt_get_fpsr()',
                (3, 3, 0, 0, 7): '4ull',
                (3, 3, 0, 0, 1): '0x8444c004ull',
            }.get(key)
            if src is None:
                raise Unsupported(f'mrs {key}')
            return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rt, src))
        dst = {
            (3, 3, 13, 0, 2): 'c->tpidr = {v};',
            (3, 3, 4, 2, 0): 'c->nzcv = {v} & 0xf0000000ull;',
            (3, 3, 4, 4, 0): 'rt_fpcr_write(c, {v});' if self.sc else 'rt_set_fpcr({v});',
            (3, 3, 4, 4, 1): 'c->fpsr = {v} & 0xf800009full;' if self.sc else 'rt_set_fpsr({v});',
        }.get(key)
        if dst is None:
            raise Unsupported(f'msr {key}')
        return Insn('op', dst.format(v=X(rt)))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ loads / stores

    def ldst(self, w, pc):
        V = bits(w, 26, 1)
        if V:
            if self.sc:
                return Insn('op', self.sc.ldst(w, pc))
            return self.ldst_simd(w, pc)
        if bits(w, 24, 6) == 0b001000:
            return self.ldst_excl(w, pc)
        if bits(w, 27, 3) == 0b011 and bits(w, 24, 2) == 0:  # literal
            opc, rt = bits(w, 30, 2), bits(w, 0, 5)
            addr = pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 19), 19) * 4
            if opc == 0:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(0, rt, f'LD32({hx(addr)})'))
            if opc == 1:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rt, f'LD64({hx(addr)})'))
            if opc == 2:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rt, f'(int64_t)(int32_t)LD32({hx(addr)})'))
            return Insn('op', '/* prfm */')
        if bits(w, 27, 3) == 0b101:
            return self.ldst_pair(w)
        if bits(w, 27, 3) == 0b111:
            return self.ldst_reg(w)
        raise Unsupported(f'ldst {w:08x}')

    def ldst_excl(self, w, pc):
        size, o2, L, o1, rs, o0, rn, rt = (bits(w, 30, 2), bits(w, 23, 1), bits(w, 22, 1), bits(w, 21, 1),
                                           bits(w, 16, 5), bits(w, 15, 1), bits(w, 5, 5), bits(w, 0, 5))
        nbits = 8 << size
        addr = XS(rn)
        if o1:
            raise Unsupported('exclusive pair / CAS')
        if o2 == 0:
            if L:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rt, f'ldx{nbits}(c, {addr})'))
            return Insn('op', f'{{ uint32_t st = stx{nbits}(c, {addr}, {X(rt)}); {set_reg(0, rs, "st")} }}')
        if L:
            return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rt, f'lda{nbits}({addr})'))
        return Insn('op', f'stl{nbits}({addr}, {X(rt)});')

    def ldst_pair(self, w):
        opc, mode, L = bits(w, 30, 2), bits(w, 23, 2), bits(w, 22, 1)
        imm7, rt2, rn, rt = sext(bits(w, 15, 7), 7), bits(w, 10, 5), bits(w, 5, 5), bits(w, 0, 5)
        if opc == 3:
            raise Unsupported('pair opc 3')
        scale = 3 if opc == 2 else 2
        off = imm7 << scale
        base = XS(rn)
        post = mode == 1
        wb = mode in (1, 3)
        ea = base if post else (f'{base} + {off}' if off >= 0 else f'{base} - {-off}')
        lines = [f'uint64_t ea = {ea};']
        if L:
            if opc == 2:
                lines.append('uint64_t a = LD64(ea), b = LD64(ea + 8);')
            elif opc == 1:  # LDPSW
                lines.append('uint64_t a = (int64_t)(int32_t)LD32(ea), b = (int64_t)(int32_t)LD32(ea + 4);')
            else:
                lines.append('uint64_t a = LD32(ea), b = LD32(ea + 4);')
        else:
            if opc == 2:
                lines.append(f'ST64(ea, {X(rt)}); ST64(ea + 8, {X(rt2)});')
            else:
                lines.append(f'ST32(ea, {W(rt)}); ST32(ea + 4, {W(rt2)});')
        if wb:
            dst = 'c->sp' if rn == 31 else f'c->x[{rn}]'
            if not post:
                lines.append(f'{dst} = ea;')
            else:
                lines.append(f'{dst} = ea + {off};' if off >= 0 else f'{dst} = ea - {-off};')
        if L:
            lines.append(set_reg(1, rt, 'a'))
            lines.append(set_reg(1, rt2, 'b'))
        return Insn('op', '{ ' + ' '.join(lines) + ' }')

    def ldst_reg(self, w):
        size, opc, rn, rt = bits(w, 30, 2), bits(w, 22, 2), bits(w, 5, 5), bits(w, 0, 5)
        base = XS(rn)
        wb = None
        if bits(w, 24, 2) == 1:
            ea = f'{base} + {hx(bits(w, 10, 12) << size)}'
        else:
            kind = bits(w, 10, 2)
            if bits(w, 21, 1):
                if kind != 2:
                    raise Unsupported('ldst reg atomic/pac')
                rm, option, S = bits(w, 16, 5), bits(w, 13, 3), bits(w, 12, 1)
                if option not in (2, 3, 6, 7):
                    raise Unsupported('ldst reg option')
                ea = f'{base} + {extend_expr(rm, option, size if S else 0)}'
            else:
                imm9 = sext(bits(w, 12, 9), 9)
                sign_imm = f'+ {imm9}' if imm9 >= 0 else f'- {-imm9}'
                if kind in (0, 2):  # unscaled, unprivileged
                    ea = f'{base} {sign_imm}'
                elif kind == 1:  # post
                    ea = base
                    wb = f'{base} {sign_imm}'
                else:  # pre
                    ea = f'{base} {sign_imm}'
                    wb = 'ea'
        nbits = 8 << size
        if opc == 0:
            parts = [f'ST{nbits}(ea, {X(rt) if size == 3 else W(rt)});']
            load = None
        elif opc == 1:
            parts = [f'uint64_t v = LD{nbits}(ea);']
            load = set_reg(1, rt, 'v')
        elif size == 3:
            return Insn('op', '/* prfm */')
        elif size == 2 and opc == 3:
            raise Unsupported('ldst size2 opc3')
        else:
            parts = [f'uint64_t v = (uint64_t)(int64_t)(int{nbits}_t)LD{nbits}(ea);']
            load = set_reg(1 if opc == 2 else 0, rt, 'v')
        parts.insert(0, f'uint64_t ea = {ea};')
        if wb:
            # writeback before the register load, so a load into rn wins
            parts.append(f'{"c->sp" if rn == 31 else f"c->x[{rn}]"} = {wb};')
        if load:
            parts.append(load)
        return Insn('op', '{ ' + ' '.join(parts) + ' }')

    def ldst_simd(self, w, pc):
        """FP/SIMD loads and stores are passed through as asm; GPR address regs are remapped."""
        rt = bits(w, 0, 5)
        if bits(w, 27, 3) == 0b011 and bits(w, 24, 2) == 0:  # literal -> LDR (imm, offset 0) via scratch
            opc = bits(w, 30, 2)
            size, o = {0: (2, 1), 1: (3, 1), 2: (0, 3)}[opc]
            addr = pc + sext(bits(w, 5, 19), 19) * 4
            new = (size << 30) | 0x3D000000 | (o << 22) | (31 << 5) | rt
            return Insn('asm', asm=AsmInsn(new, {rt}, [], consts=[(5, addr)]))
        if bits(w, 31, 1) == 0 and bits(w, 24, 6) in (0b001100, 0b001101):  # structures
            post = bits(w, 23, 1)
            rn, rm = bits(w, 5, 5), bits(w, 16, 5)
            if bits(w, 24, 1) == 0:
                n = {0: 4, 2: 4, 4: 3, 6: 3, 7: 1, 8: 2, 10: 2}.get(bits(w, 12, 4))
                if n is None:
                    raise Unsupported('ldst multiple opcode')
            else:
                n = ((bits(w, 13, 1) << 1) | bits(w, 21, 1)) + 1
            vregs = {(rt + i) % 32 for i in range(n)}
            gprs = [(5, 'sp' if rn == 31 else rn)]
            if post and rm != 31:
                gprs.append((16, rm))
            return Insn('asm', asm=AsmInsn(w, vregs, gprs))
        rn = bits(w, 5, 5)
        gprs = [(5, 'sp' if rn == 31 else rn)]
        vregs = {rt}
        if bits(w, 27, 3) == 0b101:  # pair
            vregs.add(bits(w, 10, 5))
        elif bits(w, 27, 3) == 0b111 and bits(w, 24, 2) == 0 and bits(w, 21, 1) and bits(w, 10, 2) == 2:
            rm = bits(w, 16, 5)
            if rm != 31:
                gprs.append((16, rm))
        return Insn('asm', asm=AsmInsn(w, vregs, gprs))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ data processing (reg)

    def dp_reg(self, w, pc):
        sf = bits(w, 31, 1)
        rd, rn, rm = bits(w, 0, 5), bits(w, 5, 5), bits(w, 16, 5)
        size = 64 if sf else 32
        op1 = bits(w, 28, 1)
        if not op1:
            if bits(w, 24, 4) == 0b1010:  # logical shifted
                opc, sh, N, amt = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 22, 2), bits(w, 21, 1), bits(w, 10, 6)
                if not sf and amt >= 32:
                    raise Unsupported('logical shift amount')
                b = shift_expr(sf, R(sf, rm), sh, amt)
                if N:
                    b = f'(uint{size}_t)~{b}'
                a = R(sf, rn)
                expr = {0: f'{a} & {b}', 1: f'{a} | {b}', 2: f'{a} ^ {b}', 3: f'{a} & {b}'}[opc]
                if opc == 3:
                    return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'logic{size}(c, (uint{size}_t)({expr}))'))
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, expr))
            if bits(w, 24, 4) == 0b1011:  # add/sub shifted or extended
                op, S = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 29, 1)
                if bits(w, 21, 1) == 0:
                    sh, amt = bits(w, 22, 2), bits(w, 10, 6)
                    if sh == 3:
                        raise Unsupported('add shift ror')
                    a = R(sf, rn)
                    b = shift_expr(sf, R(sf, rm), sh, amt)
                    sp_ok = False
                else:
                    if bits(w, 22, 2):
                        raise Unsupported('add ext opt')
                    option, amt = bits(w, 13, 3), bits(w, 10, 3)
                    a = R(sf, rn, sp=True)
                    b = extend_expr(rm, option, amt)
                    if not sf:
                        b = f'(uint32_t)({b})'
                    sp_ok = not S
                if S:
                    fn = ('subs' if op else 'adds') + str(size)
                    return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{fn}(c, {a}, (uint{size}_t)({b}))'))
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{a} {"-" if op else "+"} {b}', sp=sp_ok))
            raise Unsupported(f'dp_reg {w:08x}')
        op2 = bits(w, 21, 4)
        if bits(w, 24, 4) == 0b1011:  # 3-source
            op54, op31, o0, ra = bits(w, 29, 2), bits(w, 21, 3), bits(w, 15, 1), bits(w, 10, 5)
            if op54:
                raise Unsupported('dp3 op54')
            sgn = '-' if o0 else '+'
            if op31 == 0:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{R(sf, ra)} {sgn} {R(sf, rn)} * {R(sf, rm)}'))
            if op31 == 1:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rd, f'{X(ra)} {sgn} (uint64_t)((int64_t)(int32_t){W(rn)} * (int64_t)(int32_t){W(rm)})'))
            if op31 == 5:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rd, f'{X(ra)} {sgn} (uint64_t){W(rn)} * (uint64_t){W(rm)}'))
            if op31 == 2:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(
                    1, rd, f'(uint64_t)(((__int128)(int64_t){X(rn)} * (__int128)(int64_t){X(rm)}) >> 64)'))
            if op31 == 6:
                return Insn('op', set_reg(1, rd, f'(uint64_t)(((unsigned __int128){X(rn)} * {X(rm)}) >> 64)'))
            raise Unsupported('dp3')
        if op2 == 0:  # add/sub with carry
            op, S = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 29, 1)
            fn = ('sbc' if op else 'adc') + ('s' if S else '') + str(size)
            return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'{fn}(c, {R(sf, rn)}, {R(sf, rm)})'))
        if op2 == 2:  # conditional compare
            op, imm_form, cond, nzcv = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 11, 1), bits(w, 12, 4), bits(w, 0, 4)
            b = hx(rm) if imm_form else R(sf, rm)
            fn = ('subs' if op else 'adds') + str(size)
            return Insn('op', f'if ({cond_expr(cond)}) (void){fn}(c, {R(sf, rn)}, {b}); '
                              f'else c->nzcv = {hx(nzcv << 28)};')
        if op2 == 4:  # conditional select
            op, o2, cond = bits(w, 30, 1), bits(w, 10, 2), bits(w, 12, 4)
            b = R(sf, rm)
            alt = {(0, 0): b, (0, 1): f'{b} + 1', (1, 0): f'~{b}', (1, 1): f'-{b}'}.get((op, o2))
            if alt is None:
                raise Unsupported('csel variant')
            return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, f'({cond_expr(cond)}) ? {R(sf, rn)} : (uint{size}_t)({alt})'))
        if op2 == 6:
            opcode = bits(w, 10, 6)
            if bits(w, 30, 1):  # 1-source
                if bits(w, 16, 5):
                    raise Unsupported('dp1 opcode2')
                a = R(sf, rn)
                expr = {
                    0: f'rbit{size}({a})',
                    1: f'rev16_{size}({a})',
                    2: f'__builtin_bswap32({a})' if not sf else f'rev32_64({a})',
                    3: f'__builtin_bswap64({a})' if sf else None,
                    4: f'clz{size}({a})',
                    5: f'cls{size}({a})',
                }.get(opcode)
                if expr is None:
                    raise Unsupported('dp1')
                return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, expr))
            if 16 <= opcode <= 23:  # CRC32: host has the same instruction
                if self.sc:
                    return Insn('op', self.sc.crc(w))
                gprs = [(p, r) for p, r in ((0, rd), (5, rn), (16, rm)) if r != 31]
                return Insn('asm', asm=AsmInsn(w, set(), gprs))
            a, b = R(sf, rn), R(sf, rm)
            expr = {
                2: f'udiv{size}({a}, {b})',
                3: f'sdiv{size}({a}, {b})',
                8: f'{a} << ({b} & {size - 1})',
                9: f'{a} >> ({b} & {size - 1})',
                10: f'(uint{size}_t)((int{size}_t){a} >> ({b} & {size - 1}))',
                11: f'ROR{size}({a}, {b} & {size - 1})',
            }.get(opcode)
            if expr is None:
                raise Unsupported('dp2')
            return Insn('op', set_reg(sf, rd, expr))
        raise Unsupported(f'dp_reg {w:08x}')

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ FP / SIMD data processing

    def fp_simd(self, w, pc):
        if self.sc:
            return Insn('op', self.sc.dp(w, pc))
        rd, rn, rm, ra = bits(w, 0, 5), bits(w, 5, 5), bits(w, 16, 5), bits(w, 10, 5)
        vregs = {rd, rn, rm, ra}
        gprs = []
        flags = False
        if (w & 0x5F20FC00) == 0x1E200000:  # FP <-> integer
            opcode = bits(w, 16, 3)
            if opcode in (0, 1, 4, 5, 6):
                gprs = [(0, rd)]
                vregs = {rn}
            else:
                gprs = [(5, rn)]
                vregs = {rd}
        elif (w & 0x5F200000) == 0x1E000000:  # FP <-> fixed point
            opcode = bits(w, 16, 3)
            if opcode in (0, 1):
                gprs = [(0, rd)]
                vregs = {rn}
            else:
                gprs = [(5, rn)]
                vregs = {rd}
        elif (w & 0x9FE08400) == 0x0E000400 and bits(w, 29, 1) == 0:  # AdvSIMD copy
            imm4 = bits(w, 11, 4)
            if imm4 in (1, 3):
                gprs = [(5, rn)]
                vregs = {rd}
            elif imm4 in (5, 7):
                gprs = [(0, rd)]
                vregs = {rn}
            else:
                vregs = {rd, rn}
        elif (w & 0xBFE08C00) == 0x0E000000:  # TBL/TBX
            n = bits(w, 13, 2) + 1
            vregs = {rd, rm} | {(rn + i) % 32 for i in range(n)}
        if (w & 0x5F203C00) == 0x1E202000 or (w & 0x5F200C00) in (0x1E200400, 0x1E200C00):
            flags = True
        gprs = [(p, r) for p, r in gprs if r != 31]  # register 31 is zr in these encodings
        return Insn('asm', asm=AsmInsn(w, vregs, gprs, flags))


def cond_expr(cond):
    return f'COND_{COND_NAMES[cond].upper()}(c)' if cond < 14 else '1'


def emit_asm_batch(batch):
    """Emit one inline-asm block for a run of FP/SIMD instructions."""
    vregs = set()
    gmap = {}
    consts = []
    words = []
    flags = any(a.flags for a in batch)
    pool = [r for r in SCRATCH if not (flags and r == 16)]  # (x16 holds NZCV around the batch: never a guest reg's)
    for a in batch:
        vregs |= a.vregs
        w = a.word
        for pos, g in a.gprs:
            if g not in gmap:
                if len(gmap) + len(consts) >= len(pool):
                    raise Unsupported('scratch exhausted')
                gmap[g] = pool[len(gmap) + len(consts)]
            w = (w & ~(31 << pos)) | (gmap[g] << pos)
        for pos, val in a.consts:
            if len(gmap) + len(consts) >= len(pool):
                raise Unsupported('scratch exhausted')
            s = pool[len(gmap) + len(consts)]
            consts.append((s, val))
            w = (w & ~(31 << pos)) | (s << pos)
        words.append(w)
    lines = []
    ins = ['"r"(c)']
    for g, s in gmap.items():
        off = OFF_SP if g == 'sp' else OFF_X + 8 * g
        lines.append(f'ldr x{s}, [%0, #{off}]')
    for i, (s, val) in enumerate(consts):
        ins.append(f'"r"({hx(val)})')
        lines.append(f'mov x{s}, %{len(ins) - 1}')
    for v in sorted(vregs):
        lines.append(f'ldr q{v}, [%0, #{OFF_V + 16 * v}]')
    if flags:
        lines.append(f'ldr x16, [%0, #{OFF_NZCV}]')
        lines.append('msr nzcv, x16')
    lines += [f'.inst 0x{x:08x}' for x in words]
    if flags:
        lines.append('mrs x16, nzcv')
        lines.append(f'str x16, [%0, #{OFF_NZCV}]')
    for v in sorted(vregs):
        lines.append(f'str q{v}, [%0, #{OFF_V + 16 * v}]')
    for g, s in gmap.items():
        off = OFF_SP if g == 'sp' else OFF_X + 8 * g
        lines.append(f'str x{s}, [%0, #{off}]')
    clob = [f'"v{v}"' for v in sorted(vregs)]
    clob += [f'"x{s}"' for s in sorted(set(gmap.values()) | {s for s, _ in consts} | ({16} if flags else set()))]
    clob += ['"cc"', '"memory"']
    body = '\\n\\t'.join(lines)
    return f'__asm__ volatile("{body}" :: {", ".join(ins)} : {", ".join(clob)});'

```
# Build environment for the Linux AppImages (tools/linux/appimage.sh): Ubuntu 22.04, so the result runs on glibc 2.35+.
# Built once per arch (podman build --arch amd64 / arm64). The amd64 image builds everything, the aarch64 AppImage
# cross-compiled; the arm64 image is the cross build's sysroot (the same -dev packages) and freezes the arm64 seed
# generator helper (PyInstaller only builds for the machine it runs on).
FROM docker.io/library/ubuntu:22.04
ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        ca-certificates curl git file xz-utils patchelf make cmake ninja-build pkg-config nasm python3 \
        g++ software-properties-common gpg-agent \
        # SDL3's video / audio / input backends (it loads them at run time; the headers decide what it can use)
        libx11-dev libxext-dev libxrandr-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxss-dev libxfixes-dev libxtst-dev \
        libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev wayland-protocols libdecor-0-dev libegl-dev libgl-dev libdrm-dev libgbm-dev \
        libpulse-dev libasound2-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libdbus-1-dev libudev-dev libibus-1.0-dev \
        libvulkan-dev \
    && add-apt-repository -y ppa:deadsnakes/ppa \
    # clang 21 from apt.llvm.org: 22.04's clang 15 lacks the __builtin_elementwise_* the lifted FP code uses (simd_fp.h)
    && curl -fsSL https://apt.llvm.org/llvm-snapshot.gpg.key -o /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/apt.llvm.org.asc \
    && echo "deb http://apt.llvm.org/jammy/ llvm-toolchain-jammy-21 main" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/llvm.list \
    && apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3.12 python3.12-venv python3.12-dev clang-21 lld-21 llvm-21 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && for t in clang clang++ ld.lld llvm-ar llvm-nm llvm-ranlib llvm-strip; do ln -sf $t-21 /usr/bin/$t; done
